in writing. after years of negotiation, the adoption of this text marks a significant step forward for passenger rights in europe, and in particular for disabled passengers and persons with reduced mobility. with the adoption of this regulation (concerning bus and coach travel), all modes of transport in the european union are now covered by legislation which offers rights and guarantees to passengers if, for example, their journey is cancelled or delayed, or if their luggage is lost, etc. however, i regret that this regulation applies only from 250 km upwards, thus excluding three member states of the european union (luxembourg, malta and cyprus) and many routes such as brussels-amsterdam or budapest-vienna. finally, i also regret the lack of flexibility for 'travel' in cross-border areas, which is a hindrance to the mobility of europeans. in other words, it is a much less ambitious text than the one we had advocated in the conciliation committee a few months ago and much less ambitious than what i would have wished for passengers in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text not only because it aims to strengthen the rights of passengers in bus and coach transport in terms of compensation and assistance in the event of an accident, but also because it underlines the principle of non-discrimination for people with reduced mobility, who must also have real access to these modes of transport, which now account for 10% of the land transport of passengers in europe. it is also welcome that passenger rights are now protected in all modes of transport.
in writing. i am pleased that the negotiations between parliament and the member states have finally led to the adoption of a regulation guaranteeing enhanced rights for passengers travelling by bus and coach. it fills a gap in passenger rights legislation - there were no european rules on this subject until now, unlike in the air or rail transport sectors. the text provides for the introduction of a number of compensatory measures: snacks and refreshments for delays of more than 1h30; the cost of an overnight stay in the event of a break in the journey, an accident or a delay requiring an overnight stay; the maximum reimbursement is at least eur 1200 in the event of loss of or damage to checked baggage. in addition, specific rights are granted to disabled passengers: in particular the obligation for airlines to provide assistance to disabled passengers subject to having informed them of their needs 36 hours in advance and compensation or reimbursement for any damage or loss of specialised equipment. this regulation will apply to all scheduled, national or cross-border long-distance services (250 km and above) from spring 2013.

in writing. europe is moving forward... thanks to the lisbon treaty, it is now possible for a group of countries that want to move forward together on a specific issue to do so, even if some are not interested. this is already the case with regard to the rules applicable to the divorce of binational couples. this is called enhanced cooperation ... i wanted the same to be true for the protection of european innovations and for closer cooperation to be implemented to create a european patent. while the cost of patent protection for inventions is ten times higher in europe than in the united states, partly because of translation costs, 25 of the 27 member states want to create a european patent together, which is less expensive because it is unitary. the unitary patent will be filed in french, english or german and will protect our inventions in the 25 countries concerned... and this at affordable prices! even if spain and italy are not in favour of such a system for linguistic reasons, it is essential that the 25 states concerned move forward together on this subject. as this is a major step forward for the competitiveness of european industry, i voted in favour of this procedure.

in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation, which was to authorize enhanced cooperation for the creation of a european patent. in december 2010, 12 member states, including france, had wanted to use an enhanced cooperation procedure after the 27 had disagreed on the establishment of a community patent system due to linguistic differences. all member states eventually decided to participate, except italy and spain. i hope that these two countries can join the initiative at any time. our researchers and companies will finally be able to start playing on a par with the us and asia in terms of innovation, because it is now 11 times more expensive to patent in the eu than in the us.

is on the agenda. once again, rising food prices are causing social unrest and political instability in several countries. families in the poorest regions of the world are in difficulty. moreover, the food and agriculture organisation tells us that the outlook is not good, with prices set to rise further this year as a result of adverse climatic conditions. this is a pressing issue. it was discussed between agriculture ministers and wto director-general lamy in berlin on 22 january 2011, and once again in the agriculture council on 24 january this year. the reasons for this latest rise in prices are complex and are a mixture of structural and temporary factors. on the demand side, we have more people to feed than ever before. on the supply side, droughts and floods have played their part in wrecking harvests, input costs have risen and this has all been compounded by financial speculation in the commodity markets. so what can the european union do to address this problem? we need to get our internal policies right, we need to improve global governance in this area and we need to make a real contribution to the most vulnerable. now is not the time for complacency, but we did make some important progress in all three aspects as a result of the last food prices crisis. the council, along with parliament, is engaged in an intensive debate on the future development of the common agricultural policy. this is highly relevant with regard to global food security. recent council debates put food security at the centre of the discussion, asking the question how best to ensure that agricultural production in the eu will be both economically viable and environmentally sustainable in the future. let me also say that we have read with great interest parliament’s resolution on the recognition of agriculture as a strategic sector in the context of food security, based on the report by the honourable member, daciana sârbu. there are ongoing discussions in the council concerning the commission’s communication of 18 november 2010 on the future of the cap, and the hungarian presidency plans to adopt council conclusions at the council meeting of 17 march. we hope that the discussions concerning the legislative proposals scheduled to come out in the second semester of 2011 will lead to concrete progress. we have made important progress towards a more coordinated and long-term international response to world food security. we are a long way from reaching the millennium development goal to halve the world’s hungry people by 2015. hunger and food insecurity remain a reality for a billion people, but one of the un’s recent achievements, following much work by the eu, has been the creation of the global partnership for agriculture, food security and nutrition. this is being implemented by the revitalised committee on world food security in the fao. the eu has also been spearheading the renewal and modernisation of the food aid convention in order to better contribute to world food security and to improve the ability of the international community to deliver food assistance to the most vulnerable populations. this is the way forward in order to enhance global governance in this area. from a food security perspective, i would like to remind you of the commission’s communication on humanitarian food assistance, adopted at the end of march 2010, and the subsequent council conclusions in mid-may 2010, thus outlining a new policy framework for eu humanitarian action to strengthen efforts to tackle food insecurity in humanitarian crises. the commission’s communication on assisting developing countries in addressing food security challenges, also adopted last year, called at the same time for a new common food security policy framework, further strengthening eu leadership in the global food security agenda and improving the effectiveness of eu assistance. to this end, the commission and member states are jointly developing an implementation plan to translate this policy framework into concrete actions on the ground. let me also mention the eu’s eur 1 billion food facility, which was agreed by parliament and the council. we are in the third year of operation of this instrument which helps farmers in the developing world to increase agricultural production capacity. this is a tangible sign of our determination to bring real assistance to the most vulnerable. decisions are about to commence on the future orientation of the eu development policy based on the green paper on eu development policy in support of inclusive growth and sustainable development. with the green paper process, the commission takes the initiative of attributing priority to economic growth generation, agriculture and food security in development cooperation in order to achieve inclusive and sustainable development in developing countries on the grounds of pro-poor solutions. given the rising food prices and rapid population growth, enhancing developing countries’ own food production capacities is of paramount importance. we also welcome the new impetus given by the g20 seoul summit to the wto doha development agenda. the eu would give full backing to a deal which would make a significant contribution to providing stability by getting rid of export subsidies and prohibiting export restrictions. the latter only serve to exacerbate price volatility and have exactly the opposite effect of the one desired. let me now come back to the issue of financial speculation. the extent to which it contributes to price volatility is unclear, but there is a good reason to enhance transparency on the commodity markets. the french presidency of the g20 has identified this as a priority for the coming year. the hungarian presidency of the eu is ready to work shoulder to shoulder with the french presidency of the g20 to achieve concrete results. the hungarian presidency is fully committed to working with you towards a first reading agreement on the commission proposal on over-the-counter derivatives. the world’s poor and hungry deserve an adequate and lasting response to their worries about rising food prices. the european union has been at the forefront in efforts to tackle the issue since the first crisis three years ago, but more needs to be done. the council remains fully committed to a collective and coherent response, both at eu and international level. i am sure we can count on your support in all our efforts. thank you very much for your attention.
member of the commission. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank you for giving me the opportunity to make a statement on behalf of the commission on the increase in food prices. it was at my request that this matter was discussed at the agriculture council on 24 january. i therefore also welcome the opportunity to have this dialogue with the european parliament on a key issue. i would like to deal with two subjects which i believe are interrelated. firstly, the situation on the international agricultural markets, which have been rising again for several weeks, and secondly, the g20 process on food security and agricultural price volatility. let us start with the situation on the international agricultural markets. the world has been put on alert again by reports from several international institutions, including the fao, on the rise in agricultural and food prices. are we experiencing the same price spikes as in 2007-2008? even though prices, especially cereals, have risen sharply since summer and again recently , we do not seem to be at the 2008 price level. the world situation is tense for common wheat, but there is no problem with supplying the market. the current harvests in the southern hemisphere are larger than expected. nevertheless, in order to facilitate the end of the marketing years for the european union market, we are considering a suspension of import duties within the tariff quotas for low- and medium-quality common wheat and for fodder barley, as we believe that this is one of the measures which could help to relax the market a little at european level. it should be recalled that the forecasts for world stocks of common wheat at the end of the 2010-2011 marketing year are higher than in 2007. sugar prices are again reaching record levels, with a price for white sugar of around eur 625 per tonne in mid-january. the price increase follows two years of global deficit due to low production. the current crop yield has recently been revised down in some countries, notably australia. but according to the latest forecasts, the global balance for sugar is expected to be in balance for the period 2010-2011. yet, there is a lesson to be learned from all of this. even though markets may be tense, there is certainly an overreaction at the price level compared to what the physical fundamentals are telling us. clearly, food security and the underlying issue of agricultural price volatility are global issues that must be addressed at the global level as well. and i am pleased that the issue of food security and volatility is one of the priorities set by the g20 in seoul. for the commission as a whole, this is a major challenge. as commissioner for agriculture and rural development, i have already stated my commitment on this subject on several occasions, in international forums, for example in berlin at the end of january, with my counterparts from the various countries involved in the g20, but also recently in the united nations, with secretary-general ban ki-moon, during a recent visit to new york. it should also be noted that the issue of food security is explicitly included as one of the challenges of the common agricultural policy in the communication that the commission has presented for the common agricultural policy for 2020. this is a key issue both for the european union and for the poorest countries in the world, and that is why i am working closely with commissioner piebalgs on these issues, to better adapt the european union's development policy also to this issue of food security. i would like to share with you my thoughts on these issues today, particularly on four topics: transparency, stocks, volatility management options and the role of trade. it is understood that volatility is exacerbated by a lack of transparency in both physical and derivatives markets. for agricultural markets, there are data sources on production, consumption, trade and stocks. detailed data on this subject are produced by international organisations, national services or specialised organisations such as the international grains council. that said, some data can be improved, particularly those on stocks for which information is lacking, in particular on the distribution of stocks worldwide. the g20 leaders meeting in seoul have also asked the relevant international organisations to improve information on stocks and production forecasts. improving the relevance of such data is a prerequisite for better market transparency. the question of a global forum for discussion between the main market makers - exporters and importers - is also a must, so as not to simply see crises when they happen. that is why these three issues are linked: first, we need to have the information, then we need to be able to process this data, and then we need to have a place, at the international level, where we can discuss the situation. the commission has published several communications on the price of agricultural and food products and the food chain. in its last communication, the commission launched actions to improve transparency throughout the food chain, and i am working with commission vice-president tajani to advance this key topic. proposals were also announced to improve transparency and supervision of agricultural commodity derivatives. in the face of increased volatility, it is important that futures markets continue to fulfil their role as hedging and price discovery. we therefore need a balanced and rigorous approach, and i welcome the work carried out by commissioner barnier in this area and i fully support him in his work to cover the specific issue of agricultural raw materials. on 2 february the commission published a new and more comprehensive communication on the commodities market and the financial markets derived from it. this is a contribution to the discussions within the g20 on both commodity price volatility and the supervision of derivatives markets. we want to contribute, with our g20 partners and beyond, to more effective regulation of derivatives markets in the interests of producers and users. i therefore believe that we must work on the following issues as a matter of priority in the coming months - i think by the summer - firstly, the availability and transparency of information relating to private and public stocks, production and consumption; the second is the question of the collection, processing and dissemination of this information. the backstop mechanism for countries facing food stress; the role and organisation of food aid at international level and in the european union; improving international governance, for example through institutional dialogue mechanisms between key countries; levels of investment in sustainable agricultural production and research, in the european union but also in the poorest countries. the level of priority to be given to agriculture in development policies is also an issue to be addressed, especially as the commission prepares to adapt and reform development policy. i think that in this context the european union must be much more present, not only with food aid but above all with support for the countries of the south to enable them to develop their own local production capacity in a sustainable way. in the european union we need to look more seriously - and i intend to do so - at identifying market mechanisms that will allow us to avoid disasters in certain sectors as a result of this temporary strain on the level of producers' incomes and the cost of inputs. i am thinking in particular of livestock farming. i come now to the role of trade. we believe that trade can contribute to global food security by ensuring a fair distribution of food supplies throughout the world. export restrictions have only reinforced the spiral of rising prices to the detriment of already fragile countries. however, trade policy on food products should be linked to other food policies at international level if we want a coherent approach to this issue. in conclusion, i can assure you that i am following developments in food prices very closely and i want to work in the future in liaison with you here in parliament and with the council on this matter, to make concrete proposals, first with the reform of the common agricultural policy, but also with other more specific instruments.
i would like to start by sharing the point made by mrs mcguinness that there is a vital link between the food question and the agricultural question. the subject of our concern is the increase in food prices, with the consequences this may have for a number of populations in the world, but also in europe. i'd like to try and share a little bit of information first. the trend towards higher prices for agricultural products and agricultural raw materials is, in my view, a long-term trend which will continue for three main reasons: first, the world's changing demographics and the increase in the world's population. secondly, the fact that we have returned, with global warming, to climate hazards that are a problem, whether it's drought or flooding. thirdly, because the world is also developing. with new emerging countries, consumption levels are rising. so the tension in agricultural markets and agricultural commodities is a heavy trend. it is aggravated by price volatility and price volatility is a consequence of the financialisation of the world economy. this is also the subject that must be tackled if we are to solve both the agricultural and the food question. to do this - what the commissioner said is important - there are two elements: yes, we need transparency on stocks, but we also need a public policy on stocks in europe and stock management on a global scale, particularly at un level. secondly, financial markets and financial speculation must be regulated, in particular by refusing to allow speculative volume to have any connection with the physical quantities traded on the markets. we cannot accept that speculators speculate on the food question without taking into account the consequences of this, since it is the food of the world and of humanity. this brings me to two major conclusions: we need a strong european policy and we strategically reaffirm europe's commitment to be a food and agricultural player on a global scale. secondly, we need to change our development policy to make sure that on a global scale - and europe is a player - we invest again in agriculture because we will need all farms to feed the world. madam president, mr president, commissioner, i would like to address a matter which has been raised on several occasions and often presented as a single reason: speculation. i think that in speculation, we must be measured. it is clear that there is a definite link between certain financial activities and the volatility and the rise in commodity prices. but to reduce the whole question to financial speculation would certainly be wrong since part of what is called speculation is in fact the legitimate hedging of prices by producers and, as we know, these producers could not do without this possibility of hedging. on the other hand, direct investment in raw materials must be avoided from having, by reason of its massive nature or its purely speculative nature, adverse effects on price volatility. in this respect, the proposals made by commissioner barnier in the financial field, in particular the regulation of short selling, the regulation of derivatives and also the forthcoming revision of the mif directive, should give parliament the opportunity to take account of the aspects of commodity speculation in the regulation and supervision that will be put in place so that these markets are also regulated in a way that is both effective and pragmatic. as you said, commissioner, these efforts must be continued and i believe that parliament, which has followed and sometimes even gone ahead of the commission's proposals in the financial crisis, will live up to its responsibility. finally, i would like to welcome the statement by the hungarian presidency that europe would support the french presidency of the g20, which has made the regulation of commodity markets one of its priorities.

president-in-office of the council. − madam president, i would like to thank all the members for this constructive debate. i believe that the high level of political attention afforded by parliament to this issue provides a helping hand to the presidency to fulfil its agenda with regard to the rising food prices. as has also been highlighted in this debate, due to the extent and depth of this issue, it requires multifaceted cooperation and complex solutions across various areas such as agriculture, regulation of financial products and services as well as development policy. with respect to biofuel production, i would just like to repeat that the eu is fully aware that the unsustainable production of biofuels can have negative effects, notably mass deforestation and food shortages. that is why the eu is committed to stepping up the development of second-generation biofuels made of non-food crops. the eu has also abolished the perverse financial incentives for biofuel production at the expense of food production. given the deep structural global roots of the problem, europe needs to play a leading role in tackling food prices and food security at global level. this is already taking place through a number of international organisations and programmes such as fao and the world food programme, as well as through more general forums such as the g20. i would just like to add that, on a personal level, this debate has reinforced my long-standing conviction that, to tackle global challenges, such as hunger in the world, volatility of food and raw material prices, turbulence on the financial markets, regulation of financial products and services, there is a need for much more global governance and more global rule-making. europe, based upon its unique experiences with governance and rule-making, does have a very special mission and responsibility here. it is for this reason that we believe that europe and the european union have to take a leading role in combating all these challenges. the hungarian presidency is pleased to note that it can count on parliament to maintain the work being made by the eu, both in terms of policy and of efforts at international level.
in writing. global food security is a key issue for the european union. immediate and continuous action is needed to ensure food security for eu citizens and the world. it is essential to develop sustainable agriculture in developing countries and to allocate an appropriate share of eu development aid to the agricultural sector. the dramatic reduction in the level of development aid allocated to agriculture since the 1980s is to be regretted, and it is to be hoped that the recognition of this need will reverse this trend. the european commission must give priority to agriculture in development aid, in particular aid to enable farmers to access markets and aid to small and medium-sized family farms. humanitarian food assistance should respond to the needs, challenges and structural constraints of developing countries, taking into account local production, distribution and transport as well as marketing capacities in those countries to help lay the foundations for their long-term food security.
in writing. the resolution on food price increases takes up the observation of a growing increase in food prices, for which we call for urgent measures to combat price manipulation. among the causes of this increase, climatic phenomena deserve special attention, in other words, better management of water and soil. the direct impact of rising food prices on the world population, which can trigger riots and social movements, should also encourage g20 leaders to agree on market measures to combat speculation.

be tabled on behalf of the committee on regional development. i thank the coordinators of the various political groups for their cooperation, which has enabled a broad consensus to be reached. i also thank the members who have helped to enrich this text with their amendments. the atlantic region is characterised by particular features. firstly, it is a dynamic maritime area, thanks to maritime transport, fishing and marine energy. it is also an area whose environment is fragile and remains to be preserved - i am thinking for example of the scourge of green algae - and which is subject to the consequences of climate change. it is also a peripheral area within the european union with problems of accessibility and connectivity and a small number of large urban centres. these particular features give rise to problems which transcend national borders and for which political responses must be sought at european level. the resolution calls on the commission to propose that the atlantic strategy take the form of an integrated strategy addressing both maritime and territorial issues. the maritime dimension is of paramount importance, since the atlantic territories have in common that they face the sea. links with the integrated maritime policy should be encouraged. the territorial dimension of these strategies is equally important. this concerns issues such as decentralisation, the development of urban and rural areas, and the strengthening of land-sea links. the atlantic strategy could be part of the territorial cooperation objective of cohesion policy and be based on an integrated, cross-cutting and territorial approach. this will allow for better policy coordination between different levels of governance by targeting particularly relevant issues. the strategy should be open to all regions of the european union bordering the atlantic, including the adjacent sub-basins and the outermost regions of macaronesia. the external dimension of the strategy, in particular in the areas of maritime security and surveillance and international trade relations, should also be taken into account. the atlantic strategy will need to promote better coordination of objectives and means by being closely linked to the european union 2020 strategy and future post-2014 community policies. it is not a question of spending more but rather of spending better through an atlantic sweep of existing policies. to this end, the strategy will need to be well articulated with regional policy and the integrated maritime policy. it will also have to seek synergies with other policies such as the trans-european transport networks, the common fisheries policy, tourism, environmental protection, energy policy and the framework programme for research and development. the strategy will need to be implemented as from 2014 and coordinated with the next multiannual financial framework. the territorial dimension of the strategy will contribute to the european union's objective of territorial cohesion, in particular through action in favour of decoupling. synergies will of course have to be found with maritime policy in order to develop the land links of these regions. it is essential to strengthen the north-south connection of the atlantic front, in particular through the establishment of motorways of the sea from andalusia to scotland. at the same time, the west-west transport infrastructure will have to be developed, along the lines of high-speed railways. i hope that the commission will propose as soon as possible an action plan that will break down its priorities into concrete actions to enable coordinated implementation with european policies after 2013. it will also be essential to involve the many partners involved, in particular regional and local public authorities and civil society organisations. cooperation under the atlantic strategy will have to depend primarily on the needs of the actors concerned. the political priorities defined in this framework will therefore need to be the subject of consensus. in this respect, the european grouping of territorial cooperation could be an interesting tool to facilitate cooperation between stakeholders in the atlantic area. this is the result of parliament's reflection on this strategy. we will be attentive to the commission's next proposals and will certainly make a concrete and precise contribution to them. madam commissioner, could you, if you can, of course, tell us what the commission's priorities are, how you envisage implementing this strategy and to what extent you will take parliament's proposals into account? we are certainly in strasbourg, mr president, and it is better to repeat than to contradict ourselves.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i welcome the draft integrated strategy for the atlantic region. we need a shared approach to the use of our maritime spaces, taking into account the specificities of each basin and providing a concerted response to the problems encountered. in particular, as the member for normandy, i would like to draw your attention to the specific nature of the channel, which i would like to see taken into account in the draft integrated strategy for the atlantic region. it is one of the european union's strategic sea ports, a vital passageway between the atlantic ocean and the north sea. it accounts for 20% of the world's fleet and more than 500 ships of over 300 tonnes pass through it every day. in addition to this transport activity, there is fishing, boating, the exploitation of grain and soon - and to my great satisfaction - the production of energy from offshore wind turbines. this concentration of activities requires a serious consideration of the question of maritime safety, which, in my view, must be addressed at community level also in the context of the atlantic strategy. you know that the bilateral bases on which its financing is based are now under threat. i have already warned you about this, commissioner, and i shall be particularly attentive to your replies in june.

in writing. this report contains some outrageous proposals. for example, "inculcating" healthcare staff "with an intercultural approach based on respect for diversity" in the care of their immigrant patients. the commission is also proposing to eliminate discrimination in access to assisted reproduction, in particular discrimination based on age or sexual orientation, while promoting access to abortion for all. what is dominant here is a synthesis of the culture of death and the inversion of values. and finally, to require all member states to introduce the equivalent of state medical aid, that is, free access to care for illegal immigrants. it should be remembered that in france, designed to respond to emergencies or the risk of epidemics, it is actually accessible to any illegal immigrant, for any ailment, and with minimal and unverifiable conditions. without control and without limits, this system allows for comfort treatments, encourages illegal immigration, encourages medical tourism and all sorts of fraud at an ever-increasing cost. at a time when our hospitals and medical systems are in ruins and more and more of our fellow citizens are being forced to forgo medical treatment for lack of funds, such a proposal is outrageous.
in writing. the report had to take account of age-related health inequalities, and it has now done so. these age-related health inequalities translate into limited access to adequate health care and innovative treatments. older people should be able to take medicines that have been tested for efficacy and safety in people of the same age. this group is still too excluded from clinical trials. the average age of patients participating in clinical trials for treatments for high blood pressure is 63 years old, but 44 percent of patients are over 70 years old when the problem is first diagnosed! the union and the member states must also anticipate without delay the social and economic consequences of the ageing of the european population by taking account of this demographic change.
in writing. tackling health inequalities exacerbated by the economic crisis between eu countries and regions has finally become a priority with the adoption of the estrela report. as rapporteur for the opinion of the femm committee, i voted in favour of a text which aims to improve access to healthcare for all, particularly for vulnerable groups, and to support medical and pharmaceutical research, and which calls on member states to stop cutting the budget for health services. the report also takes into account the gender dimension in health inequalities and improves access to reproductive care for women. these are major advances, and only the beginning of the fight against health inequalities in the eu.
in writing. ensuring access to healthcare for all, nationals and foreigners, with or without documents, is a basic principle of public security. we protect the health of each person the better if we protect the health of all. i welcome this report which recalls this public health imperative which is essential to the common welfare.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on 'reducing health inequalities in the european union' because i believe that there are now wide disparities between member states in health. all eu member states must, for example, guarantee women easy access to contraceptives and the right to safe abortion.
in writing. while taxation can be a reliable and sustainable source of funding through the establishment of a progressive tax regime, effective tax administration and transparent and responsible use of revenues, many developing countries fail to apply a minimum tax rate to finance their public services. the european union must therefore cooperate with these countries to promote good governance in the tax area. that is why i voted in favour of this text, which will bring about a stable, more efficient but also fairer taxation to reduce poverty in these countries, and which will also bring about a transparent, cooperative and fair international tax environment.
in writing. developing countries have seen their customs resources decline as a result of market liberalisation. these losses of resources can be offset by better governance and fairer and more efficient taxation. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs for human consumption. better aid to these countries also means ending the tax havens that are hampering their development. clearly, fairer taxation and greater legal certainty will encourage private foreign investment and thus, in the long run, growth. however, all these measures should not lead to a reduction in official development assistance. the member states are always inclined to reduce the share of their gdp devoted to official development assistance.
in writing. the fight against offshore companies and other tax evasion is a necessity. the hedge funds have been given almost total freedom of movement by the majority in this parliament. what, then, is the meaning of the purely declarative restrictions in this text? the economic partnership agreements, negotiated by means of ignoble pressure techniques, are ruining the acp states without leaving them any chance of recovery in the long term. this report says nothing about that. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the application of the principle of subsidiarity. i am voting against this text.
in writing. the adoption of the report on 'taxation and development - cooperation with developing countries to promote good governance in the tax area' is of particular importance with regard to the effectiveness of development aid granted by the eu member states and the european commission to developing countries. enforcing the principles of good governance in the tax area (transparency, exchange of information and fair tax competition) and combating tax havens, which are a brake on the development of the least developed countries, is an absolute necessity and will be a priority of my mandate.
in writing. the european parliament expressly calls on the council and the european commission to take greater account of agricultural interests in international trade negotiations, particularly in discussions with south america, a large grain-producing region which does not always meet european quality standards. this is an essential text for me. i therefore voted in favour of this one.
in writing. european agriculture cannot continue to be abused in trade negotiations with third countries. this is the subject of the report we have just adopted, which recalls a number of principles and calls for non-trade aspects to be better integrated into the negotiations. european farmers are rightly required to comply with stringent environmental and health standards for production hygiene, even though some of their competitors are entering the european market with products that do not always meet these standards. in fact, far too often our farmers suffer from unfair competition and therefore from a distortion of competition vis-à-vis certain third countries. the commission must take account of the warnings from parliament and farmers, especially as regards the negotiations with mercosur, which risk endangering european livestock production and fruit and vegetable producers in the outermost regions.
in writing. the report on the relationship between eu agriculture and international trade shows the catastrophic loss of power of european agriculture and tries to alert the european institutions, which are responsible for this failure. it is now difficult to feed europe, the cap has become, through the commission, a graveyard for the agricultural sector. the burden on farmers is only growing day by day. the strength that once was european agriculture and its export capacity have been drastically reduced as europe opens up to agricultural products from outside whose production methods do not meet the standards europeans set for themselves. the future of agriculture is at stake and it is certainly no longer up to the union and its institutions to do so. member states must be able to help their farmers for the good of all.
in writing. while i voted in favour of this resolution, i wanted to express my commitment to a number of principles by voting in favour of it (in particular on certain amendments). i wanted to stress that in the many trade agreements currently being negotiated with various eu partners, it is essential to reach agreements that are balanced and based on the principle of reciprocity. in this sense, imports of products from third countries should comply with health, social, consumer, environmental and animal protection rules similar to those we have in the eu. in addition, far too often concessions on agriculture are made in order to obtain better market access for industrial products or services in third countries. this approach is no longer acceptable, and in my vote i wanted to reiterate that european agriculture cannot be seen as a tool for the eu's trade policy. finally, i attach particular importance to the defence of the european system for the authorization and marketing of gmos. as the attacks on this regime at the wto are increasing, it is essential that the european commission defends it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the papastamkos report on eu agriculture and international trade. i particularly wanted to support the european parliament's willingness to emphasise firmly the dangers posed by the european commission's trade strategy for eu agriculture. while many trade agreements are being negotiated between the union and some of its partners (mercosur, canada, ukraine, etc.), it is our duty to remind the european commission of the need to conclude, realistically but without naivety, trade partnerships based on the principles of free trade, of course, but also on the principle of reciprocity, both in respect of health and social rules and consumer, environmental and animal protection, and which do not endanger certain european sectors of activity. i am thinking in particular of the agricultural sector, which is too often sacrificed to industrial products and services in trade negotiations. as such, the european union must be consistent between its agricultural policy, which is under revision, and its trade policy in order to maintain a strong agricultural sector, with a view to ensuring the food security of our citizens in a context of increased market volatility.
in writing. i voted in favour of the papastamkos report, which sends a strong message about the importance of european agriculture in international negotiations. while europe needs to increase its agricultural production to ensure food security, international agreements are often negotiated at the expense of the agricultural sector. in order to know in advance the consequences of these agreements on european agriculture, we want the european commission to produce and publish in-depth impact assessments of trade agreements before negotiations begin. in addition, the eu's high standards for health, the environment and animal welfare must be applied to products entering the eu. border controls by member states must ensure that european legislation is properly implemented in this area.
in writing. the text has the merit of being concerned about citizens overseas and advocating food security. i'm sensitive to it. but this report endorses the "active promotion of the european union's agricultural interests", free trade areas and trade agreements between the eu and chiquita or dole. worse, he explicitly threatens argentina with sanctions for decisions i recommend for my country. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of paragraphs 53 and 54 of the report on european agriculture and international trade because i believe that it is the duty of the european parliament to defend european farmers and consumers against the danger posed by the massive export of poor quality agricultural products, especially from certain latin american countries. the quality of our agricultural products must not be sacrificed for purely commercial reasons.
in writing. in my vote, i wanted to reiterate my firm position that we cannot sacrifice our agricultural model on the altar of commercial considerations. the european union's desire to open up and liberalize trade with its partners should not lead us to revise our requirements for food quality and safety in favour of consumers. that is why i have insisted on the need to impose reciprocal trade, health and social rules on our agricultural trade with third countries and not to accept additional concessions without guarantees. i also reject the idea that we should let our guard down when it comes to defending the interests of european farmers. it is thanks to the work of farmers that europe has been able to forge a close link with its agriculture and its land and to achieve a level of excellence in its agricultural production. it is therefore our duty to ensure fair competition in the union's trade relations with its partners. i therefore call for the establishment of mechanisms at european level to protect farmers and help them to cope with any distortion of competition.
in writing. the european union's current consumption of protein and oilseeds is 70% imported, mainly from brazil, argentina and the united states. as these products are not always subject to the same environmental, health and regulatory constraints on gmos as european products, the european union has decided to review its protein policy and increase domestic production of protein products. european consumers would thus benefit from a healthier and more varied diet. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the union's vegetable protein deficit. europe is largely dependent on imports of protein crops, mainly used for animal feed. this dependence is accompanied by increasing risks linked to price volatility on international markets. to combat this, we propose that the reform of the cap should include new provisions to support farmers in improving crop rotation systems, to invest in protein seed research and to improve farmer training in crop rotation and polyculture.
in writing. the haüsling report was a good text. increasing the union's protein independence, the development of short supply chains, aid to farmers contributing to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions are all measures which i support. but the pro-gmo lobbies and their representatives have managed to turn this text into a plea for the entry of contaminated food into european territory. it also promotes the return to animal flours with the risks that such flours entail. it is time to relocate the production of plant proteins. this text, in its new form, does not allow it. i will vote against it if gmos and animal meal are approved by this parliament.
in writing. i agree with many of the points raised in this resolution, which i supported in the vote. for example, the analysis that countries where men and women are treated equally in the labour market have a positive impact on their socioeconomic development seems to me to be quite sound. in my view, the promotion of equality between women and men is a social but also an economic matter of course.
in writing. the annual report on gender equality is an opportunity to highlight the challenges facing us in these times of economic and social crisis. this report, which was voted on women's day, should be linked to the report by mrs plumb on women's poverty in the european union. women are among the so-called vulnerable groups who have suffered the full effects of the crisis. because they work part-time more often than men, because they have sometimes precarious jobs in the service sector, because their careers are fragmented, because they are still paid less than men for similar work, and because their pensions are also reduced as a result, women must be given constant attention. the most sensitive issue in this report concerned the quotas for women on the boards of large companies, both private and public. of course, quotas are not the panacea and in an ideal society we would like to do without them. but to change people's minds, quotas are probably a must!
in writing. i welcome the vote on this report on equality between men and women. in terms of pay, for example, and despite ongoing legislative efforts in this area at european level, women still earn on average 18% less than men in the european union for equal work. i would also like to point out that it has taken a long time in this parliament to even mention a fundamental right such as access to contraception. the european right does not emerge from this back-room debate with much of a vengeance. fortunately, the final text is good. it sets the target of reducing the wage gap to below 5% by 2020 and calls on the member states to do their utmost to apply the principle of 'equal pay for equal work', with sanctions for non-compliant member states. it calls for binding targets to guarantee parity in positions of responsibility in companies, public administrations and political organisations.
in writing. equal opportunities and non-discrimination do not mean the abolition and negation of the differences and complementarity between men and women in their nature, their aspirations, their way of seeing the world and life. to say that is not to say that there are stereotypes. if you go to the extreme, your gender-indifferentiation logic will only lead to absurdity. absurd, this "right", in quotes, to work at night for women. or forced to. it's a social regression. we owe you one. absurd, this french case law which grants men the validation of free semesters for their retirement, a right previously reserved for women and which compensated - somewhat - for the career problems that their motherhood and the time spent educating their children may have caused them. absurd because it threatens the very existence of this advantage for women. the recent case law of the court of justice which calls for the statistical differences between men and women in the calculation of insurance premiums, which is the basis for calculating risk, to be denied, is absurd. ladies, that's enough of this little financial advantage from your extra caution and longevity. how far will the taliban of "gender equality" go?
in writing. i am very pleased that this resolution was adopted on the occasion of the 100th anniversary of international women's day. despite the principle of equal pay for men and women being enshrined in the eu treaties, women are still paid 17.8% less than men. this inequality is reflected in all areas of society: for example, only 3% of the heads of large enterprises are women, and women are the most affected by unemployment and precarious employment, hence the alarming finding that 17% of women in the 27 eu countries were considered to be living in poverty in 2008. other struggles are still needed, such as a better distribution of family responsibilities and better protection of women against domestic violence. all these figures show that there is now a need for binding instruments. that is why i decided to vote in favour of quotas, even though i was opposed to this idea in the first place, and of positive discrimination policies in the economic and political spheres. we must now recognize that we will not achieve real equality without genuinely voluntary policies.
in writing. international women's day is an annual opportunity to take stock of women's rights and gender equality in the european union. although there have been some notable improvements, it is clear that equality has not yet been fully achieved, either in practice or in mentality. yet it is a necessary condition for achieving its objectives of growth, employment and social cohesion. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which stresses the need to target and remedy the consequences of the crisis on women, which emphasises the role of education, and which calls on the european union to combat female poverty and all forms of violence against women. i think that one of the fundamental points of this text is also in paragraph 66 which affirms the right of women to easy access to contraception and abortion. in 11 eu countries abortion is still not fully legal...
in writing. the nedelcheva report makes a sad assessment of the progress made by the union in the area of equality between women and men. it is sad that we have to wait until 8 march to remember that 50% of european citizens are citizens and that their right to equality is being violated all over europe. i welcome this report for its expressed desire to put in place binding measures to ensure equal rights. however, i regret that he is using the europe 2020 strategy and his retirement at 64 to say that 'the family is the foundation of our society'. the foundation of our society is citizenship and the law. i denounce the process of trying to swallow antisocial and culturally regressive pills in waves of good intentions that are powerless.
in writing. the report on 'equality between women and men in the european union - 2010' is of particular importance as we celebrate the centenary of international women's day today. it is clear that there are still wide disparities between men and women in europe. it is necessary to call for binding targets to be set to ensure equal representation of men and women in positions of electoral responsibility as well as in companies. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this resolution proposes an analysis of women's poverty which i share: it is certainly the result of the recent economic crisis, but also of various factors such as stereotypes, the gender pay gap, the lack of reconciliation between family life and working life, the longer life expectancy of women, etc. i therefore welcome, as does our rapporteur, the establishment of a european microfinance facility. the aim is to make microfinance more easily accessible and available to women who have difficulty entering the labour market or who wish to set up as self-employed or start their own micro-enterprise.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is very difficult for me to accept that 17% of women in europe today live below the poverty line. the unprecedented economic crisis that the european union has just experienced has only made this sad fact worse. it is therefore time to put an end to this problem and adopt a set of measures to combat this scourge. the european union and its member states must put an end to poverty and social exclusion of women in europe by guaranteeing them, in particular, quality education and access to employment, by enabling them to reconcile family and professional life, and by strengthening the fight against the violence to which they are unfortunately too often subjected. i therefore support this own-initiative report, which highlights one of the shortcomings of our modern democracies, namely discrimination against women.
on behalf of the ppe group. madam vice-president, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, what lessons have we learned from the financial crisis? we have learned from the world war that our peoples should work together and not be divided. since the fall of the berlin wall, we have learned the lessons of authoritarian and communist regimes and have been able to re-unite our continent around the values of freedom, democracy and a social market economy. from the terrorist attack of september 11th, we understood that a new balance had to be found between security and freedom. the lesson to be drawn from this financial crisis is that our member states must stop considering cooperation in the budgetary, fiscal and social fields as taboo. i'm measuring the distance i've already traveled. the establishment this year of the 27's consultation on their budgetary priorities is in itself a revolution in mentality. the rules we have been able to devise to moralise the financial markets are also exemplary, but they are not enough. my group calls for an agreement between parliament and the council before the summer on strengthened economic governance. my group also calls for the coordination of the social and fiscal aspects to be continued. this is the meaning of the competitiveness pact, the initial version of which has already been revised in a more community-oriented sense. but we must go further and ensure that both the european parliament and the commission exercise all their prerogatives in this respect and we are counting on the president of the commission. the epp group welcomes and supports these proposals, as did the national leaders of the party in helsinki. ladies and gentlemen, how can we explain to our fellow citizens that, despite being in a difficult financial situation in mid-july each year, most of our member states should continue to spend as if nothing had happened? how is the over-indebtedness of our states more acceptable, more bearable, more sustainable than that of households or firms? i've proven that at a corporate level. the crisis has led to job losses, family tragedies; the least we can do is learn from it and speak the language of truth. the first lesson is that the obligations imposed on states - regardless of their size - to respect budgetary limits must no longer be treated lightly. secondly, european solidarity can only work if - and only if - our social and tax rules are at least comparable, not necessarily identical, but comparable. but that is far from the case. thirdly, europe must have a european stability mechanism to protect our social market economy. the fourth and final lesson is that even in the midst of the storm europe is holding its own and european integration is growing stronger. our american and japanese partners have debt levels that are much higher than ours, without being - i must say - too worried, but this will probably not last forever. for our part, this is the time to consolidate our economy and our competitiveness. it's time to work on the jobs of the future. it's time to speak the truth. we can't let this chance pass us by.
madam president, mr president of the commission, mr commissioner, many things have been said which i share. i just want to use three words. the first word is 'respect': it was not this parliament that made the european parliament the co-legislator on economic governance. it is what the governments wanted in the lisbon treaty. as rapporteurs, we do not feel it is normal to be informed of important discussions involving the governance package via google or the english-language press. the first thing i ask of you, mr president, and i ask of mr van rompuy's colleagues here, is to respect us and to ensure that this parliament can work. the second word is "democracy". we have not seen a democratic system since the eighteenth century deny the separation of powers as the european council is denying it. in the separation of powers, there are those who decide and those who control. the council, with your complicity, mr barroso, is arrogating to itself the right to decide and control, that is to say, basically to do nothing. the third word is 'efficiency': if we continue to dilute the content of the proposals, we will arrive at the lowest common denominator and we know what it is. this is the lisbon strategy. it's the ten years that got us nowhere. we'll do our work. this parliament demands respect, it will defend democracy and efficiency.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, i can only agree with what mrs goulard has just said about these necessary assumptions which make it necessary for parliament to be associated with the decision-making process, even though we fully understand the need for efficiency and speed. it is the only way for our fellow citizens, whose elected representatives we are, to understand what is happening and to explain it to them. i would like to make a very specific point. every day, we are tossed by the financial markets. these financial markets that represent everything and nothing, that are populated mostly by young people who have gone from game boy to computer without any special thought, and yet our countries are shaking. if we want to control markets, we cannot do so by abolishing them. i do not belong to a group which wants to abolish markets. but what are the markets looking for? they're looking to avoid risk, and the game in the markets is to pass the risk on to someone else. so no trader is ever satisfied as long as he is taking risks. i believe that if we are to have an impact on these financial markets, europe must be able to draw clear lines, not to change its orientation every day, not to come up with thousands of ideas which are then not put into practice. in order to be able to control this financial aspect, which is essential for the economic stability of our countries, we must be able - and it is up to you, mr president, to give this impetus - to set clear horizons, clear measures and to show a clear determination to ensure good economic coordination.
the president of the council. - madam president! ladies and gentlemen of the house of representatives, first of all, i would like to express my appreciation for your interest in the enlargement issue. despite the perceptible challenges facing both member states and candidate countries, i believe that the enlargement process must proceed in a continuous and consistent manner, based on performance. to achieve this, both parties must remain committed. knowing the work of the european parliament, it is clear that this is a forum where all participants are aware of the importance of our relations with turkey. these are long-standing links, which are becoming even closer as the country becomes a candidate country. at the same time, turkey is also an important regional actor, playing a key role in several important areas, including energy security and regional security and the promotion of dialogue between civilizations. the dramatic international events taking place in our immediate neighbourhood further highlight the importance of turkey in these areas. the accession negotiations with the country are progressing in line with the relevant conclusions of the european council and the council and the negotiating framework. despite the increasing complexity of the advanced negotiations, the hungarian presidency is committed to making progress on all chapters wherever possible. the work is ongoing and is now focusing on chapter 8, competition policy. i am confident that our turkish partners will continue their efforts and that we will soon see results. in its conclusions adopted last december, the council welcomed turkey's continued commitment to the negotiating process and its political reform programme. the constitutional reform package adopted by turkey in 2010 is another important step in the right direction, as it addresses a number of the accession partnership priorities in the areas of justice, fundamental rights and public administration. the key task now is to ensure that reforms are implemented in line with european standards and through the broadest possible consultation involving all political parties and civil society organisations. it is clear that the continuation of work on the political criteria remains of the utmost importance. significant efforts will be required in several areas, as highlighted in the council conclusions of 14 december 2010, the european parliament's draft resolution and the commission's 2010 progress report. please allow me to highlight some of these areas. turkey should further improve its respect for fundamental rights and freedoms, both in law and in practice, in particular in the areas of freedom of expression and freedom of religion. further efforts are also needed to fully comply with the copenhagen criteria, inter alia in the areas of property rights, trade union rights, the rights of persons belonging to minorities, the rights of women and children, the fight against discrimination and gender equality, and the fight against torture and inhuman treatment. the areas of concern in the area of freedom of expression include restrictions on press freedom, inadequate protection of journalists' rights and the frequent and widespread blocking of websites, as highlighted in your draft resolution. let me refer you to the developments of the last few days. on march 3, turkish police arrested journalists. we must closely monitor this case and continuously remind the turkish authorities of the importance of the continued enforcement of the freedoms. as regards religious freedom, turkey should ensure its exercise both in law and in practice. a comprehensive legal solution is needed to ensure religious pluralism in line with european standards. the presidency is also concerned about the high number of news reports on torture and inhuman treatment, including abuses outside official detention facilities. strict enforcement of the amended 2007 law on police tasks and powers should be monitored to prevent human rights violations. as the european parliament's draft resolution points out, the ratification of the optional protocol to the un convention against torture and the fight against impunity are essential steps in this regard. as regards turkish-kurdish relations and the question of the south-eastern territories, we hope that the implementation and continuation of democratic opening will soon bring the expected results and ultimately lead to the economic, social and cultural development of the region. let me also remind you that the council strongly condemns the terrorist acts committed on the territory of turkey. it should also be noted that the kurdistan workers' party remains on the eu list of terrorist organisations. turning to eu-turkey relations, i note with deep regret that despite repeated calls, turkey continues to refuse to fulfil its obligation to implement the additional protocol to the association agreement in full and without discrimination. this is a key issue, which is why the council is maintaining its 2006 measures, which, as we all know, are clearly having an impact on the pace of accession negotiations. the council will continue to closely monitor and review the results achieved. similarly, there is no progress in the normalisation of relations between cyprus and turkey. the council expects turkey to actively support the ongoing negotiations in the framework of the united nations to achieve a just, comprehensive and viable settlement of the cyprus problem, in accordance with the relevant un security council resolutions and with respect for the principles on which the union is founded. the commitment and contribution of turkey is key to such a comprehensive settlement. i would also like to stress that turkey must be clearly committed to good neighbourly relations and to the peaceful settlement of disputes. turkey is a key source and transit country for illegal immigration to the eu, and we therefore welcome the conclusion of the negotiations on a readmission agreement between the eu and turkey. the council looks forward to the conclusion of the agreement as soon as possible and its successful implementation. we know that this happened at the last igc and we expect turkey to sign the treaty. in the meantime, the council reiterates its commitment to the full and proper implementation of the existing bilateral readmission agreements. with regard to the eu-turkey customs union, i would like to point out that it is time for turkey to finally fulfil the large number of commitments that it has not addressed so far. this includes technical and administrative barriers to trade, registration requirements, import licences, state aid, enforcement of intellectual property rights and other discriminatory practices and provisions. these are all issues that need to be resolved urgently. turkey should also lift all restrictions affecting trade and transport between the member states of the union and turkey. i appreciate your patience and welcome any questions you may have.

time for eu-turkey relations, and the draft resolution underlines a number of issues of great importance for the commission. the commission remains committed to the accession process with turkey. the enlargement process encourages political and economic reform in the country. the eu-turkey relationship is strong. turkey needs the european union and the european union needs turkey – this balance has not changed. the european union is and will remain a key player for turkey. the relationship is based on deep economic integration: 40% of turkey’s foreign trade goes to the eu and 80% of foreign direct investments in turkey come from the eu. the european union efficiently contributes to turkey’s modernisation through technology transfers, turkey’s participation in eu education and research programmes and our pre-accession financial support. at the same time, accession negotiations have slowed down. moreover, the negotiating chapters that turkey can aim to open under the present circumstances require significant reforms and adjustments. against this background, i welcome all the more the progress made recently, in particular as regards the competition chapter. i am confident that we can soon open this chapter, provided turkey fulfils the last remaining conditions. obviously, the cyprus issue weighs on the negotiations. positive steps on the implementation of the additional protocol to the ankara agreement or in the settlement talks would have a positive impact on the accession negotiations. let me turn now to the reforms in turkey. i welcome last year’s constitutional reform and the subsequent legislative amendments as a step in the right direction. getting the laws right is important. however, only objective and impartial implementation of the new laws will ensure the success of the constitutional reforms. turkey should continue with the constitutional reform. the process should be as inclusive and transparent as possible with the active participation of different political parties, civil society, non-governmental organisations and the general public. the commission is following with concern the recent actions against journalists. independence and freedom of the press is of utmost importance for democracy. in its 2010 progress report the commission has already highlighted the high number of court cases against journalists and undue pressure on the media which undermine this fundamental right in practice. freedom of the press entails that dissent and opposing points of view need to be heard and – more importantly – tolerated. freedom of the press means guaranteeing a public space for free debate, including on the internet. the european parliament’s draft resolution rightly underlines these issues. as for the right to freedom of religion, we welcome the initiatives taken in favour of non-muslim religious communities in turkey. however, further and systematic efforts are needed to address the problems of non-muslims and the alevis. let me turn to the issue of migration. two weeks ago, the council endorsed the eu-turkey readmission agreement. this agreement is beneficial for the eu member states, as turkey is an important transit country for migration flows to the eu. the development on the readmission agreement also opens up for the first time new and concrete perspectives for further cooperation with turkey in the area of visa and migration policies, with a view to improving mobility and contacts amongst our citizens and businesses. turkey and the european union have a shared interest in working closely together in this area. there are many good reasons to increase the ability of turkish citizens, businessmen and students to travel to europe: to familiarise themselves further with european standards; to enhance eu-turkey trade to the benefit of both european union and turkish businesses, and to give a much-needed boost to our cooperation with turkey. madam president, i assure you that the european parliament will be duly involved both on the issue of the readmission agreement and the visa dialogue, in line with the treaty requirements. relations with turkey have also to be seen in a wider context. turkey’s active foreign policy is a strong potential asset for the european union, provided it is developed within the framework of turkey’s eu accession process. the european union stands ready to intensify its existing dialogue with turkey on foreign policy issues of mutual interest. speaking about turkey today, we cannot ignore the major developments in its wider region. the events in tunisia and egypt have highlighted turkey’s stability, prosperity, and democracy. citizens in these countries look at turkey, as they look at the european union, as examples to follow. they watch turkey advocating standards and values that they are now fighting for themselves and that are associated with europe. let us be clear: while an on behalf of the alde group. mr president, commissioner, just under a year ago, 300 airports in europe were closed in 23 out of 27 eu countries. this has caused considerable financial losses, and above all - as my colleagues have pointed out - more than ten million people, not all of whom were on a tourist trip, have had to postpone their trip and find other means of transport. it is the result of the chaos caused by a totally natural event which has put us in an important context with respect to nature, and which has caused an unprecedented paralysis in the european sky. of course, it is difficult to predict a volcanic eruption and even more so the formation of this ash cloud - of course more difficult than predicting a snow episode - but the crisis that was caused by this cloud has highlighted all the shortcomings and deficiencies of air traffic management in the union, the weakness and absence of a number of management tools. these three findings lead me to three proposals to make: the first, on the order of the imperative convenience, the second on the need for the community method to respond to this kind of challenge, and the third, obviously at the centre of our concerns, on the presence of passenger rights as a central element of our concerns. as regards the first element, the crisis has highlighted the absolute need to improve the comfort of european transport, since the cloud has shown the limits not only of air systems at european level, but also of rail, since many travellers have not been able to find an alternative. it is possible to imagine - and this has been demonstrated in studies carried out over the past year - that with more ease the scale of the crisis would not have been so great and the paralysis would have been a little less severe. as regards the second element, just as in the financial crisis and just as in the debates we have on the community method versus the intergovernmental method, here, in the field of transport, it is not the intergovernmental method, it is not a fragmented response by 27 member states that will be able to solve the difficulties we have experienced, and which may recur, but a genuine community method. to do this, we must strengthen eurocontrol's powers in a community system and, of course, as the honourable members have said, we must complete the single european sky as a matter of urgency. thirdly, passengers are at the heart and centre of our concerns. (the president interrupts the speaker) as i said in the introduction, we will have understood that what i have saved for the end is the essential thing.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the eruption of the icelandic volcano last april - and many of us have said this before - provided a painful illustration of the fragmentation and inefficiency of the european skies. and every one of us in this chamber has been directly affected. five million of our fellow citizens have been stranded without any real alternative transportation solution. one year after this exceptional event, new european measures are still awaited. a first crisis exercise - as you said, mr commissioner - linked to volcanic ash is planned for 13 and 14 april under the coordination of eurocontrol, the international civil aviation organisation and the international air transport association, but it is essential that the european aviation safety agency (easa) takes a real lead in coordinating safety measures at european level. it is certain that the information provided by the vac (visual approach chart) in london and toulouse needs to be refined using more modern technological means. however, as we saw last april, these data can be contradictory and can lead to individual member states taking decisions on the closure of their airspace less on the basis of information than on the basis of emotion. in this context, the role of easa is essential to provide a harmonised interpretation of these data, as well as to ensure the centralisation and the proper dissemination of information. in addition to vac information, easa should establish a mechanism to collect available data by closely involving member states, airlines and their pilots. this centralisation of information and coordination of all the actors involved will avoid the chaos and inconsistencies we witnessed last year. i therefore expect the commission, together with easa, to be able to come forward quickly with concrete proposals which will be fully integrated into the realisation of the single european sky.
