i would remind our colleague on the left, mr murphy, that karl marx was in favour of free trade with india. and i would also remind our liberal colleagues, and particularly mr rohde, that if he was in favour of free trade, it was because of the destructive effects of free trade because, he said, no matter how much the british bourgeoisie is driven by base interests, indian society must be destroyed to hasten the coming of the world revolution. i think that we should not be dogmatic in this area. systematic free trade is not necessarily beneficial. it can be a good thing when the conditions of competition are equal. this is more or less the case in many areas with japan, but i recognize japan's right, for example, to protect the rice market, to protect its rice farmers, to give its producers a price above world prices and not to want massive imports which would completely destroy its farming industry, in the same way that i recognize our economies' right to protect certain sectors of their activity. that is why i did not vote for the majority resolution. i would have preferred other resolutions which i felt were more appropriate. the conditions of competition must be balanced, but in sectors which are clearly defined.
in writing. i voted for the manders report on the new labelling rules for textiles. i welcome the fact that parliament, in this second reading vote, has reintroduced a number of amendments despite the council's opposition. it is important that consumers are able to make informed purchases and do not buy leather or fur inadvertently, as is the case in particular when fur is used as a lining for cheap clothing. the text also stresses the need for the traceability of clothing manufacture and a study will be commissioned from the commission on the health consequences of the use of products such as synthetic fibres or dyes.
in writing. this report endorses the pressure that the european union is exerting on the balkan countries to serve its interests. it even instructed parliament to take, together with the council, 'appropriate measures' if the governments of these states did not show sufficient willingness to liberalize their economies. the arrogant imperialism! i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr hökmark's draft report, which supports the release of the 800 mhz band for mobile services by january 2013 and sets very ambitious targets, such as releasing 1200 mhz for mobile data traffic by 2015. the rapporteur also stresses the need for efficient use of spectrum, greater flexibility to promote innovation and investment, and the need to strengthen the inventory of existing and future uses of spectrum.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will, in the short term, make it possible to meet the exponential demand for high-frequency mobile internet access, in particular by making available to electronic communications services the entire 800mhz band freed up by the switchover to digital television in our various states. in the medium to long term, our aim should be to increase the efficiency of spectrum use in a transversal way, taking into account its social, cultural and economic value. at the same time, we are encouraging innovative technologies (femtocells, cognitive technologies) to meet the demand for frequencies in a qualitative way. this will contribute to the union's objectives, including closing the digital divide, so that all europeans have access to broadband by 2015.
in writing. one of the main objectives of the strategy is to ensure internet access throughout europe by 2013 and broadband coverage of at least 30 mbps for all europeans by 2020. many relatively isolated rural or island areas rely on wireless mobile internet connection to access broadband. to ensure uninterrupted communication, dedicated radio frequencies are required. the allocation of frequencies is a matter of national competence, but the rules for the sharing of spectrum between operators and users are a matter for the european union. universal access to broadband is largely a function of this sharing of frequencies. i voted for the report on spectrum policy because it lays the foundations for universal coverage of the mobile internet. on 1 january 2013, the 800 mhz frequency will be the frequency of mobile internet, providing high quality access to wireless users and thus reducing the digital divide. the project goes even further, with the allocation of a new frequency band of 1.5 to 2.3 ghz for 2015.
in writing. there has been a lot of talk in recent weeks about the role of lobbyists in the european parliament. since four members were accused of accepting money from 'fake' lobbyists in exchange for tabling amendments, the institution has embarked on a process of clarifying and reforming the rules governing lobbyists in parliament. the relationship between elected representatives of the european parliament and representatives of the interests has long been surrounded by a sort of permanent suspicion. this led to the creation of a first register of lobbyists in 1996. today it is this register, in which lobbyists will have to register, that is being reformed. registration is 'voluntary' but de facto compulsory, as only those who have registered will be able to enter parliament. i also welcome the adoption of the so-called 'legislative footprint': the idea of publishing the names of people we have met when writing a report seems to me to be a perfectly normal guarantee of transparency. it is regrettable, however, that the council, unlike the european commission, has not joined the initiative.
in writing. in view of the undeniable role that lobby groups, whether they represent private or public interests, play in european affairs, greater transparency on the relationship with our institution is essential. i think that their inclusion in the transparency register should be compulsory. i particularly support the idea of a 'legislative footprint', which will allow a list of lobbyists encountered by members of parliament during the legislative process. it is essential to do everything possible to restore or strengthen citizens' confidence in the functioning of the european institutions, and this register is leading us precisely in that direction.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it is important to clarify matters, and this at a time when the role of lobbies still raises many questions and sometimes fantasies among european citizens. we regret, however, that the registration of organisations is not made compulsory, especially since the issuing of building access cards allows for compulsory registration 'in fact'. on the other hand, we have fought for the local, regional and municipal representative offices to the european institutions not to be affected by this measure, contrary to what was envisaged in the original text. we consider these structures to be the direct outgrowth of democratically elected entities. they represent the general interest and must therefore be distinguished from lobbyists who represent particular interests. nevertheless, this register is an important step forward, because in many areas the opacity of the role of lobbies can pose a real democratic problem.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the casini report on the establishment of a joint transparency register between the european parliament and the commission. the establishment of a public register in which lobbyists must register if they want access to these two institutions is a real democratic advance for the benefit of the citizens. the future obligation for rapporteurs to disclose the names of lobbies encountered is therefore a further step towards the full independence of the european parliament and will ensure a balanced representation of the interests of all european citizens.
in writing. it is commonly accepted that more than 15 000 lobbyists are active in brussels to try to influence the legislation adopted there, and this at all stages of the legislative process. although this activity has an extremely negative connotation in france, it is not totally illegitimate for commercial, social, trade union interest groups, etc., to assert their views and expertise, especially with less informed officials and elected officials. it is therefore logical that these lobbies and their representatives should be registered, and that their main sources of funding should also be listed, especially if they come from the european budget. this should be compulsory not only for these organisations but also for any group outside parliament, including those which are supposed to play a role under the treaties (trade unions, churches, philosophical associations, local authorities, etc.), including when they are made up, in whole or in part, of members of parliament, such as the efi, since they then act as interest groups and not as parliamentarians. the agreement we are voting on today does not go far enough in terms of transparency in this respect.
in writing. following recent events which have highlighted the possible deviations of lobbying, it has become all the more necessary to increase the transparency of the work of interest groups in the european institutions. merging the lists of lobbyists registered with the parliament and the european commission is a first step towards the comprehensive enumeration of all lobbies operating in brussels and thus towards greater access by citizens to democratic checks and balances in the decision-making process. i have fought, however, to ensure that the representative offices of local authorities in the european institutions are not affected by this measure. i consider these structures to be the direct outgrowth of democratically elected bodies (municipal, general, regional councils, etc.). they represent the general interest and must therefore be distinguished from lobbyists who represent particular interests. on the other hand, i hope that this register will one day be made compulsory and will include all lobbyists working for the european institutions: transparency is a key concept in the policy of the european union and it is essential to extend it to all the interest groups involved in its functioning.
in writing. more than 1700 organisations are accredited as interest groups in the european parliament, and 3900 in the commission. these organisations are so far listed in two separate registers for each institution. in 2008, parliament called for the pooling of these collections to make the census easier. an institutional agreement was reached between parliament and the european commission with the aim of establishing a common register. this agreement was awaiting ratification and was put to the vote of the european parliament. i voted in favour of this text because it will make the work of interest groups more transparent. the register is not yet compulsory under the act, but parliament will make it necessary for organisations wishing to have access to its premises. the text also proposes the introduction of a 'legislative footprint' for lobbying, indicating in the annex to the legislative acts the interest groups that have participated in its development. the common register should be available online in june.
in writing. no lobby group for commercial interests should be granted a permanent passport to the european institutions. their access to the european parliament must be strictly limited to the appointments given to them by the members and the political groups. the proposed 'transparency register' is nothing more than an administrative legitimization. it serves to maintain the status quo. lobbyists have a great day ahead of them. i am voting against and denouncing this hypocritical report. it would be better to oblige the above mentioned persons to declare their personal links with the media and their parliamentary and administrative links with the european parliament.
in writing. having noted, and i quote and practice the euphemism, a 'lack of values and ethics in the behaviour of certain market players and financial institutions', this parliament is embarking on a pathetic crusade to moralize the sector. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them. a pathetic chatter about social, cultural and "gender" diversity on boards (roma quotas perhaps?); the commission has already adopted proposals on the subject of unfair wages in the sector, which can be improved considerably. a few risk checks here and there... in short, you forget that companies are only playing by the rules of the game that you set. but these rules, which you fundamentally refuse to call into question, are the free movement of capital worldwide, the financialization of the economy, the focus on the short term, securitisation, complex financial products based on no concrete creation of wealth, the creation of large multinational groups that are more powerful than states and uncontrollable. until you touch the foundations of this system, you'll change nothing.
in writing. i voted against the resolution proposed by the european right because it advocates an ultra-liberal view of the eu's trade relations with india. the right has consistently opposed the amendments which i tabled on behalf of the s&d group to exclude any liberalization of public services, to strongly condemn child labour, to call for legally binding clauses on corporate social responsibility, or to demand respect for the principle of equal pay for equal work for indians who will come to work in europe tomorrow. the compromise was impossible, the differences of opinion were obvious and irreconcilable. only the resolution tabled by my group, together with those of the greens and the gue/ngl, proposed a progressive vision of eu-india trade relations. unfortunately, and unsurprisingly, it has not been able to resist the right-wing majority in this parliament.
in writing. i voted against this report. we want an eu-india free trade agreement to help promote sustainable development, and to be accompanied by clear clauses on compliance with ilo standards, environmental standards and corporate social responsibility obligations. it is particularly regrettable that the right has rejected such demands. we also regret that the right wing of parliament has rejected the amendment to guarantee equal treatment for european and indian workers. it is not only harmful to indian workers, but it is also very dangerous for european workers. we cannot accept the opening up of services and social dumping aimed at levelling european wages downwards. the european union cannot forget its founding principles. the lisbon treaty states that trade policy must contribute to sustainable development, poverty eradication and the protection of human rights.
in writing. as you have so often said, the common foreign policy must respect the overall objectives of the european union, as defined in particular in article 3 of the treaty, which includes the eradication of poverty. but for years you have been signing free trade agreements with all the countries of the world, especially those which systematically practice social, monetary or environmental dumping, and you are only creating poverty for all the victims of the relocations or closures of businesses directly linked to this unfair competition. with this agreement with india, you are going even further: exit the polish plumber, welcome the indian computer scientist or accountant! you intend to open up the european market for many services to mode 4 of the general agreement on trade in services (gats), a barbaric term for the global version of the bolkestein directive. as the french nobel prize winner in economics, maurice allais, pointed out, there is mutually beneficial free trade only between countries of comparable levels of development, and again, i would add, in targeted areas that preserve each country's strategic sectors. otherwise, the game is never win-win. it has, in fact, for a long time had only one loser: europe.
in writing. the text has the merit of taking into account the possible negative consequences of gmos. but it is pushing for the liberalisation of trade in services between the european union and india. it leaves the states only the right to 'regulate' public services which such liberalisation condemns. it also calls for the liberalisation of legal and accounting services, the opening up of the banking and insurance markets and the facilitation of investment opportunities. the oligarchy is served in europe as in india. i am voting against this text.
in writing. i voted against the european parliament resolution on the state of play of the negotiations on the eu-india free trade agreement. this report is in line with the policies of increased liberalization, particularly in the public services sector, and standards which have a negative effect not only on the supply of medicines but also on the development of research. it is still the ultraliberalism that the eu seeks to impose on all its partners. it is the eu's largest agreement in this area, and is more about protecting the interests of large multinationals than about engaging a balanced partnership of all stakeholders and contributing to the economic and social development of this great country. no, this agreement is not a 'win-win' initiative as claimed in this resolution.
in writing. in the run-up to the eu-japan summit at the end of the month, parliament adopted this resolution expressing its views on trade relations between the two partners. against a european right wing which has spoken very strongly in favour of opening negotiations with a view to reaching a free trade agreement, i have advocated a more cautious approach. japan is a trading power which calls for caution when it comes to trade liberalization. that is why my group opposed the text put forward by the european right, stressing that precise impact studies should be launched, assessing the consequences of a strengthening of trade relations on all the sectors concerned (in particular the automobile sector) and on employment in europe, before any negotiations are launched. at the same time, we stressed the problem of non-tariff barriers which block european companies' access to japanese public contracts. it is unacceptable that the european union, the most open region in the world in terms of foreign investment, should not be able to intervene on equal terms with its industrialized partners.
in writing. just a few weeks after the natural and nuclear disaster in japan, the european right feels inspired to threaten the japanese government. the aim is to oblige japan to remove the obstacles to european companies' access to its public procurement. not a word about the nuclear disaster. no cooperation proposal to get out of this situation. barely a solidarity line after the single nuclear disaster in japan. shame on the european right!
in writing. to achieve a consistent approach in the european union by reconciling the forestry policies of southern and northern europe is a challenge that is far from obvious. but in adopting this report we have emphasized the need for a stronger commitment to environmental protection in forestry policy. we also emphasise the challenge that climate change poses to forests. i am not sure that we need a legislative initiative to prohibit building on land ravaged by fires, but i am in favour of thinking about firm and lasting solutions to the terrible phenomenon of criminal forest fires aimed at freeing up building land.
in writing. the arsenis report demonstrates the importance which the european parliament attaches to forestry policy. the content of the report emphasizes the need for sufficient and ambitious financial resources for the future for the forest and the wood sector. i therefore support the adoption of this text, and i renew my support for the adoption of a specific financial instrument for the protection of the forests of the union.
in writing. the european parliament has sent a strong political message to stress the need for sustainable forest management. it is necessary and urgent to put into practice the recommendations on disaster prevention. the commission has also proposed that the european union should be able to provide a financial contribution to the european union for the period from 1 january 2000 to 31 december 2003. protecting forests against climate change also helps to preserve the forestry industry and its competitiveness. with a turnover of over eur 300 billion, the european wood sector provides over two million jobs and is a major source of growth. finally, it is essential that the debate on the future of the cap after 2013 takes into account the role of forests. rural producers and public bodies must be eligible for forestry measures under the second pillar of the cap: the eu must support the planting of forests under national rural development programmes.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the commission's green paper entitled 'forest protection and forest information in the european union; preparing forests for climate change". forests must be seen as a fundamental element in the fight against climate change. it is crucial that the european union reinforces its strategy to combat forest-damaging phenomena such as fires and air pollution. against these threats, the ability of forests to recover to normal development in the face of the impacts of climate change depends on biodiversity, not only of the trees, but also of all other organisms living there, especially wild animals. for example, wildlife that naturally colonizes the prime habitat of forests deserve special attention from landowners as they contribute to the maintenance of biodiversity.
in writing. the preservation of forests is a fundamental issue for the benefit of all mankind. it is a pity that it is once again used as a pretext for the development of the carbon market. european green capitalism is a dead end. capitalism and ecology are incompatible.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on the green paper on forests presented by the commission. forests are part of our landscape, our heritage, and are essential to our well-being. as threats become more serious, better protection of these exceptional natural resources is essential. the consequences of climate change on forests are well known, but the inertia to address them seriously jeopardises their preservation. but they are fragile ecosystems, a priceless biodiversity and a strategic economic channel that we have to preserve. i therefore welcome the strong political message sent by our parliament in this international year of the forest. the measures we need to take to adapt to climate change cannot be delayed. the european tactical forest fire reserve should also be strengthened, given that prevention is as important as response. if we are to preserve the forest as we know and love it, we must be at the forefront of the fight to ensure sustainable management of forest areas and protect them from the threats that threaten them.
in writing. i did not vote in favour of paragraph 85 of the albertini report, which welcomes the resumption of negotiations on an association agreement with mercosur. such an agreement, which aims to liberalize trade, must be considered with the greatest caution in order not to weaken community agriculture even further. mercosur's production is not subject to environmental and social standards comparable to those of european agriculture. there is a strong risk of unfair competition in these conditions. it's important to protect yourself.
in writing. the real fundamental choice of the cfsp in 2009 was that of the high representative. i have to admit, he's not the best. it is clear that mrs ashton is more adept at the corporate-lady-like, moralizing press releases than she is at the diplomatic issues you want her to face on behalf of the 27. thanks to it, the european union has been absent, or present against the tide, in all the important events. but as is usual in times of crisis, a handful of states took the initiative, for better or for worse, organized themselves and acted. the rest either followed or grumbled, since he was expected to have an opinion. the union's foreign policy is essentially a matter of distributing funds and trading, which is often in contradiction with the political principles it sets out. and it makes sense: diplomacy is the royal function of states. it is the product of history, of economic or geopolitical interests, and of individual means. the interests of the union are neither a synthesis nor a sum of those of its members. they are peculiar to the country and often conflict with national interests. it's totally illegitimate for them to take precedence over them.
in writing. the eu is calling for the broad guidelines of the common european defence policy (cfsp) to be defined in the light of the increasing global instability. i welcome the fact that this report stresses the need to involve parliament. as the representatives of the peoples of europe, we must play a role in the development of a european defence policy. one of the fundamental objectives of the european union is to defend the values of peace, human rights and democracy. the promotion of our principles must be based on an ambitious strategy of external action and diplomacy. the lisbon treaty has given the union a voice with the high representative/vice-president. our cfsp cannot allow for division. this vote is therefore a call for better coordination between all the institutional actors: the european external action service, the european commission, the member states and, of course, the european parliament. in a changing world, our union must be more than economic. we have a historic responsibility to make it a political union. the cfsp must be a vehicle for achieving this. that is the message that our parliament has wanted to send, and the position that i support.

mr president, on 9 may 2010 the eu/ecb/imf troika triumphantly announced that they had saved greece from total bankruptcy with a €110 billion loan. a year later, greece plunged into recession. public debt is soaring to 150% of gdp and two-year interest rates are reaching over 25% per year. if greece is now breathless, it is because the method used to save it is not the right one. while the greek economy would now need a weak currency to emerge from the depression, the troika will impose a new and even more drastic budgetary austerity plan. and just as it didn't work yesterday, it won't work tomorrow. the punitive interest rates which affect greece today prohibit its private economy from any investment, whether in the productive apparatus or in real estate. greece is becoming a third world country, destroying all hope of repayment. the draft of a new €60 billion rescue plan envisaged last friday shows that the €110 billion loan already granted a year ago must be considered a gift. how long will european taxpayers fill the danaid barrel? to continue in this way is suicidal and will lead to the break-up of europe. there are two possible solutions: either the restructuring of the greek debt, with the restructuring of all the public debt of the states in difficulty and, in the end, the bankruptcy of our banking system, or a concerted, rational and pragmatic exit from the euro zone allowing greece to catch its breath. europe is at a crossroads. is saving the euro worth the sacrifice of the people?

a powerful motor not only for jobs, growth and export earnings, but also for social inclusion and cultural and linguistic diversity, as well as intercultural dialogue within the european union and beyond. as you rightly say in the report, these industries have a vital contribution to make to the europe 2020 strategy and must be given a more prominent place in the eu for the years to come. we also share the view that their potential is not fully developed. if we want these industries to develop fully, we have to make progress on various fronts: skills adaptation and capacity building, prompted reactions from 350 public authorities, the general public, civil society bodies and companies active in the field of culture across europe. i am pleased to see that our green paper has sparked, in europe and within the european institutions, a very rich debate on the right environment to put in place to meet the specific needs of creating entrepreneurship in order to seize the new opportunities offered by globalisation, digitisation and cultural diversity. i am firmly convinced that our joint efforts will help to create a better environment in which these vital industries can play an important role in the discussions on eu funding mechanisms post-2013 and implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. finally, i am very happy to see parliament’s enthusiasm – and in particular that of my good friend doris pack – for the european capitals of culture and sarajevo’s interest in holding the title. the commission, of course, shares your view of the historic and cultural importance of sarajevo. the city symbolises some of the darkest episodes in recent european history but also carries our hopes for a better future. in the face of repeated conflicts, sarajevo has retained its multicultural spirit. let me say a few words about the rules governing the european capitals of culture. in 2006, parliament and the council adopted the decision on which the initiative is based. this legal text lays down all the rules concerning the selection of the cities, and you know better than i do that a decision of this nature can be changed only through a new initiative following the ordinary legislative procedure. the decision states that the initiative is open exclusively to the 27 member states of the european union. as an integral part of the decision, a chronological list indicates, for every year until 2019, the two member states which are entitled to hold the title. two cities have already been selected for 2014, and the council is about to confirm the two cities for 2015. the decision lays down the procedure for awarding the european capital of culture title, and the rules leave no scope for the council to designate a city outside these procedures. the commission is fully and solely responsible for implementing the decisions adopted by parliament and council. a derogation from the decision on the european capitals of culture in relation to a matter as fundamental as its geographical scope would simply break the rules that we have been asked to follow. i believe it would be particularly difficult to justify an exception so soon after we have all agreed the rules of the initiative. parliament and the council adopted the current decision less than five years ago. that was the moment, surely, to make the case for the participation of non-member states or to make provisions for exceptional cases. however, at that point it was decided that the participation of non-member states would not continue beyond 2010. looking to the future of the european capitals of culture, the commission is currently working on renewal of the initiative beyond 2019. we launched a public consultation and are conducting an evaluation of the current scheme. we will then prepare a proposal, which we expect to adopt at the beginning of 2012. as part of our preparatory work, the commission is exploring the idea of candidate countries joining the initiative after 2019. i would also inform you that a number of cities in other third countries have already shown an interest. allow me to finish by underlining once again how much i appreciate sarajevo’s place in european history and its cultural significance. while the capitals of culture action is not available, the eu can offer other types of support for sarajevo, in 2014 and beyond, through our cultural programme.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, since the digitisation of cultural and artistic goods, i believe the question is: is europe destined to become a consumer country for the united states, and soon for the emerging countries, or will it finally wake up and implement the means to develop its information, cultural and economic potential? i am of course convinced of the richness and diversity of european culture, but i am putting myself today in a competitive perspective to denounce nonsense and absurdity. nonsense is the free dream of some, the access to everything for nothing. if we were to go down this road, there would be no more investment in this sector. the creators and inventors would not be able to receive a fair wage and would eventually disappear. so the economic models that we're going to implement for the online circulation of our cultural heritage exclude free. the absurdity is the taxation of dematerialized cultural property in two aspects. firstly, there is a distortion of vat according to the country of establishment. for example, the us platforms have been under a moratorium since 1998, which has allowed them to grow tremendously. on the other hand, there is a discrimination in the vat rate, which penalizes digital goods compared to physical goods. i think we need to provide legislative answers to both of these questions.

in writing. i supported this report which reaffirms our ambitions for young people in europe. the europe 2020 strategy puts education at the heart of its objectives and sets targets for 2020: reducing early school leaving from 15% to 10% and increasing the percentage of people with a higher education qualification from 31% to 40%. i would like to stress one point, however: the obstacles to the mobility of young people. at present, it is estimated that only 4% of european students receive an erasmus grant at any point in their studies. this is still too little when we know the value of a cv of one year of mobility abroad in terms of learning - especially language learning - openness and competence. three problems can explain this figure: the ignorance of many students about the existence of mobility opportunities, the cost that a year of erasmus can represent for a student's budget, and the complexity of the recognition of learning. on all these issues, europe and the member states must commit themselves so that the erasmus programme, which is one of the eu's greatest successes, becomes a success for all.
in writing. while the youth unemployment figures in europe are extremely worrying (in january 2011, the unemployment rate for those under 25 was 20.6% in the eu), the report on the flagship initiative of the 2020 strategy 'youth on the move' calls on member states to increase their investment in education, training, mobility and youth. youth policies, whether in terms of education, initial, continuing or vocational training, must be seen as an investment, not as a cost! the development of human capital is essential for the future of our european societies. strengthening synergies between the various actors, developing the autonomy of young people, combating early school leavers, giving new value to vocational training and apprenticeship, or adopting a binding european quality framework for traineeships - these are all good ideas that now need to be passed on at national level. the success of the 2020 strategy will depend on the ownership and political will of the states responsible for implementing it, since these policies remain largely within the remit of national competences.
in writing. youth mobility programmes such as erasmus, erasmus mundus and comenius are attracting more and more applicants. however, practical obstacles to mobility still exist, including for obtaining visas and medical documents in different languages, for transferring scholarships abroad, and for the recognition of qualifications acquired in another member state. in 2004, when the erasmus mundus exchange programme was launched, i had obtained, with a large majority in parliament, that the european commission take the necessary measures to ensure quality mobility. a 'european quality charter for mobility' has even been created. but seven years later, the same obstacles are still present. the european parliament has therefore stressed the need for increased investment in education and training. opening up european mobility programmes to all young people, regardless of sector or social level, is essential to allowing them better access to the labour market. it is time for member states to make a real commitment to guaranteeing quality education for all young europeans.
in writing. because young people are the future of europe and it would be irresponsible not to make them a priority, even though they are facing an unemployment rate of almost 20%, i strongly supported the zver report on improving education and training systems in europe. in the face of the ever-increasing demands of employers, integration into the labour market is often a real test for many students. this is why the proposals in the report youth on the move increased investment in higher education, development of international mobility programmes, recognition of informal skills, combating school drop-out, support for the professional integration of young people were very favourably received by the european parliament.
in writing. common sense says that "travel is the education of youth"... it is in this context that i support the idea, as put forward in the zver report, that funding for education and youth mobility is an investment in europe's future, not an additional burden on budgets, despite the current difficult economic situation. moreover, a person's social background or financial situation should not be a barrier to access to opportunities to travel abroad. the disability must not be a barrier, and therefore additional support must be provided for disabled young people. finally, legally binding rights must be put in place to prevent precarious employment and the exploitation of which young trainees may be victims.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by milan zver, 'youth on the move - a framework to improve education and training systems in europe'. through this report, i believe it is important to support the various programmes set up at european level to enable young people to move, which is beneficial both in terms of acquiring new knowledge and skills and in terms of developing genuine european citizenship. at european level, it is important that we continue and strengthen, beyond 2013, the appropriations allocated to european mobility programmes (erasmus, leonardo da vinci, among others) so that they benefit more young people, students, but also apprentices, young professionals, young farmers. i also felt that there was a need to move towards a better recognition of qualifications acquired through any form of learning, whether non-formal or informal, given the skills that this enables. finally, i would like to stress that one of the keys to combating youth unemployment is to continually adapt education and vocational training systems to the ever-changing needs of the labour market.
in writing. the economic crisis is hitting europe's young people hard: while one in five young people is unemployed, 40% of young workers have part-time contracts. in this context, i support the report by my colleague, mr milan zver, which proposes a series of recommendations to improve the systems of education and training for young people. while action is needed to encourage the widest possible participation in higher education and to combat dropout rates - only 31% of europeans have a university degree, compared with 40% in the united states and 50% in japan! - graduates' employability must also be guaranteed. the report makes several proposals in this regard: improving the dialogue between enterprises and universities, bringing university programmes and structures closer to the specific needs of the labour market, introducing high-quality, fairly remunerated traineeships in study programmes which respect the social rights of young people.

in writing. this resolution was adopted following the commission's proposal to open negotiations on the renewal of the protocol to the fisheries agreement between the european union and mauritania. unfortunately, voting on a resolution is the only way parliament can make its voice heard in the fisheries partnership agreements (fpas). at present, parliament has the power to intervene only after the negotiations have been concluded, leaving it with little choice but to approve these agreements or to refuse to ratify them, leaving it with very little room for manoeuvre. the treaties provide that parliament is to be 'immediately and fully informed at all stages of the procedure'. it is therefore essential and legitimate that we ask to be associated with the commission and the european council in these negotiations. this is not a new problem and the members of the fisheries committee regularly ask the european commission about it. it is regrettable that we cannot give a binding opinion on our priorities in relation to the allocation of european funds to the countries concerned, even though parliament has the power to exercise financial control.

in writing. i welcome the adoption today of the joint resolution of the european parliament on equal access to public procurement in the european union and in third countries and on the revision of the legal framework for public procurement, including concessions, which i was a co-signer of. the proper functioning of public procurement is essential to stimulate the single market. it is therefore necessary to clarify and improve the legislative framework governing their allocation, given their role as a catalyst for the recovery of the union economy. the european union must act with realism and pragmatism, and above all without any naivete, when it comes to access to public procurement contracts in the european union for companies from third countries. it is not a question of opposing the opening up of our markets, but rather, and quite legitimately, of advocating reciprocal access in this area, not by closing our public markets but by ensuring that our partners outside the european union open theirs in an equivalent way and, if necessary, develop appropriate mechanisms to achieve this objective of reciprocity and balance.
in writing. the questioning of public-public partnerships, the downward revision of the requirements of public authorities (guarantees of the general interest, need i remind you?), the orientation of the choices of these same public authorities to promote competition... these are just a few examples of the tremendous 'advances' promised in the european commission's green paper on public procurement. the text does not merely endorse such nonsense but makes the fight against protectionist measures the central point of its message. i'm against all these policies. i vote against it.
in writing. public procurement plays a crucial role in stimulating the single market, developing innovation, enhancing growth, and supporting employment and competitiveness in the eu. but to do that, they have to work well. for this reason, as the text of this resolution, which i support, recalls, it is important that the question of simplifying and clarifying the rules for the award of public contracts be answered quickly. it also seems to me essential that access to public procurement be improved as quickly as possible for smes - which represent 99% of all european enterprises and more than 100 million jobs! in addition, in order to support their activities, i call on the european commission to implement the principle of reciprocity and to consider new ways of improving access for european companies to public contracts outside the union, so as to guarantee a level playing field for european and foreign companies competing for the award of public contracts.
in writing. this vote is important because the commission must take the necessary measures to prevent unfair competition and non-reciprocity in access to public contracts vis-à-vis third countries. it is not a question of putting up protectionist barriers, but the union can no longer be the only one to respect the rules of the game. we can no longer ignore the social and economic dumping of companies from emerging countries who are winning markets in eu countries, in defiance of social rights and state aid legislation, when the markets of these countries are inaccessible to european companies! but we must not forget that the major industrialized countries, although signatories to international agreements, do not follow the rules either! after years of inaction, the commission seems determined to act, and it is necessary: the survival of our businesses and our jobs depends on it. finally, i welcome the adoption of the amendments by the socialist group concerning compliance with the labour, social and environmental standards in force in the member states in the context of public procurement. it is now up to the commission to take full advantage of this call.
in writing. the commission must adopt emergency measures to remedy the difficult economic situation facing many european fishermen as a result of the increase in oil prices. this includes increasing the de minimis ceiling for public aid from eur 30 000 to eur 60 000 per three-year period and per beneficiary company. beyond compensation, a longer-term strategy is needed to enable fishermen, but also professionals in other sectors, such as farmers or road hauliers, to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels. the commission must therefore encourage, at both european and national level, investment in new technologies to increase the energy efficiency of maritime, land and air transport.
in writing. the adoption of a parliament resolution on the crisis in the european fisheries sector due to the increase in oil prices is an opportunity for me to stress the urgency of helping fishermen. in a context where recruitment is proving increasingly difficult and the practices to be adopted are becoming more restrictive, the increase in fuel prices is making conditions even more difficult in this crisis-ridden sector. the sharp increase in oil prices has weighed heavily on the operating costs of fishing vessels, which has reduced their income between 2008 and 2010. as the elected representative of a port city, it is my duty to demand that the commission authorise the increase in the ceilings for de minimis aid. this would reduce the pressure on fishermen to live with the income from their activity without hindering the renewal of stocks. the future reform of the cfp will have to seek the support of fishermen: showing them already that the european union is aware of their needs would be a good start.
in writing. i wanted to support this resolution which calls on the commission to take strong measures to support the fisheries sector. the rise in oil prices is causing a real crisis in this sector. the crisis, which started as a cyclical one, has become structural and threatens the economic viability of this activity. operating costs have skyrocketed, and are weighing heavily on the incomes of the fishermen, to the extent that the entire production chain and all coastal regions are now affected. i therefore welcome the call from our assembly for more flexibility in the de minimis aid system. despite a difficult budgetary environment, fishermen would not understand if the union did not act to address their concerns. the resolution also calls for special attention to be paid to small-scale coastal fishing and the regions concerned. i think this is essential, because if the whole sector is concerned, the increase in the energy bill is more fragile for small-scale fishing than for industrial fishing. i believe that in exceptional circumstances, exceptional measures are required. i shall therefore be attentive to the proposals that the commission will make to reassure and support our fishermen.
in writing. smes are essential to the dynamism of the european economy. these enterprises, which employ fewer than 250 people and have a turnover of less than €50 million, number 23 million in the eu, represent 99% of european enterprises, and employ almost 70% of the private sector workforce. in a context of difficult recovery and increasing international economic competition, the establishment of a european strategy is not too much. the small business act aims to increase entrepreneurship in europe and help businesses to grow. it is therefore imperative to reduce red tape and to set up a modern administration adapted to the needs of smes. the commission must therefore establish a unified system for business creation. it would also be useful to introduce an 'sme test' to assess the impact of all future legislation on smes and to verify that it will not hamper the growth potential of these enterprises.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the european parliament resolution on the revision of the small business act, which adapts european support measures for smes to the new context arising from the 2008 economic crisis and brings them into line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. smes have been the first to be hit by the financial and banking crisis of recent years, which has reduced their access to finance and markets. the new version of the small business act should therefore provide greater support for innovation by smes by diversifying funding instruments and minimising the administrative burdens faced by smes.
in writing. the european parliament today supported the 23 million small and medium-sized enterprises in the european union, which represent over 100 million jobs and make a vital contribution to economic growth, social cohesion and job creation. the aim was to assess progress made and to identify new actions to address the challenges of the economic crisis. the role of smes has improved markedly, but there is still work to be done. smes continue to face considerable problems in expanding their activities or even in surviving. it is therefore necessary to continue the process of reducing bureaucracy through increased control and smart regulation. the status of a european private company must therefore be decided on swiftly; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of intellectual property rights. at the same time, we must ensure that the sme test is properly applied in all new legislative proposals, particularly at national level. finally, as smes play a key role in european innovation, it is necessary to continue to simplify the financing of research and development in order to strengthen their innovation capacity throughout the innovation cycle.
in writing. smes account for 99% of enterprises in the european union. i therefore voted in favour of the revision of the small business act, a resolution which recognises the vital role of smes in the european economy. i support a policy framework that goes even further in helping smes in times of economic crisis, and in many areas. i welcome smart regulation, which reduces the administrative burden on these first-class economic players and facilitates their access to finance and new markets, so that they can invest and develop. finally, it is important to remember that research, innovation and training must be supported if our smes are to benefit fully from the single market.
in writing. another text that aims to lower the level of public authorities' requirements in favour of entrepreneurs. the european small business act and its revision are not concerned with the general interest or the employees of smes. the only merit of this resolution, which is common to all the groups except mine, is that it regrets this state of affairs and boasts of energy efficiency, which it undermines by promoting exports at all costs. hypocritical and malicious. i abstain to encourage intent and sanction hypocrisy.
in writing. ninety-nine per cent of european enterprises are smes. two thirds of private sector jobs are provided by the sme sector. more than half of european value added is generated by smes. there will be no real economic recovery, no long-term economic growth, without a thorough action by the public authorities, local, national and european, in favour of small and mediumsized enterprises. with the adoption of the small business act in 2008, the european commission took a first decisive step towards small and medium-sized enterprises by introducing the 'think small first' principle in all areas of legislation. despite the many proposals that have been completed in three years - i am thinking in particular of the directive on late payment - much progress remains to be made in facilitating the activities of small and mediumsized enterprises, not only in view of the administrative burdens they face but also in view of the difficulties they encounter in accessing finance. the european commission must continue on the path it set out with the sba in 2008. that is the call made by this resolution, which i support.
in writing. i voted against the resolution on the revision of the sme pact, presented by the european commission in february 2011. this revision is in line with the current framework of the pact, including the reduction of administrative and bureaucratic burdens and burdens. the commission's proposal to harmonize tax systems must not reduce the tax burden on small businesses once again, while workers are being hit by austerity plans. while the revision aims to improve access to finance for smes, it ignores social and environmental issues, not even referring to the european commission's project for a social entrepreneurship initiative announced for the end of this year. the revision of the sba does open a small gap in favour of the social economy, but its weakness in relation to the issues surrounding these other forms of enterprise. like the sma, the revision of the sba does not draw the consequences of the monti report to restore citizens' confidence in the european union. it is therefore still part of the same ultra-liberal logic of european construction, centred first and foremost on the market and its needs, which we have condemned for years.
in writing. european smes are the lungs of our economic activity. their development, modernisation and competitiveness must be at the heart of our economic strategy. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution on the revision of the small business act, which aims to unlock the growth potential of smes. there is still a lot to be done to simplify the regulatory environment and the administrative procedures which are too burdensome for the activity and dynamism of our companies. i welcome the approaches advocated in this report, such as the creation of a european private company statute. this would help our smes to take full advantage of the single market, allowing them to carry out their cross-border activities without having to fulfil obligations that are often onerous and discouraging. i therefore call on the council to take a swift decision on this initiative. finally, we must support innovative smes by facilitating their access to diversified financing. this is achieved by significantly simplifying the use of european funds, which still lack flexibility. these funds exist and i believe they must be mobilised to support more effectively the development of the real economy, innovation and employment.
in writing. 'an innovation union' remains the most important community initiative for the development of an integrated european research and innovation strategy. increasing the pace of research and innovation is crucial to building a fair and competitive economic model, to securing the jobs of the future, to moving towards sustainable resource management, to addressing energy challenges or to boosting a knowledge-based society. innovation is therefore one of the major challenges facing the european union in terms of employment, the environment and development, and will have a real impact on citizens. as both drivers and beneficiaries of innovation, european citizens must therefore be able to participate fully in this 'innovation union' in order to ensure its success, as we have stressed in this report. finally, we wanted to emphasize the need for an innovation policy and the added value of a coordinated approach at european level. to tackle the major shared societal and economic challenges of european society, we need ambitious initiatives, so we now await the legislative phase of the commissioner for research and innovation's action.
in writing. in the face of a world economy in crisis, the european parliament stressed the importance of making europe more innovative and more efficient, adapting to the new challenges of the 21st century. it is essential to encourage the maximum involvement of all the actors involved: smes, industry, universities, governments... everyone has a role to play. for example, we need to modernise our education systems and address the skills shortage in science and engineering. we will only get out of the crisis if we support innovation. the european union must allow the creation of new financing instruments which encourage research expenditure and private investment. in addition, public-private collaboration through the implementation of partnerships is an important way of encouraging a more innovative economy. i believe that the adoption of the single european patent is essential to facilitate the transition to trade outside the community. patents are currently far too expensive: it is essential to reduce the costs of their creation. finally, in the face of the phenomenon of 'brain drain', it is important to promote the retention of researchers in europe! without them, funding and other mechanisms are of no use.
in writing. european innovation scores have so far remained very low. innovation should help to address key societal challenges such as population ageing, the need for sustainable resource management or economic recovery. that is why i voted in favour of this own-initiative report, which places particular emphasis on the concept of social innovation and stresses the active role that regions and local authorities can play in innovation. finally, we must promote a balanced system of intellectual property rights protection which respects the rights of inventors while offering our citizens the widest possible access to knowledge. these are the challenges that innovation can help to meet in the future.
in writing. the eu's innovation lag has not been bridged despite the lisbon strategy. in a context of budgetary constraints, which exclude the use of public funds, and increased global competition, europe must react to get back on the innovation track. it seems to me essential to focus on structural reforms that will remove the obstacles that are holding back the considerable potential for innovation in europe. i therefore supported this report, which points in particular to the high costs of filing patents in each member state and calls for a rapid agreement on the single european patent. i am also pleased to see the proposals of my political family taken up, in particular the creation of a european innovation fund, which will simplify access to european loans for our smes. unlocking europe's innovation capacity calls for a minimum r&d spending threshold in each member state, which would ensure a fair sharing of the effort and prevent the development of a two-speed europe that would disrupt eu cohesion and governance. this is essential if europe is to maintain its position at the top of the world economy.
in writing. while most domestic workers are precarious workers, often discriminated against and sometimes exploited, the employment committee decided to adopt a resolution at the same time as asking the european commission about its action towards this category of workers. in june, the international labour organization (ilo), meeting for its annual conference, is expected to adopt a convention on domestic workers calling for domestic workers to be treated equally with other workers and for all conditions to be met for decent work. we support the ilo's stated ambition in our resolution. this is only the first step, and we will then have to ensure that the member states ratify this convention once it has been adopted.
in writing. the international labour organisation (ilo) is currently working on a convention on domestic workers. the adoption of such an ilo domestic workers convention will be an essential element in ensuring respect for the human, social and employment rights of domestic workers. domestic work accounts for between 5% and 9% of total employment. this work is often precarious, undervalued and unreported.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, in order to make it possible to transform what is too often an operating report into a report on law, in a field which represents between 5 and 9% of total employment in the european union. we need to ensure that all those who work with our seniors have the freedom to associate, have time off, and not be subject to harassment and arbitrariness. this is why we wanted to send a strong message of support to the ilo and the trade unions ahead of the negotiations which will open in june at the 100th international labour conference for the adoption of these new instruments. we regret, however, that the right accepts the concern for undocumented domestic workers while refusing to recognize that it is far too often undocumented workers who are the first victims of precarious situations and abuse.
in writing. in europe, nearly two out of three immigrant women have low-skilled jobs, often in personal care or domestic work. these women contribute to our economy and yet suffer from very degraded working conditions and violations of their most basic rights. the international labour conference in june this year will be the occasion for the members of the international labour organisation to adopt a 'convention on decent work for domestic workers'. this instrument is a step forward for the rights of workers worldwide, since it extends the standards of labour law to a category which is currently excluded, that of domestic workers. the ball is now in the court of the member states, which must commit themselves to ratifying the convention. at european level, we must also stop looking at public immigration and labour policies separately and systematically. it is not right that domestic workers are forced into informal work, with no respect for their rights, because of too strict and inadequate immigration regulations.
in writing. i fully support the adoption, ratification and implementation of an ilo convention on domestic work. domestic workers are often working in precarious conditions, are often in irregular administrative situations which increase their vulnerability, and are often subject to discrimination, inequality and unfair or abusive treatment. yet their services are indispensable to our society, from early childhood to care for the elderly. we must have a legal framework that strengthens the rights of these workers and promotes decent working conditions.
in writing. the precarious position of workers is at the heart of the logic of domination of the oligarchy, in europe as elsewhere. among the various forms of organized precariousness, there is one that is more difficult to eradicate than the others, namely that of domestic workers. this report supports the drafting of an ilo convention to protect the rights of these workers, especially those who work in the shadows. it also denounces the proliferation of atypical contracts, a sign of the growing precariousness of the population. i support this initiative, but i regret that it has no real weight.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution calling on member states to commit themselves to the ilo draft convention on domestic workers. this agreement can help to combat the unacceptable working conditions of too many workers in this sector, who are mainly women and many of whom are immigrant workers, especially those without papers. it will complement other ilo conventions or other international organisations. the european parliament also called for the eu and its member states to ratify the international convention on the protection of the rights of migrant workers. i regret, however, that the epp, thanks in particular to the abstention of a number of socialist members, has had an amendment adopted which refuses to put immigrant workers, particularly those without papers, on an equal footing with all other employees. this amendment is part of the increasingly negative perception of immigrants which fuels xenophobia. it will then be necessary to implement the provisions of the convention, which is not the easiest thing to do, but we consider the approach to be positive.
in writing. the report sends a clear message: the european union must integrate a coherent and coordinated cultural strategy into its foreign policy. the links linking europe and the countries of the southern mediterranean in particular are undergoing profound changes. a wind of freedom is blowing in the arab world. culture is a decisive asset. it is playing for a living and sustainable democracy. cultural and educational exchanges encourage the emergence of an organised civil society. cultural cooperation is also one of the keys to the success of the union for the mediterranean. it brings people together to share, to dialogue, to respect and to understand each other better in everyday life.
in writing. it was important that the european parliament send a strong message to remind how much diversity, heritage and cultural exchange must be promoted in all eu external actions. culture, a factor of integration, tolerance and mutual understanding, is an essential component of our societies and must be promoted in our diplomatic efforts to promote human rights and democracy. however, the report stresses that the cultural dimension of external action is still underdeveloped and undercoordinated and that a common and coherent strategy is needed in this area. we also renewed our support for a free internet, condemning censorship and the threats it poses to human rights, but also to access and sharing of the world's cultural heritage. while european citizens share a common set of cultural values, it is by speaking with one voice that we will best serve european interests.
in writing. many people question the reality of european culture, often contrasting it with a europe of cultures or even a europeanization of cultures. for those of us who believe that europe has an identity, values, the answer is obvious: there is a european cultural identity. it is this cultural dimension that the eu must take more into account in its diplomatic efforts, particularly with a view to promoting human rights, democracy and development in third countries. to this end, the high representative should establish a directorate-general for cultural diplomacy within the european external action service, and appoint a person responsible for cultural relations and the promotion of european culture in each eu representation in third countries. in parallel, consideration should be given to the introduction of cultural visas for artists and other cultural professionals.
in writing. by voting in favour of the marietje schaake report, i am advocating the establishment of a genuine european cultural diplomacy to promote our values outside the eu. thinking of culture as a strategic element of foreign policy would indeed allow europe to catch up with certain states - china in particular is investing heavily in cultural diplomacy to improve its image and attract tourists. europe must do the same if it is to continue to play a major role on the world stage. the report proposes several measures to this end: for example, that one person be appointed in each eu representation in third countries to coordinate cultural relations and interactions between the eu and these countries, or that the draft organisational chart of the eeas include posts relating to cultural aspects and that a coordination unit be created. i also think it is appropriate that third countries should be more involved in eu programmes on culture, mobility, youth, education and training: young people from these countries should have easier access to these programmes.
in writing. in 1990, joseph nye, a prominent american professor, coined the concept of "soft power" in his book "bound to lead". what does it mean ? soft power is the ability for an international actor to influence others through non-coercive means, including cultural dynamism. why is it that the united states, after a quarter of a century, is still the superpower we know? because, in addition to their military arsenal, they manage to export their culture and ideas, and make them attractive. europe must do the same; it must defend its cultural model and its values on the international stage. the european parliament, through this report, is measuring the influence that europe can have if it succeeds in adding a cultural dimension to its diplomacy. i therefore support the recommendations contained in this report. the european union must not be allowed to become a mere spectator, but must be a spectator of the world.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report on the cultural dimensions of the eu's external action, which affirms that culture must be at the heart of european diplomacy. despite their diversity, europeans share many strong values, such as respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law, which must be heard on the international stage. this 'europe brand' must be carried by true ambassadors. i welcome the new proposals, such as the creation of a culture division within the european external action service, or the appointment of a cultural attaché for each member country. it is by coordinating national initiatives that a europe of culture can emerge. the development of new information technologies makes culture accessible to the greatest number. i believe that the european union must seize this opportunity to assert its cultural exceptionalism and encourage creativity. i voted in favour of this report, which considers our culture no longer as a legacy of the past but as one of the great strengths of european diplomacy of tomorrow.
in writing. cultural and creative industries are crucial for european citizens because of their economic and cultural nature. while these industries contribute to the promotion of cultural and linguistic diversity and the development of a european cultural heritage, they also contribute to economic development by stimulating employment, economic growth and wealth creation. with this vote we are clearly committed to greater recognition of the cultural sector, stressing that its potential remains great as it still faces legal or economic obstacles. in order to increase this potential, we therefore propose concrete solutions, such as a european licensing system, or improved access to credit and microfinance. we also affirm the enormous advancement the internet represents for our societies, even if it raises new challenges, such as ensuring access for all or the economic model of the cultural sector. the european parliament has therefore clearly called for increased support for cultural actors, aware of the crucial role of culture in european society.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs sanchez-schmid, which contains proposals to encourage the development of cultural and creative industries. the report calls for the creation of a european status for artists, so that they can benefit from satisfactory working conditions and appropriate tax, labour, social protection and copyright measures to improve their mobility within the european union. i also agree with the rapporteur that it is necessary to preserve the specific nature of certain professions and the transmission of knowledge, especially in the cultural, creative and craft sectors, and to guarantee mechanisms for the transmission of knowledge.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the sanchez-schmid report on the development of cultural and creative industries. with almost 14 million jobs involved and growth continuing even in times of crisis, continued support for these industries remains essential, given their significant economic and cultural contribution. the creation of a european status for artists, the introduction of a reduced vat rate for cultural goods and the improvement of the dissemination of legal digital offers are all appropriate and essential measures for the european union's international cultural influence.
in writing. the cultural and creative industries account for 5 million jobs and 2.6% of eu gdp. they are one of the main drivers of european growth, as they create new jobs and stimulate innovation. they also add value as a factor of social cohesion and play a major role in promoting the eu's cultural and linguistic diversity. it is therefore crucial, from both an economic and a social point of view, to support these industries. that is why i am voting in favour of this report. i therefore encourage the member states and the european commission to promote both artistic and cultural education at all ages, from primary to higher or vocational education, and the entrepreneurial skills of cultural professionals - including in the context of lifelong learning. to enable these industries to develop, it is also essential to improve access to finance for professionals in this sector: setting up microfinance, developing public-private sponsorship and partnerships, thinking about the introduction of new innovative financial instruments, or training banking professionals in the specificities of these industries.
in writing. i voted against this report, which is dragging cultural goods towards a logic of market and competition. the 'cultural industries' and, therefore, the cultural goods they produce cannot be treated as businesses like any other on the grounds that they are wealth generators and potentially job creators. first and foremost, they must continue to be recognised as a means of empowerment for the greatest number of people and as a tool for sharing knowledge and experience. it is therefore urgent to reaffirm the principle of cultural exceptionalism in all areas, otherwise the fine phrases about the driving role of the creative industries, the recognition of a status for artists, or the desire to find a balance between the dissemination of digital works and the fair remuneration of creators, will remain wishful thinking in the face of the cultural desert that will be established.
in writing. the evolution of our development model, which has now turned towards the knowledge economy, has made culture a strategically important sector. i welcome the adoption of this report, which proposes ways of making better use of europe's cultural resources. in my view, the unlocking of the creative industries' potential must include a review of the european copyright management system, in order to allow the creative industries to take better advantage of the single market. the system for acquiring licences is, as the report points out, far too complex and calls for the establishment of a single point of sale for the payment of copyright. i also believe that there is a need to stimulate creativity by introducing a specific tax on innovative products such as digital cultural content. it is not right that these products should be subject to full vat while other cultural products benefit from tax rebates. in my vote i wanted to call on the commission and the council to respond to the european parliament's request for concrete measures to take full advantage of the growth potential of this sector. only an ambitious and joint approach can preserve europe's cultural exceptionalism.
in writing. sarajevo, a multicultural city that is a true model of tolerance, undoubtedly holds a special place in european history and culture. it was in sarajevo that the assassination that started world war i in 1914 took place. it was also the site of the longest siege of a capital city in modern warfare history, from 1992 to 1996, during the conflict in bosnia and herzegovina. as the city, which wishes to turn its back on the past and looks forward with enthusiasm to its future in europe, will be celebrating several important anniversaries in 2014, i would like sarajevo to be designated as european capital of culture that year.

relation to the armed conflict in sri lanka. the panel found credible allegations which, if proven, would indicate that serious violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law were committed by the sri lankan military and the ltte, some of which would amount to war crimes and crimes against humanity. the panel also makes a series of recommendations to the un secretary-general and to the government of sri lanka which, in the panel’s words, will serve as the framework for an ongoing and constructive engagement between the secretary-general and the government of sri lanka on accountability. recommendations include the launch of genuine investigations by the government of sri lanka and the establishment of an independent international mechanism by the un secretary-general. the un has stated that the un secretary-general is carefully reviewing the reports, conclusions and recommendations, and the un high commissioner for human rights has urged the sri lankan government to quickly carry out the measures suggested by the panel and ensure justice. the government of sri lanka, on its side, has rejected the report in the strongest terms. should contribute to strengthening the process of reconciliation and ensuring lasting peace and security in sri lanka. the high representative has stressed that the issue of accountability should be seen as an essential part of the process of national reconciliation. the eu therefore hopes that the government of sri lanka will recognise the constructive objectives of the report, and encourages it to engage with the un secretary-general on its contents.

framework programme took place in 2006 and cover the period 2007-2013. since that negotiation, we have had three new elements which have led us to reflect on its assessment. first, the european union is emerging from the failure of the lisbon strategy, defined by the european council in 2000, which aimed to make the european union the world's knowledge economy by 2010. we now have the europe 2020 strategy. the second new element is the failure of the constitutional treaty. today, the treaty of lisbon is in force, with new powers. the third new element is the financial crisis that came to us from the united states in 2008. these three new elements make us question the years 2011 to 2013. we are living in extremely fragile post-crisis years and, in these times of scarcity of public money,
