in writing. the expected benefits of global satellite navigation systems currently for the european economy are estimated at between €55 and €63 billion over the next 20 years. approximately 6% of the eu's total gdp depends on these applications, which are currently mainly based on the us gps system. in this context, i voted in favour of mrs ticau's own-initiative report, which calls on the commission to provide adequate financial support for the development of applications based on the european global satellite navigation system, egnos and galileo. access to such financing by smes should be particularly encouraged in order to stimulate innovation based on these european systems.
in writing. the adoption of this report is an important step forward as it lays the foundations for the general deployment of global satellite navigation systems, and more specifically the development of egnos, which is to support the establishment of the galileo system. i also voted in favour of it because it will allow the introduction of concrete measures which will facilitate the development of transport in europe and which will have a significant impact on safety and the environment and on improving the flow of traffic for road transport.
in writing. the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009, has broadened the circumstances in which parliament's consent is required before concluding an international agreement. air transport agreements are now in this category. that is why i support the report by my colleague brian simpson on the introduction of a set of criteria for assessing their content. i therefore believe that balanced access to markets and investment opportunities, as well as fair competition, should be promoted, particularly in the areas of public subsidies and social and environmental standards.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report for two main reasons. firstly, the report calls for a greater role for the european parliament in the context of the new powers conferred on it by the treaty of lisbon for the conclusion of international agreements with third countries. it stressed the need to strengthen dialogue with the european commission at the various stages of the negotiations and in the follow-up to existing agreements. secondly, the report stresses the need to conclude agreements on aviation safety with third countries where there is a large aircraft manufacturing sector. this is a necessity in the light of the legitimate requirement to ensure ever-increasing aviation safety.
in writing. since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament has more powers to intervene in the conclusion of international agreements between the european union and third countries. the report by brian simpson, adopted today, will thus help to define better the role of parliament in international aviation negotiations. i welcome the fact that parliament is insisting in particular that agreements concluded by the european union provide for mutual recognition of standards of safety and security in air transport and for guarantees to better protect passenger rights.
in writing. with the draft directive on the taxation of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures (eurovignette), member states will now have the possibility of taxing air and noise pollution from road transport. this measure, which applies the 'polluter pays' principle, is intended to encourage the gradual renewal of trucks on our roads. it could also provide a new source of finance for cleaner transport such as rail and waterways. i therefore supported the report by mr el khadraoui. however, i call on the member states to exercise caution when introducing the euro badge: it must not jeopardise the commercial and financial health of transport companies or of companies which use transport.
in writing. while i welcome the agreement reached on the eurovignette directive, i am still far from fully satisfied. by approving the compromise reached between parliament and the council, we are putting an end to long years of negotiations. it is a step in the right direction, but it is a minimum agreement with no restrictions! the member states will only have the possibility, but not the obligation, of making the heavyweights pay for the external costs they cause. the fact remains that the idea is being put forward and that is the real positive point which allows me to vote for the compromise. by introducing the polluter pays principle for heavy goods vehicles, the directive paves the way for the internalization of the external costs of transport to be recognised in our public policies. the principle of transparency of revenue and investment is also respected, which we hope will set a precedent in the evaluation of public policies: the states will have to report to the commission regularly. the low threshold for the allocation of revenue to tens (15%) is nevertheless regrettable. and we will have to ensure that the commitment made by the states to invest the proceeds in sustainable projects is implemented.
in writing. parliament has just given its consent to the new rules on road transport taxation, thus guaranteeing the development and financing of a transport policy more in line with environmental requirements in terms of pollution and noise. if road hauliers are now required to pay for the air and noise pollution generated by lorries, member states will, in return, be obliged to reinvest the revenue from this charge in transeuropean transport networks and, above all, in more efficient and less polluting transport systems. this taxation is a step forward but it is not enough. it is time for the member states to commit themselves to a genuine policy of developing freight transport and thus to make coherent use of all rail and road transport infrastructures.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr saïd el khadraoui, on the revision of the european legislation on the eurovignette, which will allow heavy goods vehicles to be taxed. for the first time, the 'polluter pays' principle will apply to road transport and heavy goods vehicles will be able to be taxed for noise and air pollution when travelling on motorways in the european union. this is an innovative initiative which i welcome, since it allows the environmental and social costs to be taken into account, and is not limited to the cost of infrastructure. it is regrettable, however, that the european parliament's ambition for strong environmental requirements has been held back by the council of ministers, on the pretext of excessive additional costs. nevertheless, this report is a real step forward in the field of the environment.
in writing. i voted for the resolution on heavy goods vehicle taxation because it endorses a difficult agreement on the revision of the 'eurovignette directive'. this 1999 directive, revised in 2006, aims to harmonise the taxation of heavy goods vehicles. the adopted revision is a first step towards internalising external costs in road transport and thus towards a concrete application of the 'polluter pays' principle. air and noise pollution from traffic will be taxed electronically at a rate of 3 to 4 cents per kilometre, depending on the euro class of the vehicle, the location and the congestion rate. the revision now makes it possible to better manage traffic by increasing tolls during peak periods (up to 175% over 5 hours) but also provides for a corresponding reduction in off-peak periods in order not to penalise road transport companies financially. the resolution also calls on the member states to use the money raised to finance certain types of sustainable transport projects.
in writing. the report has the merit of holding the member states to account. about the gifts they give to the automakers of small trucks first. this is a good thing because these irresponsible practices must stop. the allocation of the revenue from the euro-vignette then. again, opacity cannot be the rule! these revenues should be used exclusively for environmental policies. it is unfortunate, however, that the text has come to such a standstill. there is almost nothing on the presentation to the euro vi vehicle manufacturers. worse, the inclusion of the euro-vignette in the carbon market is promoted. i am voting for this text to encourage efforts and to validate the idea of the eurovignette, while at the same time regretting these two serious failures.
politics is about finding the best possible solutions to the problems that arise... but how can we do that if we don't know the problems and the possible solutions? this is a fundamental issue, not only for environmental policy, but also for others... it is therefore essential that policy-makers have reliable and as comprehensive information as possible about the world today and the state of the environment... this is the conclusion reached by the european council in june 2006 when it asked the european union and its member states to extend the national accounts to the main aspects of sustainable development. i welcome this initiative and the european commission's proposal, because it will make it possible to learn more about atmospheric emissions, environmental taxes, etc.
in writing. there is a need to agree on the development of model statistics on the environmental consequences of member states' and eu policies and on the accounting of taxes supporting certain environmental policies. it's obvious. it is unfortunate, however, that statistics and taxes are included indiscriminately in an 'environmental accounting'. the aim of such assimilation is the implementation of the climate package and its pollution rights fund. the delegation of powers to the commission is also in line with this. i vote for it, though. i want to validate the idea of statistical tools being necessary even though i reject the policies that they are supposed to serve.

mr president, the report by mr salvador garriga polledo - whom i thank and congratulate for his work - is an ambitious and forward-looking synthesis. the report calls for increased resources to enable the european union to better achieve its objectives as set out in the lisbon treaty. it raises forcefully the question of own resources and therefore, in fact, the question of the freedom of our institution in its fundamental political act, the vote on its budget. it proposes to extend and extend the common policies, in particular the cohesion policy, which has made a strong contribution in the past and may continue in the future to make the european union a model of understanding and cooperation between peoples. with the future multiannual financial framework, if the european parliament is consulted, cohesion policy can enter a new phase through the creation of intermediate regions. we are therefore proposing a new architecture for this fund which strengthens equal opportunities for all european territories, whatever their economic past, whatever their handicap in relation to the more developed areas, whatever their vulnerability in the face of the economic crisis we are experiencing today or that which we may experience tomorrow. the cohesion between the various territories of the european union is a key strategic objective on which the very future of europe depends. the proposals made are in the right direction and, if they are taken up, they are a valid preparation for the future. mr president, the vote on this report by mr garriga will be a simple choice, a choice for a europe that moves forward, a vote by those who, regardless of their political affiliation, believe in the future of europe.
mr president, the debate on the financial perspectives of the european union is in fact about the european project, its content and its ambition. the great merit of this report is that it aims to mobilise the union's budgetary resources in line with and in service of the europe 2020 strategy and, therefore, stands in contrast to most member states, which have a narrow view of it. while member states reduce europe to the amount of their contribution, which they want to see reduced, and to its financial returns, which they want to see increased, this report argues for strong integrated community policies, both in terms of historical policies and the new competences conferred by the lisbon treaty. so yes, this own-initiative report of parliament must form the basis of the future debate, even if, in my view, it fails to reach an excessive consensus and to be cautious. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. the crucial question, however, and probably the stumbling block, will be to set the course in line with the policies outlined in this report. we know the harm of austerity policies, their impact on employment, the despair of a growing number of our citizens and we have a responsibility to finance counter-cyclical policies, particularly through a strong cohesion policy, mr pieper, which supports public investment and jobs in the territories. i would like to stress the importance of creating a category of intermediate regions for a distribution of the structural funds as closely as possible to the economic and social realities of the territories. i would conclude by saying that we must achieve taxation of speculation, which is likely to encourage greater citizenship for a better-funded european project.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is often said that money is the lifeblood of war. it must be remembered that money is also the nerve of a peace project such as the european project. if europe is to implement the policies enshrined in the treaties, including the most recent ones - those of the lisbon treaty - it is essential that it has the financial means to match its ambitions. i am therefore in favour of the collection of own resources and the creation of a financial transaction tax. this necessary increase in the european budget will have to be accompanied by substantial savings through the optimisation of expenditure. let us, for example, have a genuine common foreign and defence policy, to ensure greater european influence throughout the world, but also to make the best possible use of public money. the garriga polledo report is a fundamental text, almost a groundbreaking text, because it gives the european union very strong political and budgetary prospects. in addition, two key policies of this union have their full place in it. the cap, which is a policy crucial to the food security and independence of our continent; the budget will have to be renewed. cohesion policy, i.e. the financial instrument for solidarity between european regions and their economic development; the commission's proposal is to strengthen the ambition of the european union by creating an intermediate category of regions so that regions at the same level of development benefit from the same level of development.
in writing. the purpose of my colleague garriga polledo's report is to define the european parliament's political priorities for the post-2013 mff, both at legislative and budgetary level. two aspects in particular caught my attention. first, a political priority is cohesion for growth and employment. i strongly support the creation of an intermediate category for regions with a gdp per capita of between 75% and 90% of the union's gdp. the challenge is to achieve greater equity between regions. this proposal reflects the principle of territorial cohesion enshrined in article 174 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. secondly, as regards the financial perspective, i am in favour of introducing a financial transaction tax with a view to creating budgetary resources specific to the european union.
in writing. the vote on my colleague salvador garriga's report will be an important milestone for our mandate: the european parliament sets out in a clear, pragmatic and realistic way its budgetary ambitions for europe after 2013. i would like to stress first of all the need to defend the cohesion policy, which is so important for the development of our territories. i am convinced of the need to maintain its budget and to introduce fair aid for all middle-income regions in order to make visible and fair the future investments that the eu is allowing in our regions. the reasonable increase in the budget by 5% is not a sign of european weakness, as the eurosceptics would have us believe, but of the courage to say that if we do not give ourselves the means to build together, we will sink into isolation and powerlessness. so, in order to be able to finance the actions linked to the new powers that the treaty of lisbon has given the eu, i would like to support the request that we consider new own resources and revenue at community level to relieve national budgets and avoid the economically false and politically unhealthy notion of 'just return'.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the entry of romania and bulgaria into the schengen area. this is the second assessment of the application of the schengen provisions by romania and bulgaria, following the one carried out in 2010. it should be recalled that romania and bulgaria adopted the schengen acquis (data protection, schengen information system, air, land and sea borders, police cooperation and visas) when they joined the european union in 2007, but that it is now up to all member states to decide on their effective entry into the borderless area. the european parliament is consulted.
in writing. the schengen area, and especially the free movement of persons, is one of the community acquis that speaks most to our citizens. mr barroso said that 'freedom of movement is to europe what foundations are to a building'. free movement is one of the union's great achievements. i welcome the entry of bulgaria and romania into the schengen area following the vote in parliament. a great deal of effort has been put into ensuring border security, with their 4th generation surveillance system being more exemplary than our 2nd generation. however, obstacles to the free movement of workers persist: first, legal and administrative obstacles affecting all aspects of citizens' lives; social dumping is next, because while article 45 of the tfeu ensures equal treatment for workers, the work of the committee on petitions nevertheless shows that the opposite is still the case; finally, social protection differs from one country to another, which does not encourage mobility. i therefore propose that a minimum social protection threshold be set in the union. while social protection is a matter for the member states, this lack of harmonisation clearly harms the internal market.

in writing. i voted in favour of this report. member states such as france, germany and the netherlands want to change the rules of the game. it is not possible to add other criteria such as the evaluation of anti-corruption and anti-crime policies, which are important but whose suspicious assessment is strictly political and would introduce a two-speed mechanism between the different member states.
in writing. in the light of the results of the evaluations and follow-up visits carried out by the expert teams, it was found that bulgaria and romania were ready to integrate into the schengen area. that is why i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr carlos coelho.
in writing. i have nothing against our friends, colleagues or neighbours, bulgarians and romanians. i have many complaints about the schengen system. this agreement, which was signed in secret and ratified in august of the 1980s, has proved to be a total disaster. the dismantling of internal borders does not guarantee freedom of movement for european citizens, but creates unmanageable insecurity, demographic and migration situations within the eu, in the countries of destination and in the countries of departure. it is also a great incentive for illegal immigration, which is assured, whatever its point of entry into europe, that it can go and settle wherever it wants, and especially in france. the problems of the roma and lampedusa, which have been mentioned many times here, are only a few examples of this situation. i don't want schengen for my country. so i don't wish that for the others either. states must retain full control of all their borders and, where appropriate, cooperate with each other to strengthen their 'external' borders.
in writing. i fully supported the adoption of this report which gives its consent to the accession of bulgaria and romania to the schengen area. these two states have made considerable efforts to strengthen border controls and have succeeded in doing so; this is evidenced by the expert visits and evaluations carried out under the supervision of the council working party on schengen evaluation, which have reached positive conclusions. these two countries meet and fulfil all the technical criteria set by the european union. i am therefore fully in favour of their full participation in the schengen area. states cannot add new criteria (such as the evaluation of anti-corruption and anti-crime policies) and change the rules along the way. this week we are celebrating the 26th anniversary of the schengen agreements: it is one of the most beautiful constructions of the european union, which must be defended, just like our right to free movement, one of the most fundamental rights of the citizens of the european union.
in writing. i support the green light for romania and bulgaria to join the schengen area. a thorough and objective analysis of the fulfilment by these two countries of the criteria laid down in the schengen acquis has been carried out and it has been concluded that they fully fulfil these conditions. it is therefore not conceivable to add other criteria such as the evaluation of anti-corruption and anti-crime policies, which are important but whose suspicious assessment is strictly political, and would introduce a two-speed mechanism between the different member states. this vision of a europe of 'two weights and measures' depending on whether it is a question of old or new member states is simply unacceptable.
in writing. bulgaria and romania have made all the efforts that fortress europe demanded of them to ensure that their citizens can move freely within the schengen area. this report calls for more. he called for a common approach with greece to be taken against migrants from arab countries. such a request is unacceptable. i abstain in order not to oppose free movement within the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr carlos coelho proposing the entry of bulgaria and romania into the 'schengen area'. this is one of the major achievements of the european construction. the admission of a new state is subject to strict compliance with the criteria of the schengen agreements. however, in the case of bulgaria and romania, the european parliament's civil liberties committee - as well as the european commission - have concluded after investigation that these two countries fully meet the conditions. as a result, there is no longer any obstacle to their integration into this area of free movement. i think it would be unacceptable if some states, on the basis of false pretexts and motivated by internal political considerations, continued to oppose it. the community acquis cannot be regarded as a tailor-made system in which the member states could adapt or suspend provisions as circumstances require. i therefore solemnly call on the council to endorse the progress made by bulgaria and romania and to admit them to the schengen area.

in writing. i supported the alexander graf lambsdorff report because i believe that we need to strengthen the cohesion of member states' positions, as well as our capacity to negotiate with other regional groups. the aim is to improve the efficiency and transparency of the united nations and the management of its financial resources. i am convinced that a reform of the functioning and composition of the un security council is necessary in the medium term.
in writing. as the 66th ordinary session of the united nations general assembly approached, the european parliament addressed its usual recommendations to the council, representing the member states, which are the only full members of the organisation. but this year the union will be able to use its new super-observer status, which gives it special rights to speak at the sessions. i voted in favour of this resolution because it gives full weight to the union's new ambitions at international level. the lisbon treaty gives it new prerogatives, confirms the development of its international capacity and introduces new tools. this act requires the union to put this new ambition at the service of effective multilateralism, in which its values must be fully effective. it also calls for a strengthening of global governance, at a time when global challenges require global solutions. finally, it focuses on the core issues that the union has traditionally been called upon to help advance: development, human rights and climate change.
in writing. as rapporteur for the committee on development's opinion on this report, i welcome its adoption today by the european parliament as a whole. it is essential to reaffirm the need to harmonize the efforts of the various united nations bodies in order to promote more efficiently and effectively development action. the development assistance implemented by the united nations must focus in particular on the achievement of the millennium development goals, with particular attention to the least developed countries.
in writing. my colleague jean-pierre audy's report on the european union's seventh framework programme for research, technological development and demonstration (fp7) denounces a low level of participation by smes and industry in general, a low number of female researchers and an under-representation of some member states. i believe that there is a need for effective coordination of research between the eu and national and regional authorities. that is why i voted in favour of this excellent report.
in writing. the eu's 7th framework programme is a crucial programme to improve european added value in r & d and innovation as europe lags behind the us and loses its lead over emerging economies in these areas. this report therefore underlines the relevance of an unknown programme, while calling for changes: - to change the administrative and financial rules which are too burdensome and the low success rate which make this programme still too dissuasive for smes, while they play an important role in the transformation of research results into products and services; - to ensure better cooperation and coordination between the various actors while research funding remains fragmented between national and european sources. these are some of the ways in which we could finally achieve the objective of financing research and development at 3% of gdp by 2020, which is far from being achieved, especially for france, which still spends only 2% of its gdp on this.
in writing. this report highlighted the factors that are essential to meet the requirements of the future of research in europe, particularly in the context of the objectives set by the europe 2020 strategy. it has now become essential to reduce excessive administrative burdens, in particular to encourage greater participation of smes in the 7th framework programme. it is also imperative that eu programmes continually bring together the benefits of research and innovation for the benefit of education and job creation.
in writing. the 7th framework programme for research and development for the period 2007-2013 is the subject of a mid-term evaluation by the european parliament. this is an opportunity to remind the european commission of the importance of making the right investment choices in research and innovation for the future of europe. for the years 2011, 2012 and 2013, eur 28.5 billion remains to be programmed. this amount should be allocated as a priority to projects promoted by smes and industry in general, in particular in the fields of energy supply, sustainable development and the fight against climate change. the best distribution of research infrastructures throughout the european union will have to be ensured, while respecting the principle of excellence which makes it possible to welcome the best researchers in the world to europe.
in writing. in 2010, the european union had not met the lisbon strategy target of devoting 3% of its gdp to research and development. this objective has been included in the europe 2020 strategy, but the eu must now equip itself to meet this objective in order to remain an internationally competitive economy. i therefore welcome the adoption of the audy report on the mid-term review of the 7th framework programme, taking into account the effects of the economic crisis of recent years, which have particularly affected the capacity of small and medium-sized enterprises to invest in r & d. in order to avoid administrative burdens and to facilitate access to european funding for businesses, simplification and greater transparency of procedures are essential.
in writing. research and development play a major role in modernising our economies and enhancing our competitiveness. with a budget of €54 billion for the period 2007-13, the 7th framework programme is the largest research support programme in the world. the adoption of this report by a large majority shows the strong interest of parliament in the success of this programme and the next ones. efforts still need to be made to ensure sound management of public money and to avoid the dispersion of funds into projects that are inefficient or do not meet our needs. the future of european research depends on simplifying the implementation of programmes, facilitating access to finance, involving smes, but above all adapting our priorities to the major societal challenges (demographic ageing, climate change, etc.). i am convinced that the european union has a leading role to play in the development of major research programmes and that it can, by consolidating the european research area, bring real added value. that is why i have decided to give my full support to this report.
in writing. every year since 2007, the european union has spent over €6 billion to fund research and development on the continent. this is one of the major challenges facing europeans in the coming decades. europeans, who are lagging behind the united states and are being caught up very quickly by emerging countries, must quickly put innovation back at the forefront of their social model. the report by my colleague jean-pierre audy draws on the lessons of the first part of the framework programme for research. with a view to achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, it recommends that the remaining programming should address the union's most urgent challenges in the sectors identified in the seventh framework programme's 'cooperation' chapter: health, agri-food and biotechnology, information and communication technologies, nanosciences and nanotechnologies, energy, the set plan and the use of biogas, environment, sustainable transport, economic and social sciences, humanities, space and security. i voted for this report because it not only takes stock of the situation but also sets ambitious objectives for the union, which are in line with the expectations of the european citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr audy's report on the mid-term review of fp7. the european parliament reiterates its commitment to this programme, which is of major importance for the development of european research and the improvement of the competitiveness of our enterprises. it advocates the sustainability of its budget, which is essential if it is to achieve its objectives. the report then makes concrete proposals to correct the programme's malfunctions. it rightly stresses the need to simplify its financing procedures and to optimise existing tools in order to facilitate access for smes. the report also stresses the need for the european commission to ensure that the promotion of innovation does not come at the expense of progress in basic research.
in writing. by voting in favour of this resolution on the current trade negotiations between the european union and canada, i wish to reaffirm the importance of international trade (including with canada) for the development of our economies. as stated in that resolution, while europe must continue to give priority to the international trading system, i.e. the doha round negotiations, the current negotiations with canada can usefully complement this international approach with an equally necessary bilateral approach. so by discussing and negotiating, we are able to find solutions to the questions relating to our trade and to the respect of certain principles, for example those relating to the environment. however, as vice-chair of the public services working party, i am concerned about the approach taken to this sector. the definition of a negative list (excluding certain public services from the liberalisation process) rather than a positive list (exempting public services from liberalisation, except those mentioned in the list) risks weakening public services. the resolution therefore urges the european commission to abandon this approach.
in writing. while a trade agreement is being negotiated between the european union and canada, the european parliament, through the resolution we have just adopted, expresses its concern at the attitude of the european commission towards public services. the european commission, which is negotiating the agreement, seems to want all services to be included a priori. by negotiating a negative list of services which would not be included in free trade agreements, the commission, if this is confirmed, reverses the logic which has prevailed until now. public services are not services like any other: because they bring social and territorial cohesion and provide essential support to vulnerable populations, they have characteristics of the general interest they pursue. it is therefore essential to continue to take a protective approach to these services, in particular by protecting them from international competition.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on eu-canada trade relations aimed at the conclusion of a comprehensive trade agreement. canada is a privileged partner of the european union, as canadian investment in europe has almost doubled over 10 years, reaching €119.5 million in 2009. it is therefore necessary to set an advanced legal framework to ensure positive effects on growth. i would like to stress the issue of access to the markets for agricultural products. as the rules of origin differ between canada and the eu, the commission must ensure that the interests and priorities of european agriculture are properly taken into account. in particular, efforts must be made to find a satisfactory solution to the problem of rules of origin so that canadian products do not lead to the products of other nafta members being traced.
in writing. in the context of the ongoing negotiations on the trade agreement between the european union and canada, the commission must commit itself to respecting the requirements of the european parliament. in a free trade agreement, two things are essential: firstly, to guarantee reciprocity in respect of social and environmental legislation, and secondly, to adopt a coherent and protective approach to services of general interest. the european environmental and health standards must not be lowered just to satisfy our partner. the european commission must consider the consequences of its choice to include all services automatically and by default. although this method allows certain public services to be excluded on a case-by-case basis and at the request of each member state, by drawing up a 'negative' list, it nevertheless presents the risk of potential forgetting. parliament does not want this new negotiating model to be able to be used as a case law. until now, the commission has negotiated free trade agreements by means of a 'positive' list of the services covered by the agreement. this method, which is commonly used in international trade, is more likely to preserve certain sensitive sectors for the eu and should therefore be the only one used by the commission.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution but against amendment no 10 supporting the eu's ban on the import of seal products. this is not scientifically or legally based. the conclusions of the scientific opinion delivered by the european food safety authority (efsa) at the end of 2007 are based on data on the killing of animals in slaughterhouses and are not reliable for the seal hunt. the legal basis is also questionable, as is shown by the legal opinion of the european parliament of 1 april 2009: 'it seems almost impossible to justify the ban on the basis of animal welfare alone, since the treaty contains no legal basis on animal welfare'. the protection of the species is not in question, but its population has tripled in greenland in 25 years. finally, an embargo which the commission ensures does not have an impact on traditional inuit hunting is utopian. in this context, canada's request to the wto for the establishment of a special dispute settlement group on the european embargo is justified.
in writing. the european commission will conclude negotiations with canada on an unprecedented free trade agreement. she's been negotiating since 2004. the european citizens were never consulted or even informed. the report welcomes this harmful agreement, the contents of which are only known through leaks. this is unacceptable! i am voting against and denouncing this agreement which places the peoples of europe in a subordinate position on the model of those of nafta.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague wolf klinz on credit rating agencies. credit rating agencies are useful in providing information on the quality of credit products, in providing access to global and domestic markets for borrowers and investors, and in helping to set prices. however, the crisis has demonstrated the dangers of the current system: lack of competition and lack of accountability and transparency of agencies in particular. this is an own-initiative report from parliament, which calls on the european commission to clearly identify the weaknesses of the current framework and to provide an impact study outlining the various alternatives to be considered to improve the system, including new legislation if necessary. i would urge the commission to respond to our request as soon as possible.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr wolf klinz. it contains interesting proposals for continuing the necessary supervision of credit rating agencies. the current situation in the euro area is a near daily reminder of the impact of the decisions made by these agencies and the dependence of the global financial regulatory system on them. i particularly welcome the request to the european commission to study the feasibility of setting up an independent european credit rating foundation. this is a concrete proposal to deal with the excessive reliance of the global financial regulatory system on a few private rating agencies.
in writing. one after another, the rating agencies are lowering or putting under negative surveillance the ratings of the european countries most affected by the crisis: portugal, ireland, greece, spain. without triggering the global financial crisis, the agencies have nevertheless contributed to it by acting in this way. they encourage speculation, jeopardizing the chances of success of the already very draconian recovery plans imposed on their populations. this is why it is urgent to create a european rating agency which would take the legal form of an independent foundation. the conflicts of interest inherent in rating agencies, which are currently able to issue ratings while acting as consultancies, must also be addressed. this should be in line with the commission's assessment of the need to increase disclosure for all products in the area of financial instruments.
in writing. almost the entire market for financial ratings, which are sometimes made mandatory for regulatory purposes, is held by three major us agencies. opening up this sector to competition, or creating a public agency at european level, will not change the perversity of the system. because today, it's always crazy: you don't know who markets or agencies are controlling the reactions of the other. if a country's bad rating triggers a panic over sovereign debt, or if cynical speculation drives a bad rating; whether a good rating influences the ownership of certain assets or whether, because they are good and you want to own them, the assets are rated well. closer monitoring of the activities of the agencies is a minimal service and of course insufficient. despite repeated criticism in europe and the united states, the reputation of the agencies has not really suffered. no doubt, holding them legally and even financially responsible for the consequences of their errors and carelessness could have an impact. but again, unless you change the system fundamentally instead of trying to plug the holes in it to ensure its survival, nothing will be solved.
in writing. this hypocritical text claims that the main difficulty with rating agencies is the barriers to competition. his solution to the "over-reliance" of banks on these workshops is that banks themselves assess the risks. the banks that are responsible for measuring sobriety! if they are not able to do so, they are asked to apply the least favourable rating to better protect themselves! the problem is not to protect the interests of the banks but to protect the general interest. once again, the people are the least of the eu's concerns.
in writing. i supported the report by our colleague mr richard falbr because i believe that the union must promote higher labour and social standards in third countries in order to preserve its credibility in international trade and to build strong relations with major trading partners. the rapporteur advocates a balanced relationship with ngos and international organisations to facilitate ratification of the conventions. in order to negotiate with the union, third countries must respect internationally established labour standards.
in writing. having a uniform form of social clause that could be inserted into all bilateral trade agreements is what the report we have just adopted on the external dimension of social policy and the promotion of social standards proposes. what a step in the right direction! the report notes that free trade agreements still rarely mention social standards, and suggests a number of ways, including the social clause, but also respect for ilo conventions - which have already been ratified by all the member states! - and the strengthening of cooperation between third countries and member states. the development of the concept of corporate social responsibility is the other interesting aspect of the report. for while it is a useful concept for the time being, it is still based on voluntary action and can therefore be improved upon! in addition to extending the concept to several areas and integrating csr into our trade policies, why not make it a binding one day? beyond the political signal, this would make it possible to make real progress in achieving our social policy objectives.
in writing. the external dimension of social policy aims to promote labour and social standards in third countries and to combat social dumping, sometimes as a result of globalisation or international trade. the union can no longer accept without action the social, health and environmental dumping which is responsible for too many relocations from our european territory. the commission should no longer regard the low labour costs or the poor working conditions as 'natural competitive advantages'. i would urge the commission to change its approach on this point.
in writing. i voted in favour of the falbr report because i believe that, in the light of the recent weakening of the role of the international labour organisation, it is necessary to stress the importance of respect for the social rights of workers throughout the world. the european union must play a leading role in the world in order to impose on other countries the observance of international labour law standards and thus limit the unbridled use of social dumping. it is important that all european actors are involved in the implementation of this policy, whether governments in the context of the conclusion of international agreements or european companies developing their activities in third countries.
in writing. globalisation is really about putting workers from all countries in unfair competition. whether through relocations, through so-called labour immigration, or finally through the famous mode 4 of the general agreement on trade in services. the problem is that the european union, while making fine speeches on the subject, never puts them into practice. when did the practical and concrete consequences of the finding of intolerable exploitation situations come to light? when have such situations prevented the signing of trade agreements with any country? i never will. because if you pretend to be concerned about the situation of foreign workers, european workers are eliminated from your thinking. as the rapporteur points out - and i agree with him - the world bodies say that 'labour standards cannot be used for protectionist commercial purposes'. but what principles, what values, what considerations could be opposed to the all-powerful market? you're talking about corporate social responsibility, which, after all, is just playing by the rules you make. when will the very heavy social responsibility of eu policy-makers be discussed here?
in writing. i welcome the fact that the opinion of the committee on development, for which i was rapporteur, is included in this report. the 100th international labour conference is currently taking place and we all know that the current rules are ineffective. in a context of global crisis, it is essential that the eu sends a strong message calling for a new era of social justice. the proposals contained in mr falbr's report would make real progress in this direction. we cannot but deplore the double standard in the application of social rights. implementation mechanisms (with incentives and penalties) are necessary for social standards to be effectively enforced. a social clause must be incorporated into all eu trade agreements and be legally binding. i would like to say that i am not happy that the report (paragraph 31) insists that there should be no european directive imposing corporate social responsibility. i stress the need to move towards greater social justice and to ensure that the rights of workers are respected throughout the world and particularly in our relations with developing countries.
in writing. the economic and financial crisis which is currently raging in europe and the rest of the world is being combined with a serious social crisis. in this difficult context, the european union and its businesses have a great social responsibility in their relations with third countries. i therefore wanted to stress in my vote the need for the european union to guarantee respect for social standards and workers' rights in the agreements it concludes with these countries. the european union, by virtue of its values, must ensure the development and dissemination of the standards governing its labour law throughout the world. europe must be a model. that is why i also voted in favour of provisions which emphasize corporate social responsibility.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the external dimension of the european union's social policy. the european union is a magnet and a sought-after partner throughout the world, and this is due in large part to the unique way in which it combines economic dynamism and social model. it must be promoted by the community in its relations with other countries and must be the subject of coherent action between the two strands, internal and external. this text stresses the need to promote corporate social responsibility in particular. it requires companies to integrate social and environmental concerns into their business. the resolution stresses that such promotion should not be mandatory but should be the result of interaction between stakeholders on a voluntary basis. it also aims to integrate workers' rights, which the world labour organisation is responsible for defending, into international negotiations and to promote global economic governance that takes these parameters into account.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it recalls the leading role that the european union wants and must play vis-à-vis third countries, in particular its trading partners. the failure to respect basic international social standards is a form of social and environmental dumping to the detriment of european businesses and workers. this is one of the points i wanted to stress in the opinion of the committee on international trade on this matter, for which i was rapporteur. but the eu alone cannot be fully effective: it must cooperate more closely with the relevant international organisations (ilo, wto, oecd), in particular to combat the phenomenon of free zones, which derogate from all social legislation. furthermore, while corporate social responsibility is now well developed in europe, european companies, their subsidiaries and subcontractors play a fundamental role in promoting and disseminating social and labour standards worldwide because of their weight in international trade. the commission should encourage them in this direction, in particular by seeking out and promoting best practice.
in writing. i voted in favour of the nadja hirsch report, which aims to make comparisons between and within education systems. i believe that education should be better adapted to the needs of the labour market and encourage creativity, innovation and entrepreneurship. the report also aims to facilitate the mobility of teachers and students and to simplify the procedures for the recognition of foreign professional qualifications, which is essential.
in writing. with youth unemployment currently at 21% in the european union and close to 25% in my country, it has become a major challenge for europe as unemployed young europeans are threatened with social exclusion and poverty. the eu has only marginal competence on these issues, but it seems that it can provide, if not solutions, to the interesting lines of thought: it seems obvious to me that training and education must be at the heart of the political priorities of today and tomorrow. the report calls on the member states to exchange good practice on their systems of alternance vocational education and training, which should be extended in many member states, particularly in france. these recommendations are a step in the right direction towards improving education and training in relation to the labour market and reducing unemployment and social exclusion, but they will remain insufficient if the member states and the commission do not make sufficient efforts, as youth unemployment is becoming the major political challenge in many member states, particularly in my country, france.
in writing. tackling youth unemployment is one of the most urgent challenges facing europe. therefore, member states should rapidly adopt targeted strategies that take into account national specificities and needs. learning methods must be more flexible and accessible throughout life. we must develop opportunities for all to gain experience abroad. the learning periods must also be better recognised. education and vocational training must be treated as a common long-term policy priority to enable european workers to adapt to the demands of a changing economy.
in writing. at a time when the unemployment rate among young people in europe is twice as high as that of the working population, the hirsch report's proposals are a useful contribution to the policy pursued by the governments of the 27 member states to combat unemployment. in the face of the challenges posed by an ageing population, but also by the globalisation of our economy, the development of lifelong learning programmes should be encouraged, in particular through the exchange of good practice between member states, and the initial training of young europeans should be improved by promoting partnerships between universities, research centres and businesses.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which puts vocational education and training at the centre of the concerns of the european union and its member states. at a time of budgetary austerity, a direct consequence of the world crisis which has hit the european labour market hard, it is necessary to reflect on our strategies for increasing employment, especially among young people, without losing sight of national specificities and needs. young people are the first victims of unemployment and are highly prone to drop out of school. it is therefore imperative to modernise teaching and training so that it can be more closely adapted to the needs of our enterprises. these efforts must also be made in the field of continuing training and the promotion of mobility. these objectives can only be achieved if all the stakeholders (european institutions, member states, local and regional actors) are involved.
in writing. the eu 2020 strategy aims to reduce the school drop-out rate to below 10% and to ensure that at least 40% of the younger generation has a qualification or diploma. these objectives pursue the european ambition, first set out in the lisbon strategy, to make the union the most competitive knowledge-based economy in the world. this is why the copenhagen process, which has been in place since 2002, is of particular importance as it sets the stage for better cooperation between member states' policies in the field of vocational education and training. i voted for this resolution because it sets ambitious targets for improving european education and training programmes.
in writing. i voted in favour of the nadja hirsch report. to meet the economic challenges of the 21st century, and in particular the increasing competition from our trading partners, europe's vocational education and training systems need to be more efficient, more attractive and more responsive, in order to better prepare our citizens for the jobs they will have to fill. the commission has therefore to work to make these systems more suited to the needs of the world of work. i also believe that it is necessary to facilitate access to quality traineeships in europe and thus to maintain and strengthen existing programmes to increase the mobility of apprentices. to set up a genuine 'erasmus for apprentices', that was my commitment during the 2009 european election campaign: it is for young and old people, while entering the world of work and gaining professional experience, to have the opportunity to move around our european space and to rub shoulders with the economic realities of our internal market. finally, the system of recognition of professional qualifications in europe must be simplified and improved in order to revive the internal market and to give our fellow citizens the keys to greater professional mobility.
in writing. the eu and the member states must step up their efforts to promote youth employment and reduce youth unemployment, in particular by improving the matching of training systems with labour market needs. with 12 million low-skilled jobs expected to disappear in europe by 2020, and with the need to extend the working lives of workers to ensure that our social model is maintained in the face of the demographic challenge, it is also crucial, in parallel, to deepen efforts to improve the continuing training of workers in the course of their careers. in this respect, the idea of setting up incentive mechanisms for employers to encourage their employees to participate in training programmes, which my colleague nadja hirsch has proposed in this report, seems to me to be interesting. in addition, to combat the unemployment of the low-skilled and to promote the employment of the elderly, it is imperative to encourage the development of recognition of national qualifications between member states, as well as the development of certification by validation of skills acquired through informal learning.
in writing. the fight against youth unemployment must be a priority for all european governments. european youth must be offered a comprehensive, attractive and competitive training and education system which will make it easier for them to enter the labour market. i believe that vocational education and lifelong learning should be more in line with the needs of the labour market. furthermore, higher education must be combined with vocational training, for example by giving priority to alternating between training and employment. that is why i voted in favour of the hirsch report.
in writing. i supported the gay mitchell report because i believe that we need to increase the involvement of parliaments in developing countries in the development of policy documents for these countries, for example for the poverty eradication strategy. in addition, european development aid must be adequately funded. the european union has committed to collectively devoting 0.7% of its gni to official development assistance (oda) by 2015, which will require an increase in the current amount of eu aid.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the gay mitchell report which sets out parliament's position on the new financing instrument for development cooperation in the european union, based on the lessons learned from the implementation of the icd (development cooperation financing instrument). in this connection, i would like to point out that a high level of poverty remains in developing countries, territories and regions and that funds for the causes of poverty, in particular malnutrition, health problems, education, access to clean water, should be increased rather than moving towards immigration regulation systems which are the responsibility of other financial arrangements. development aid must be such as to keep the populations concerned in their geographical area. immigration regulation must be transferred to another financial instrument and must lead to a strengthening of the resources of the frontex agency. that is why i voted for this report.
in writing. development aid policy is neither an altruistic obligation nor a way of giving the former colonizing powers a good conscience, when colonization has taken place. it is a branch of foreign policy in its own right, but it should also be an important element in a strategy to reverse migration flows, allowing people to stay in their countries of origin, or to return to them, and live there in dignity and, increasingly, in prosperity. and because these two areas are sovereign, most of the institutional and financial requirements of the mitchell report are not acceptable.
in writing. i voted in favour of the mitchell report because it is necessary to draw lessons from the last four years of operation of regulation (ec) no 1905/2006 establishing a financing instrument for development cooperation (dci). the objectives and scope of development aid must be clearly defined. migration is an area where policy coherence for development needs to be prioritised. for example, development aid should finance projects to tackle the root causes of migration (combating poverty), but should not be used to improve border management or to combat illegal immigration.
in writing. i am convinced that impact assessments should help in the preparation of policy decisions. that is why i supported the report by our colleague angelika niebler on the necessary developments in impact assessments, and in particular on the establishment of an independent mechanism. the members of the impact assessment commission (iac) would be scrutinised by the european parliament and the council. they would therefore no longer be subject to the instructions of the president of the commission.
in writing. i have already had the opportunity to say in this house that it is time that impact studies were not only systematic but above all serious. that we should objectively assess the consequences of legislation before we put it into effect, rather than seeking to justify it by all means. and it is not the commission's departments, judges, parties and executioners all together, that are responsible for these assessments. i do not know whether the solutions proposed by the rapporteur are the right ones. but i do know that i agree with his diagnosis and that some of his remarks are particularly relevant. the member states must therefore be closely associated with these studies, because they are better able to judge the national impact of the initiatives taken in brussels. these studies should inform the choices and reflections of the national parliaments, which are now responsible for ensuring that the principle of subsidiarity is respected. they must be able to lead to the commission abstaining if its action proves to be unnecessary, redundant or costly. finally, we must be able to draw the consequences quickly of legislation whose implementation creates more problems than it solves. for all these reasons, but without any illusions about its implementation, i voted for mrs niebler's report.
in writing. i welcome this text which denounces the european commission's partiality. it is a pity that he does not denounce the fact that it alone has the power of legislative initiative.
in writing. in recent years, the potential benefits of a european contract law for the internal market have been the subject of much debate. on this point, i think that we should encourage the introduction of an optional instrument by means of regulations so that this parallel system does not impede the national system. that is the approach taken in the report by our colleague diana wallis, and i have therefore supported it.
in writing. the wallis report sets ambitious targets on the actions that can be envisaged with a view to creating a european contract law for consumers and businesses. the challenges are key to helping to improve the functioning of the internal market by better including businesses and consumers. on the one hand, differences in contract law should be eliminated in order to remove the obstacles faced by firms. on the other hand, a high level of protection for european consumers must be ensured.
in writing. as an important step in the implementation of the single european market act, i welcome the adoption of the wallis report. while the heterogeneity of national laws is a major obstacle to cross-border trade, especially for smes, the establishment of a european contract law regime is a real step forward that should be supported. by regulating both contractual relations between businesses and those between consumers and businesses, the adoption of an optional instrument coupled with a toolbox could ensure better protection of consumers in europe.
in writing. what mrs wallis is proposing is nothing more or less than the creation of a 28th legal order, parallel to national laws and intended to replace them in practice, the words 'harmonisation' or 'legislative uniformity' now being feared in the european political context. this new european law is supposed to remove the obstacles to cross-border trade arising from the differences in national laws. the problem is that nothing in mrs wallis' report objectively proves the existence of such obstacles. so that's a problem to solve. and so nothing but the desire to initiate a new method of imposing supranational law justifies such a position. it would also create a real risk of being used to circumvent national protective provisions, in particular consumer rights. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. when it comes to establishing the common market, it is not enough to simply remove the positive barriers between the member states of the union. to reap the benefits of an effective integrated market, it is also necessary to tackle the indirect causes of our citizens' crossborder anxieties. in addition to a number of administrative difficulties, european entrepreneurs are too often confronted with the diversity of contractual rules in force in the member states. these obstacles are particularly difficult for smes to overcome, which are the most effective lever to boost growth. the european commission has therefore published a green paper on the subject and launched a wide public consultation. i voted for this resolution of parliament because it chooses a common sense option of proposing a competing instrument of national rights which would facilitate cross-border trade. this 'european contract' would be optional, accompanied by a 'toolbox' to clarify its use and would promote greater consumer protection.
in writing. as the stieglitz commission in france in 2008-2009 showed, new development indicators need to be considered to complement gdp. the current reference value, although it can lead to certain errors of assessment (for example, reparations for natural disasters are perceived as economic progress), is no longer sufficient. i voted for the anna rosbach report because it asks the commission to continue its research in this area, ignoring the frivolity of the conservatives who believe that only gdp is reliable and the illusions of a part of the left who would like to measure precisely ... happiness! the commission's work will have to be followed closely because it could lead to an important development: a new (more adequate) method of calculating the distribution of european funding to the regions (regional policy), hitherto allocated according to the level of gdp per capita of the regions concerned.
in writing. gdp has been the main economic measure for many years, but its shortcomings are increasingly highlighted when it comes to judging social or environmental progress. this is why this resolution is so important, because it stresses the need for the european union to develop additional gdp indicators to take better account of, among other things, climate change, biodiversity and social integration, which are major political challenges that i am very keen to tackle. i voted for this report because defining and implementing a new set of indicators is a major challenge to better measure the quality of life of european citizens and to improve policy responses which cannot be developed in the light of gdp alone. i believe that this initiative is an encouraging first step towards a better integration of social and environmental issues into european public policies, but to be fully useful and effective it will have to be followed by a real introduction of a new range of indicators and a real and coherent political use of them, not as gadgets but as real tools to help in decision-making.
in writing. the galileo (satellite navigation) programme is extremely important for the european union's mastery of advanced technologies. unfortunately, galileo is facing delays and additional costs. when faced with situations, it is essential to think of new solutions. that is why i supported the report by our colleague, mr remek, which aims to examine all possible sources of funding, alongside the contribution from the european budget.
in writing. i was pleased to vote in favour of this report, which shows the culmination of a major political decision, notably on the establishment of galileo. it is absolutely crucial that the autonomous european satellite radio navigation system be put into operation quickly and, as the report emphasizes, with long-term financial guarantees. the competition from the united states (with the global positioning system - gps) requires us to implement galileo quickly in view of the economic, technical, political and strategic challenges.
in writing. the european union has set itself the objective of becoming the world leader in global navigation satellite services (gnss) with the egnos and galileo programmes, thus ensuring its technological independence from the us gps. given the importance of the economic impact of such programmes, i voted in favour of the remek report which calls on the commission and the member states to ensure sufficient funding to ensure that these projects are completed by 2018 and thus establish themselves as a credible challenger to the us system.
in writing. ten years ago, the european union launched two satellite navigation programmes: galileo and egnos. the first will be operational in 2014 and will offer accuracy of less than one meter whereas gps is accurate to several meters. this technological advance will enable european companies to innovate and be at the forefront of the services that geolocation enables. but galileo is also a strategic issue. europe is currently dependent on the gps system, which is american. when galileo is in place, the union will have complete independence and superiority in this area, and everyone will understand the value of applications. the civil and military resources of the member states will be much more efficient. i voted for this resolution of parliament which, while welcoming the technical success, reminds the european commission of the points where the programme can be improved: funding, public awareness, involving our international partners.
in writing. i voted in favour of this excellent report by my colleague garriga polledo because it represents a very good presentation of the budget that the european union will need beyond 2013 to meet the political challenges it will face. if europe is to implement the policies enshrined in the european treaties, including the most recent ones, it is essential that it has the financial means to match these ambitions. i therefore voted in favour of the collection of own resources and the creation of a financial transaction tax to feed the budget of the european union. this necessary increase in the european budget will have to be accompanied by substantial savings through the optimisation of (joint) expenditure! the cap (essential for the food security and independence of our continent) and the eu's regional policy (reinforced by the creation of an intermediate category of regions allowing additional financial support for regions whose gdp per capita is between 75% and 90% of the european average, such as auvergne and limousin) are also given their due place. so this is a real report in the service of the citizens!
in writing. i voted on wednesday 8 june 2011 for an increase in the 2014-2020 budget. we know that the budget is the beginning of every political act. without a budget, there's no plan. the budget for the european union must therefore reflect the eu's growth strategy and ambitions for its citizens. the member states have suggested freezing the eu budget for two reasons. on the one hand, the money comes from the contribution of the states, and on the other hand, with a stable budget for the period 2014-2020, all the major eu projects to restore growth and invest in the future of the continent are put to the test. member states want the eu to play a decisive role in taking risks, but criticize it when it does. i therefore voted with the majority of my colleagues (except the eurosceptics) for a 5% increase in the budget to finance future major projects. we now know that states are incapable of solving the problems of globalisation on their own. the next step will be to provide the eu with a budget based on its own resources so that it is no longer dependent on the 'wrong' will of the states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. the great merit of this report is that it aims to mobilise the union's budgetary resources in a coherent manner and in the service of the europe 2020 strategy, and is therefore the opposite of the narrow vision of most member states. while the latter sum up europe in terms of their contributions, which they want to see reduced, and their financial returns, which they want to see increased, this report argues for strong integrated community policies in terms of both the historical policies and the new competences conferred by the lisbon treaty.

in writing. ladies and gentlemen, at a time when food security is a crucial issue in globalisation, we must preserve our capacity for self-sufficiency. this requires the maintenance of an ambitious common agricultural policy (cap) that can satisfy our most basic need in the long term: food. the cap does, however, need adjustments to better meet the criterion of fairness. the european citizens would not understand that the aid goes mainly to the large farmers: small farmers must also be able to live off their production under decent conditions and be paid fairly for their work. we also need to take better account of natural constraints, such as global warming, mountain areas and water scarcity, in the allocation of aid. the drought that is now raging shows that it is urgent to give our farmers concrete means of coping with water stress within the framework of the cap. i therefore call for a subtle and relevant revision of the cap, which can ensure both our food independence, the vitality of the agricultural sector and the preservation of our landscapes.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, our citizens are questioning the validity of austerity policies which are reducing the scope of their public services and the scope of their social protection. where they do, these policies fail to reduce public debt and unemployment. economists themselves are appalled, as the content - i say the content - of this "governance" package we are discussing today is absurd, because it prohibits fiscal policies from reacting to economic cycles. during the trilogue, the commission representatives themselves admitted to us that they do not rely on any theoretical or econometric model to make rigorous predictions and recommendations. they admit to thinking purely intuitively. in these circumstances, how can we understand that the conservative, liberal and eurosceptic members of this parliament have blindly tried to harden the text proposed by the commission? vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i am not sure if i can respond to all of the members. we would not have time for that, but i will try to provide some insights as regards the points made this evening. i want to, first of all, thank you all for a very substantial and substantive debate which reflects an overall sense of responsibility for europe’s economic future, for growth and stability, and for our citizens’ welfare. i believe we all broadly share the view that balanced and healthy public finances are a necessary condition for sustainable growth and improving employment, which is the goal of the current legislative package. that is why it deserves your support. as many of you have underlined, it is an essential building block in our comprehensive policy response to the current and still ongoing financial and sovereign crisis. why is it so important to adopt this package at the current juncture? because we must be able to show our citizens, economic actors and the international partners that the european union really can in future prevent a fiscal crisis such as the one we have recently experienced, in the case of greece for instance. never again. that is the first building block of this legislative package. that is why we need preventive budgetary surveillance and effective enforcement as proposed in the package and indeed by your rapporteurs and your committee. that is also why we need a genuinely and effectively functioning mechanism to identify and correct macroeconomic imbalances, in order to prevent the kind of crises we have seen, for instance in ireland or the credit boom we have seen in spain. that is why we need the second building block in this package: an effective mechanism to identify and address macroeconomic imbalances.
