in writing. the european parliament adopted a report on food labelling. the report shall include a visible indication on the food of the energy content, as well as the amount of fat, saturated fatty acids, carbohydrates, sugars, proteins and salt. the length of the procedure leading to this text, and the legislative and political battles that surrounded it, make it a mountain that gives birth to a mouse. the european parliament was the subject of intense lobbying at various stages of the vote on this text, particularly on the question of a green, orange and red light system, aimed at making products containing a high dose of salts, sugar or fat visible very quickly. this procedure was rejected by the european parliament at first reading. the adoption of this text today marks the final stage in this procedure, which does not deserve to be called a victory. i abstained on this text which could have gone much further in consumer information and protection.
in writing. while parliament adopted an ambitious position in 2008 to strengthen the cross-border exchange of information on road safety offences, the matter had been blocked in the council for more than two years. the belgian presidency has made progress in changing the legal basis for police cooperation, and i welcome this, even though the council should have been more ambitious. this is a first step which should make it possible to improve road safety by not leaving those who commit offences in a member state other than their own unpunished. i therefore voted in favour of mrs ayala sender's report and i hope that these provisions will come into force quickly.
in writing. i fully support the agreement reached between parliament and the council on the crossborder exchange of information on road safety offences. the agreement is much less ambitious than the commission's initial proposal, but it should nevertheless put an end to the impunity of certain motorists who endanger their lives and the lives of others by committing serious offences. the identity of these drivers can thus be transmitted to the authorities of the state where the offence was committed. i hope that this provision will help to reduce the number of offences and accidents, which are particularly frequent on our roads during the summer holiday season.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text because too many europeans are still dying on our roads every year. it is the leading cause of death worldwide among young people aged 15 to 29. the commission's white paper on european transport policy (2001) set an admirable target of halving the number of road fatalities by 2010, but since 2005 the decline has slowed. one of the problems in the union is that penalties imposed for offences committed in a member state other than the driver's country are often not enforced. this impunity undermines road safety objectives. it was therefore essential to legislate to remove this inconsistency by facilitating the enforcement of sanctions against motorists who committed the most dangerous offences outside their member state.
in writing. ending impunity and inequality of treatment between european citizens for road traffic offences in europe is the aim of this new legislation to which i have voted. it has been shown that when drivers are outside their own country, they are more likely to break traffic laws. this is very damaging in terms of road safety. despite the council's strong resistance, a balanced approach was achieved: while respecting the penalties provided for at national level, it targets eight behaviours identified as risky (speeding, alcohol driving, not wearing a seatbelt, crossing a red light, drugs, not wearing a helmet, driving on a prohibited lane and using mobile phones), some of which cause fatal accidents, which is significant. thanks to its determination, the european parliament has also obtained a strong clause for a further revision of the text to consider moving further in the future towards common road safety rules, which i welcome.
in writing. i voted in favour of the draft directive to set up a system for exchanging information on traffic offences committed by nationals of one member state in the territory of another. until now, there has been no specific coordination of this exchange of information and the infringements and offences committed abroad by european motorists have been largely ignored. road violence cannot stop at the borders of its own state. dangerous behavior is outside of it. from now on, motorists will be held accountable wherever they are, and this in a systematic way. it will be the end of impunity for drivers. however, this system will only apply to the most serious offences and minor contraventions in order to ensure the full effectiveness of the new legislation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the crossborder application of road safety legislation. the amendment of the legal basis for police cooperation will allow for the monitoring of road safety offences such as driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, speeding, not wearing a seat belt, illegal use of mobile phones, failure to observe a red light or using prohibited or bus lanes. in practice, after a letter informing the owner of the vehicle of the offence, the penalty will be that of the country where the offence was committed. if the text is adopted unanimously by the members of the council, it shall enter into force not later than two years after its adoption.
in writing. eu drivers who allow themselves to drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs, to drive too fast, to cross red lights, to use their mobile phones or to take prohibited lanes in another member state will no longer be able to go home with a clear conscience after this report. the proposal for a directive requires the national authorities to exchange the driver's registration data. then, an information letter would be sent to the offender. finally, the possible penalty would be imposed on the offender according to the rules of the country where the offence was committed. however, this cooperation must comply with certain rules on transparency and the protection of the data exchanged so that this information is not misused for other purposes and that the user can rectify or contest it. i welcome the adoption of this report and hope that the council will follow parliament's recommendations to put an end to the impunity of crossborder drivers who often poison road use in border regions.
in writing. i voted in favour of the inès ayala sender report because it is an important step forward for road safety, but also for european citizenship. how can we make drivers in one country understand that they must obey the rules in their own country, when they see foreign license plates that go unpunished? it is above all about equality before the law. although i regret that three member states have refused to participate, it is a first step towards harmonization, and the objective is clearly road safety, since only serious offences can be prosecuted across borders, and not parking for example.
in writing. the fight against road fatalities is a goal shared by all european countries and it is urgent that the eu develops an adequate strategy in this area. how can we explain to the public that free movement guarantees the right to travel freely throughout the community without the infringements of the road traffic code having a cross-border application? i am therefore pleased that our parliament has convinced some of the reluctant member states. however, it is a minimum compromise that has been found at second reading and i would like to see european action that goes beyond a system of information exchange to punish drivers. i therefore naturally supported the introduction of a review clause. the safety of our roads is an imperative which cannot suffer from any economy of means or ambition. it is up to us to ensure that the improvement of road safety is constantly reinforced. i also think it is essential to link our road safety strategy with the need to improve the quality and resilience of our infrastructure. the welfare and safety of european citizens, whether they are drivers or not, is at stake.
in writing. i take advantage of the böge report on the current budgetary programming period to return to the commission's crazy proposals for the next period 2014-2020. with a budget of 1 000 billion euros, an increase of 30%, the latter is in fact doing away with the budgetary efforts it imposes on the states. it proposes to cut back on the common agricultural policy, its black sheep, while prohibiting partial renationalisation, at a time when the problems of food independence and food security are more important than ever. it promotes policies whose functioning and effectiveness are increasingly being called into question by the member states, and even by the court of auditors. this is particularly true of those which are financed by the structural funds. regional policy, with its obligation to co-finance, is an incentive to public spending. it is aimed mainly at a clientele of baronesses and at the destruction of states. finally, there is the very worrying proposal for a 2% vat rate as a new own resource to be used to feed the coffers of brussels. it is not clear whether it will be 2% of the revenue from this tax that will have to be allocated to it, or 2 additional points for its own benefit. in short, an unacceptable one.
in writing. the european parliament is fighting to assert its right to negotiate the european budget. this right should be clearly conferred on it in the treaties, as should the right of legislative initiative. but the eu does not want a european parliament. it prefers this assembly, which approves or rejects the proposals of the commission and the council. i am voting for this report to show my support for this battle, but also my rejection of a budget that serves the liberal eurocracy. i am voting to block an anti-european budget.
in writing. this resolution expresses what the epp, s&d and alde groups expect from the commission in 2012. the commission's request to respect the general interests of the member states and citizens and their competence in the field of wages and pensions can be accepted. the rest is not good. europe 2020 strategy, the energy market, strengthening military capabilities in the service of nato, combating protectionism by third countries and the establishment of the single transatlantic market by 2015 - all is almost done! europe is sick of this majority. i am voting against this text.
in writing. although a majority of meps voted in favour of a very restrictive authorisation of processed animal proteins (animal meal), this is not the case for me: i refused to allow the reintroduction of animal flours. it should be noted that scientists have made considerable progress on the question of the dangers of using animal flour and that it now seems possible for some to define the conditions for the safe use of these animal proteins. however, i felt it necessary to take the time to reflect and study, not to change the rules on animal flour again and thus to uphold the precautionary principle. that is why i voted against this reintroduction. as regards the specific case of france, i would like to recall that the french minister of agriculture has already indicated that animal meal will remain banned in france: 'as long as i am minister of agriculture, animal meal will not be reintroduced in france. i'll make a commitment. there is nothing to prevent a member state from defining a more protective rule than that defined at european level.
in writing. while animal meal is considered to be one of the direct causes of mad cow disease, which is one of the most serious health crises in europe, the european parliament today voted by a majority in favour of partially lifting the ban on animal meal in europe. in an own-initiative report without legislative value, the european parliament favours the lifting of the ban on feeding processed animal proteins to non-ruminants, under certain conditions. like the other members of the modem, i voted against this report. while bse has been virtually eliminated, the extent of the creutzfeldt-jakob disease epidemic is still unknown and there are still too many uncertainties about the health guarantees for animal flour. in addition, other economically and ecologically viable solutions exist, including the development of plant protein crops. do we want to align ourselves with practices that have proved to be dangerous in the past, or do we want to defend common sense and a european agricultural model that guarantees the safety of consumers and the preservation of their health? i therefore voted against this report to reiterate that there is no need to compromise on food and health protection.
in writing. while animal meal is considered to be one of the direct causes of mad cow disease, which is causing one of the most serious health crises in europe, parliament voted in favour of partially lifting the ban on animal meal in europe. the commission, no doubt under pressure from industry, but also the french national food council, have dared to assert that the risks are now "negligible"; they believe that a change in practice would be sufficient to reduce them. while bse has been virtually eliminated, we still do not know the extent of the creutzfeldt-jakob disease epidemic we may be facing, as the disease may take decades to manifest. there are still too many uncertainties about health guarantees. there are other economically and ecologically viable solutions. the development of plant protein crops is a more virtuous path. do we want to follow practices which have proved to be dangerous in the past, or do we want to defend common sense and a european agricultural model which guarantees consumer safety? we therefore voted against it to reaffirm that there is no compromise on food and health protection.

in writing. the number of cases of mad cow disease (bse) and other communicable diseases such as scrapie (std) has decreased significantly in recent years, which is evidence that the measures taken by the union to eradicate these diseases have been effective. but this downward trend must not lead to a relaxation of these surveillance measures! that is why i voted against this report which calls for the lifting of the ban on animal meal under certain conditions for feeding non-ruminants and in particular poultry, pigs and fish. there is a real concern in society about this and a lifting of the ban on feeding processed animal protein to non-ruminants, even under conditions, does not seem to me justified or free of health risks such as cross-contamination in mixed farms or in slaughterhouses.
in writing. i voted against the european commission's proposal on transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (tses) which proposes to relax the ban on animal flours. for reasons of food safety, i think it is important to oppose the lifting of the ban, even under certain conditions, on animal meal for feeding non-ruminants, and in particular poultry, pigs and fish. although cases of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (bse) such as creutzfeldt-jakob disease are declining in europe, the context of the e. coli crisis reminds us of the importance of maintaining a high level of animal and public health.
in writing. the european commission wants to lift the ban on feeding processed animal protein to non-ruminants, subject to conditions! the number of mad cow diseases and other diseases (such as tse) has decreased considerably, but this is due to the eradication measures adopted by the union. this reduction should not lead to a relaxation of such measures. i therefore voted against this proposal. we must have a long-term view and promote a genuine policy for the development of plant protein production. the ban on animal meal is out of the question!
in writing. the european parliament voted to lift the ban on animal meal and to allow its use for non-herbivores, i.e. poultry, fish and pigs. i voted against this authorisation. the european parliament is constantly bragging about the importance of traceability in the food sector, but it also admits that there is no guarantee at present of a clear separation of products derived from animal flour from the rest, either at the time of slaughter or transport. in this text, the european parliament is giving in to lobbying pressure, to the detriment of public health. i object to this vote. the argument put forward in this resolution that there is a protein deficit in europe seems to me to be far from justifying such a risk. we can see that, in the face of pressure from the lobbies, the majority of the european parliament is denying the precautionary principle and is not afraid to take risks for public health, with the only counterpart being a request to the commission to improve traceability.
in writing. like the french socialist delegation, i voted against the roth-berendt report on eu legislation on transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (tses) and related controls of feed and food. how can we explain that 15 years after the mad cow crisis began, we are pretending that nothing has happened and are considering putting animal meal for ruminants back on the market, even with strict controls? the current crisis in the livestock sector, linked in particular to the rise in world cereal prices, must be solved by economic and trade regulations and by a fight against speculation, certainly not at the expense of health security!
in writing. despite our opposition for years, security scanners are now a reality. security scanners must not compromise our civil liberties and our health. their use must therefore be governed by common european rules to ensure discretion and be subject to clear and strict conditions. member states will have to use technology which is as harmless as possible to people's health and which respects privacy. the images generated should be stick figure silhouettes and the data should be destroyed immediately after the security check on the person. the european commission is expected to present new european rules this summer. parliament may reject them within three months if it wishes to do so by the comitology procedure. the european commission should not therefore regard this vote as a blank cheque, but as a warning, a red line indicating what is acceptable to parliament and the citizens of the european union.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by parliament of the report by luis de grandes pascual proposing to allow the use of body scanners in european airports provided that standards concerning the health and privacy of passengers are respected. security scanners are more effective in terms of security (detecting non-metallic objects such as plastic explosives or ceramic knives), and less intrusive to passengers, as they avoid full body searches, and do not take longer than the time required for hand luggage inspection (3-30 seconds depending on the type of scanner). the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'commercial vehicle' to cover vehicles with a maximum mass of less than 100 kg.
in writing. i voted against the report by mr de grandes pascual. in the face of the 'civilization war' initiated by mr bush and the continuing terrorist risks, air safety is a real concern. but the organization of the system, and in particular the control of passengers, is the responsibility of the member states, not the commission, because it is a matter of public order and public security. it is also for each member state to decide on the use of body scanners at airports, taking due account of the health and privacy concerns raised by such use. as for the systematic call for non-discrimination, the refusal of profiling, we must remind those same members who approve of the occupation of afghanistan by western armies - which proves that they have a vague idea of where the danger may come from - that it is highly unlikely that a lutheran swede wearing explosive tennis shoes will ever be arrested on an airplane.
in writing. while remaining sceptical about the real effectiveness of the use of body scanners in the fight against terrorism, i supported this report, as it includes a ban on x-ray scanners, in order to avoid any harm to the health of passengers, especially vulnerable passengers (pregnant women, elderly, children, sick people, etc.). in addition, several elements of this report address my concerns about respect for human dignity and privacy, since passengers will be able to refuse the body scan and submit to other more conventional inspection procedures, such as the body search. in addition, only "match-maker" silhouettes should be used, images which will be destroyed immediately after the inspection and which, therefore, cannot be stored. however, the question of 'who will pay the bill' in this case remains. the cost-effectiveness of such a measure will have to be seriously considered in the course of this process, particularly in a context of economic crisis where everyone is called upon to make an effort.
in writing. while security scanners or body scanners are undoubtedly a step forward in aviation safety in that they detect prohibited objects hidden under clothing, their introduction should not be done without extreme caution. on the one hand, the health of the public must be protected, which is why i support the ban on monitoring technologies using ionising radiation. on the other hand, the dignity, privacy and intimacy of individuals must be protected. thus, allowing only matchstick figures, destroying data and having the possibility to refuse to submit to such a check are essential conditions for adding security scanners to the list of permitted inspection methods. the use of these scanners must be harmonised and subject to common protective rules ensuring respect for fundamental rights in each state that would choose to implement this system. regular updating of standards will be necessary to take account of new risks, technological advances and their possible negative impacts. in addition, i believe it is particularly important to lift the ban on the transport of liquids, aerosols and gels in 2013 and to move to a system of inspection of these substances.
in writing. i voted against this report because the use of this monitoring device, which is akin to a full body search, infringes both the privacy and intimacy of individuals. it is true that semantic precautions are taken to make the use of the body scanner at airports, the so-called 'security scanner', admissible. its use is surrounded by "guarantees" of privacy and data protection (possibility of not submitting to them and going through a means of control right of option , remote location for viewing images, limitation of data storage, etc.). as always with the use of technologies that involve data protection and privacy, questions of purpose and proportionality arise. the reduction of the terrorist threat requires the resolution of the political causes of terrorism and the strengthening of the human resources allocated to the services concerned, victims as well as others, despite the optical effects of austerity policies. the proliferation of ever more sophisticated technological means is quite illusory. it only masks, by a leap forward, the failures of the fight against terrorism and the exploitation of it for 'political' purposes.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to start by thanking you all for giving me the opportunity to make a statement on behalf of the commission on the european scheme for food distribution to the most deprived persons. first, i would like to emphasise the importance of this programme for the most deprived citizens of europe. i can mention two figures here. each year more than 18 million people receive more than 440 000 tonnes of food distributed under this programme. over the years this programme has become one of the main sources of supply to charities working in the field of food aid. more than half the products distributed by the members of the european federation of food banks in 2010 originated from this programme. so it is really important. last april the general court set aside the provisions of the 2009 plan for products purchased in the market. specifically, the court ruled that the commission cannot define the volume of the programme independently of the volume of existing stocks. the total volume of the plan must also be adapted to the volume of the existing stocks when the plan is drawn up. the proportion of products purchased in the market in relation to the total volume of the plan must reflect their exceptional nature. following the court’s judgment and given the limited volume of intervention stocks available, the 2012 plan had to be greatly reduced. the commission has recently adopted the 2012 plan in order to give the participating member states and charities time to find additional resources to replace the volume that will not be provided at european level. as regards the future, the commission made various initial proposals in 2008, followed by an amended proposal in september 2010. the express aim of these proposals was to make the scheme sustainable as intervention stocks become increasingly scarce. this subject was thoroughly discussed in the committee on agriculture and rural development of this parliament and in the plenary on the basis of the report prepared by mr siekierksi. the commission has always appreciated the clear stance of parliament on this matter. however, a sufficient majority has not yet been obtained in the council. but the commission is firmly committed to the continuation of the scheme in the future and is ready to make any adjustments. against this background, in its recently released communication for a multiannual budget for the period 2014-2020, the commission has proposed a budget of eur 2.8 billion at current prices. considering the important contribution that the programme makes to meeting the poverty reduction target of the europe 2020 strategy, it will in future be financed from the budget for social policies. the necessary legal proposals will come in due course. in the meantime, the commission recalls that an agreement on the basis of its 2010 proposal is needed with a view to securing a food distribution plan in 2013. i am confident that this package will help an agreement between the council and parliament to be reached, so as to ensure legal certainty and stable financing for the scheme. for this compromise we need strong support from this body.

in writing. i voted against the european parliament resolution on the schengen area because it is against the idea that, in the event of a massive influx of migrants, a state can re-establish controls at its national borders and thus protect itself more effectively against illegal immigration. the position i have defended is shared by all the heads of state and government of the 27 member states of the european union, from the right and the left, who at the last european council wanted to broaden the criteria for reintroducing this type of controls at internal borders. of course, free movement remains the principle of common law, and restrictions the exception.
in writing. schengen is a failure. the european citizens were promised that the dismantling of internal border controls in the union would go hand in hand with a strengthening of external border controls and the maintenance of a high level of security. the reality? europe is a sieve. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new rules. the widespread political laxity in the management of migration flows in general and of alleged asylum seekers in particular. this laxity is now being fuelled by european laws drawn up by brussels, which firmly believes that the massive import of non-european immigrants will solve our economic and social problems, and even demographic ones! every state has the right, indeed the duty, to control its borders, to control the goods and the men who cross them. what the recent, still ongoing crisis in lampedusa has shown is that the absence of internal border controls is a powerful incentive for illegal immigration applicants to rush to any easily accessible point in europe. they know that afterwards, it'll be easy for them to play by our rules and that lack of control to go where they want. the reform of the safeguard clause in the schengen agreement is not what we need to do. it's the abolishment of this agreement!
in writing. i did not support the resolution on the schengen area because i do not think it is appropriate to have a resolution which would reject in principle any extension of the criteria for establishing internal border controls and which would thus go against the conclusions of the european council and against the commission's proposals. if we limit ourselves to the criteria of 'public order and public security' that exist today, states will continue to act unilaterally by interpreting these criteria broadly in the event of strong migratory pressures and, in doing so, we risk pushing for the equation of immigration and insecurity when it is necessary to react to migratory pressures. the proposed mechanism is intended to create a mechanism for the reintroduction of border controls as an exceptional last resort and within the framework of a european mechanism. today we need to strengthen the governance of the schengen area. the purpose of this initiative is precisely to be able to respond to the current crisis situation in the schengen area, linked in particular to the fact that some member states are no longer able to ensure compliance with their obligations under the schengen acquis concerning the effective control of their external border section.
in writing. i have decided to vote against the joint resolution on the schengen area. we need to strengthen the political governance of the schengen area, develop a genuine european immigration and asylum policy and develop the role of frontex. the aim is not to undermine freedom of movement within the schengen area, but to adapt the agreement to the realities of migration. the content of this resolution does not seem to me to be appropriate, because it rejects in principle any extension of the criteria for the temporary and exceptional reintroduction of internal border controls. this resolution goes against the conclusions of the european council and the proposals recently made by the commission, which appear to be balanced and realistic. it is important to review the current criteria of 'public policy and public security', which are not appropriate to the current situation and leave too much room for interpretation to the states, especially in the case of strong migratory pressures, with the risk of equating immigration and insecurity. i therefore believe that the creation of a european mechanism to allow the reintroduction of border controls in an exceptional way is highly desirable and would make up for the shortcomings of some states in controlling their external borders in the event of strong migratory pressures.
in writing. this text sends a negative signal to the attempts of presidents sarkozy and berlusconi to exploit the arrival of refugees at europe's borders for the benefit of a security and xenophobic policy. no, there is no need to introduce a temporary reintroduction of frontiers clause in the schengen agreements. that possibility is already provided for. no, there is no need to strengthen the capacity of frontex. she's already done enough damage. but this text is weak on the latter point and promises sanctions for those who do not comply with the dictates of fortress europe. i'm not going to do it for these reasons. i support the call against the unjustified reintroduction of internal frontiers.
in writing. the european programme for aid to the most deprived (pead) (which is part of the cap) is helping 13 million people in need by allocating €500 million in european aid to 240 food banks, including secours populaire, restos du cœur and the red cross. almost 25 years after the launch of this initiative, germany has lodged a complaint against this mechanism which allows the financing of social aid not through the budget of a social policy but through the budget of the agricultural policy. the mechanism was found to be illegal and the european commission was forced to announce that it was being challenged. to prevent this eur 500 million aid from being reduced to eur 100 million this winter, my colleagues and i have asked the european commission and the member states to provide a transitional mechanism in the short term and to change the legislation in the medium term to allow this programme to continue (i personally propose involving the esf). we will continue to fight for this because we cannot leave 13 million europeans on the side of the road!
in writing. the european commission's decision to drastically reduce the programme of aid to the most deprived (pead) has caused an outcry among the beneficiary associations and a feeling of incomprehension among citizens more generally. it is true that this is a legal problem, but following a decision by the court of justice, the commission had no other choice. but the question of the sustainability of this fund has been raised for several years. the commission should have already found solutions to avoid this extreme situation, since the matter was blocked in the council. by adopting today by a very large majority this resolution on the future of the pead, we reaffirm our support for the programme, which we believe should retain a budget of around eur 500 million per year, and for the commission in its search for a solution. it must, on the new legal basis, formulate a proposal as soon as possible but also quickly find a transitional solution to enable associations on the ground to continue to play a key role in the fight against poverty and social exclusion.
in writing. i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the european food aid programme for the most deprived (pead), because i am concerned about the future of this programme following a decision by the european court of justice which called into question its financing mechanism. this decision implies a drastic reduction in the programme's budget, from an average of €500 million per year to €113 million for 2012. this is unacceptable when the pead benefits over 13 million europeans and supports the activities of the vast majority of european charities. i therefore fully support this resolution which calls on the commission to find a rapid solution to the lack of funding for this programme which is essential in the fight against poverty in europe.

in writing. in europe, almost one in ten people (43 million) is at risk of food poverty, according to estimates by the european commission. europe is helping them through the european programme of food aid for the poor, and i am very attached to this arrangement. following a ruling by the court of justice of the european union that only the supply of food from intervention stocks is covered by the programme, as opposed to expenditure generated by the purchase of food on the market, the commission is planning a drastic reduction in funding: from eur 500 million in 2011 to eur 113 million in 2012. it seems inconceivable to me that the european programme of food aid to the poor should suffer a sharp reduction in the funds available to it, especially when this is due to a problem of legal basis. i hope that a solution will be found as soon as possible, and i of course support this resolution which demands that a solution be found, whatever legal arrangements allow it!

on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, i too would like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur on the results he has achieved - not without difficulty - in a particularly delicate and difficult matter in negotiations with the member states. it is obvious that there are a number of positive points which can be described as some progress, although i do not hide from you that my group and i would have liked to have been able to go a little further in this reform. we have thus succeeded in making the agency more concerned about respect for fundamental rights in the context of its missions. this seems obvious but it had to be clearly formalised. a specialised officer will therefore have access to all information relating to fundamental rights and will perform his duties independently. the agency will have to assist member states in humanitarian emergencies and rescue at sea, and we have seen how important this has been in recent months. operations will be suspended in case of violation of fundamental rights. agreements concluded by frontex with third countries will have to meet european standards on fundamental rights. the principle of non-refoulement of migrants will be respected in all circumstances. this is all going in the right direction. the new regulation also aims to make frontex more operational. to this end, member states will have to make a firm commitment to make staff and resources available to the agency. third, a notable step forward: frontex will be subject to increased democratic transparency, which will involve the european parliament very directly, although in this area future developments - i hope - of this regulation will have to increase the right of scrutiny of parliamentarians. three themes, three types of progress that sound like obvious ones but that have been, nevertheless, very complicated to obtain. two final thoughts to finish. frontex is and must continue to be seen for what it is, that is, a tool for the european union's strategy on external border surveillance. frontex is not the perfect alibi or the backstop for member states to use for their own migration policy, which will continue in my view and we will have to work on this to ask a number of questions about the respective responsibilities. on the other hand, in the midst of the debate on schengen, we must all bear in mind that european migration policy has many more challenges to face than frontex in the areas of, for example, integration or resettlement, or access to fair and equitable protection. we want the union, in all its components, to show the same political will on these issues too. i believe that we can thus speak of progress in the area of a europe of asylum and migration.

in writing. i voted in favour of the revision of the frontex agency's regulations, as it was essential to clarify its role and responsibilities while ensuring that it acts in a way that respects the fundamental rights of migrants. the need for this revision became all the more evident in the context of the arab revolutions and the subsequent migratory movements. i therefore welcome several of the proposed amendments, such as the establishment of an advisory forum, which will exercise greater control over frontex's activities, and the obligation for the agency to provide rescue at sea in humanitarian emergencies, or else it will be suspended. the possibility for the agency to be independent of the member states, acquiring its own equipment, and the increased information to be provided to parliament are changes which will help to clarify the relationship between the frontex tool and political decisions. one aspect which has particularly attracted my attention is the creation, through this regulation, of the status of european border guards. this development, which is for the moment only terminological, is a novelty which will hopefully have repercussions on other professions requiring the same coordination, such as the coastguards of the various member states, for example.
in writing. the agency, which is responsible for securing the external borders of the schengen area, where citizens from 25 countries, including 22 eu members, can move freely, has often been criticised for its lack of resources. it has to monitor some 42 672 kilometres of external maritime borders and 8 826 kilometres of land borders. the european parliament adopted new rules on frontex this week by 431 votes to 49, with 48 abstentions. this is the most important reform of the law that established frontex in 2004. our evaluation of the first six years of the agency's activities shows that it needs to be strengthened and made more effective. the agency will now buy or lease its own equipment, such as vehicles or helicopters, and will no longer be dependent on the member states' powers. the staff designated by the member states will thus feed the european border guard teams. the current 'joint support teams' and 'rapid border intervention teams' will be merged under the name 'european border guards'. the agency's budget was increased from eur 6 million to eur 88 million between 2005 and 2011.
