in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr simon busuttil, on the proposal for a regulation to strengthen the role of the european agency frontex in the european union's external border surveillance system. this revision will provide the agency with more financial and human resources to meet the tasks assigned to it. in particular, the agency will be able to buy or lease its own equipment, such as vehicles or helicopters, and will no longer be dependent on the member states' allocations as before. a union border guard system will also be set up, forming a reserve of national guards from which the agency will be able to draw for its various border surveillance missions from the end of 2011. the revision of the frontex regulation will improve the support of this european agency to the member states in the management of the union's external borders: as migratory pressures intensify at the eu's borders, it is imperative to strengthen the role of frontex. this was an objective of the european pact on immigration and asylum, adopted in 2008 under the french presidency of the european union.
in writing. this report endorses the empowerment of the frontex agency and the possibility for it to send its patrols to fight against illegal immigration even in third countries. a lot of it! it is not with a consultative forum that the logic of "everything is safe" will be overturned, which is here endorsed and amplified. without me. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the amendment of the frontex regulation, the eu external border management agency created in 2004. objective: to define better the mandate of the agency and to make it more efficient. how did you do that ? first, by addressing a recurring problem: frontex's over-reliance on member states for the deployment of staff and equipment. the agency will now have the means to acquire or lease its own equipment, and member states will be required to respect their commitments to provide national border guards. the question is the actual creation of a european system of union border guards, from which the agency will be able to draw for all its operations. secondly, by reducing the time taken for deploying rapid border intervention missions, so that we can really deal with emergency situations. finally, and this is essential, by strengthening the provisions relating to the respect and defence of fundamental rights by frontex in all its areas of competence. this is one of the main victories of parliament in this text, which we hope will soon have direct and tangible implications on the difficult terrain of the areas on the external borders of the union.
in writing. i wanted to support this text, which enshrines my political family's vision of the principle of integrated management of our external borders. if freedom of movement is one of the greatest achievements of the community, it must be accompanied by a high and uniform level of surveillance and control of the union's borders. recent events have demonstrated the need to revise the rules for the operation of frontex, in order to be able to deal with either a failure of a state to control its borders or exceptional circumstances. sharing an internal market and an area of freedom, security and justice requires, in my view, common rules. the sustainability of the schengen area is therefore closely linked to the success of frontex missions. if the external borders of the union become porous, each state is liable to be exposed to threats. any state which considers that its fundamental interests or security are threatened would therefore be entitled to take measures to ensure public order within its territory. in this area, european solidarity must be exemplary.
in writing. far from being a myth of a galloping bureaucracy, the european union regularly reviews european legislation to remove outdated texts and thus ensure that the applicable law is more easily readable. i believe that this approach is essential for citizens and businesses alike, and that is why i supported this report.
in writing. the priority given by local authorities to large structural local development projects raises the question of taking into account their impact on the environment. this is all the more so when these projects are carried out through public-private partnerships, either because of their technical complexity or because of the scarcity of public funds that can be devoted to them. i therefore welcome the fact that our parliament has taken up this matter and reaffirms the polluter pays principle on this occasion. i believe that there can no longer be any compromise when it comes to protecting our environment, our quality of life or our health. some of these projects are likely to have a real impact on people, biodiversity and our living environment, and it is up to us to ensure that the precautionary principle prevails and to establish a system of adequate liability and compensation. i believe that this approach must be applied from design to implementation, with public consultation and consideration of the risks, alternatives and ways of eliminating all risks to the environment and the population.
in writing. the galileo programme is a european initiative to develop a world-wide state-of-the-art satellite navigation system, providing a highly reliable and accurate global positioning service under civilian control. the public regulated service (prs) is one of the three initial services that galileo could start offering from 2014. it is reserved exclusively for governments and authorised users; it will provide high-level continuity of service, coupled with very robust encrypted signals for certain sensitive applications. the use of the prs should protect critical infrastructures that depend on satellite navigation and could be used in a crisis situation. i supported this proposal, which lays down the rules for prs-only access and sets up a framework for the proper implementation of these access arrangements. i consider galileo to be one of the symbolic projects of european construction, and i hope that the initial difficulties of launching it are now behind us.
in writing. i supported this proposal for the galileo programme because, following this vote, operators authorised by the governments of the member states will be able to use the data from the satellite navigation system from 2014 onwards to carry out emergency, defence and security services. we can welcome the strengthening of the independence of european governments from the american gps system. the european space policy is essential to ensure europe's strong position on the international stage. the european union should therefore strengthen its commitment in this area, in particular by providing european funding for flagship programmes such as the gmes earth observation programme.
in writing. as from 2014, the future satellite navigation system galileo will offer several services, including the public regulated service (prs). this will consist of a highly secure gps signal reserved for certain users. the prs will be used for the identification of critical infrastructure and all types of traffic, including police operations, border controls and civil protection operations. it will thus be a channel for the transmission of highly strategic information for the internal and external security of the member states. it is therefore essential to define, before its implementation, the rules on how it is to be used. in its report, parliament provides in particular that member states, the council, the commission and the european external action service will have unlimited access to the prs in all parts of the world, while third countries, european agencies and international organisations will only be able to access it if they have been duly authorised. the report also provides that each member state will designate a prs authority responsible for the management and supervision of all authorised users. i'm glad he was adopted.
in writing. i voted in favour of the conclusion of this international agreement on tropical timber, as it will make it possible to strengthen the fight against the illegal trade in certain timber. by limiting the profits from this trade, the european union will help to reduce deforestation in tropical areas and thus protect biodiversity and the climate. however, 20% of producers and importers of tropical wood products are not involved in this agreement, so the work started should be continued to ensure real protection of tropical forests.
in writing. i voted in favour of approving this agreement in plenary as it is in line with the measures already taken by the european union in this area, in particular the flegt agreements (action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade). this agreement, although less binding than the bilateral flegt agreements, has the advantage of binding a larger number of tropical fruit producing countries (60 in total, including 33 developing countries), thus allowing the development of the principles of sustainable management and restoration of degraded forest areas on a larger scale. in addition, in 2008 parliament had expressly asked the european commission to give its approval to the agreement, and not simply to be consulted, as it had originally planned. this change in procedure entails additional obligations for the commission, which will have to inform parliament clearly and without delay of the application of the agreement, including its renegotiation. parliament will be able to check the consistency of the actions undertaken at multilateral level, via this agreement, and bilaterally, via the flegt partnership agreements.
in writing. the new agreement with switzerland aims to amend the previous ec-switzerland bilateral agreement on geographical indications for agricultural products. the european union and the swiss confederation aim at the mutual recognition of protected designations of origin (pdos) and protected geographical indications (pgi) in order to improve the conditions of bilateral trade, promote quality in the food chain and preserve the value of sustainable rural development. the proposal under consideration is the result of bilateral negotiations, which took place between october 2007 and december 2009. it provides for the reciprocal protection of protected designations of origin and geographical indications in the respective parties. i fully support this agreement.
in writing. as a member of the european economic area (eea), norway benefits from the internal market, but agriculture and fisheries are excluded from free movement in the 1992 eea agreement. instead, it provides for a gradual liberalisation of agricultural production through reviews of the terms of trade in agricultural products every two years. from march 2008 to january 2010, further negotiations were held to conclude this draft agreement, which contains further concessions from norway to the eu and vice versa. i support this agreement.
in writing. this report concerns the extension to the principality of liechtenstein of the agreement between the european community and the swiss confederation on trade in agricultural products. so the protection of geographical indications will also apply to liechtenstein, which i support.
in writing. in 2009, in auckland, new zealand, the convention on the conservation and management of high seas fishery resources in the south pacific was adopted and opened for signature for a period of 12 months from 1 february 2010. the european union signed it on 26 july 2010. the aim is to ensure the long-term conservation and sustainable exploitation of fisheries resources in the south pacific. it is regrettable that the majority of states are still reluctant to accept the implementation of management measures in their waters which are in accordance with international law. it is absolutely disheartening to find an example of this resistance in countries that are supposed to be or seek to be seen as champions of good fishing practice, such as australia, new zealand or chile, which are the origin of the creation of this new convention. i support our rapporteur who believes that the union must be present in all regional conventions, both to defend its priorities in terms of sustainable fisheries management and to defend the interests of its fishing fleet. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the presence of european vessels in the south pacific obliges the european union, under the united nations convention on the law of the sea, to cooperate with other parties concerned with the management and conservation of fisheries resources in the region. the commission has therefore negotiated a regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) agreement in the south pacific for fisheries resources not yet covered by an existing rfmo. the objective of this convention is to ensure the long-term conservation and sustainable exploitation of resources in the south pacific. the european union must be present in all the rfmos, both to ensure sustainable fisheries management and to defend the interests of its fishing fleet. a presence in rfmos also allows the union to provide the necessary counterweight to ensure that there is no possibility of undermining efforts to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. this report concerns the conclusion of an agreement between the european union and brazil on civil aviation security. the agreement was signed on behalf of the european union on 14 july 2010 and is not being applied provisionally. the enhanced role of the parliament under the lisbon treaty goes hand in hand with the responsibility to monitor more closely the conduct of the negotiations. in this respect, union and brazilian companies should benefit significantly from the application of the agreement through faster and simpler product authorisation procedures, and thus cheaper, and through mutual acceptance of certification results. in addition, the agreement constitutes a net benefit for the european union, as it will establish the mutual acceptance of certification findings in all areas of airworthiness for all member states. i am therefore our rapporteur and i propose that we approve this agreement.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement signed between the european union and brazil because it is important to harmonise standards and processes relating to civil aviation safety. this should enhance aircraft safety and benefit companies in both our territories, which will be spared the long and costly procedures of inspection, evaluation and technical testing.
in writing. this report concerns the agreement between the european union and norway on the surrender procedure between the member states of the european union and iceland and norway. the aim is to improve the procedure for surrender for the purpose of prosecution or the execution of sentences by making it compulsory to base the surrender on a warrant of arrest. a warrant of arrest may be issued for offences punishable by the law of the issuing state by a custodial sentence of a maximum of at least 12 months or, where a sentence has been imposed or a custodial sentence has been imposed, for sentences of at least four months. our rapporteur proposes that we support this agreement, and i support it insofar as it is a question of extending to the kingdom of norway and the republic of iceland, at the request of those two countries, the provisions which already exist among the member states of the european union.
in writing. this own-initiative report follows the commission's green paper on audit policy in the context of the financial crisis. the commission is examining the possibilities of strengthening audit to help improve financial stability. the last two decades have seen the concentration of the major audit firms, leading to the 'big four' today. the report calls on the commission to ensure that the conditions of competition in the audit market guarantee market access for small companies. it advocates a clear line of demarcation between audit services and services other than audit that an audit firm provides to a client, in order to avoid conflicts of interest. i support these guidelines and have voted in favour of the report, and we are now awaiting the commission's legislative proposal.
in writing. the european union is clearly not learning from the crisis. it has already given a european passport to the rating agencies, and now it is giving a european passport to the audit firms. the operation of these private workshops has proved to be completely ineffective. a credible audit is a public audit carried out according to standards developed by elected officials. a joint audit, carried out by two different bodies, is a guarantee of reliability. that should be the rule in europe.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which begins by recalling that europe has the highest proportion of elderly women in the world. however, older women face discrimination in the labour market related to gender and age, combined with a higher vulnerability due to women-specific career paths: the employment rate for women aged 55-64 in the eu was 37.8% in 2009, compared to 54.8% for men. women are four times more likely than men to work parttime in this age group: 38% compared to 11%. to address these problems, the report calls on the member states to apply the principle of equality between men and women in pension reform and to encourage the use of the same calculation of pensions on an actuarial basis for men and women. it called on the member states to promote initiatives to improve the use of new technologies by older women, so that they can better manage their independence, and to integrate older women into lifelong learning actions.
in writing. in the european union, the elderly population is increasing every year and the risk of poverty for women approaching retirement age is increasing. in addition, the employment rate and the wage of women over 55 are much lower than those of men of the same age. i therefore supported this own-initiative report because it calls on the member states and the commission to improve the situation of older women and to take the necessary measures to complete their legislation, in particular by implementing the principle of equal pay for equal work, but also, in the field of pensions, by not penalising them in the acquisition of their pension rights. the report also suggests tackling age discrimination, taking into account the most vulnerable groups of women, ensuring that women age with dignity and closing the digital gap that isolates this population. other measures are also proposed to improve the provision of quality care services and to take into account the needs of families who have to take care of dependent persons.
in writing. i voted for the report on the situation of women nearing retirement. the situation of women over 50 in europe is a cause for concern. because of their age and gender, women are in more vulnerable situations and have a harder time finding work. they are much more affected by precarious employment, parttime work and isolation. the report promotes equality between men and women, particularly in terms of pay and pension calculation. it stresses the need to take account of women over 50 in european policies. it makes many relevant proposals, such as extending parental leave to those who care for their parents, or training policies for older women. the report does not merely make enlightening recommendations, but also draws attention to the problems affecting women over 50. for example, it is essential to bear in mind all the forms of violence faced by older women which are often underestimated.
in writing. under the guise of fighting discrimination and violence, the aim is to oblige all european women to work until the age of 64, with precarious contracts if necessary. in addition, the pension system is being funded through capital injections and the abandonment of services for the elderly to ngos. i am voting against this text.
in writing. the situation of older women is a matter of concern from a socioeconomic point of view. indeed, major inequalities between men and women persist in many areas, strongly affecting employment and, therefore, pensions and, therefore, women's incomes. this situation is all the more worrying in view of the ageing of the population we are experiencing in europe: it is estimated that the rate of informal carers for the elderly is now 80%; it is therefore often these women who, in an already unfavourable labour market, have to leave their jobs partially or completely to help their dependent relatives. the percentage of this unpaid work is likely to increase very strongly in proportion to the ageing of the european population, affecting the pensions of these older women. the european union must take measures to promote their family and professional balance in order to reduce their risk of poverty. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, including the establishment of a european centre for the development of vocational training.
in writing. this is an own-initiative report on the details of the application in the member states of the 2008 directive on certain aspects of mediation in civil and commercial matters, which is to be applied by the member states by 21 may 2011. the rapporteur welcomes the efforts made by the member states to implement the directive and considers it important to examine the way in which this legislative act is implemented by the member states in order to hear the opinions of practitioners and users of mediation and to identify needs and ways of improving it. the rapporteur concludes that member states are, on the whole, well committed to implementing the directive and that, although they use different regulatory approaches and some have complained of slight delays, the fact remains that most member states not only meet, but even go beyond, the requirements of the directive. i supported that report.
in writing. in may 2008, the european union adopted a directive on mediation on construction sites since 2004. its purpose is to promote the amicable settlement of disputes and to ensure a satisfactory link between mediation and judicial proceedings. it is clear that well-designed mediation procedures are an alternative, cheaper and quicker form of justice, with the added advantage of preserving the relationship that existed before the conflict began. this report, which i supported, examines in detail how the member states have transposed the main provisions of this legislative act. it shows that while there are varied regulatory approaches and there are some slight delays, most member states are not only meeting the requirements of the directive but are going beyond them, which i welcome. in view of the publication of the legislative proposal on alternative dispute resolution this year, and the commission's communication on the application of the mediation directive in 2013, this in-depth review was necessary in many respects. it also allowed us to hear from practitioners and users of mediation and to identify ways of improving it.
in writing. i supported this text because it allows council regulation (ec) no 378/2007 to be adapted to the new legal provisions resulting from the treaty of lisbon, which entered into force on 1 december 2009.
in writing. most industrialized countries, including all eu member states and most emerging countries, have at least one publicly supported export credit institution. together, export credit agencies represent the largest source of public financing for private sector projects worldwide. this report is the result of an agreement reached with the council. it aims to ensure greater transparency, in particular through the submission of an annual activity report by the member states. i supported this report when i voted to allow these guidelines to be applied.
in writing. the few advances made in the previous vote are downplayed or even eliminated in the compromise amendment adopted by the committee on international trade. exits the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in line with the ipcc recommendations. exits the assessment of the social and environmental consequences of projects financed or insured by the states. the same logic applies to exports and free and undistorted competition. the relocation of the economy, which is necessary for the survival of our ecosystem and food sovereignty, is far away. i vote against it.
in writing. public export credit agencies are a key source of financing for european enterprises, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, and are an important factor in supporting their development abroad. the guarantees that these public bodies provide in the event of customer defaults or non-repayment of loans would not, in most cases, be provided by private banks. i supported this report because it adds to the oecd arrangement, which has hitherto been the reference framework, transparency requirements for financial statements and activities financed by these bodies. these additional obligations, which take effect this year, are welcome in the current context of the financial crisis. they are useful to complement the monitoring already carried out by the member states and will enable the european commission to verify the consistency of national policies in support of enterprises. finally, the new transparency provisions will ensure a fairer playing field.
in writing. as raw materials are essential for the growth of our economies, the question of the conditions under which they are used is of great importance for our developed economies. i supported this resolution because it offers a balanced approach and solutions to the economic (access to resources) and ecological (recycling) challenges of this issue.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr bütikofer on an effective raw materials strategy for europe. this report emphasises resource efficiency, recycling and substitution. it also stresses the importance of a fair and sustainable supply of raw materials to the european union. however, i do not think that a mineral resource tax is an appropriate instrument for increasing resource efficiency.
in writing. i voted in favour of this 'effective raw materials strategy for europe' as it is essential to ensure the european supply of strategic and critical raw materials in a fair and sustainable way. this strategy should enable the european union to regulate the derivatives markets for raw materials by strengthening cooperation between member states.
in writing. i did not vote in favour of this report for the following reasons: i share the view that the european union must have a real strategy for raw materials because the current situation is not sustainable. but the reason is not the eu's difficult access to resources. on the contrary, i would have liked the report to have focused on other issues: the effect of extraction on the environment and global warming, its consequences for local populations and the conflicts that can result. as we can see from this report, there are many solutions. however, i do not agree with all of them and consider that for others they should be prioritized. first, european companies do not have a right of access per se to resources outside the eu. secondly, consideration should be given to the possibility of a mineral resource tax to shift the comparative advantage of extraction to recycling. thirdly, we must respect the sovereignty of countries in their choice of export policy. i think the wto does not have to intervene to prevent these trade restrictions. finally, i would have liked to see more of this text on agricultural raw materials, which also deserve protection against speculation and over-exploitation.
in writing. in the run-up to the next g20 in cannes, nicolas sarkozy has made this issue one of the priorities of the french presidency. he chastised speculators who create immense instability in commodity prices and risk causing hunger riots. by 2050, our planet will have 9 billion people. our needs will increase in every area. europe needs a common strategy: better resource efficiency, recycling and innovation. the urgent need to address the shortage of raw materials and to meet these needs while fighting against speculators is the whole point of the next g20. the report also addresses the sensitive issue of rare earths - precious metals used in the manufacture of our mobile phones, for example - in which china holds a monopoly. europe must ensure a fair and sustainable supply of these strategic lands, but also find alternative solutions. we must ensure that future generations have access to raw materials at an affordable price. we cannot afford to lag behind, nor can we allow markets to act at the expense of citizens and european industrial competitiveness.
in writing. the report recognises the right of states to regulate access to their natural resources. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the concept of 'commercial'. i support all these proposals. but it also proposes that the financial markets play a greater role, that all trade restrictions be abolished and that even the raw materials which our citizens and our companies may need be placed in the hands of a european private holding company. it's inconsistent. i vote against it.
in writing. i supported this report because europe needs a genuine raw materials strategy to strengthen its competitiveness. this need is further underlined by the recent case brought before the world trade organization (wto) between the european union, the united states and mexico and china. the wto has supported the former, which accused china of protectionist practices aimed at raising the price of nine raw materials (including zinc, bauxite and magnesium). while china disputes this judgment, the eu's reaction is in the right direction: an 'internal' strategy, including incentives for recycling or transparency of stocks, is no longer sufficient. the eu must use all the tools at its disposal, including trade defence instruments, to ensure free and fair access to raw materials for its businesses. in addition, the eu, in its role as a driver for the promotion of human rights and fundamental freedoms, must fully combat the trade and use of conflict minerals, including by strengthening the mechanisms for tracing raw materials and introducing a mandatory certification system for raw materials.
in writing. i welcome the fact that the european union, with its limited traditional natural resources, has adopted this roadmap to ensure a sustainable and responsible supply of raw materials. it is a question of our development potential, our competitiveness, the protection of our industries, which are largely dependent on imports of raw materials. european cooperation on this subject is all the more crucial as the emergence of new powers on the international scene, hungry for minerals, leads to an unbridled race and speculation on these materials. this roadmap thus contributes to the efforts already made by some member states at the last g8, which clearly understood the need to guarantee fair access, price stability and the sustainability of raw material supplies. while this strategy of supplying resources is of paramount importance, the union must also become aware that it will become essential for it to generate within itself alternatives to traditional raw materials. i am thinking in particular of algae, which are being used experimentally to produce third-generation biofuels and which will have the advantage of meeting the challenges, which are discussed at length in this report, of stabilising the prices of agricultural products. we must explore these opportunities without further delay!
in writing. the main objective of this report is to establish the medium- and long-term framework for the development of fisheries in the black sea region. it is of great importance since, so far, no coordinated action between all the fisheries actors has been able to be carried out successfully in the black sea. however, institutional coordination could produce tangible results in protecting fishermen's livelihoods, ensuring the economic development of coastal regions and preserving the ecological balance and fisheries resources in the basin. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which calls for the establishment of a separate regional fisheries management organisation (rfmo) for the black sea, on the model of what already exists in the baltic sea.
in writing. the reform of the eu's common fisheries policy will include the black sea. in this context, it is important to coordinate the policies of the various coastal states. i voted in favour of mrs iotova's report, which proposes, firstly, to put in place a specific policy to preserve and improve the situation of fish stocks and to ensure the existence of a fisheries sector adapted to the black sea basin, secondly, to support more targeted and better coordinated scientific research at regional, national and european levels in order to preserve ecosystems, thirdly, to provide for an appropriate status within the framework of community policies to promote sustainable fisheries, and finally to implement a specific regional organisation for the management of fisheries in the black sea.
in writing. following the april 2010 deepwater horizon oil rig disaster in the gulf of mexico, the european union decided to review the safety rules for its own offshore oil and gas operations. i voted for this report because it proposes to raise safety standards, for example by providing for the implementation of emergency plans in the event of a disaster. the basic principle of the polluter pays principle is also at the heart of the system.
in writing. widening the scope of environmental responsibility: this is what the report we have just adopted is all about. securing offshore platforms is a key challenge: we all remember the gulf of mexico disaster caused by the deepwater horizon explosion in april 2010. the damage to the surrounding flora and fauna was immense. as we have said after every disaster: never again... but in practice, everything still needs to be done: it is absolutely necessary that operators present operational emergency plans before being allowed to exploit new oil or gas fields. what we also need to do urgently is to make operators financially liable in the event of an accident! we could have done better in this report, but the principle has been adopted: operators must prove that they have sufficient financial means to repair any damage caused to the environment. the polluter pays principle should be applied to them. it is high time that operators were able to deal with the consequences of their activities.
in writing. the ford report argues that the highest safety and environmental standards should be applied to all offshore oil and gas activities. it states that, with regard to disaster response, responsibility lies with industry on the basis of the 'polluter pays' principle. however, the public sector must oversee the safety and coordination of this response. i supported the paragraph that the introduction of a union-wide moratorium on all new offshore oil drilling in union waters would be a disproportionate response to the need to ensure high safety standards throughout the union.
in writing. in april 2010, the deepwater horizon oil rig explosion spilled nearly 800 million liters of oil into the gulf of mexico. it took bp five months to plug the leak. such a catastrophe must never happen again. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to meet its own needs. in addition, financial liability will have to be introduced, requiring oil and gas producers to have sufficient financial capacity to repair any damage caused to the environment.
in writing. i supported this own-initiative report on the security of offshore oil and gas activities, as i believe it is essential to draw lessons from the disaster in the gulf of mexico in april 2010. such an initiative allows the european union to strengthen the security of these offshore activities and to provide an inventory of capabilities to provide for environmental crisis management mechanisms at european level.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this own-initiative report on enhancing the security of offshore oil and gas platforms. after the gulf disaster, i spoke in favour of increased security to prevent a repeat of this type of disaster, which not only endangers marine ecosystems but also has a devastating effect on the economic sectors of fishing and tourism. parliament has spoken in favour of stricter checks by independent experts and the adoption of contingency plans before each operation, which seems to me to be an effective and proportionate response to the need to strengthen the security of these platforms. parliament also stressed the responsibility of industry in the event of a disaster, in accordance with the polluter-pays principle, without neglecting the role of supervision and coordination which falls to the public sector. i am glad that we have insisted, together with my political group, the epp, that no moratorium should be imposed on this subject. indeed, the introduction of a moratorium on new offshore oil drilling in eu waters would be a disproportionate response to the need to ensure high safety standards throughout the union.
in writing. we must draw the consequences of the explosion last april at the deepwater horizon oil rig in the gulf of mexico, which caused immense environmental, economic and social damage in the region. we are wise to guard against such a catastrophe. that is why i supported calls for an eu-wide moratorium on new offshore oil drilling in eu waters, to ensure high safety standards throughout the union. we must have common european rules, based on the highest standards, before we allow any further exploration and exploitation in deep waters. i believe that oil and gas companies should be held responsible for all the damage they cause and should assume full coverage of potential damage, without a ceiling. finally, i support the ban on exploration and exploitation in sensitive areas to be protected, particularly the arctic, and i urge the oil industry to invest more in prevention.
in writing. given the urgency of securing offshore oil and gas installations, it was only natural that i should support this report. the challenge is well identified: how to reconcile security of supply with security of energy exploration and exploitation? more and more europeans are concerned about the impact on their environment of intensifying these activities to meet the growing demand for fossil fuels. these legitimate concerns call for a maximum level of protection. that is the choice we made, and i am glad we did. i am also pleased that our parliament has established the competence of the european maritime safety agency to ensure the safety of offshore installations and to combat pollution at sea and on the coasts. the tragic consequences of oil disasters and oil spills require an ambitious prevention strategy. the whole point is to establish the precautionary principle as an intangible precondition for any authorization of offshore activities. nevertheless, this prevention component must be supplemented by a reaction component, and i renew my call for the establishment of a european rapid reaction force that can be mobilised as soon as an incident occurs. we have no time to waste on how to protect our environment!
in writing. at a time when only one in 10 women in the eu is a business owner, compared with one in four men, it is essential to work to support female entrepreneurship. this report proposes a number of ways of doing so and calls on the commission and the member states to promote the exchange of best practice in this area. i voted for him.
in writing. i voted for the report by mrs yannakoudakis, which proposes ways of encouraging female entrepreneurship in small and medium-sized enterprises in europe. i voted in favour of an amendment calling on the member states to facilitate access to entrepreneurship for roma women, in particular through micro-credit. i also supported the paragraph calling on member states to support programmes enabling immigrant women to become selfemployed or to set up businesses. finally, i voted in favour of the paragraph calling on the member states to promote a balanced representation of women and men on the boards of directors of companies, particularly where these states are shareholders.
in writing. surprising report by mrs yannakoudakis on a subject which the report itself says we know virtually nothing about, in the absence of relevant statistics and studies! so the report is a bit of a stereotype. in his view, the apparent 'under-representation' of women at the head of smes could be due mainly to discriminatory practices or the persistence of 'societal' stereotypes, from which women themselves suffer. it therefore proposes, first and foremost, specific and preferential measures to assist women in the management of their businesses. we are navigating between guardianship and affirmative action, this counterproductive policy that casts permanent doubt on the real abilities and talents of the people who are supposed to benefit from it. when will quotas and the obligation to undertake for all women be introduced? mrs yannakoudakis could have focused on the objective and concrete reasons why women are reluctant to start a business. there are plenty of them, starting with the difficulties of balancing this very busy activity with their family life. it could also have insisted on the social and financial recognition of mothers and "caring" spouses, which are practical activities that are rarely paid. she preferred to be a pseudo-feminist dogmatist.
in writing. although women represent 60% of all university graduates, they are underrepresented in full-time employment in the labour market, particularly in the corporate sector. this own-initiative report highlights the fact that men and women do not have the same opportunities to run and develop businesses and proposes concrete measures to remedy this situation. i therefore voted in favour of this report because it encourages, among other things, the european union to invest in women's entrepreneurship and in smes run by women, which are a major source of employment, for example through special grants, venture capital, interest rate subsidies and social security provisions. it also called for the fight against stereotypes and obstacles faced by women wishing to start their own businesses, called on the commission to launch a campaign to promote women's participation in the labour market through the creation of their own businesses, wanted to raise awareness among women of the exchange programme erasmus for young entrepreneurs and encouraged the implementation of policies enabling women to reconcile work and family life in a satisfactory way.
in writing. i voted for the report on women entrepreneurs in small and medium-sized enterprises. as european economies are losing steam and the economic crisis still affects large numbers of citizens, investing in women is essential. the remaining gender imbalance in business creation is unjustified and ineffective. the report promotes both financial support instruments for the creation of smes and information for women on the various opportunities available to them to facilitate the creation of enterprises. it also calls for policies to take account of the specific problems faced by women. it stresses the importance of measures to facilitate the reconciliation of work and family life, which is a major obstacle for many women, preventing them from entering the business world. the emphasis is also on preventing all forms of discrimination against women: it is high time that equal treatment applied to all aspects.
in writing. i welcome the vote on the report on access to documents. there are many examples where the work of the institutions should be more transparent in order to prevent corruption, fraud, conflicts of interest and maladministration. i am thinking in particular of the european union agencies, whose geographical remoteness makes it more difficult for parliament to monitor them. agencies should give precise reasons for refusing access to documents on the evaluation and authorisation of various products and medicines, and not hide behind commercial reasons. transparency, access to documents, must be a central tool to ensure their proper management. similarly, in other institutions, the constant use of experts and lobbies could undermine the objective assessment of reality. transparency as required by the treaties is not limited to legislative procedures but also covers the non-legislative work of the union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. the functioning of working groups should therefore be as transparent as possible, by means of the publication of their members, draft agendas and meeting minutes.

author. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, finally a debate in this parliament on the situation of the homeless! i would first like to pay tribute to all the associations that, on the ground, work all year round to help the most vulnerable among us, the homeless. homelessness is a serious violation of human rights and human dignity. it is the most visible and sad link in the chain of bad housing. it's an unbearable injustice. it is essential to understand why people end up on the streets, in order to put in place effective prevention policies. rather than looking for ways to get these people off the streets, it is much easier to not rush them into it. when are we going to stop evictions? when will we stop speculating in real estate? when will we finally understand that growing poverty and precariousness lead to exclusion? the faces of the homeless have changed, the image of the bohemian tramp has lived on, the reality today is much more complex but much harsher. more and more young people, women, families - including migrants - and even poor workers, are homeless. homelessness comes in many forms. there are homeless people lying on the street in the winter, under cardboard boxes or in tents, in public parks, but that is just the tip of the iceberg. millions of people are living in emergency shelters, in makeshift homes, with friends and family, sleeping in cars or in unsanitary hotels. in the face of an emergency that is getting worse by the day, the associations are sounding the alarm bells. but governments have succeeded one another, and the scandal of inaction remains. it is high time that governments took responsibility. it is high time that this shameful situation was brought to an end. europe must commit itself to supporting the states in the path of fundamental values, in the path of lasting solutions to this reality, because our first duty is to protect the weakest. in the face of this unacceptable reality, we cannot continue to look the other way, just as we avoid looking at the homeless on the street. worse, the homeless are excluded from the city centers to the periphery, far from the eyes of businessmen and tourists. but just because you can't see them doesn't mean they don't exist! there's no point in hiding the problem, it has to be solved today. in a country which you know well, commissioner, homeless people are considered criminals. they are forbidden to sleep on the streets, under penalty of a fine, and the police are chasing them even in the subway stations and railway stations, where no proper services are set up to receive them. it is no longer the time for communication, for false political promises, for campaign slogans, as we see in some states. the european parliament therefore calls on you, following the european consensus conference on homelessness, to put in place an integrated strategy to end homelessness by 2020, building on the work already done. this strategy should be based on five main objectives: first, the prevention of homelessness; second, the reduction of its duration; third, the concentration of efforts on the most severe forms; fourth, the improvement of the quality of services for the homeless; finally, an adequate supply of affordable housing. this strategy must be coordinated with national and regional strategies. the results obtained in relation to indicators defined jointly at european level should be regularly reviewed. emphasis should be placed on social innovation, in particular on housing-oriented approaches as the first step in a social reintegration process. finally, adequate funding must be ensured at both european and national level. the commissioner, beyond words, therefore, has urgency. we need action now. it's a matter of political will: homelessness is not inevitable. we don't have to wait for winter to remember that people die on the streets all year long. ending homelessness is possible and i think the european parliament is showing the way.

member of the commission. − madam president, i would like to give particular thanks to mr seeber and mr skylakakis for this opportunity to explain the commission’s approach regarding man-made non-co2 climate-relevant emissions. you are quite right; non-co2 gases are a significant contributor to climate change. if we wish to cut our greenhouse gas emissions substantially, we must address emissions from non-co2 gases in an effective way. i fully agree with your motion for a resolution on this point. the recent roadmap for moving to a low-carbon economy by 2050 explores cost-efficient pathways for key economic sectors in order to meet the 2050 eu objectives for greenhouse gas emissions reduction. this analysis clearly shows that the eu should reduce agricultural non-co2 emissions by 42-49% and other non-co2 emissions by 70-78% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels. both gentlemen spoke about what is economically beneficial, and here these non-co2 gases come very much into the picture. as you know, the eu has already taken a number of measures to reduce such emissions. the effort sharing decision covers co2 as well as the five non-co2 gases included in the kyoto protocol. the annual binding greenhouse gas emission targets for member states will deliver a 10% reduction of emissions from the covered sectors in 2020 compared with 2005 levels. we already address hfc emissions through the regulation on certain fluorinated greenhouse gases and the directive on fluorinated emissions from mobile air-conditioning. the commission will adopt a report reviewing the regulation in the coming weeks, which will show that the regulation has already contributed to the eu commitments under the kyoto protocol. moreover, if properly applied, the regulation on certain fluorinated gases (‘f-gases’) could, together with the directive on mobile air-conditioning, prevent almost half of the projected fluorinated gas emissions by 2050. even more importantly, the report shows that there are options which could contribute to further cost-effective reductions. therefore, i intend to put forward a legislative proposal in 2012. in addition to domestic action, internationally the commission has repeatedly called for global action to address the use of hydrofluorocarbons (hfcs). at the meetings of the parties to the montreal protocol, the commission, as the negotiator for the european union, supports the north american and micronesian proposals to phase down global production and consumption of hfcs as a complement to mitigation action under the united nations framework convention on climate change. the commission is also fully aware of the short-term climate implications of black carbon and tropospheric ozone, particularly – as i think mr seeber mentioned – in the arctic area and in the alpine regions. the joint research centre of the european commission has played a key role in several recent science assessments, in particular in the united nations environment programme (unep) 2011 integrated assessment of black carbon and tropospheric ozone. within the eu, the commission is preparing a review of the thematic strategy on air pollution. the review will be concluded in 2013 and will address air quality matters and their interlinkages with climate change policy. black carbon and tropospheric ozone issues will be considered as part of that review. finally, in an international context, the eu is addressing pollutants like black carbon and tropospheric ozone under the convention on long range transboundary air pollution. together with other european and north american countries, we are presently negotiating binding emission targets for ozone-creating pollutants. if a successful agreement can be struck by the end of this year – and i understand from my colleague commissioner potočnik, who is responsible for these negotiations, that this outcome is within reach and there is a very good chance of achieving it – some improvements can be expected by 2020. finally, i know that unep will publish a report very soon setting out possible measures to reduce levels of black carbon in an effort to push for an international action plan for which international backing can be secured at rio+20 in brazil next june. needless to say, europe will push very hard for that to materialise.

mr president, mr president, mr minister, the present uncertainty about the european response to the crisis is particularly damaging, first of all for the countries concerned, but also for the markets, whose pressure is becoming unbearable and dangerous. i shall deal with a purely technical question on this point. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. when a company is in default, there are exceptional rules to protect it. on the other hand, there is no rule for the states, because it has long been accepted that the states could not be in default. the example of greece shows that the constant pressure on the state does not allow the planned measures to be implemented effectively. the european union must therefore determine, within the framework of the euro area, which rules are to prevail. membership of the eurozone creates an original and ambiguous situation for each country: it is no longer the issuer of its own currency, but its financial policy is still poorly coordinated with that of other countries. the first imperative is of course the rapid completion of the mechanism for the coordination of economic policies and the european stability mechanism, but the rules must also be defined. the aim would be to introduce a system requiring in the case of countries with contracts with the european union or the imf the freezing of clauses of early call-off, of the expiry of terms or of credit events which, today, prevent a real recovery. the establishment of such a mechanism would ensure both transparency and credibility.

mr president, i believe that the bankruptcy of one member of the euro zone would in fact lead to the bankruptcy of the whole of europe, and that it would have incalculable consequences and an exorbitant cost, not only in financial terms but also in economic terms, in terms of employment and in political terms. so this is not an option, and we have to make that clear here. the only solution is to help greece: first by keeping our commitments, then by giving it time, then by helping it to carry out and complete the structural reforms it needs and, finally, by giving and guaranteeing prospects to its people. only then, i believe, will greece get back on its feet. but the crisis of confidence in the euro has reached such a level that it is obvious that we cannot stop there. it will be necessary to implement the euro-bonds that have been discussed for months now, to pool part of the debt of the euro-zone member states up to 60% of gdp, to make progress on the question of economic governance, but also on the question of political governance, which, in the crisis, has been largely inadequate.
in writing. the eurozone crisis is reaching its climax in a europe governed by the far right. but it is these governments, each more frivolous and selfish than the next, that demand multiple guarantees, promises, sanctions for "bad students", before agreeing to grant a single ounce of solidarity. by dragging its feet on the implementation of the aid plans for greece, the reluctant coalition is simply turning what should be a strong solidarity movement into a waste of public money towards a bottomless pit. the aid granted to the drop-in account is of no use to our greek partner, who is still under fire from speculative attacks. do we want to let the patient die while we quarantine him? but until what? do we do the same tomorrow with italy, ireland or spain showing the same symptoms? the epidemic is being spread by the banks, since it is to them that the states are indebted, let us stop lying to ourselves: breaking up the eurozone and the european union will not save anyone from a general economic collapse. what we need is to get back to investing in sustainable growth, but when will this message be heard?
in writing. some argue that greece's exit would cure all the ills of the eurozone. but they're wrong. beyond the domino effect, this event would send the world the dramatic message that europe would no longer be able to undertake its own project of economic unification. let us not give in to the rush, nor to the demagogy of the surrounding world. the idea of being withdrawn has always been a bad one. unfortunately, history has shown us that, and that is why we wanted to build europe. there is only one remedy for the crisis: the community method. commission, member states and parliament: we have all shown the will to come together. today is the time for concerted action. we have a common currency, let us now set up a genuine economic government and bring our fiscal policies closer together, as germany and france are proposing. above all, let us not forget that we are acting for the people of europe. to clean up our finances is to invest in innovation and research for the long term to create growth and jobs. we must explain this to our fellow citizens who, as they observe the reforms under way, are rightly asking questions about their future.
in writing. it would be an illusion to hide it: the crisis we are going through is serious. the daily turbulence in the governments, stock exchanges and banks portends the worst if europe does not react immediately. what are the reasons for this crisis? first, there is a structural flaw: how can the long-term stability of a single currency be ensured without the establishment of genuine budgetary coordination? the old stability pact was weak and out of touch with reality. secondly, there is a cyclical reason: states have long been - and even more so since the 2008 crisis - showing approximations in the management of their public expenditure, which must be stopped. finally, the crisis has been aggravated by the political selfishness of certain states, which are acting in a dispersed manner according to their short-term interests and the opinion polls of the moment. france and germany have proposed solutions. they are necessary, but they will not be sufficient. the answer must come from europe itself. will the eu dare to take a 'step into the unknown', a genuine integration where everyone's solidarity for the growth of all is expressed? if the euro collapses, trust in the european project will collapse with it.
