in writing. energy is at the heart of human activities. it is essential that it is accessible at a reasonable price and that there is no abuse of the market. i therefore voted in favour of this draft regulation because it will ensure greater transparency in the wholesale energy market and thus greater price stability for the benefit of final consumers.
in writing. the energy market integrity and transparency regulation aims to outlaw market abuse by requiring players to provide insider information to regulatory agencies. this regulation is a major step forward in the regulation and transparency of energy markets. it has the dual advantage of being limited to wholesale energy markets and of being a tool against price volatility, in order to guarantee financial security to the consumer.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which will ensure greater transparency in energy market transactions within the european union. this new regulation of wholesale electricity and gas markets should help to strengthen confidence between the various players and the member states of the european union by establishing a european control framework.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the integrity and transparency of the energy market. it sets out new rules to put an end to abusive practices in the wholesale energy market, including giving more powers of control and sanctions to the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acre), which was set up in 2009. at a time when the completion of the internal market in gas and electricity is one of the main objectives of european energy policy and when research and investment are being directed towards the development of transeuropean energy networks, it is more than necessary that this new market be subject to rules to protect consumers. energy exchanges between member states are also expected to increase in the coming years. the research currently being carried out in the north sea to create a network capable of transporting offshore wind energy is just one example of what is needed for the future. it is therefore desirable to provide an adequate legislative framework for this new market to allow it to develop and flourish properly within a well-established legal framework.
in writing. i voted in favour of the remit regulation to combat market abuse in the energy sector. trade in wholesale energy will now be independently controlled throughout the european union. the text provides for the agency for the cooperation of energy regulators to monitor the electricity and gas markets in cooperation with the national regulatory authorities. the regulation will prohibit the unlawful use of inside information and market manipulation practices. as regards sanctions, we wanted to take account of the 'damage caused to consumers'. we have also called for the creation of a european register of energy operators.
in writing. this report provides for the establishment of an internal energy market based entirely on free and undistorted competition. it delivers energy resources to the law of profit. the citizens will pay the bill again and the ecosystem will suffer. what europe needs is a public energy hub.
in writing. competition must be free and not distorted! this rule, which is a true pillar of european law, not only creates a form of emulation between private players, which is a guarantee of innovation and productivity, but also a wall protecting consumers from possible cartels or abuse of a dominant position. all contracts must be subject to this basic rule. it is therefore only natural that i should have voted in favour of this regulation, which aims to put an end to abusive practices in the wholesale energy market which would be to the detriment of consumers. among the measures adopted, i would particularly like to mention the firm condemnation of insider trading: the unlawful use of inside information and market manipulation practices must be sanctioned by the national authorities and commensurate with the damage suffered by consumers. i welcome the fact that wholesale energy trade is now independently monitored throughout the european union and hope that the commission will be able to give the european agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer) the means to carry out its monitoring and investigation function in respect of infringements of the regulation.
in writing. the lisbon treaty introduced several new legal bases to facilitate the implementation, application and enforcement of eu law. this report focuses on the commission's fundamental role in initiating infringement procedures against member states which have failed to comply with an obligation under the treaty. it called on the commission to propose a 'code of procedure' in this area, regretting the current lack of transparency. it recalled the need to draw up and publish correlation tables so that the commission could monitor transposition measures in all member states. i support these demands and have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i supported the report by eva lichtenberger on the monitoring of the application of community law. it is clear that without proper transposition there can be no effectiveness of union legislation. yet in 2009, there were still close to 3000 complaints and infringement cases, and the member states were still lagging behind in transposing directives in more than half of the cases! i am also concerned about the high number of infringements in the areas of recognition of professional qualifications, services and public procurement. however, i am not one of those who constantly invoke the bad faith of the member states in this matter: i see in this bad result more of a call for a better clarification of the legal framework applicable in these areas in order to help the national authorities in the understanding and the implementation process. i would like to take this opportunity to remind you of the importance of the solvit network and of the usefulness of initiatives such as 'eu pilot' and the 'europe is yours' internet portal, which provide practical information on the application of community law in the single market.
in writing. the right of access to european parliament, council and commission documents is provided for in article 15 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the european transparency initiative, the adoption of a parliamentary resolution in april 2006 and the adoption of the aarhus convention (on access to documents containing environmental information) have forced the commission to propose an amendment to the existing environmental regulation to extend its scope to other eu bodies and agencies. i consider that access for citizens to the work of the eu institutions, bodies and agencies is not a side issue. it is fundamental to the democratic legitimacy of the eu. i therefore supported this report, which expands on the commission's original proposals.
in writing. i supported this report, which recalls that since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, the obligation to grant access to eu documents has been imposed on the european parliament, the council and the commission, as well as on the eeas. this is in line with the increased focus on the relationship between citizens and the eu administration, for greater transparency. however, resistance remains strong in some member states to access to national information and documents exchanged in the legislative process, to the refusal of access to documents relating to international agreements, or to the omission of the names of member states in the conclusions of deliberations. this secrecy is unacceptable! we must rely on the arguments of the ecj in its turco judgment, according to which transparency allows 'to guarantee greater legitimacy, efficiency and accountability of the administration towards the citizens in a democratic system'. we have everything to gain from transparency. that is why i support the principle of access to documents, whereby refusal should remain a duly justified exception.
in writing. this report calls for parliamentarians and citizens to be kept informed of decisions taken at european level. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. i hope the same applies to the european parliament. it also called on the member states to be transparent in transposing eu legislation into national law. it is regrettable that we should have to make such requests in a union which claims to be democratic. i vote for and i denounce the opacity of the european union.
in writing. access to documents is provided for in the treaty on the functioning of the european union through article 15 which states that 'every citizen of the union and every natural or legal person residing or having its registered office in a member state has a right of access to documents of the institutions, bodies, offices and agencies of the union'. the sargentini report reviews annually the application of this right, which governs the exercise of citizens' right of access to documents of the eu institutions. i voted in favour of this report because it follows a policy of ensuring access to documents and transparency during the legislative process, where this is necessary and understandable to the public.
in writing. the aim of this resolution is to amend the european parliament's rules of procedure in order to define identical conditions for the hearings of all candidates for the posts of european commissioner and to ensure that they allow the best possible expression of the views of meps. i supported this report because it reinforces the extremely important democratic exercise of the hearings, which, as we will recall, allow the european parliament, at the beginning of each parliamentary term, to reject candidates who do not correspond to the mission of european commissioner.
in writing. in many areas, the european parliament is still the eternal second, and the appointment of new european commissioners is a good example. that is why, despite this minor role provided for in the treaties, we as representatives of the peoples of europe must do our utmost to check the quality of the candidates chosen by the member states and presented in a single package, in order to go beyond a mere formal approval of the college as a whole. these hearings are therefore a unique opportunity to ascertain the quality of the commissioners-designate. that is why i have supported the proposals which have been put forward in order to organise them as well as possible and to give the elected representatives as many opportunities as possible to test whether the candidates actually meet the requirements for the portfolio which will be allocated to them. i would like to ask the commissioner to give us a clear answer to this question.
in writing. the commissioners have the legislative powers that should be those of the european parliament. their election should be the subject of a real debate and an individual election. this text does not make this minimum requirement. it restricts the possibilities for debate. i vote against it.
in writing. the doha round, launched in 2001 to open up new trade prospects and address current imbalances in the trading system, has been at a standstill since 2008. the 8th ministerial conference of the wto (world trade organisation) will meet in december 2011 to try to conclude this "doha round". we hope that it will at least achieve results in favour of the least developed countries. the world trade organization must establish international rules to limit food price fluctuations and thus ensure greater food security. it also needs to introduce simpler and more transparent preferential rules of origin for imports from the least developed countries (ldcs). if wto members fail to agree on a contribution to ambitious and balanced global development, to economic growth and to the eradication of poverty worldwide, then a major reform of the wto will be required. only a regulated and fair global trading system will put trade at the service of sustainable development.
in writing. since 2001, the doha round of negotiations in the wto has been designed to rebalance the rules of global trade in favour of developing countries. these negotiations have since stalled. the obstacles are many and the responsibilities are shared, but it is the developing countries that are most affected by the failure of the negotiations. all efforts must be made to achieve this, but the negotiations must take greater account of the concerns expressed, including in developing countries, and in particular of the situation of the fragile industrial and agricultural sectors, for which the priority must be food security for the population. public services must be able to remain regulated by each country in the public interest and not liberalized in the context of forced bargaining unrelated to social needs. in these circumstances, the conclusion of the doha round is desirable and necessary. the proliferation of bilateral agreements such as those currently being negotiated will not make it possible to establish clear and fair rules. multilateralism remains the best framework for ensuring fair trade that contributes to the sustainable development of all continents.
in writing. this report is an ode to the fight against all forms of protectionism. it is a lesson to emerging countries and a threat to anyone who dares to restrict their exports of natural resources. it is a crude and brutal imperialism. i vote against it.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it highlights the positive aspects of this round of negotiations, in particular its developing country approach. it also puts forward some ideas which i think should be promoted more in this cycle: food security, access to green goods and technologies, or the extension of the european initiative 'everything but arms' to other countries. above all, while recalling our commitment to multilateralism, it recognises the difficulties involved. the doha round negotiations have stalled and wto members must now work on a 'post-doha' approach. they must reassess the level of development of the countries taking part in the negotiations and give them their proper place and responsibilities. they must also commit to including social and environmental standards in the negotiations, because they are the basis of current dumping. a new mandate, drawing all the useful lessons from the previous one, must be drawn up now, with a view to a rapid reactivation of the multilateral trade negotiations.
in writing. the 8th wto ministerial conference will be held in geneva from 15 to 17 december 2011. however, the doha round, which was launched in 2001 to review the rules of global trade, has reached an impasse. beyond technical agreements, it is essential to look at the substance. what is the wto for? what interests does it defend? in this resolution, parliament wishes to stress the importance of the wto and the doha round, and above all their objectives: to ensure better management of globalisation, a fairer sharing of its benefits and more balanced economic growth. in addition, they must help to address new global challenges in which trade plays a role, such as food security, energy, sustainable development and trade assistance. world trade will be balanced if, and only if, the more developed states make the necessary efforts to promote the integration of the least developed countries (ldcs). nevertheless, europe must be fair without being naive: ultraliberalism is living its last moments with the crisis. we must return to an approach that protects our economy and our values, while ensuring the development and prosperity of others.
in writing. the rules of procedure of the european parliament provide that the committee on petitions shall inform parliament annually of the results of its deliberations and actions. for the year 2010, the european parliament registered 1655 petitions, which represents a decrease of 14% compared to 1924 petitions in 2009. the environment remains the petitioners' main concern, followed by fundamental rights, the internal market and justice. the germans remain the most active petitioners, followed by the spanish and the italians. petitions are increasingly being sent via the internet, with 63.2% of petitions received in 2010. i for my part welcome the fact that the treaty of lisbon introduced the possibility of a citizens' initiative and i continue to follow the work of the committee on petitions, whose annual activity report i have approved.
in writing. as a full member of the committee on petitions, i voted in favour of my committee's 2010 annual report. it's about defending his role. in 2010, the committee on petitions received 1 655 petitions from european citizens. the environment remains one of their main concerns. in addition to its success, other important factors must be taken into account. it is the only committee to organise hearings of european citizens at each of its meetings. it enjoys undeniable expertise and legitimacy in parliament through its direct relationship with the citizen. my colleagues and i have dealt with painful cases, such as the expropriation of thousands of people in spain because of the spanish coastal law or cross-border divorces. the committee on petitions represents the europe that it should be: "a community that listens to the problems of its citizens and works together to find solutions and protect them". unfortunately, the means of action and the means of evaluation are still limited. this is because of the lack of cooperation from the member states and certain public authorities. the most important thing is that citizens continue to have confidence in our institution and do not hesitate to continue to ask for help.
in writing. i voted for the annual report of the committee on petitions. the right to petition is a central democratic instrument which allows every european citizen to address the european parliament directly to find a solution to his or her individual problems, to draw attention to failing european policies, or to ask the european union to intervene in a specific area. once again this report shows us the particular interest of european citizens in environmental issues and the need to become more involved in the environment. the report also points to the lack of transparency regarding petitions: it is essential that each petition received is published online as the petitioner has not expressed disagreement, so that every citizen can be informed about the petitions filed and join them if they wish. it also recalled that the committee on petitions was dependent on the cooperation of the other institutions: it was essential that the council cooperate even more closely with the committee on petitions. i would like to support the committee on petitions in its democratic work by voting for it.
in writing. the legitimacy of the european project is based on citizens' support. this accession is only possible if citizens have the opportunity to express themselves, to express their concerns and to enforce their rights with the institutions. i welcome the work of the committee on petitions of the european parliament in this respect. with the creation of the citizens' initiative by the treaty of lisbon, this fundamental right has been strengthened. it must be supported and disseminated, since the committee on petitions is best placed to follow up petitions. but in order to be as effective as possible, to respond as best as possible to the citizens, i think that joint, transparent work between the european commission, the member states and the european parliament is essential. finally, the participation of all depends on the clarity and accessibility of the procedure. in this sense, a single window for petitions should certainly be set up. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report.
in writing. in these times of financial and budgetary crisis, it is necessary to stabilise our banks and budgets, but it is not enough: it seems to me that the balance with the consideration of the needs of the most vulnerable in our societies is not ensured, far from it! at a time when we still have no certainty about the survival of the programme of aid for the most deprived for the years to come, this resolution, supported by a very large majority in parliament, on the european union's strategy for the homeless, is a reminder that poverty and social exclusion affect millions of people in europe and that it is unthinkable to leave them out of the picture. it calls more specifically for a focus on housing policies in the european union. ensuring decent housing for all, meeting basic needs and access to quality services remain urgent and daily challenges.
in writing. i voted for the resolution on a european strategy to help the homeless. while member states are trying to redress the wrongs of the financial markets, very little is being done to prevent or to lift citizens out of the abyss of homelessness. this resolution is a wake-up call! states must look at the case of the homeless. they are asked to collect information about these people to better meet their needs and are encouraged to exchange information to respond in a supportive manner. monitoring progress at european level in each member state will enable us to have a global view of the problem in order to move towards a europe where every citizen has a roof over his head. a homeless citizen is a citizen without rights. housing is absolutely essential for the exercise of a whole range of other rights, including civil and social rights. the resolution sets the goal of ending homelessness by 2015. that is very good, but now the states must give themselves the means to win this bet! it is time to go beyond declarations, as this resolution calls for.
in writing. 17% of the eu population lives below the poverty line; 8% of europeans live in extreme material deprivation; 3 million people, including a growing number of young people, families and children, are homeless. this situation is unacceptable and intolerable in the light of the values we defend in the eu, in the light of fundamental rights, in the light of respect for and dignity of persons. although last year was designated as the 'european year for combating poverty and social exclusion', the phenomenon continues and poverty is growing at an alarming rate. i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on the member states to make progress and put an end to homelessness by 2015. it must now be followed by a genuine commitment: governments must now act. our resolution also calls for a genuine european strategy to help the homeless, because very little is being done at present to prevent citizens from falling into homelessness or to help them to get out of it. the eu can do more (especially not to reduce the budget of the european programme for aid to the most deprived)!
in writing. following the adoption by the european parliament of a written declaration in favour of an eu homelessness strategy in december 2010, the vote on this resolution will only reinforce our message of firmness and urgency to the commission and the member states in favour of a european strategy against homelessness, the clearest manifestation of poverty and social exclusion. we have a duty to ensure a dignified life for all citizens, no matter who they are. social policies can no longer be put on the back burner, behind policies of budgetary austerity, which are already in full swing. we must use all the tools at the disposal of the european union so that tomorrow the stability pact does not lead to the blind cutting of any possible funding for services which help these populations. we must also encourage the member states not to apply the competition rule to social housing but to finance social housing so that the problem of homelessness will no longer be an urgent one in the future.
in writing. while 2010 has been designated as the 'european year for combating poverty and social exclusion', the phenomenon of homelessness continues to affect all european countries, reaching alarming proportions in some states. the european union has committed itself, in the framework of the europe 2020 strategy, to reducing by at least 20 million the number of people affected or threatened by poverty and social exclusion by 2020. this is clearly a priority objective and the concerns related to the debt crisis must not obscure this phenomenon. the fight against homelessness requires concrete and ambitious measures. i hope that the member states of the european union will really empower themselves to fight poverty and social exclusion by implementing a comprehensive strategy that deals with all aspects of homelessness (housing, support, coordination of actions and actors on the ground). that is why i welcome the adoption of the resolution on an eu strategy for the homeless. at a time of sluggish economic growth and financial markets, this resolution is a way of refocusing the debate on the human dimension of the crisis and sending a strong political message to the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on a european strategy for the homeless. we want a european strategy to put an end to the situation of the homeless. when we know that the life expectancy of a long-term homeless person is only five years in an urban area, we understand the urgency of putting an end to this situation in europe. the text proposes that the european commission and the member states monitor the progress of national and regional strategies and report on progress achieved through half-yearly or annual reports. to deal more effectively with this situation, to gather reliable information and to work together on this issue, member states should agree on a common definition and typology of housing-related exclusion.
in writing. the fact that there are homeless people today is unacceptable in the world's leading economic power. the report rightly points to this when it denounces "an unacceptable violation of human rights". it called on the member states to put an end to this situation by 2015 and on the european union to help them do so by putting in place an ambitious strategy, and not just monitoring the results of the states. all these proposals i share. it is a pity that the framework of the europe 2020 strategy, which is the text of which is claimed, puts precariousness at the heart of the european system and inevitably leads to an increase in the number of homeless people. i am voting for this text to encourage the crucial demand to combat the most widespread precariousness.
in writing. 2010 has been declared the european year for combating exclusion. the european union decided that the homeless problem should be solved by 2015. yet we are far from it... according to caritas, as we approach the dawn of 2012, 3 million europeans will be homeless. the european union must give itself the means to achieve its ambitions! that is why i support the european parliament's resolution on a european union strategy for the homeless in the vote in plenary. the text calls on the council to consider the development of an eu strategy for the homeless and on the commission to set up a working group to consider the content of this strategy. it also urged member states to make progress towards ending the situation of homelessness by 2015. to this end, it would be valuable to draw up half-yearly or annual reports on progress. the areas of concern should cover reducing the time spent by homeless people without accommodation, but also the quality of services for homeless people, or access to affordable housing.
in writing. parliament is today urging the member states and the commission to develop real strategies for the homeless and i welcome this. according to some reports, 3 million europeans are homeless. however, we do not have a harmonised study of this sad phenomenon, and despite the good intentions expressed in the eu 2020 strategy (to reduce the poverty rate by 25% by 2020) and during the european year for combating exclusion in 2010, the situation is only getting worse. the crisis and the migratory pressures generated by the arab spring force us to move beyond the stage of reflection, to actually act against these injustices. europe can do much and above all do better: it can impose a uniform framework for analysing poverty and homelessness, develop the progress programme which allows the exchange of experience and the experimentation of new initiatives and facilitates micro-credit. in addition, the current system, which makes projects concerning housing for marginalised communities eligible for erdf support, deserves to be promoted and extended. finally, europe must clarify its regulations on social services of general interest, in particular social housing and emergency shelters for the most deprived.
in writing. this resolution calls on the european commission to adopt a comprehensive approach to combating climate change, i.e. not to forget black carbon, hfcs, fluorinated gases, etc. in its fight against climate change, as these gases also have an effect on the climate. i have, however, spoken in the plenary to remind you of two essential points: firstly, yes, we must prepare ourselves to take action against these gases, which have consequences similar to those of co2 on the climate, and secondly, no, the time has not yet come to act on this issue: it is essential to give our industry a chance to breathe and to adapt! i think this resolution is an interesting sign of the european parliament's determination to address the international community on climate issues: more than ever, especially on environmental issues, governance is planning...
in writing. states must accelerate their efforts to combat global warming and further reduce their emissions of fluorinated gases, used in refrigerators and air conditioning systems, among other things. the policy to combat global warming is mainly focused on carbon dioxide. however, taking stricter measures against other greenhouse gases would be effective and inexpensive. targeting emissions of hfcs is profitable because they can be reduced at a cost of 5 to 10 cents per tonne compared to 13 euros per tonne for carbon dioxide. the european commission also needs to tackle 'carbon black' (small particles of carbon found in soot), including through legislation on car emissions. carbon black has a significant impact on global warming by absorbing heat from the sun and accelerating the melting of snow and ice.
in writing. rapid and coordinated action is essential to tackle global warming. co2 is not the only cause of global warming. greenhouse gases such as carbon monoxide (co), nitrogen oxides (nox) and methane also contribute. we need to support innovation in our environmentally responsible industries. we also need to put pressure on our business partners to take their responsibilities, as we do - not to do it alone!

member of the commission. − mr president, the european commission is of course deeply concerned about the food crisis in the horn of africa. the impact of the region’s worst drought in 60 years is being felt most severely in southern somalia, north and eastern kenya, and in the south-eastern pasturelands of ethiopia. the drought has led to livestock losses and crop failures, which have affected the livelihoods of millions of people. the situation is made worse by insecurity, conflict in somalia and high food prices. altogether, we are looking at the most severe humanitarian emergency in the world today. more than 12 million people in the horn of africa have already been affected and this number continues to grow as the crisis deepens. with below normal rains forecast for the coming months, food insecurity is likely to persist into the next year. last week, famine conditions spread to a sixth region in somalia. child malnutrition is at alarming levels, both in southern somalia and among refugees arriving in kenya and ethiopia. a human tragedy is unfolding. we must act to stop it now. the eu has responded robustly to the crisis. so far this year it has provided more than eur 700 million in humanitarian assistance to the horn of africa, with eur 160 million of that sum coming from the commission’s dg echo. commissioners piebalgs and georgieva have visited the regions and engaged in dialogue with the national authorities. the immediate priorities are food assistance, nutrition, water, sanitation and health. if the crisis persists, additional humanitarian assistance will have to be mobilised. however, insecurity and restricted access mean that not all relief is getting through to the neediest southern-central regions of somalia and working to improve access conditions should be a priority.droughts are recurring phenomena, intensified by climate change. an immediate response needs to be coupled with long-term measures to prevent this type of crisis repeating itself. this is a conclusion shared by the governments of the region and the international community and it was reiterated at the african union conference on 25 august. the eu is also working more structurally in the region to improve food security and to invest in disaster risk reduction measures. plans are under way to provide recovery assistance in order to link relief to long-term development. in all countries in the region food security is a focal factor for development cooperation for the eu, the aim being to build sustainable and resilient livelihoods among farming and pastoralist communities.

in writing. according to the world health organisation (who), 86% of deaths in europe are caused by non-communicable diseases such as cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, cancer and diabetes. therefore, every effort should be made to reduce the identified causes of these diseases (poor diet, smoking, etc.). i therefore contributed my voice to this action programme prepared for the united nations high-level meeting on the prevention and control of noncommunicable diseases to be held on 19 and 20 september 2011 in new york.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the position and commitment of the european union on the prevention and control of noncommunicable diseases. noncommunicable diseases are the leading cause of death in europe. europe has a leading role to play in global health policies. the resolution advocates a strong target of reducing the number of deaths caused by noncommunicable diseases. it stresses that we can do more to achieve this goal by tackling smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, pollution, and by promoting physical activity and healthy eating. it also calls for more research and prevention for the four most common non-communicable diseases: cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, cancer and diabetes. it places the problems of patient and hospital staff care at the heart of the issues to be addressed. this report is comprehensive and helps to outline the contours of a responsible health policy.

member of the commission. − madam president, i am very grateful for the debate today and very grateful to mrs gardini for leading the preparation of the report. as she so clearly stated, we live in a world where the frequency and intensity of disasters is on the increase, and climate change, population growth and urbanisation, as well as terrorism, put us at a higher risk. we have witnessed over the years the role that parliament has played in creating a high level of ambition to make solidarity work for european citizens and for the citizens of the world. i would quote the initiatives taken on the eu forest fire tactical reserve, on creating multi-country pilot modules like the baltfloodcombat module, as well as on bringing transportation capacity to bear. we saw how much it helped us during the libya crisis. against that background of growing needs, the commission has taken its responsibility very seriously, and has put forward the communication that is now to be turned into a legislative proposal, for which i very much count on parliament’s help. that communication is based on four very important principles. the first is to respect the primary role of member states in securing the safety of their citizens. therefore, what we have put forward is a ‘bottom-up’ approach where we bring the assets of member states together for collective action when either a member state or a third country is overwhelmed by a disaster. second, we recognise that we must be better in anticipating risks so that we can act decisively when they materialise. therefore, we raise the role of the commission in bringing member states into scenario plannings. third, there is a very important move away from the ad hoc response we currently have to one that is pre-planned, pre-arranged and predictable. fourth, we are very mindful of the tough budgetary times in europe, so we are looking at ways in which working together will create savings for member states. in this sense, the proposal which we have designed is a very modest increase, at the level of the commission, from eur 25 million to eur 65 million, but generates on that basis not only high impact but also savings for member states. let me finish with one very crucial point. we are doing this for our citizens, and over 90% of them want us to act together in the face of disasters. we owe it to them to do exactly that.

on behalf of the ppe group. madam president, commissioner, i would first like to congratulate our colleague, mr daniel caspary, not only on the high quality of his report, but also on the open and collaborative approach which has guided all his work. the text we are about to adopt reflects the aspirations and doubts of members of parliament, regardless of their political group or nationality. it particularly highlights one of our main concerns, namely the need for a genuine long-term commercial strategy. and i think, despite what you have just told us, commissioner, that the commission's communication of november 2010 is insufficient in this respect. it does not take account of the current crisis, not only the economic crisis but also the crisis in international trade. i am thinking, for example, of the deadlock in the doha round of negotiations or the emergence of new non-tariff barriers, which are being observed even among our oldest trading partners. and this communication does not take account of the development of trade policy. the rapporteur has made it clear: 'commercial policy is no longer an end in itself'. however, we have the impression that the commission has not yet incorporated this new reality into its work. i would like to take another example: your services regularly come to the committee on international trade to inform us of the progress of the negotiations on free trade agreements. in this context, we ask them about the consideration of social and environmental standards, the role of the agricultural sector, and reciprocity in market access. and often, in the elusive answers we get, these questions are evaded in favor of purely commercial chapters. that bias is no longer valid today. i would like to support mr caspary's request, commissioner, that the commission should present us with a clear, comprehensive and long-term vision of trade policy.
the caspary report rightly points out that free trade is not an end in itself, that there are economic, social, environmental or moral interests to be defended and that globalisation may not be as happy as the commission continues to believe. the problem is that the caspary report believes in the inevitability of this globalisation and, inevitably, in the virtues of free world trade, slightly amended by some marginal regulation. but this system, as it has been for nearly 60 years, has proved to be deeply unjust and perverse. so we have to change it. the widespread free movement of capital, goods, services and people has led to mass unemployment, relocations, deindustrialisation, wage pressures, unbridled speculation and, ultimately, whether you like it or not, the unprecedented global crisis we are experiencing today. we will not be competing in the near future with countries that use and abuse their comparative advantages, that do not respect their international commitments or that practice dumping and counterfeiting. the global trade war is unfair; we must restore the necessary protections.
