in writing. while it is urgent to find ways of tackling the crisis europe is currently experiencing, we must also think about the future and the levers that will be needed to ensure a return to sustainable, smart and inclusive growth. to this end, the european commission has proposed in the europe 2020 strategy to invest 3% of the eu's gdp in research and innovation. i can only support this objective, especially since at present only six countries, including france, devote more than 2% of their gdp to these themes. to reach that 3%, europe must give itself the means. i am glad to see that the commission has made ambitious proposals in this area. the €80 billion for research proposed in the next multiannual financial framework is good news. however, the next common strategic framework for research will need to simplify its procedures and shorten its decision-making times compared to the current cprd and allow for better participation of smes. it will also need to ensure better coherence with other instruments that invest in innovation, in particular the structural funds, which spend more than €86 billion on innovation.
in writing. − in view of the current situation in the eu countries and in particular in the euro area, particular attention should be paid to sustainable economic development, productivity and global competitiveness. increasing the practical contribution of innovation and research is key to achieving this objective. this is why the eu must provide much larger budgets for research projects and a more strategically-minded, simplified allocation mechanism. it should also take care of small and medium-sized enterprises, the main drivers of eu industry and business, by ensuring that they are involved in innovation projects in a more active and informed way. the commission's green paper on 'from problems to opportunities: moving towards a single strategic framework for eu research and innovation funding' very rightly supports the commission's proposals for a strategic single framework for research and innovation funding after 2013 by combining existing eu programmes and funds, namely the research framework programme, the competition and innovation programme, the european institute of technology and cohesion and structural funds funding. in addition to the commission's recommendations, the report recommends the creation of a european sme investment bank and project bonds, the separation of funding for large-scale projects (such as galileo) from the rest of the budget for innovation projects, the introduction of a new organisational budget model based on three tiers according to the innovation objectives set, and the requirement to double funding for eu research and innovation programmes (available from the structural funds, eib loans of over €50 million, etc.) from 2014. i can fully support the recommendations contained in the report.
in writing. meps have today been more demanding than the commission in defining the priorities for the future common strategic framework for research and innovation in the face of the alarming situation of the sector in the european union. this report by my colleague and friend marisa matias sets as its main objective the increase in spending on research and the development of a scientific culture to 3% of the union's gdp by 2020, which would significantly improve the infrastructure and the capacity for funding in the sector, combat the precarious situation faced by researchers and replace the competition between regions or institutions by strengthening collaborative structures. asked about the pursuit of excellence as the main criterion for research funding, repeated ad nauseam by the commission, marisa matias replied that since the nature of excellence is as varied as the nature of the projects and institutions or companies that support it, other criteria had to be put on an equal footing, such as technical improvement or societal contribution, in order to arrive not at the pursuit of excellence but at the excellence of research.
in writing. i voted for the cavada report on european schools. this report emphasises the diffusion of culture, values, european integration and european languages. the recognition of the 'european baccalaureate' by all the member states represents a real development, accompanied by the creation of a certificate of completion of studies, other than the baccalaureate, for students who wish to move towards a vocational path. the following measures will also be taken to ensure better follow-up of pupils with special educational needs, in particular by better integrating these pupils into the classroom. the report also proposes to review the financing model for european schools in order to lighten the burden on some member states in this period of crisis, in particular by proposing the use of the vernacular languages for non-basic subjects. i support this proposal.
in writing. over the last fifty years or so, european schools have developed to ensure that children whose parents, mainly european civil servants, were unable to work in their home country, can learn the basics in their mother tongue. it was not a luxury but a necessity. these schools now provide quality education and convey european values and culture, the merits of which are no longer to be demonstrated. the report, adopted almost unanimously, calls for the promotion of this model in national education systems, while ensuring respect for the competences of the member states. these schools contribute to the emergence of a european identity based on strong educational principles: multilingualism and mobility. i believe that these models of success, which can always be improved, should be an inspiration for national school systems. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which allows for further reflection on the relevance and performance of existing education systems.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european school system. at a time when a petition on european schools has been presented by several european citizens and has even been the subject of the emergency procedure in the committee on petitions for the first time, it is essential that the whole of parliament should take up this subject in order to meet their expectations. european schools help to build europe on a daily basis by training european citizens in multiculturalism, mastering several languages. the report calls for greater budgetary autonomy for the european schools and for a change in their legal basis. it calls for the development of european schools, for more infrastructure to be provided for them and for them to be better known and less elitist. it also stressed the importance of the european baccalaureate being recognised in all member states. he rightly criticises the reduction in the budget for european schools and the withdrawal of the european union. finally, it draws attention to pupils with specific needs and to the need to provide qualifications other than the baccalaureate to enable reorientation.
in writing. in these times of crisis for the european union, it must be stressed that cohesion policy is one of the great achievements of european construction. it embodies the solidarity between the member states and the regions of europe. but the capacity of the member states and the competent authorities to absorb the structural funds is problematic: there are many disparities within the union, but overall the funds are not used enough and are used badly. each year, a portion of the funds is unallocated. the report we adopted lists the various causes, stresses the need for simplification in access to funds, the need for more developed coordination between levels of governance. the structural funds are a key instrument in the present period for dealing with the consequences of the crisis (through the esf, for example, by financing training and/or vocational retraining measures) and for moving forward by developing infrastructure projects through the erdf. but we must be able to exploit its full potential!
in writing. the theurer report calls for an improvement in the use and management of the structural funds to meet the requirement of budgetary discipline. this commitment is all the more important as we are now in a period of crisis which requires rigorous measures to put an end to mismanagement and the risk of fraud. despite an acceleration in the absorption of funds for the period 2007-2013, absorption rates remain low in some eu member states. we must simplify procedures without radically changing the existing system in order to overcome the administrative burdens and facilitate access to european funding for small project promoters.
in writing. many member states are failing to make full use of the financial resources from the structural and cohesion funds. these funds represent around 37% of the eu budget and enable regions to invest in major infrastructure projects that can create jobs and economic growth. we must therefore help and encourage these states to make better use of this funding. if these funds are to be an effective tool for regional development, procedures must be simplified, local and regional authorities must be able to manage the use of grants autonomously and obstacles to co-financing projects must be removed. the action plan which the commission will present shortly should be based on the sharing of best practice and ultimately allow for the best possible use of these funds.
in writing. the problem is not whether member states manage to spend all the regional funds allocated to them by the union, but why they fail to do so most of the time. the rapporteur was not unaware that one of the reasons for this under-use was that these funds can only be co-financed: the union is being generous with other people's money. another local authority, or the state, must put its hand in its pocket to access partial financing from brussels, which in these times of budgetary austerity is becoming increasingly complicated. another reason is the complexity of the licensing and control procedures. they are time-consuming, wasteful, and require the involvement of public employees, and therefore generate a significant management cost for the state. the question of the relevance of these funds is not raised. what if it is difficult to find national or local projects that can provide access to structural funds? what if the projects actually financed were of limited use in relation to the stated objectives and, above all, to the real needs of the territories? mr theurer's report does not provide the right answers, because it does not ask the right questions.
in writing. i fully supported this report, because it perfectly illustrates the paradoxical situation in which we find ourselves, with abundant structural funds, but which remain largely underused, for various reasons: insufficient administrative capacity, extremely complicated and too strict national procedures, especially for small project promoters, or the lack of involvement of local partners in programming measures. another major factor in this situation is the obsession with austerity, which has the effect of reducing the possibility of cofinancing, even though we need a more ambitious effort by the european public authorities to get out of the economic and social crisis. we must therefore deplore the fact that, because of long administrative procedures and complex rules, implementation of the esf is slower than expected and that, as a result, many potential beneficiaries are reluctant to apply for funding. the structural funds are, however, indispensable tools for supporting many projects for integration, training, combating discrimination and, more generally, for returning to work, which is worth emphasizing in this period of crisis.
in writing. regional policy now represents 35.7% of the community budget. this funding is essential for the development of europe's regions. however, we note that, despite the acceleration in the absorption of the structural and cohesion funds for the period 2007-2013, rates remain low in some member states. the president of the commission, mr barroso, himself underlined this in his state of the union address to meps on wednesday 28 september: growth also requires improving the absorption capacity of the structural and cohesion funds. we are currently experiencing a particularly severe economic and financial crisis. all good management measures should be encouraged. that is why i welcome the adoption of this report, which shows how much parliament is concerned to ensure that european funds are used to the fullest and to remove all those obstacles which often give the impression that europe's money is being thrown out of the window. we are preparing to start negotiations on the next financial perspective for 2014-2020. with this report we are sending a clear signal to the commission and the council. parliament, as the budgetary authority, will be keen to ensure sound management and proper implementation of the union's finances.
in writing. this report gives us an opportunity to discuss again the means we are putting to use for cohesion policy. in addition to the general principles we set out every seven years, regional policy is also a matter of daily life in our territories. it is important that parliament address this issue in the run-up to the next debate. that is why i voted in favour of this text. this report is an excellent opportunity to take an initial look at the management of the structural funds by the new entrants. it thus demonstrates that the tools of cohesion policy are of course not assimilated and used in the same way throughout europe. the new entrants have encountered some major difficulties in setting up. it is essential to maintain an open dialogue with all national and local authorities on good management practices in order to improve our tools. nothing is fixed and our means can constantly change. i want to see the very likely creation of the new category of intermediate regions as proof of this. we started from the observation that the allocation of funds had to be reviewed in the light of the realities on the ground.
in writing. cohesion policy has a budget of €347 billion for the period 2007-13, or 35.7% of the community budget. these appropriations represent 25% of public investment in europe and are essential to ensure economic, social and territorial cohesion within the european union. however, their use is often delayed. greece, for example, which could benefit from a total of €20.3 billion, spent only €4.9 billion in mid-2011 and still has to spend €15.4 billion by 2013. that's a winner! the country is suffering from one of the worst budgetary crises in europe for decades. the causes of these delays are clearly explained in this report: slow implementation of the new management systems, the world economic recession, the crisis of public finances, overly complicated rules, changes in the procedures in the course of programming, lack of qualified staff, insufficient preparation of projects, etc. there are solutions to better use of these funds: let us have the courage to apply them! reform and simplify procedures, empower and support the actors! cohesion policy will be legitimate and helpful in the face of the crisis if, and only if, its appropriations are well spent.
in writing. this report on the structural and cohesion funds calls on the member states to improve access to european funding. every effort should be made to ensure that all local partners can make the best use of these funds. however, the complexity of the rules leads to errors, delays and even difficulties in accessing funds. parliament called for the controls to be concentrated on actual fraud rather than on the verification of formal irregularities, for procedures to be simplified, particularly in relation to the amounts of aid, for the ceilings for co-financing to be lowered, for the european rules to be transposed more rapidly and for measures to make them more accessible. we could have gone further and asked for the conditions for co-financing by the states to be dropped. nevertheless, this report is a step in the right direction, particularly in view of the french government's blockages. that is why i voted in favour, as did all the members of my group.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the gardini report, which calls for the creation of a european civil protection force. it echoes the proposals set out in a commission communication and precedes legislative proposals expected by the end of 2011. the proposal for the multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020 already provides for a budget of eur 455 million for the financial instrument for civil protection. i now call on the commission to be ambitious in its legislative proposals for the end of 2011 so that we can finally create a genuine european civil protection force.
in writing. in the face of the scale of european or international disasters, such as the 2004 tsunami, haiti in 2010, fukushima in 2011, it is time for europe to have an effective system that can ensure a rapid response in the event of a disaster. i therefore welcome the adoption of this report, which is a first step towards a harmonised, organised and united response by the european union. i tabled a number of amendments, which were adopted in the final report, to emphasize the importance of prevention in crisis management and the organization of this prevention through operational tools, which i welcome. pending further consideration of the establishment of a real european civil protection force in the future, i believe that the creation of a european emergency response centre will be a simplification of the current european civil protection mechanism. i asked for two community instruments for the protection of forests, effis and effics, to be associated with this european centre, and this was adopted in the final report.
in writing. the question of european cooperation in civil protection does not even arise and seems obvious, since natural disasters, fires, tsunamis, etc. have nothing to do with borders. in 2010, there were more than 373 natural disasters worldwide, killing nearly 300,000 people and affecting 207 million people. these figures are a strong reminder of the urgency for the eu to organise itself better in order to provide a massive, rapid and effective operational response. they urgently call for systematic action at european level, both within and outside the eu (this is what the commission's communication proposes, and what our report endorses). the current community civil protection mechanism is effective, but insufficient. i will therefore give my full support to any proposal which goes in this direction, to give greater visibility to european action in the field of civil protection, but also to the action taken by all the volunteers in the service of civil protection. i believe that this visibility should go beyond that and be achieved by creating a genuine european civil protection force, with a common logo, a european flag and a common dress code.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution, in order to provide the union with a genuine rapid reaction mechanism in the event of a disaster. there are many examples where member states have had to call on the solidarity of their european partners to deal with natural disasters that hit several regions, such as madeira, western france and different regions of spain in early 2010. as an elected representative, i remain deeply concerned about the human and material consequences of the violence of such weather phenomena. the european institutions can make progress in this area and in that of humanitarian aid, moving from simple coordination to a predictable and planned system of civil protection in the european union. the union will thus be able to carry out disaster relief operations through immediate deployment. this system should not, of course, replace the action of the member states, which have competence at national, regional and local level, but should complement this action through european solidarity.
in writing. between 1975 and 2010, the number of recorded disasters per year increased fivefold, from 78 26 years ago to nearly 400 today. the earthquake that struck japan in march 2011 is the latest example. in europe alone, disasters have killed nearly 90,000 people and caused economic losses of €211 billion over the past 20 years. climate change, population growth associated with urbanisation, industrialisation and environmental degradation are all possible causes of this increase. what is europe doing in the face of these tragedies? does it take advantage of these events to show its added value in terms of coordination, mutualisation and solidarity? i'm afraid not in 2006, michel barnier proposed a number of urgent reforms, which are only now beginning to be seriously discussed, and which are echoed in the gardini report. the lisbon treaty gives the european union a legal basis to develop its capacity to respond to such tragedies. the member states must now play their part and pool certain means of prevention and response so that european solidarity can finally be visible and effective.
in writing. this report on the creation of a european civil protection mechanism is part of a logic of solidarity, both at european and international level, in the face of emergency situations, with an emphasis on the prevention and coordinated and effective management of disasters. i think the proposals are rather positive, such as the dissemination of expertise and good practice, the prior identification of the resources available to states, the simplification of bureaucratic procedures, references to climate change but also to the responsibility of private actors and the provision of assistance and humanitarian aid independently of any political considerations. however, some aspects remain questionable, such as the inclusion of references to bioterrorism, the satisfaction given to the follow-up of the haitian disaster, the use of a highly centralized civil protection mechanism with many powers, the measures for the training of youth in a period when the budgetary room for manoeuvre is extremely limited. however, since the emphasis is on the principles of solidarity and subsidiarity and on international humanitarian aid standards, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. in recent years, the number and severity of disasters have increased. it was important that parliament renewed its call for the creation of a european civil protection force, capable of immediate deployment inside and outside the union. the shocking images of the earthquake in haiti, the floods in pakistan, the forest fires in southern europe, the oil spill in the gulf of mexico and fukushima have shocked the world and revealed the urgent need for an optimised european response at all stages of disaster management. i have always supported the demands of our assembly that the commission should make proposals for the pooling of the material and human resources available to the member states and for better coordination of these resources in support of a european civil protection force, which unfortunately is not forthcoming. each disaster brings its share of human tragedy and destruction. it is therefore essential to support europe's capacity to intervene for prevention, response, reconstruction and humanitarian action. in this area, it is up to us to put the principle of european solidarity into practice.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this report by our colleague auconie, which will facilitate the transfer of funds between the member states of the union. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which will also make it possible to improve the safety of persons and transported funds while preserving the social conditions of the staff.
in writing. i voted in favour of this amendment to the regulation on the export of dual-use goods and technology. the proposal for a regulation should make it possible to increase transparency in the export of goods and technology which can be used for civilian and military purposes.
in writing. i voted for the fidanza report on 'europe, the world's number one tourist destination, a new policy framework for tourism in europe'. this is the first report by the european parliament on tourism policy since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, which made it a european competence. the objective set out in the report is to ensure that the european union remains the world's leading tourist destination, through four pillars: quality, visibility, competitiveness and sustainable development.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which helps to support the european tourism sector by developing concrete measures for the players in this sector. a europe label should thus be created, a genuine recognition at european level of the quality of the services provided by the actors in our territories. the measures proposed also provide for greater visibility and diversification of tourism activities, which we must fully support in a difficult economic environment.
in writing. for many years now, europe has been the world's leading tourist destination. i am convinced of this, and as competition with other destinations around the world is growing, i welcome the adoption of this text, which aims to strengthen this position by providing innovative and original solutions. i would like to mention three of the measures proposed which are particularly close to my heart. the first is to strengthen regional tourism hubs, but also intra- and inter-regional tourism. the second, equally essential, is based on the principle that europe is founded on cultural and linguistic diversity and in fact requires that access to tourist sites for the greatest number of people be facilitated by various instruments. finally, the last measure to which i pay particular attention is the preservation and rehabilitation of industrial sites for tourism purposes, rather than their destruction.
in writing. i voted for the report by my colleague mr fidanza on european tourism. this report supports for the first time the creation of a genuine european tourism strategy, aimed at making europe the world's leading tourist destination. given the economic weight of this sector, particularly in france, and the cross-cutting nature of tourism, at the crossroads of many european policies (transport, environment, regional development, consumer protection), it is time to have a coherent vision and objectives to make the tourism sector more sustainable, competitive and a vehicle for growth. above all, europe must be promoted as a 'brand' in its own right, where cultural diversity is combined with the common heritage of the european nations. although member states and regions in some countries are the only ones to decide on their tourism policies, the union has a coordinating role to play and can improve certain existing legal frameworks such as the recognition of professional qualifications, to allow better mobility of tourism professionals, safety requirements in tourist facilities or package travel, to ensure greater clarity and legal certainty for consumers and businesses in the tourism sector.
in writing. tourism accounts for 12% of employment in europe. in the south-western euro-zone and in our region of languedoc-roussillon, it forms a large part of our economy, in all seasons and in all places. i voted in favour of the report because it sends a strong message for the first time in favour of the revival of european tourism. we are the world's leading tourist destination, our continent is attractive both for its history and its heritage. despite our potential, our tourism suffers from certain shortcomings. what is lacking is, first of all, the harmonization of our criteria for classifying sites, accommodation and catering establishments. the lack of transparency often leads to confusion for foreign tourists as well as european ones. finally, tourist tastes and habits are constantly changing. the offerings are now facing fierce competition and tourists have become real consumers. to achieve its full potential, europe must bring its tourism offerings into greater coordination and adapt to new markets. since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, europe has a decisive role to play.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report which makes tourism an eu priority, as an important driver of the economy and a breeding ground for employment. our parliament has adopted an ambitious strategy, identifying four pillars of action to ensure the attractiveness of the destination 'europe': competitiveness, visibility, quality and sustainability of tourism. tourism faces several challenges, particularly climate change, which has a major impact on the infrastructure and organisation of the industry. i think it is essential to work to limit its impact on the cycle of tourist seasons and on jobs. the way i prefer is to reduce the 'season' effect by developing alternative forms of tourism. it is also a solution to limit the precariousness of tourist jobs, which are generally seasonal. tourism will be the subject of an own budget from the 2014-2020 programming period. i will be vigilant to ensure that substantial support, coordinated with cohesion policy, is given to all forms of tourism, to strengthen the competitiveness of this sector and job security. tourism is intimately linked to our way of life, and the benefits expected from community tourism policy are all the more important.
in writing. reducing the number of road accident victims is an objective which should be shared by all member states. road safety is not just a matter of subsidiarity. it requires a collective awareness to ensure the same protection for all european drivers throughout the european union. parliament supports the objectives proposed in the future european road safety action programme until 2020. governments must take more radical measures, such as "zero tolerance" for drunk driving and speeding. but we must also insist on training and educating from an early age about the dangers of driving. the fight against road safety must also be achieved by improving the infrastructure of the secondary network and by developing a 'street code' in urban areas, particularly with the help of new technologies.
in writing. no one is happy about the number of road accident victims, but like its predecessors, the koch report on road safety at european level contains elements that cannot be accepted. first, the background of the usual suspicion on the behaviour of motorists. the report also includes the obligation to place an electronic bug on all vehicles, which will systematically record all traffic data, with no guarantee that it will only be used in the event of an accident: big brother will watch your car, and your car will be able to denounce you! we want to impose the generalization of the point permit, the equally generalized installation of the famous "educational" radars, which we now know become erratic on multiple or fast lanes, destabilize motorists and are therefore accident factors. the ban on all radar warning devices is counterproductive, since the authorities believe that radar is supposed to be placed in dangerous places and not in the most profitable ones! in short, the usual mixture of tautologies, good feelings, policing all the way, sprinkled with more pertinent thoughts on the quality of the road network and the importance of driver training. there's nothing exciting about it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the road safety resolution because i am convinced that the number of people killed on the roads of the european union could fall considerably in the coming years. the goal of halving their number by 2020 must be supported by simple measures such as the use of anti-start brake pads in commercial transport, reducing speed to 30km/h in residential areas and harmonising traffic rules. the text also recommends consistent harmonisation of road signs by 2013 and a maximum blood alcohol content harmonised at eu level with a scientifically based tolerance of 0/1000 for the first two years for novice drivers and permanently for professional drivers.
in writing. i abstained on all the amendments and on the final vote on this report, not because i am uninterested in road safety issues but because i think that the european union is already taking a great deal of action in this area and it seems to me that at this moment other priorities could be set. this is all the more so since the report goes into a rather hallucinating degree of detail (urban traffic speed, blood alcohol levels, ban on control sensors, harmonization of legislation on winter tyres and so on). the report also emphasizes, once again, a safety approach rather than a preventive one. on the other hand, it is astonishing that there is no mention of the working time of lorry drivers, whose tragic consequences are well known.
in writing. the schengen area has considerably increased the mobility of workers, tourists and goods, so that road safety has become a european priority. in 2009, 1.5 million people were injured and 35,000 people were killed in road accidents. we must at all costs synchronise our national efforts to avoid these human tragedies. europeans would not understand if we did not do what was necessary to combat road deaths. this is precisely the aim of our recently adopted strategy, which sets the target of halving the number of people killed on the roads by 2020. to do this, we must bring our national rules together in terms of traffic, signalling, technical controls and blood alcohol levels. it is no longer acceptable that the majority of accidents are caused by uncivil driving. the road cannot be a no-go zone: only by respecting common rules will we be able to save lives.
in writing. i am pleased that the report on dam infrastructure in developing countries was adopted by such a large majority. if mr deva's draft report was initially very questionable, the amendments of the green group adopted in the committee on development, of which i am the coordinator, have made it a particularly important text. it is a great victory, among other things, that parliament recognises that the belo monte dam in brazil can cause serious damage to the invaluable ecosystem and the precious biodiversity of the amazon and to indigenous peoples.
in writing. the report voted on tuesday by the european parliament on dam infrastructure in developing countries is positive on a number of points, such as population displacement linked to dam construction. the resolution also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's financial instruments are used to support the implementation of the eu's external policy. the risk of using large dams to prevent flood damage is also considered, as their safety is threatened by the increase and intensity of floods, the primary cause of which is global warming. the european parliament took the opportunity to call on the union to make greater commitments on the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions to meet its objectives of limiting climate change to 2°c above pre-industrial levels. however, one fundamental element is missing from this report: the recognition of water as a basic public good and the consequences that should follow. so i abstained.
in writing. access to adequate food is a universal human right and a major concern for developing countries. the report, which endorses the positive elements of the communication, deplores the lack of policies to tackle the root causes of food insecurity, such as: usurpation, lack of policy coherence (between trade, agriculture, fisheries and development), speculation, the impact of the cap, agrofuels, the liberalisation of financial markets, etc. to ensure food security, the report suggests addressing three major areas of concern: supporting small and medium-sized farmers, combating speculation and implementing coherent policies. as a member of the green group, i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. it is our responsibility to help developing countries meet food security challenges. financial speculation and the increased liberalisation of financial markets and trade in agricultural products have contributed significantly to the price volatility affecting agricultural commodity prices worldwide, with a worrying impact on developing countries. in this context, we must work towards the establishment of regulatory mechanisms to ensure a certain level of market stability and to reach fair and development-friendly trade agreements, which are essential for global food security. we must also aim to ensure fair pay for farmers whose primary mission is to feed the population.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by my colleague from die linke, gabi zimmer, which could help the european union to make progress in the fight against hunger in the world. it is intolerable that only 3% of european aid to developing countries goes to agriculture while 80% of the world's hungry people live in rural areas. this report clearly raises a number of questions and makes a number of proposals. it could have gone further, but it is the result of discussions with the other groups in the european parliament. it affirms the right to food, stresses the need to increase support for the agricultural sector, in particular for small farms, and to focus on sustainable production. it also opposes the high volatility of prices and advocates regulations to prevent speculation in foodstuffs. it also condemns the massive purchase of land by large companies and calls for the involvement of local communities in the negotiations and guarantees of their rights. i was able to note during the plenary that many proposals were adopted despite the opposition of the epp.
in writing. i regret the council's bad practice of including unilateral declarations on legislative acts adopted under codecision. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which stresses that these unilateral declarations cannot in any case produce legal effects. they also risk creating confusion, uncertainty and a lack of transparency in the community legislative process, which is far from satisfactory.
in writing. i voted for this report. parliament today reaffirmed its desire to see social, environmental and human rights standards as binding and legally binding in all trade agreements concluded by the union. in the face of the pressing demands of our citizens for more regulations and new forms of solidarity, the union must redefine a new doctrine for a different trade policy. if europe does not stand up for fairer trade, based on values and creating quality jobs in europe and the rest of the world, who will?
in writing. the european union needs a more coherent and better targeted trade policy. instead of trying to negotiate trade agreements at any price, it should focus on defending a number of principles such as the requirement of reciprocal market access with industrialized and emerging countries, respect for intellectual property rights or the needs of european industry and european farmers. similarly, the european union must develop a genuine strategy for access to raw materials and rare earths from a competitive, social and environmental point of view to ensure that european industry has efficient and secure access to resources in the years ahead and to increase research and development on the recycling of these rare materials in order to reduce its dependence on them. finally, if the european union is to maintain its key role in world trade, all current and future trade negotiations must be instruments for promoting european social and environmental standards.
in writing. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by mr caspary asking the commission to present a real trade strategy for the eu to integrate social and environmental components into agreements between the european union and its partners. i also welcome the rapporteur's proposal that the european agricultural sector be given special attention when new agreements are signed, so as not to jeopardise this key sector for the economy of our territories.
in writing. i supported the caspary report on a new trade policy for europe. the future of the european union's trade policy is at stake on several levels. of course, every effort must be made to bring the negotiations under way in the wto to a successful conclusion. in parallel, the european union must also continue to conclude bilateral free trade agreements. but our trading partners are also our competitors and that is why these discussions must be conducted with no naivety. i am therefore pleased to see that this report advocates reciprocity and mutual benefit in our agreements with our trading partners. the removal of non-tariff barriers must also be one of our objectives, because they too often hinder our trade: more regulatory convergence with our partners, more concrete results in the high-level structured dialogues with china, japan and the united states: these are the paths we must follow. the same is true of international public procurement: the objective is not to close our markets and give in to protectionism, but rather to ensure that the degree of openness of public procurement in europe is offset by the same degree of access to public procurement in third countries for union suppliers.
in writing. a thorough reflection on europe's trade strategy is needed, for example in view of the decline in global exports of goods, which fell from 19% in 1999 to 17.1% in 2009. such a strategy must be based on a careful analysis of current trends in international trade and the internal and external development of the union, as well as on the diversity of european enterprises, their know-how and technological advances. negotiations within the world trade organisation and free trade agreements are the preferred tools for a multilateral approach and market access. the drafting of new agreements should not make us forget to take account of other policies such as corporate social responsibility, agricultural policy, job creation and job security and the policy of combating poverty within and outside the union's borders.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because it calls on the commission to come forward quickly with a genuine long-term strategy for the union's trade policy. i particularly support the idea that free trade agreements are important instruments of this new strategy. why would you do that? the multilateral negotiations are at a standstill and we cannot expect any tangible results; they also help to communicate the union's values by including basic social and environmental standards. i also support the idea that parliament is committed to fighting poverty outside the union. of course, trade cannot be the only remedy. but when combined with other eu policies, instruments such as the generalised system of preferences or economic partnership agreements add real value to development policy. finally, i think it is crucial to note that the union, which is the most open market in the world, is struggling to obtain reciprocity from its trading partners. the concept of 'positive reciprocity' incorporated in this report should eventually facilitate access for our companies to foreign markets.
in writing. on 27 september, the european parliament adopted a report, pompously entitled 'a new trade policy for europe in the context of the europe 2020 strategy', which is nothing new. the european parliament is firmly committed to a vision of international agreements dominated by economic needs alone and reaffirms that the opening up of markets and access to them remains the main objective. while humanitarian, development and environmental issues can no longer be dismissed, 'the commission must give the union's trade interests a high level of priority' and other policies can only be considered in terms of their impact on those trade policies. that's all there is to it. in other words, the european union is not likely to be disturbed by this report. it is always economic interests and the fight against distortions of competition that prevail over everything else, and in particular the interests of the people, whether they live in the european union or in the countries of the south.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which gives a fair assessment of european trade policy and guides its renewal. to maintain its position as the world's leading trading power, the european union must encourage free trade and the conquest of new markets, but not at any price. we must negotiate trade agreements without naivety and impose the principle of reciprocity. these requirements must of course be adapted to the level of development and the sectors of activity of our partners. i believe that the union must adopt an integrated approach to its trade policy, since it covers many issues: competitiveness of production, socioeconomic, health and environmental standards. that is why i believe that it is no longer possible to write blank cheques to our partners in bilateral agreements or at the wto. we cannot accept any longer the continuation of unfair competition which weakens our businesses and our workforce. it would be tragic to sacrifice our economic, social and agricultural model on the altar of short-term considerations. when it comes to our trade agreements, realism and a sense of responsibility must prevail over the uncertainty of the expected economic gains. globalized trade must not be unbalanced trade.

of the european union to the entitlement of all people, wherever and whoever they are, to enjoy the full range of human rights and to do so without discrimination or the fear of discrimination. around the world, the issues of gender identity and sexual orientation continue to be used as a pretext for serious human rights violations: lesbian, gay, bi-sexual, transgender and intersex people are still subject to persecution, discrimination and ill-treatment, and that ill-treatment often involves extreme forms of violence. there are 80 countries which still criminalise same-sex relations between consenting adults, and seven which apply the death penalty. let us be clear: this is incompatible with international human rights law. it is a cause for which i was proud to fight in my native country, and it is a cause which i take up now on behalf of the 27 member states of the european union. we continue to protest against these abuses and to offer practical support on how to end discrimination and to encourage inclusiveness. through the channel of the united nations, the european union takes this message to the world: 15 of our member states were part of the group which prepared the statements on ending acts of violence and other human rights violations based on sexual orientation and gender identity, which was agreed by 85 countries at the un human rights council in march this year. we also welcomed the resolution on human rights, sexual orientation and gender identity tabled by south africa and adopted at the council three months ago. elsewhere in the un system, the eu has supported lgbt rights in the ngo committee of the un economic and social council, and in december 2008 we were instrumental in delivering a un general assembly statement on human rights, sexual orientation and gender identity which had the support of nearly 70 countries on five continents. that statement reaffirmed the principle of non-discrimination and condemned all executions and arrests made on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity. it calls on all states to decriminalise homosexuality, especially including capital punishment. the eu is an organisation of values, and it brings those values into the heart of its relationship with its partners beyond its borders. with its african, caribbean and pacific partners, for instance, we proposed the amendment of article 8 in the cotonou partnership agreement. we wanted to adapt that non-discrimination clause to the language of the lisbon treaty by introducing a reference to sexual orientation. the acp side could not accept the proposal, and a compromise was agreed which uses the language of the 1948 universal declaration on human rights. this says that the dialogue shall focus on discrimination of any kind such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status. we knew that a matter of principle had to be raised. and we will keep raising it. madam president, i want to set out briefly some of the practical examples of how we work. over the last year we have raised the same principles in uganda and malawi: in uganda, against a proposed parliamentary bill further criminalising homosexuality and raising serious human rights issues, and in malawi against the long prison sentences imposed on a gay couple. we spoke out and made public statements together with members of this house and ngos, and we worked behind the scenes with our delegations to argue the case for justice and human rights with these two governments. in this we succeeded. the eu also uses our regular human rights dialogues with individual countries to promote tolerance and non-discrimination for lgbt people. in countries like moldova, those dialogues have resulted in expert-level follow-up, and in countries like russia, croatia, turkey, montenegro and brazil the union has used its instrument for democracy and human rights to support local and international ngos in their campaigns against discrimination. our action has ranged from physical protection, which we offered to lgbt people who had received death threats in the wake of the assassination of david kato in uganda, to the practical promotion which saw 4 000 people attend a gay pride march in la paz, bolivia. we can always do more to promote awareness throughout our delegations worldwide and guide them in their work. in june we adopted a guide called ‘a toolkit to promote the enjoyment of all human rights by lesbian, gay, bi-sexual and trans-gender people’. i much appreciated the support of this house and joint working in order to produce this toolkit. it sets out ways to bring about decriminalisation, promote equality before the law and in society, and support and protect those who campaign for lbgt human rights. it also gives guidance on taking this issue onto the international stage in the un. so we stand by the principles of human rights and we articulate that view. so, too, do we give practical support to establishing those principles. we cannot allow discrimination over sexuality and gender anymore than we can allow it over colour and creed. human rights are as indivisible as they are universal.

in writing. in the light of current international developments, the management of migration and refugee flows is a challenge to which the european union must respond swiftly. the draft jędrzejewska report, which i supported, is in this direction. the mediterranean countries of europe, including france, are the most exposed to the problem. in a spirit of solidarity, the european union has therefore committed to providing additional funds of €43.5 million to help the member states most exposed to these flows. the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union (frontex) and the european refugee fund will be the main beneficiaries.
in writing. the eu's 2011 budget was increased to €52.2 million in commitments to better manage migration flows and refugee flows. the additional funds will be used to help member states most affected by these flows, and to strengthen maritime controls carried out by frontex, the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders. this increased funding stems from the aftermath of the arab spring in terms of migration and a request from european leaders. beyond this increase, if we really want to help the countries, both in the european union and in the southern mediterranean, then we must finally develop a real immigration policy. this is the only way to deal with the issue of migration in a calm and responsible way.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the council's position on the draft amending budget. the report endorses the council's position. this budgetary change allows for more resources to be allocated to frontex, the external borders fund, the european return fund and the european refugee fund. frontex has a fundamental role and should be given the means to fulfil its tasks. the importance of these various funds should not be overlooked either. this amendment allows recent events in north africa to be taken into account and the resulting migration and refugee flows to be managed appropriately. the funds allocated come from the under-implemented energy networks part of the european economic recovery plan.
in writing. the budgetary amendment proposal which the commission is proposing to us to approve is a shameful mixture of funding for the hunt for immigrants and funding for the reception of refugees. i can't possibly vote against it, wanting the second part. i cannot possibly vote for, rejecting the first part. i'm forced to abstain.
in writing. following the democratic revolutions in the arab countries, the union decided to increase the allocation of its budget for managing migration and refugee flows (heading 3a) for 2011. the union is taking one of its first concrete decisions in response to the uprisings in the arab countries, even though its support for them, which we know from the past, has been delayed and hesitant, apart from humanitarian aid. the promises of financial aid, especially to tunisia, are long in coming and remain for the most part beautiful speeches. this decision is all the more questionable as this increase is taken from the budget for the 'european energy networks for economic recovery plan', which could have been used otherwise. it concerns the strengthening of frontex and thus border control and aid to refugees, which we know is not easy to achieve. it is a reflection of the contradictions of the union. so i decided not to.
in writing. as always, i abstained on the vote on this new mobilisation of the globalisation adjustment fund. i cannot oppose the european union's financing of individual training measures for workers who have been made redundant, in this case workers employed by shoe factories in portugal. however, i cannot support the very principle of the globalisation adjustment fund which, by means of one-off interventions, on specific companies and regions and within the framework of strict criteria, serves to finance social plans. it seems to me that the european union is thus giving itself a good conscience at the expense of the social consequences of its economic deregulation policy. many workers across europe are affected by the crisis; they all deserve the support of the european union and they are waiting for the establishment of a social europe that ensures that workers' rights are finally put before the interests of shareholders. the globalisation adjustment fund is a mere caulk on a wooden leg and is by no means an appropriate response to the crisis.
in writing. in the face of the economic and financial crisis, the european union must be resolute and ambitious. the house is voting on the so-called '6 package' or 'governance package', which contains six legislative proposals to strengthen european economic governance. the wortmann-kool report is intended to amend and strengthen the stability and growth pact, which in its present form is inadequate. this report provides for preventive measures which should make it possible to anticipate any new crisis. it aims to strengthen budgetary discipline by monitoring the increase in government spending, and by establishing a 'european semester' where european and national policy-makers will meet to discuss economic issues. the european commission may also make recommendations to the member states. i am convinced that economic and budgetary coordination between the european states must be profoundly strengthened, and i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr wortmann-kool.
in writing. the economic governance package was adopted. i voted against (for the vast majority of the reports) because i think we are too late with these reports. we are completely out of step with the current crisis situation. the crisis in europe is such that there is an urgency... but an urgency to do something else: such a package might make sense in a period of stability but it seems very far away today. it is a mistake to focus on tightening sanctions and rules without proposing a large-scale economic, environmental and social investment project. austerity is already a reality for all the peoples of europe; what we need is a positive vision for the future. the eurobond project, which is mentioned in my colleague s. goulard's report, is one of the ways of overcoming the crisis. it should be noted that these european loans should not only be used to repay the debt but should also be used for investment. to finance future projects in the fields of energy, transport, research and innovation, we need these so-called 'leapfrog projects' now, not in three or five years' time.
in writing. the adoption of the economic governance package is a historic step for the euro area and the union as a whole. the greek sovereign debt crisis is daily proof of the need for genuine european economic governance and a strong, credible and respected stability and growth pact. we will only get out of this crisis by permanently restoring our public finances. the measures we have adopted today will strengthen the stability and growth pact and improve the surveillance mechanisms to prevent and correct macroeconomic imbalances that could lead to contagion. strong and courageous action is needed to address all the factors that have contributed to the worsening of the crisis. i welcome the announcement by commission president josé manuel barroso of the creation of a financial transaction tax. i have been campaigning for several months for the creation of such a tax, which president sarkozy and chancellor merkel have called for. in march, the european parliament called on the european commission to make proposals to this end. i am glad that this appeal has finally been heard.
in writing. i voted against the wortmann-kool report because it does not in any way ensure a lasting solution to the financial, economic and social crisis. by limiting itself to a punitive dimension, the economic governance package locks member states into austerity policies. instead of providing policies to stimulate consumption and investment for the future, this report makes citizens pay for the crisis by stifling growth and destroying jobs, and will therefore effectively prevent the return to budgetary balance. the consolidation of public finances must not be achieved without a policy of growth and recovery, and this economic governance package is nothing but an abdication to the omnipotence of the financial markets and the rating agencies. there was another way; the european right will have to bear the heavy responsibility for not having chosen it.
in writing. after a year of debate, parliament is putting its package of measures for a new economic governance of the union to the vote of this house. the aim is to require member states to keep their deficits below 3% of gdp and their public debt below 60% of gdp. national budgets will therefore be monitored and evaluated upstream by the commission and the member states; this is called the european semester. then, recommendations will be given if the debt reduction policies are not followed. and if this continues, the bad students will be threatened with a demand for a deposit of funds equivalent to 0.2 percent of their gdp, this deposit turning into a fine if the bad student refuses to comply with the rules. control, evaluation, recommendations and then sanctions - that is what the sovereign peoples of europe will have to endure from a commission without democratic legitimacy. this economic governance package is a real stewardship, an unacceptable attack on the sovereignty and freedom of peoples to decide their own future. worse, all this will be of no use because the austerity plans that will be imposed will strangle growth and dramatically and irreversibly accentuate the crisis and then bankruptcy.
in writing. this text organises the commission's control of all the components of national budgets in the context of the european semester. it prepares the arbitration between the "good students", those who will keep their budgets between budget balance and 2% of gdp, and the "bad students", those who will not. there are penalties. states which reform their pension systems will be exempted. the commission will also be able to provide the necessary information to the member states in order to enable them to take action. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. i vote against this text and denounce its intolerable aggression against the popular sovereignty of the nations.
in writing. the european parliament today takes a historic step in the fight against the crisis that is shaking europe and dangerously threatening the euro area. the vote on the governance package that has been under discussion for over a year is an important step forward that we should welcome. the six texts in this package reflect a delicate balance between national sovereignty and the need for european coordination in budgetary matters. it will also ensure the viability of the single currency and the confidence of the markets. sanctions against irresponsible states will no longer be left to the arbitrary bargaining of the council, but will be the subject of transparent measures implemented under the aegis of the european commission, comprising a preventive and a curative component, intended to restore sound management of public deficits. we must nevertheless be clear: these measures are essential, but they will not be sufficient. two conditions are intrinsically linked to the success of the system: a real investment in growth on the one hand, and a deeper integration and solidarity of the european economies on the other, thanks in particular to the creation of a european ministry of finance and the introduction of eurobonds. let us not shrink from this historic occasion.
in writing. prevention is better than cure! the serious difficulties faced by most member states today were directly revealed by the crisis of 2008. let's stop making decisions when it's too late and we have no choice! it is easier and cheaper to anticipate and deal with problems in depth in advance than to deal with them superficially afterwards. this is the whole point of this directive, which aims to guarantee transparency, accountability and budgetary coordination in the euro area. to avoid the mistakes of the past, we take responsibility for the introduction of a preventive component in this monitoring, which i regard as the necessary complement to the corrective component. the commission will have the legitimacy to carry out this monitoring and will thus be able to warn states which do not respect the rules they have accepted. the aim is to take the bull by the horns while there is still time, before the sovereign debt crisis reaches the proportions it has reached in greece. these measures are, in my view, an essential step towards strengthening our single currency and returning to growth and stability.
in writing. if a financial and economic crisis in the euro area is to be prevented, effective budgetary surveillance is important. that is why i voted in favour of the goulard report, which proposes a series of sanctions against member states which depart from the stability and growth pact. the member states meeting in council will thus be able to punish a 'bad pupil' by means of recommendations or by asking him to make a deposit, with or without interest, to correct his excessive deficit. if these measures prove insufficient, he will have to pay a fine. interest on deposits and fines will be allocated to the european financial stability facility and then to the european stability mechanism, which will replace it in 2013. the european parliament is associated with these budgetary surveillance measures in the framework of the economic dialogue . the member state concerned by the sanctions will thus be able to express its views on its budgetary situation to the council. finally, as part of the strengthening of economic governance, the european commission will prepare a report on euro-bonds by the end of the year.
in writing. the 'six-pack' gives more weight to the current stability and growth pact (sgp), through better quality controls and earlier deficits and debt. it innovates by forcing policy makers to act quickly to restore the health of economies threatened by macroeconomic imbalances, such as bubbles in the housing price sector or a decline in competitiveness. finally, it aims to ensure that statistics, which are essential for sound budgetary decisions and budgetary control, are more accurate, in particular through more independent collection. but this text is only a first stone in the building. other decisions will have to be taken to strengthen economic governance (creation of a european monetary fund and a bond market, mutualisation of part of the debt, etc.). likewise, decisive action in favour of education, innovation and competitiveness will be needed.
in writing. i voted in favour of the six reports in the legislative package on the reform of economic governance because it provides a number of answers to the serious crisis facing the european union, but also and above all because, in the face of the great instability we are currently experiencing, confidence must be restored. these measures will certainly not bring europe out of the rut it is in, but they provide the first foundations for what we must move towards. i am thinking in particular of the creation of a genuine economic government for the euro area, the mutualisation of debt, the introduction of euro-bonds and the creation of a financial transaction tax, all 'measures' which i have been calling for for many months.
in writing. i voted against the goulard report because it does not in any way ensure a lasting solution to the financial, economic and social crisis. by limiting itself to a punitive dimension, the economic governance package locks member states into austerity policies. instead of providing policies to stimulate consumption and investment for the future, this report makes citizens pay for the crisis by stifling growth and destroying jobs, and will therefore effectively prevent the return to budgetary balance. the consolidation of public finances must not be achieved without a policy of growth and recovery, and this economic governance package is nothing but an abdication in the face of the omnipotence of the financial markets and rating agencies. there was another way; the european right will have to bear the heavy responsibility for not having chosen it.
in writing. this report sets out the sanctions that will be imposed on those states which do not comply with the european commission's injunctions. it is not concerned for a moment about the consequences of such sanctions on the people and the legitimacy of the commission to sanction elected governments. the only exception proposed is public debates to be held in the european parliament on the proposal of the european parliament. not in the state concerned. shouldn't the people be involved in the plot that's being played out against them? i pledge myself never to let the commission strike france. i vote against it.
in writing. in the light of the greek crisis and the worrying situation in several other member states with very large deficits, it is essential to ensure that fiscal discipline is a reality in the future. i am relieved that the long months of tough negotiations on the 'governance package' between parliament and the council have finally come to fruition - although i would of course have liked it to happen sooner. the regulation, which concerns budgetary surveillance in the euro area, establishes a system of sanctions - a deposit of 0.2% of the gdp of the member state in default, with or without interest - aimed at better enforcing the preventive and corrective components of the stability and growth pact. it also aims to combat inaccurate statements by member states on their public deficit or public debt data by means of a system of fines for those who have been negligent. the text also calls on the commission to submit a report to parliament and the council before the end of 2011 on the possibility of issuing 'euro bonds'. i look forward to the commission's next steps in this direction.
in writing. the current crisis has shown that member states are suffering rather than acting. the european union has therefore decided to put forward a package of six proposals aimed at strengthening european economic governance. i therefore support a more involved and ambitious europe in this area so that it can anticipate any new crisis. to this end, the european union has decided to set up a new system capable of preventing macroeconomic imbalances, especially trade imbalances. this system, which is also included in the haglund report, will introduce a series of measures which will complement those contained in the ferreira report. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european stability mechanism (esm) to support the implementation of the euro. as i am in favour of increased economic surveillance, i voted in favour of the haglund report.
in writing. i abstained on the vote on this report. it provides for sanctions by member states in the event of macroeconomic imbalances without providing itself, or the legislative package to which it belongs, with the economic governance structures that europe so badly needs. at a time when the crisis is striking deeply at the heart of the european people, the european parliament cannot send the message of austerity, which is incomprehensible, inexplicable to the citizens and which is damaging to the european project. moreover, this report is not ambitious enough. we must be careful not to run public deficits, but not at the expense of social justice and the investment in the future that is necessary for a sustainable economy. in other words, we need more europe to deal with the crisis: a more complete fiscal, social and political union and a european budget with its own resources.

in writing. the regulation will enable the commission to impose annual fines on states which fail to comply with its authority. the sums thus obtained will be allocated to the eu-imf stability fund, the effects of which are being felt by the greek, irish and portuguese peoples. the only drawback the council has made is a graduated deposit with interest and penalties which does not change the substance of the case. i am voting against this text.
in writing. we cannot have a common currency on the one hand and an uncoordinated management of public money on the other. the current events show that the lack of convergence and the imbalance between the european public accounts are breaches into which speculators seek to take advantage of the difficulties of the euro area. today we are reacting so that we do not leave this opportunity to the financial markets. for this, my political family has had the courage to allow the development of preventive and curative instruments which will strengthen the stability and growth pact. while the deficit-control method has so far relied on the goodwill of states, the commission now has the possibility of recommending financial sanctions, ranging from cash deposits to financial fines, for states that fail to meet their obligations. by adopting these measures to limit public deficits, the union is avoiding the devastating reflex of withdrawing into itself, is showing its determination to emerge from this crisis on the upside and, above all, is reminding that sharing a common currency requires maximum solidarity, but also sharing responsibilities.

the president of the commission told us so strongly yesterday, and everyone mentioned it in the subsequent debate on the state of the union - are not closed, to say the least. in this context, it seems to us absolutely essential to extend this system as it stands, that is to say by allowing this recourse in the event of 500 redundancies, either in a pool of jobs or in a company, and to allow co-financing. that is the main message that this parliament wants to convey, especially to the council, which we urgently ask - i perhaps regret that it is not here to hear our message - to unblock this situation. it would be quite paradoxical if, at a time when greece is at stake, one of the proposed tools, namely the mobilisation of the structural funds to deal with crisis situations - where we have already adapted the system to this end - were not extended. in our resolution we give some indications of the future reform that the commission will propose to us, and that is the subject of our debate this morning. in this future revision, parliament proposes, for example, that the situations of restructuring and those of multinationals, which may possibly use this mechanism to compensate for their relocation strategy, be examined. but we also indicate and, as the chairman of the committee on employment and social affairs, as you know, we examine, on a case-by-case basis, each mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. we appreciate how valuable this tool is in bringing to life a concept that is at the heart of the european union's strategy, the europe 2020 strategy, in bringing to life social innovation so that, when a situation linked to the effects of globalisation and the crisis is to be examined, there is a mobilization of social dialogue and that the situation of each person is examined according to his or her ability to enter phases of transition, training to be able to take on new jobs tomorrow and return to work. it is, from the point of view of european legislation, a very exemplary tool. of course, there are things that will probably need to be re-examined, refined, corrected, but this is not the time. we shall have this debate in the context of the financial perspective, the new proposals which the commission will put on the table. the urgent need now is not to interrupt this system by 31 december this year and to allow it to be extended. i hope this house will join us. we shall then have a debate on the conditions under which this fund is to be applied to multinational companies and on the conditions for its sustainability in budgetary terms, in order to ascertain exactly where these resources should be allocated in order to finance this action.
