in writing. we have just reiterated our support for romania and bulgaria's accession to schengen. reaffirming our position from before the summer, we adopted this resolution by a large majority, urging all member states to take the decision to extend the schengen area to these two countries. the european commission considers that romania and bulgaria have met the criteria and should not be prevented from joining. however, the matter was blocked in the council by several member states who considered it necessary to add certain criteria. i fully agree that more attention should be paid to such problematic issues as the fight against corruption and organised crime. however, these criteria should apply in the same way to all member states. in the meantime, a compromise must be found in the council for those countries which currently meet the schengen criteria.
in writing. the problem is not what criteria must be met to be able to be part of the schengen area, if others must be added on a case-by-case basis, the problem is schengen itself. this agreement has considerably weakened the external borders of the european union, creating a breath of fresh air for illegal immigration applicants at their most vulnerable points. one of the countries concerned today shares a border with turkey, which is both a source and transit country for this illegal immigration. greece, although "assisted" by frontex, has enormous difficulties in controlling its own borders with this neighbor, to the point that it is considering building a wall! the control of frontiers, including internal frontiers, and the flow of goods, capital and people across them is becoming more and more vital for our countries. control is not about closing the door. everyone should understand that. i am aware of the harmful effects of schengen on my country and wish it to get out of it, so i refuse to let others suffer the same fate!
in writing. the free movement of persons must be organised with safeguards. we must develop a permanent monitoring of the application of the schengen agreements, in order to see whether each state is playing by the rules. bulgaria and romania have undertaken major reforms to reorganise their border management, investing heavily in their law enforcement services. their institutional and legal framework has clearly been strengthened, as evidenced by the latest schengen evaluation reports. i regret, however, that the proposal to consolidate the schengen acquis by incorporating additional criteria on organised crime and corruption has been rejected.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution to reiterate my support for romania and bulgaria's accession to the schengen area. this, which can only be done by the unanimous vote of the members of the council, was blocked on 22 september. i think it is indecent to continue to block these memberships. this leads to a situation of double standards, which is contrary to reality. romania and bulgaria fulfil the criteria for accession to schengen as laid down in the texts, which finland and the netherlands cannot ignore. corruption, which is highlighted in order to deny membership, although it must be combated vigorously, is not one of the technical criteria. changing the rules at the end of the process is not based on any legal justification, and the refusal of access to the free movement area to these countries is a political decision. these countries, which already play a special role at the eu's external borders, cannot be treated as if they were secondary. the eu must continue its commitment to the fundamental acquis of the free movement of persons.
in writing. refusing romania and bulgaria to join the schengen area is a de facto admission that not all states are treated equally in the european union. but to accept their accession would be to undermine the freedom and sovereignty of the netherlands and finland, which are now openly opposed to it. if we recognize the rights of some, it will be at the expense of the rights of others. this dilemma clearly exposes the absurdity of the schengen treaty, which entrusts the responsibility for the surveillance and protection of the borders of the 25 member states of the area to the peripheral countries of europe. giving such responsibility can only be done in trust. the dutch and finns do not have confidence. without schengen, we would not be in this situation. each state would be free and responsible for its own borders without requiring a third party to assume responsibility that it no longer bears. the treaty must therefore be revised as a matter of urgency so that everyone can be in control of his own home. it's not a step back, it's just a step back into the good old days. i therefore vote against this resolution.

in writing. in the european union, the population with a disability represents 80 million people, or 16% of the total population. unfortunately, their employment rate is currently only 45%. in addition, their poverty rate is 70% higher than the average. i therefore voted in favour of this own-initiative report, which is part of the european strategy 2010-2020, one of whose objectives is to achieve an employment rate of 75% of the working population, because it calls on the member states and the commission to promote the integration of disabled people, in particular by facilitating access to the labour market. the report also stresses the need to ensure universal, effective and non-discriminatory access for people with disabilities to social protection, social benefits, health care and education, as integration into working life and financial independence are important factors for social integration. finally, other measures are also proposed: the creation of a 'european committee on disability' to assess progress in the european strategy, the adoption by the member states of sign language as an official language, the adoption of a european mobility card to reduce obstacles to freedom of movement (to study, work, travel).
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the mobility and integration of disabled people, which takes account of a problem that is often overlooked. while 80 million europeans suffer from disabilities, few measures are being taken to fully integrate them into our societies. the aim is to improve the accessibility of goods and services to disabled people so as not to add additional barriers to disability. access to new technologies, for example, could be developed to facilitate their use by people with disabilities. the report calls on the member states to ratify the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the commission is proposing to set up a european disability committee. it calls for improvements in the design of urban spaces and transport, for better consideration in education and in general in policies of the specific needs of disabled people. it stresses the importance of access to employment for disabled people and of combating poverty, which particularly affects this part of the population. it is a necessary text which recalls that equal treatment must apply to all, and not leave disabled people behind.
in writing. we all have a disability at some point in our lives. infrastructure, whatever it may be, transport, community care services, education, media, culture, everything must be designed to be accessible to all citizens. the 'universal design' must prevail in all areas. the austerity policies which the european union is currently imposing on the peoples of europe do not allow the implementation of the ambitious policies which the general interest, and therefore the interests of disabled people, requires. worse still, the precarious situation of all and everyone which austerity leads to aggravates the situation of the disabled. the text sets ambitious goals, but does not give the means to achieve them. i shall abstain from voting in order not to give credence to this hypocritical text.
in writing. 80 million european citizens are living with a disability today - that's more than one in six europeans. these people, who are often the victims of discrimination, are hard hit by exclusion, unemployment and precariousness - only 30 to 40% of them are employed, 70% have a poverty rate above the average. this report deals with the two major challenges faced by disabled people: mobility on the one hand and social inclusion on the other. ambitious policies must be undertaken at european level as soon as possible to ensure their access to the labour market and genuine freedom of movement. the proposals of mr kósa, concerning the improvement of physical access to public places and the creation of a european mobility card, the introduction of disability allowances and specific support for parents of disabled children, go in this direction, and i welcome them. i also welcome the inclusion in the report of the challenge of an ageing population - the rate of disability for people over 65 will increase by 77% in the next few years. this increase in the number of vulnerable people requires us to make a choice now for a more inclusive model of society.
in writing. as highlighted in the europe 2020 strategy, eu public procurement policy is central to achieving the objectives of innovation, competitiveness and the environment. this policy needs to be modernised. the rühle report, which i supported, makes several recommendations: a clearer legal framework; better exploitation of the potential of public procurement, for example by focusing on the most advantageous offer in the long term (economic, social and environmental benefits) rather than on the lowest price criterion; the commission will also be proposing a simplification of procedures to improve access to public procurement, particularly for smes.
in writing. public procurement accounts for about 17% of the eu's gdp. this is the importance of good policy in this area in times of crisis. the current rules on public procurement should be amended to better support the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. contracts should be awarded not only to the lowest bidder but also to the most innovative or to the one offering the most attractive environmental or social benefits. it would also be useful to have a clause in the public procurement agreement allowing the eu to give preference to european producers, especially smes.
in writing. in the resolution on public procurement, the european parliament reinforced the commission's proposal for a social europe: the most significant advance is that local authorities should no longer opt for the economically lowest bid, but for the most advantageous one, for example, one that integrates environmental aspects. the question of subcontractors is also taken into account in order to avoid abuses in terms of working conditions and worker safety. however, there is still progress to be made in european public procurement policy. the commission must in particular impose the principle of reciprocity on its trading partners: if the union agrees to open its public procurement to operators from third countries, then european companies must also have access to public contracts and works in these non-eu countries. european enterprises and jobs in europe must be a priority of trade openness. the commission must ensure that its next directive on public procurement serves the dual purpose of more quality jobs and quality services for users.
in writing. this text contains several ecological considerations and a concern for the respect of collective agreements which i approve. but he focuses his remarks on respect for the sacred principle of free competition. it also welcomed the green paper produced by the commission last january, which advocated, among other things, a downward revision of the requirements of public authorities to promote competition. the public interest is once again sacrificed to liberalism. i vote against it.
in writing. public procurement - which represents 17% of the eu's gdp - is a major instrument in supporting economic growth, innovation, employment, environmental protection and the efficiency of public spending in europe. ensuring that they function optimally is therefore a crucial challenge for the european economy. this report, which i support, sets out six priority objectives for the reform of the current legislation which the commission should propose in the coming months. among these is the improvement of access for smes to public procurement. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment. i'm all for it. other objectives include the achievement of better value for money, in particular by replacing the lowest price criterion with the most economically advantageous offer, taking into account the life cycle of the relevant goods as a whole.
in writing. this report is an important step ahead of the european commission's formal proposal, which is due to be published at the end of the year, and i therefore voted in favour of it. the rapporteur has in particular argued that the criterion of the lowest price is no longer appropriate in the present context, and i support that. indeed, there is a cost to lowering the price of a bid by flouting basic social or environmental standards. and that cost is borne by the citizens, not by the company that wins the market. this is no longer acceptable, and we must change this rule. the same applies to commercial naivety: when our companies apply for non-european markets, they are almost always excluded. on the other hand, foreign firms can easily bid for, and even win, european public contracts. the union must use all the instruments at its disposal to open up the public procurement markets of our partners in a reciprocal manner. this will ensure that european companies benefit from fair and equal conditions of competition when they try their luck abroad.
in writing. concerned about the respect of the fundamental right of every european worker to move freely within the eu, i voted in favour of the resolution tabled by my colleague, traian ungureanu. the resolution encourages the integration of workers from the new eu members, in particular bulgaria and romania, into the european market and denounces prejudice. we must fight discrimination against workers on the basis of their nationality: this is one of the major foundations of the european project!
in writing. the figures are known. the mobility of europeans remains extremely low: only 2.3% of eu residents reside in a member state other than their own. yet 17% would intend to work in another member state, and almost half would consider looking for a job in another member state if they were made redundant. these figures reveal the gap between a so-called integrated single market and a european area of free movement of people and workers which remains rather compartmentalized. the reasons for this are many: social, linguistic, cultural, legal and administrative obstacles. enabling eu citizens to enjoy the full benefits of the free movement they enjoy under the treaties remains an objective to be achieved. this requires improved coordination of national systems, whether in terms of social security, pensions or the recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications. too many people in europe are still hampered in their life plans by the lack of coordination and recognition of national rules.
in writing. i supported the adoption of these measures, which should thus allow for better implementation of eu legislation in this area. these measures to harmonize and combat discrimination within the union are a real opportunity for our peoples and allow the maintenance of temporary barriers to the opening of our markets to the citizens of the new member states. with these measures we should regularize the current status of european workers.
in writing. i supported this report which calls on the european commission to give itself the means to make worker mobility and equal rights a reality throughout the union. the main point to be taken from this text is our unconditional demand that the transitional provisions introduced by certain member states restricting access to the labour market for certain european nationals be brought to an end. so france, along with others, must lift these restrictions on bulgarian and romanian nationals as soon as possible. this would be a great step forward, among other things, for the social inclusion of the roma. the principle of equal work, equal pay, which makes it possible to combat social dumping, and the fight against direct or indirect discrimination against migrant workers, should also be taken into account.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on measures to encourage the mobility of workers within the european union. the mobility of our citizens enables exchange and builds europe on a daily basis. the mobility of workers is all the more essential as it balances supply and demand in labour markets by meeting any labour needs that may arise. it thus contributes to making markets more efficient. many barriers still stand in the way of mobility. it's about taking them out. the report calls for the restrictions which still prevent some european citizens from working in another member state to be lifted. another pillar of the report is the call for greater recognition of diplomas to enable everyone to promote their training throughout europe. to facilitate mobility, social security and pension systems need to be coordinated so that workers' rights can be easily transferred. the principle of non-discrimination is also clearly reaffirmed. finally, information on the different mobility opportunities and related rights should be made more accessible.
in writing. this report reduces european workers to the condition of the internal market adjustment variable. it simply concedes that mobility must remain voluntary. it also advocates the liberalisation of regulated professions. i abstain because it enshrines the right of all european citizens and their family members to work in another member state. citizens are not commodities. the right to free movement cannot become a nomadic obligation for one's work.
in writing. living and working in any member state of the european union is one of the fundamental freedoms of european citizens. however, only 2.3% of them reside in a member state other than their country of origin. on the other hand, when asked about their intention to use this freedom in the future, 17% of europeans said yes. the difficulties faced by european citizens in this area need to be addressed, particularly in the current economic context. that is the spirit of my colleague traian ungureanu's report, which i support. in order to determine the nature and extent of these difficulties, the text calls on the commission to draw up a scoreboard of the obstacles faced by workers wishing to move to another member state. i think that's a great idea. as far as the solutions are concerned, ensuring better recognition of vocational qualifications in the eu is absolutely essential. i look forward to the commission's legislative proposal in this area. similarly, the possibility for migrant workers to benefit from the portability of their pension rights is a fundamental element in ensuring the effective exercise of acquired rights.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. the proposals it contains will make real progress for all european citizens. 48% of citizens plan to look for work in another eu country, but only 2% actually do so. this lag shows that there are still too many obstacles of all kinds (administrative burdens, problems with the recognition of diplomas, discrimination, lack of information, etc.) which discourage potential candidates. in the present economic context, however, the occupational and geographical mobility of workers makes it possible to match the supply of and demand for employment, and thus to reduce unemployment. it also helps to limit social and wage dumping. a long-term and comprehensive work programme, including european education systems (language teaching, harmonization of diplomas, exchanges), national employment agencies and enterprises, is a necessity. the union must play both a driving and coordinating role in policies so that citizens can fully benefit from the opportunities offered by free movement.
in writing. the eu's single market for services is a process under construction. i am convinced that its proper functioning is essential to generate growth and enhance competitiveness in europe, and i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs malgorzata handzlik. a review of the situation has made it possible to identify the remaining problems in consolidating the european internal market. the report calls in particular for the full operation of the single points of contact set up under the services directive. these offices enable european service providers to carry out their administrative procedures electronically. the report also denounces the delays in the implementation of the directive in some member states. however, it welcomed the european commission's initiative to carry out a mutual evaluation of the single market for services and called for such an evaluation to be further developed for crossborder services.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report by mr handzlik, which describes the process of mutual evaluation of the services directive and calls for better application of the european rules adopted in recent years in this field. better transposition of these rules should enable the european economy and the economies of our territories to benefit more from the positive effects of the single market for services.
in writing. the report regrets the delays in transposing the services directive and calls on the commission and the member states to go further in its application. i'm glad these failures happened. if the left front comes to power in france, it will repeal all the provisions transposing this harmful directive.
in writing. in the face of the economic and financial crisis, global economic governance needs to be reformed. therefore, my colleagues and i voted in favour of a responsible monetary policy and stronger financial regulation. we also call for the democratization of the international monetary fund (imf), the end of banking secrecy and a clear separation between deposit and speculative banking. finally, the role of the european union at the global level must be strengthened. it needs to speak with one voice, for example by having a single seat at the imf and the world bank.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because of the interesting proposals it contains to address the current global macroeconomic, monetary and financial imbalances. to achieve this, it stresses the need for and offers ways of strengthening the international organisations responsible for correcting these imbalances, based on the principles of legitimacy, transparency and accountability. in particular, it stressed the urgency of better governance of the global financial sector, including better cooperation between financial supervisors worldwide.
in writing. the next summit of the group of 20 industrialised and emerging countries (g20) will be held in cannes on 3 and 4 november. these 20 countries account for 85 percent of the world's economy and two-thirds of the world's population. the stated objective is to try to find concerted responses, in particular to finally strengthen international financial regulation and supervision to remedy the current imbalances. the g20 leaders are also invited to agree on the minimum common elements of a global financial transaction tax. in the context of a new global regulation, the imf should play a more important role. it will therefore have to operate more transparently, with a more equitable distribution of voting rights, and the election of its director-general will have to be carried out by a more open procedure. its mandate could be extended, not only to enhance international surveillance, but also to ensure better monitoring of systemically important economies. this new democratic accountability should become a requirement, not only for the imf, but also for the world bank and the g20.
in writing. as soon as the ink has dried on new european texts strengthening the foundations of the european superstate, we are in the process of creating a world financial government under the auspices of the imf! the art of using crises to pursue less-than-admitted ideological goals. without ever questioning the underlying reason that has brought us to the dramatic situation we are in: the financial globalisation of the economy. but this is not a scientific phenomenon, nor a historical fatality: it is simply the work of politicians who have made certain decisions at certain points in history, as the first of them, the choice of gatt instead of the havana agreements in the post-war years. a very clear choice in favour of ultraliberalism against regulated trade and the primacy of the political will of the states over the commercial interests of private actors. this choice was further aggravated by the marrakesh agreements and the creation of the wto, now headed by the socialist pascal lamy. that is to say, the collusion of the pseudo-elites ruling our states! globalization is also a matter of choice. it requires will and courage against all the lobbies of the profiteers of the system. we in the national front have that political will and that courage.
in writing. one thing to remember: making sdrs the new world currency of reference means that the dollar can no longer be. the rest of this text is a collection of liberal nonsense and inept projects. giving power to the imf, ignoring the un and its legislative committees - all this is appalling. i vote against it.
in writing. the subprime crisis, the trivialization of automated trading, or the downward spiral of speculation on the debt of certain states, show us that the current rules are inadequate and make us considerably vulnerable. it is high time we took back control of the financial economy, so that it serves the real economy! this must be achieved through courageous decisions by the international institutions dealing with the world economy (imf, world bank) and informal forums (g7, g20). i therefore welcome this report, which calls for the development of a financial transaction tax that can both limit high-frequency trading and create new revenue for states, regulate excessive speculation in the debt of states in difficulty, or even better control the rating agencies, which were partly responsible for the 2007 crisis. if the eu has decided to lead the way, by developing binding standards on all these points, it cannot be the only one to reform the system. emerging and developed countries must contribute to this global effort.
in writing. representing 5% of women in europe, single mothers face poverty and social exclusion. the european parliament's barbara matera has therefore proposed a series of measures to improve their situation and promote their integration into the workplace. as president of the association "women at the centre", i am deeply committed to solidarity and social inclusion actions for women. i therefore supported the proposal.
in writing. in recent decades, society has changed a lot. today, more and more single parents are raising their children. yet, 85 percent of single parents are women. hence the adoption of an own-initiative report on the situation of single mothers in europe. we are aware of the difficulties faced by these women and we ask that more attention be paid to them. one of the priorities today is to achieve a balance between work and private life: governments and companies must act in this direction in order to ensure working conditions that are more favourable to reconciling work and family life. among the proposals to be taken up in this report, i would like to highlight the major role that the esf can play in providing scholarships for single mothers or in supporting the resumption of education.
in writing. the european union must do more and better to help single mothers and their children. the economic crisis has further weakened these single-parent families, which are already highly exposed to poverty and social exclusion. 85% of these are women raising one or more children alone. given that european women earn on average 18% less than men, the picture of the fragility of single mothers is stark. to cope with the problems of these growing families, the resolution adopted in parliament proposes the setting up of 'home centres' capable of providing them with accommodation, advice and assistance in training and education. these measures to help single mothers should obviously be extended to men in the same situation.

in writing. the report has the immense merit of focusing on those who are often the most in demand in society: single mothers. trapped in a precarious situation made worse by the economic crisis, they struggle more than others to find decent work, decent housing, and to provide for their families. this is unacceptable. the text calls for action to be taken against unjustified dismissals. he insists that they have access to accessible childcare and housing assistance. he wants single mothers to be given appropriate scholarships. it is a pity that the aim of the commission is to provide only 50% of care for children aged 0 to 3 and that it does not ask for worthy employment contracts for those it is advocating. i vote to approve the denunciation and the proposed advances.
in writing. europe is characterised by the development of single-parent families, mostly composed of single mothers: 85% of single parents are women. these families often find themselves in difficult situations: 32% of these single parents are at risk of poverty, compared with 12% of couples with children. the government must pay more attention to these fragile families. that is what barbara matera is asking for in her report, and i support it. the text encourages member states to adopt public policies, in particular in the fields of education, public health, employment, social security and housing, in order to respond to the needs and realities of single-parent families. as regards employment aid, the report stresses the major role that the european social fund can play in offering scholarships to single mothers and in supporting pregnant women in continuing their training. it also stresses that member states and companies should do more to support work-life balance by introducing more family-friendly working conditions (flexible working hours, teleworking, development of childcare facilities, etc.).
in writing. as a threat to the eu's internal security, organised crime must be combated in order to uphold the democratic values promoted by the union and to put an end to the distortions of the internal market which it exerts by putting pressure on the legal economy. i therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution by mrs sonia alfano.
in writing. organized crime is a major challenge for the european union: in 2010, mafia-like criminal organisations operating in europe benefited from a turnover exceeding the total annual budget of the eu! the report by my colleague, mrs sonia alfano, which was adopted by a very large majority, proposes concrete initiatives to develop a european strategy to combat organised crime and the mafia. the union is still far from being an area of integrated justice and freedom. new instruments are undoubtedly needed, both in terms of judicial and police cooperation and in terms of the use of the european authorities already responsible for combating transnational organised crime. in this report we call on the european commission to propose a directive to criminalise the mafia association or any other criminal network in all member states and to mobilise appropriate resources, including financial resources, to support them in this fight.
in writing. contrary to the rapporteur's claim, the explosion of organised and transnational crime in the european union is one of the consequences of the disappearance of internal border controls without a serious reinforcement of external border controls. it is true, as we have said at all the meetings, that the trafficking in drugs, in human beings, in arms is a scourge and that the imagination of traffickers is boundless. but once again we find ourselves trying to manage at european level problems that we would not have had, or to a much lesser extent, without the european union. and when it comes to crime, the states have not waited for the union to react. the prüm treaty is an example of this, even though its content has been partially taken up at community level, which is also detrimental to its effectiveness. but what motivated our vote against was above all the intention to give the future european public prosecutor's office powers in these areas. we are opposed to the very principle of this office, and therefore to the possibility for this supranational body to conduct judicial investigations or to give orders to our police services.
in writing. i voted strongly in favour of my colleague's report on the fight against organised crime in the european union. organised crime is unfortunately one of the main threats to the internal security of the eu and, given the scale of this global phenomenon, it is essential that europe has a european strategy, legislative and operational instruments and financial means to combat this threat. moreover, we must work towards a common and comprehensive european approach to how to respond to emerging security threats and challenges, in building a secure europe in which we tackle together threats beyond our borders. in particular, i welcome the provisions in this report on the importance of protecting victims of organised crime and on the importance of ensuring that they have an adequate defence. i hope that the texts we are currently working on on crossborder crime, internal security, terrorism and so on will make it possible to move towards the creation of a genuine european prosecutor's office whose competence will have to go far beyond the mere protection of the financial interests of the european union and cover all these areas.

in writing. established in 2002, the high-level forum on aid effectiveness provides a forum for debate between government and non-government representatives with the aim of improving the use of development aid. in the run-up to the 4th forum, to be held in busan, south korea, in november, it is essential that the eu takes a clear and ambitious position. concerned about the respect of the commitments made by the union in the field of consolidating the coherence of development policies, allocating 0.7% of gni to official development assistance by 2015 and enhancing the effectiveness of aid accountability, i voted in favour of the report by my colleague christian dan preda, which emphasises the participation of parliaments, local authorities and civil society in development policies, democratic ownership as a condition for aid allocation and finally transparency.
in writing. the fourth high level forum (hlf-4) on aid effectiveness is to define the eu's future commitments for more effective development aid. the eu contributes more than half of the world's official development assistance (oda), but much remains to be done to address the causes, not the symptoms, of global poverty. it is an extremely difficult subject: how can we create a development policy, and above all a policy of co-development, which is relevant and allows the least developed countries to escape poverty? high-level conferences and statements remain focused on aid delivery mechanisms when thinking about the development of effective development policies is needed. aid has decreased due to the financial crisis but also to the significant reduction in the level of oda, which for some donors lacks short-term results. we cannot accept this short-term view which does not correspond to the deep and long-term action inherent in development aid. the fhn-4 will only be successful if it leads to a strong eu commitment to aid effectiveness, through clear and measurable objectives.
in writing. this future meeting is much more than a forum on aid. the major challenge will be to reverse the logic of development policy: democratic ownership is a key element to be defended in order to encourage the endogenous development of poor countries. this resolution emphasises the importance of the principle of democratic ownership, the principle of non-fragmentation of aid, the need to give priority to the local and regional public market, the integration of horizontal issues such as gender equality, social inclusion, climate change. the greens particularly welcome the introduction of binding measures to ensure that aid schemes are in line with human rights agreements. it is regrettable, however, that the idea, advocated by many ngos, that there is a need to move from an aid effectiveness agenda to a development effectiveness agenda, thus highlighting the urgency of real policy coherence for development, has not been adopted. it is also important to note the attempt by the epp group, which was thwarted by the opposition of the green group, to weaken our proposal for a financial transaction tax as an alternative source of finance.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the wave of redundancies affecting workers across europe should make us reflect on the role we as policy makers have to play in dealing with multinational companies that act without any social ethics, that carry out mass redundancies and relocate to reduce costs, increase shareholder profits and please rating agencies, in defiance of social and environmental standards. in its resolution of 29 september on the future of the european globalisation adjustment fund, parliament clearly expressed its desire to support, above all, employees affected by the negative effects of restructuring. we also asked the commission to ensure that the assistance from the egf is consistent with the industrial policy of the european union, in particular through the use of the structural funds. we also insisted that the future regulations on the egf should include improvements so that the fund does not have the moral hazard that it has today, as demonstrated by the examples of arcelormittal and nokia. commissioner, we can no longer continue to look at the question of the structural funds and the globalisation adjustment fund separately without taking account of the restructuring strategies of the companies that benefit from them and without examining the cost-benefit ratio of a policy, i repeat very clearly, for the benefit of european workers.

in writing. this is the first time i have abstained on a report on taxation. the explanatory statement is a major factor in this choice. the rapporteur notes in particular that the legislation in force, together with the free movement of capital, allows large transnational companies to play with the location of their various subsidiaries in order to avoid corporation tax as much as possible. some call this tax optimization. i say it's a scam. in france, the large firms in the cac 40 pay an average of 10% tax, while smes are taxed at the maximum. the establishment of subsidiaries in tax havens, where they have no other activity than to store a part of the profits made elsewhere, such as the practice of transfer pricing, are scandals that must be stopped. the legitimate desire to limit double taxation to the greatest possible extent has in fact created endless possibilities for non-taxation or under-taxation, tax evasion and even fraud. and i now have a completely different view of the common consolidated corporate tax base, which parliament is advocating, which would prevent multinational companies from playing this unhealthy and harmful little game within the union.

in writing. some of the structural unemployment that our societies are experiencing today is due to the gap between qualifications, training and job requirements. the bastos report stresses the need to anticipate future skills needs in order to match the training supply to the realities of the labour market. i believe that a better match between supply and demand is one of the keys to employment policies, especially for young people. we will have to link this strategy for new skills and jobs with the one we are developing for young people (youth on the move initiative). finally, i regret that the amendment rejecting the european commission's proposal to consider the creation of a single indefinite-term contract in the eu offering progressive social rights has been rejected. such a contract would only introduce new discrimination, creating a new category of workers who would also be weakened by not having full social protection.
in writing. the european union has set itself the target of achieving an employment rate of 75% by 2020 for the 20-64 age group. this rate might be considered excessive in view of the particularly violent times we are living in. we are facing a series of challenges today: the economic and financial crisis, demographic change, migratory flows affecting the competitiveness of our companies, especially smes, in a market subject to increased competitive pressure. however, we must not give in to the pessimism and if we look to a growth rate of employment of slightly above 1% per annum by 2020, this target could be achieved. i therefore welcome the adoption of the bastos report, which proposes priorities for action to meet this challenge - improving the functioning of the labour market, increasing the skills of the workforce, improving the quality of jobs and working conditions, strengthening policies to promote job creation and support the demand for work - and the practical measures to achieve this: strengthening cooperation between educational institutions and enterprises, simplifying administrative procedures to promote worker mobility...
in writing. the text calls on the states to officially recognise the contribution of the social economy and its essential role in economic, social and territorial cohesion. it called for the social protection of european workers to be strengthened and promoted the role of the social partners. but he gives with one hand what he takes back with the other. he advocates flexicurity, teleworking, self-employment and even employee volunteering as well as lowering the retirement age. it supports university-enterprise partnerships and offers internships as a response to youth unemployment. it's inconsistent. i vote against it.
in writing. unemployment now affects almost 10% of europeans. the economic and financial crisis that we have been experiencing since 2008 has only made the situation worse. while the europe 2020 strategy sets the target of achieving a 75% employment rate for the 20-64 age group by 2020, it is clear that we face increasing challenges in preserving our social model. the training of workers and the labour market must adapt to this new difficult economic situation. that is the direction in which the measures proposed by regina bastos in her report are going, and i welcome that. major progress is now needed in supporting continuing education and training, protecting the social rights of workers throughout their careers, and investing heavily in research and innovation to create jobs for the future and improve working conditions. ambitious policies to match workers' expectations with labour market needs must be undertaken, including, as the report wisely proposes, through the creation of european sectoral councils on employment and skills.
in writing. i voted against this report, which is not in itself negative and even makes a number of observations which i can only share. but it is a report paved with good intentions, which does not call into question the policies of the european union and the famous europe 2020 strategy. the focus is always on 'facilitating effective competitiveness', 'promoting smart growth', 'improving human capital' (sic), promoting european centres of excellence, 'strengthening the four strands of flexicurity' or 'ensuring that older workers can stay longer in the labour market'. these few words, taken at random from the reading of this report, show that there is no will to change the fundamental orientations of the european union's policy, to finally draw the consequences of the crisis.

in writing. the european ombudsman plays a central role in the european institutional game. elected by the european parliament, it is responsible for examining complaints from citizens, businesses and associations against the european institutions. i was convinced that the ombudsman contributes to greater democratic transparency and therefore voted in favour of the iotova report. most of the complaints relate to the lack of transparency in the union's administration. the ombudsman made recommendations, endorsed by the european parliament, to deal with complaints in a shorter time (more coordination with the european institutions, simplification of the procedure, etc.).
in writing. in the face of growing criticism that europe is distant from its citizens and that it is not transparent in its handling of affairs, i voted in favour of this text which encourages the ombudsman to increase access to documents of the european institutions. the ombudsman, by offering every citizen free and transparent access to the documents of the european institutions, is a key element of european democracy. as a real link between citizens and institutions, its action helps to strengthen the openness and transparency of the european union. in this area, there is still much to be done, as the resolution stresses, but above all as the number of complaints registered by the ombudsman attests. the european union is moving forward on the path of transparency, and the institutions and the ombudsman must continue to work to make the european union a genuine modern democracy.
in writing. the presence of a mediator is essential for any democratic and effective relationship between administrations and the administrate. according to the ombudsman's 2010 annual report, 2667 complaints were lodged in 2010 by citizens, non-governmental organisations, associations and public authorities. it is very encouraging to note that the mediator has succeeded in helping the complainant in 70% of cases, in most cases seeking to find an amicable solution. i am also pleased to note that almost 58% of complaints were lodged via the internet. the online forms make this right more accessible to citizens and i hope they will help to facilitate and speed up the procedures. the report by iliana malinova iotova, which i support, highlights these developments, while proposing concrete measures to improve the ombudsman's work: continuing the dialogue with complainants and stakeholders, improving transparency by promoting full access to documents, increasing the dialogue between the european ombudsman and national ombudsmen, and disseminating best practice. these advances are necessary and i welcome their inclusion in the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text which presents and assesses the annual report of the european ombudsman. the existence of a link between citizens and the european institutions allows the former to highlight shortcomings and instances of maladministration. so it's a useful asset in trying to strengthen the link between citizens and institutions and promote democracy. this annual report, which is provided for in the texts, is proof of the importance attached by the european parliament to questions of citizenship and good administration. the european parliament's role is to evaluate the work, suggest possible improvements and indicate new objectives. among the objectives to be achieved, this report mentions two that i find interesting: improving citizens' access to documents so that they can better understand the work of their elected representatives, and developing a document on public services to establish a culture of public service within the european union. it remains to be seen what practical action will be taken on this report. i am more skeptical, however, on this point.
in writing. deeply committed to respect for fundamental rights and to the fight against sexual abuse of children, i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs roberta angelilli. the report introduces measures to prevent such abuses, prosecute offenders and protect victims.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on sexual exploitation and abuse of children and child pornography. this report is a real step forward in the fight against child pornography. it provides for the possibility for employers, when recruiting a person for activities involving contact with children, to request information on the person about the existence of convictions for sexual abuse of children.
in writing. the internet is a powerful tool for information, communication and exchange. but unfortunately the internet has also become a tool for the dissemination of child pornography material, because of its anonymity, speed, availability and low prices for access. child pornography is the fastest growing online criminal activity, generating up to $20 billion, according to a un study. it is therefore urgent that more effective action be taken against the perpetrators of such abuses and those who spread them. this type of crime takes full advantage of the 'no-boundary' nature of the new means of dissemination via the internet, which facilitates the creation of highly organised criminal groups. it is therefore at european level that we must react. the member states must now remove from the source or, if this is not technically possible, block internet pages containing or disseminating child pornography. to this end, states may take legislative, judicial or other measures. the european union will also need to cooperate more closely with third countries to obtain such deletions when the offending sites are hosted outside the eu.
in writing. i supported the report on combating exploitation, child pornography and sexual abuse of children. it is the second european criminal law legislation to harmonise penalties and prison sentences for these crimes. after lengthy debate, the final text restores the principle of removing child pornography images and data from the internet, a much more effective method than simply blocking offending sites, as previously envisaged. the union has a real judicial and criminal arsenal to combat this crime and its recurrence.
in writing. the massive development of digital communication has unfortunately allowed sex offenders to exchange criminal images and videos more quickly and anonymously. at present, it is estimated that between 10 and 20% of children are at risk of sexual assault, either within their family or in meetings with strangers. the deepening of the internal market and the free movement of persons and goods require coordinated action by the european union. i fully support the proposals in the roberta angelilli report, namely: the establishment of a minimum system of protection for minors in all member states, the cross-border exchange of information on persons convicted of sexual offences, the strengthening of penalties, the creation of support structures for victims. we are facing a threat of a vast scale, and we had to act. i welcome the adoption of the report by mrs roberta angelilli.
in writing. i abstained from voting on this report, whose guidelines on combating sexual abuse of children i quite broadly share. but the text put to the vote this morning, the product of a compromise with the council, is not as satisfactory as parliament's initial position in terms of definitions of crimes, preventive measures and safeguards for the protection of freedoms on the internet. but one provision is particularly worrying: the possibility for member states to block websites and censor images or sites. in the very sensitive context of attempts by some member states to control the internet, this provision sets a dangerous precedent which i cannot vote for, given the risks of extension and generalization it may entail.
in writing. the definition of common criteria for the identification of persons in need of international protection is part of the establishment of a european asylum policy by 2012. in order to clarify these eligibility criteria and the content of the protection granted, i voted in favour of the lambert report.
in writing. this directive on the conditions for third-country nationals to be granted international protection is a further aggravation of immigration policy in europe. cases that may give rise to such protection are increasing, including cases of alleged persecution based on 'gender' or sexual orientation. mr sarkozy proposed a few years ago that all battered women in the world should seek refuge in france. he dreamed it, europe does it! and that's a lot of people, given the way women are treated in most countries that have based their laws on sharia. the text also broadens the definition of the family that can claim to join the applicant for international protection, such as the rights to social, housing, work, etc. to which these persons may claim. in short, a wonderful invitation to use the asylum application as a means of immigration to europe! i'm not saying all applications will be accepted. on the other hand, the influx of unfounded or opportunistic requests will have the immediate effect of drowning out genuine requests for asylum from political persecution and delaying their completion. and the unsuccessful applicants, rest assured, will be staying here illegally!
in writing. this report expands on some of the commission's proposed developments concerning the conditions under which a victim may benefit from international protection within the european union. i'm glad you did. the report nevertheless reintroduces an unacceptable discrimination between refugees and beneficiaries of subsidiary protection in the area of social assistance and the granting of residence permits. i'll abstain, in respect of the advances, but denounce these retreats.
in writing. the european union, both the cradle of human rights and the land of asylum, had to put in place a coordinated policy for the reception of third-country nationals and stateless persons. the revision of directive 2004/83/ec on minimum standards on the conditions for third-country nationals or stateless persons to be granted international protection was therefore necessary. the report by jean lambert, which i welcome, states that a compromise was reached after lengthy negotiations between the institutions. it contains decisive progress on the grounds for which a person is eligible for refugee status or subsidiary protection and on the content of such protection in the territory of the member state responsible in terms of residence permits, employment and access to social security. in this regard, i am particularly in favour of including gender identity and customary and legal traditions as eligible grounds for persecution. i therefore welcome the vote on this first text adopted under the asylum package.
in writing. only the gue/ngl group had the democratic conscience to ask that at least the court of justice of the european union rule on the compatibility of the eu-australia pnr agreement with the rules in force in europe on the protection of personal data. if the court were to give a favourable opinion on this agreement, we would know how much our fundamental freedoms in the european union have been reduced. i am voting for this salutary report.
in writing. despite improvements and lengthy negotiations, this agreement is still too unsatisfactory. the criteria for data protection are not all met, and there are legitimate concerns. the european commission has not demonstrated the need to collect masses of data, it has not requested the opinion of the fundamental rights agency on this agreement. i also regret that the legal basis is not data protection, which is the subject of the agreement. for these reasons i voted against the motion in plenary.
in writing. i voted in favour of this agreement, which incorporates a number of the priorities which the social democrats have consistently defended in the course of the negotiations. there are still concerns about the legal basis chosen (article 16 of the feu treaty on data protection should have been given priority over that on police cooperation) and about the storage period (5 and a half years, which is still excessive as there is no justification for the proportionality and necessity of long-term data storage). but the terms of this agreement are really a step in the right direction to prevent any misuse of european citizens' pnr data. such data may be used only for the purpose of combating terrorism and serious international crime. there is a right of access, rectification and erasure, and the possibility of bringing an administrative or judicial action. in short, this agreement contains a number of guarantees to ensure a good level of protection for european citizens and i hope that it can serve as a model for the future negotiations on the agreement with the united states, the known terms of which are still very much in doubt.
in writing. i voted in favour of the parliament's recommendation on the agreement between the european union and australia on the processing and transfer of passenger name record (pnr) data from the european union by air carriers to australian customs. the pnr data collected by air carriers shall include, in particular, the name, address, passport number and credit card details of the passenger concerned. this new agreement will bring the transfer of this data to the australian customs service in line with european data protection rules. the main points of the agreement include the restriction of the use of eu pnr data for the sole purpose of preventing terrorism and crime.
in writing. only api data of citizens should be able to be transmitted to foreign authorities. such a transfer should only be managed by european authorities. the agreement between the european union and australia which we are being asked to accept allows the australian authorities to receive and store not our api data but our pnr data, and this under conditions for which they and the airlines alone will be responsible. it also allows the australian authorities to transfer this data to law enforcement authorities in third countries. under the pretext of fighting terrorism, freedom of movement is being trampled underfoot for profiling purposes. i vote against and i denounce this agreement.

in writing. i abstained on this resolution which is alarmed at the situation of the 'christian communities'. on this issue, our gue/ngl group tabled a resolution with a very different message. i have no problem defending the right of coptic christians to practice their religion freely without being attacked and without risking imprisonment or worse, murder. but the defence of human rights cannot be satisfied with having two standards. murders and human rights violations are a daily occurrence in syria and the situation in egypt is far from stable. the european union does not have to defend this or that community. it must not discriminate but must instead defend without distinction freedom of thought, conscience, religion and, more broadly, public freedoms and democracy. it is this truly universal conception of human rights that i defend.

in writing. as a member of the parliamentary committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i supported a european parliament resolution which draws attention to a health reality: more than 25 000 deaths in the eu each year are linked to the growing resistance of bacteria! we therefore call on member states to introduce new antibiotics, improve vaccination coverage and use antibiotics prudently in livestock farming in order to limit antimicrobial resistance and thus the risk of animal-to-human disease transmission.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on antibiotic resistance. the resolution calls for support for innovation to facilitate the introduction of new and more effective antibiotics on the market. it also calls for better vaccination coverage in both human and veterinary medicine. the resolution also calls for the use of antibiotics in livestock to be encouraged in order to reduce the risk of animal-to-human transmission.
in writing. ultra-resistant microbes kill about 25 000 people in the european union every year. to combat the growing resistance of these bacteria, stricter controls on the use of antimicrobials, such as antibiotics, are therefore needed. half of europeans mistakenly believe that antibiotics can treat viral illnesses or colds. the european union and the member states must therefore improve the quality of information and organise prevention campaigns. similarly, the risk of antibiotic resistance passing from animals to humans should be reduced by distinguishing, where possible, between the active substances used in veterinary medicine and those used in human medicine. finally, the use in agriculture of antibiotics as a last resort , intended to control problematic human pathogens, should be allowed only under authorisation, accompanied by surveillance for resistance, preferably on a case-by-case basis .
in writing. human antimicrobial resistance is constantly developing. this is due to the excessive and/or inappropriate absorption of antibiotics in medical treatments and the indirect absorption of such products through the ingestion of farmed animals. this antimicrobial resistance is a major challenge to our health, as these antibiotics are becoming less effective. the resolution calls for intensified research into new antimicrobial agents, the adoption of a legislative framework to combat antimicrobial resistance and massive prevention policies in all member states to raise awareness among european citizens of the rational and effective use of these agents. these are points i support. i therefore welcome the adoption of this text by the european parliament in strasbourg.

in writing. in times of economic crisis, insolvency proceedings are more frequent. it is therefore important that they are well regulated. in his own-initiative report to the european commission, my colleague klaus heiner lehne favours the procedure for rescuing insolvent companies over liquidation. the latter must be the last resort. the report recommends that the procedures be harmonised so as not to penalise certain companies, particularly those with cross-border activities. i am in favour of convergence of the rules to which european companies are subject, and i therefore supported this report.
in writing. insolvency procedures vary widely between the 27 member states of the union. the aim of regulation at european level is therefore to avoid the incentive for parties to move their assets or to relocate legal proceedings from one state to another in order to obtain the most advantageous jurisdiction. in recent years, the phenomenon of company groups has become widespread. this means that several separate proceedings have been opened in different jurisdictions against each company in the bankrupt group, with the risk of splitting the group rather than restructuring it. the future regulation will therefore have to concern groups of companies and specify that the procedure must be initiated in the member state where the group's registered office is located. the interests of the workers must not be forgotten. the level of priority for claims of employees in relation to those of other creditors will therefore have to be increased.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this own-initiative report by our colleague mr lehne, which should make it possible to harmonise the insolvency procedures of european companies. the european union needs to support our companies in difficulty by simplifying the administrative burden and by strengthening communication between the various intra-community courts.

in writing. the financial crisis has highlighted many failures in the financial system, including short selling and credit default swaps , the famous cds . cdss are financial insurance to cover the risks taken by the buyer. these risks may be the bankruptcy of a company or a state. by fuelling speculation, cdss contributed to the bursting of the financial bubble in 2008, and led to the bankruptcy of the us bank lehman brothers. the cdss have not disappeared, however, and threaten the euro area in the event of a greek default. it is therefore imperative that financial markets be more regulated. i am in favour of a stricter framework for these csds and i voted in favour of the report by pascal canfin.
in writing. stop speculating on the sovereign debts of the member states! on tuesday 15 november, the european parliament adopted by a large majority the ban on naked cdss on sovereign debt. with the canfin report, parliament has thus put an end to the speculative games with sovereign debts, which have no place in a social market economy. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the european parliament is able to take part in the debate on the future of the european union. the ban was not easy to impose in the present context: by its success the european parliament shows that it intends to play its full part in bringing the crisis to an end. while the debt crisis is being resolved behind closed doors, parliament is playing its full role as co-legislator here: going further than the commission's proposal, parliament has succeeded, through long negotiations with the member states, in banning naked cdss on sovereign debts. this is good news both for the return of regulation in finance and for the european parliament.
in writing. let us stop speculating on the sovereign debts of the member states. the european parliament has adopted by a large majority the ban on naked cdss on sovereign debt and has thus put an end to speculation on sovereign debt, which has no place in a social market economy. as the contagion is now spreading to italy and spain, it is in the public interest of the european union to prohibit the sale of these speculative financial instruments. however, in the present context, this prohibition was not obvious. parliament thus shows that it intends to play its full role in helping to bring the crisis to an end. while the inadequate responses to the debt crisis are too often decided behind closed doors, parliament is fully fulfilling its role as co-legislator. going further than the commission's proposal, parliament succeeded, through long negotiations with the member states, in banning naked cdss on sovereign debts. this is good news, both for the return of regulation in finance and for european democracy.
in writing. i voted in favour of the canfin report, which seeks to better control and limit some of the most speculative financial practices, and to prohibit some of these practices for sovereign debts. but as with all other european texts on financial market regulation, i remain hungry. the european union is content with a minimum of measures, partial and circumstantial, whereas we should be tackling the root of the problem: the questioning of all the actions that have led us to this point. all of them: the abolition of controls on capital movements, the securitisation of debt, floating exchange rates, the prohibition of monetisation of public debts... this means that the general philosophy that has governed economic globalization for decades must be abandoned. there is no doubt that the financial sector is already preparing the instruments which will enable it to circumvent or distort these measures. and governments are still under the thumb of the markets and the rating agencies to be able to finance abysmal deficits that are partly self-fuelled by extravagant levels of interest charges. i feel like we're trying to put out a forest fire with water pistols. i'm willing to push the pump on mine. but it won't eliminate the arsonists.
in writing. the adoption of this report is a world first in the regulation of financial markets. the terrible pressure of the markets and the rating agencies on the states is politically unbearable and socially very violent for the europeans who suffer from repeated austerity plans. the ban on naked sales on cds is a real step forward: speculators will no longer be able to take out credit default swaps (financial products that insure against the default of the debtor) on government bonds without holding these bonds. in other words, there will be no more speculation and enrichment by betting on the collapse of an economy. this is a real step forward in the fight against the all-powerful financial capitalism. the aim remains to ban all short selling on financial markets in the same way. finance must remain at the service of the real economy and not the other way around.
in writing. i supported the report by pascal canfin which paves the way for agreement with the council on the adoption of the regulation on 'short selling and certain aspects of credit default swaps'. this is the first time that the european union will legislate in this area to ban these complex and potentially perverse and destructive financial products which allow speculation in sovereign debts of states and cause volatility and overreaction in markets. this is a decisive new step that we meps are taking to better regulate european financial markets and break the vicious circle and the chain of events that led to the recent financial crisis.
in writing. i voted for the short selling report. the financial crisis has hit europe hard and weakened the economies of many countries. it's time to learn the lessons. the report aims to limit payment defaults to stabilise markets. the naked sale of credit default swaps (cds) is prohibited, which prevents speculation on a country's default. notifications and reporting are also increased, allowing for better monitoring of financial systems upstream and for anticipating potential problems. the powers of the european financial markets agency are strengthened so that it can fully fulfil its role as arbiter and monitor the markets. this report thus helps to prevent and prevent market volatility, the negative consequences of which on the economy are all too well known.
in writing. i supported the report on the short selling regulation and certain aspects of credit default swaps. this is one of the key regulations to combat the financial crisis. in particular, we have won the ban on naked short selling on sovereign cdss. it was necessary to limit the current possibilities for speculation on the debt crisis of a country! it is perfectly shameful to allow speculation on the failure and failure of others... the entry into force of the text will enshrine the prohibition in principle of such sales, if the buyer is not exposed to the sovereign debt concerned. the national market authorities will, however, have the possibility to temporarily suspend this prohibition in the event of a real dysfunction in the sovereign debt market. we should also welcome the progress made in the field of notification: this should enable the regulatory and supervisory authorities to carry out their tasks better, by ensuring better preventive work and closer monitoring. lack of information was a major problem faced by supervisory authorities before the crisis, and it was time to learn from this.
in writing. the ep has passed a law that limits sovereign debt speculation by banning cdss (credit default swaps). this debt insurance can be held by a speculator even if he does not hold any debt. in practice, this means insuring your neighbour's house and then reselling the insurance when the fire risks are greater. the cds has led to rampant speculation with speculators buying these insurance policies en masse to increase the perception of a risk of collapse of the country and artificially raising the price of these insurance policies to sell them at high prices to the debt holders. it's an aberration, you know. the ban on debt insurance if the buyer does not hold bonds of the country concerned is a positive step. this measure will certainly not be enough to stem the crisis, but it has the merit of demonstrating to all those who still doubted that the financial crisis is not the result of fate but the result of political choices. choices that can be reversed. the desire to control the markets and regulate speculators is not a utopia, as is shown by the evidence.
in writing. i have been keen to support this legislative resolution, which extends the process of financial regulation initiated by my political family in 2007. this text prohibits malicious financial actors from precipitating the default of eurozone states by banning naked credit default swaps (cds). these financial instruments, which were originally designed to provide insurance when buying a government bond, constituted a separate market. in other words, you could have the insurance of a house (the cds) without being the owner of the house (the bond of the state), so the interest for the insurance holder was to see the house burned to collect the premium. this unfortunate situation has led speculative funds to create a climate of panic around greece by buying cdss en masse, which have become increasingly lucrative as the worries spread. greece, in the grip of this excessive speculation, was then forced to borrow at exorbitant interest rates, thus accumulating ever more debt. it is to prevent other states from falling prey to such speculative folly that we now require that the holder of the cds be also the holder of the state bond.
