in writing. the european parliament voted by a large majority on tuesday 15 november on the brezina reports to extend research and training activities under the european atomic energy community framework programme for the years 2012 and 2013. the main objective was to ensure the consistency of these activities and the continuity of the commitments made with the financial perspective for the period 2007-2013 and the 7th framework programme for research and development. i share the emotion aroused by the nuclear explosion at the fukushima site and its disastrous consequences both in human and material terms. the french authorities have recognised the need to learn from this to ensure that this never happens on their own territory. but that's not the issue with these reports. research in the broad sense on nuclear fission is essential to deepen our knowledge in this field and the continuation of the iter programme must not be exploited by those who oppose nuclear energy as an energy resource. i am therefore pleased that the european parliament has been able to identify the issues at stake and to mobilise to provide massive support for the continuation of nuclear research.
in writing. three reports by jan brezina were put to the vote today. they aim to extend the euratom framework programme for nuclear research and training activities to 2012 and 2013 in order to align it with the current financial perspective and the seventh framework programme, both of which will end in 2013. i supported these reports, which were followed up brilliantly by my colleague brezina.
in writing. respect for the freedom of movement for workers, which is necessary for the functioning of the internal market, leads to mutual recognition of professional qualifications. in 2005, the eu adopted a directive to this end. today, the question is to ensure its implementation within the union. to this end, member states must trust each other and promote the mobility of skilled workers, particularly young graduates. i therefore voted in favour of the report by mrs mcclarkin, which calls for simplification of recognition procedures.
in writing. it must be admitted that the recognition of vocational qualifications in the european union is still far from complete. many obstacles remain, as the 2005 directive did not address all the problems. it is therefore more than necessary to simplify and modernise the existing system. the member states must cooperate more closely with each other, as the recognition of professional qualifications is a matter of trust. it is obvious that greater mobility must not be at the expense of quality. that is why we must continue to reflect on the famous european professional card, which we have been talking about since 2005 but which is still provoking resistance. pilot projects have shown that it can be a useful tool for better recognition of qualifications. we therefore ask the commission to take this forward, by showing the added value of such a map and by providing the necessary guarantees, particularly in the area of data protection.
in writing. i voted for the mcclarkin report on the implementation of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications. the report focuses on four areas: simplification for citizens, updating existing data, progress in public health and safety, and the integration of professionals. i agree with the rapporteur on these points.
in writing. better recognition of professional qualifications will strengthen the competitiveness of the european economy, while stimulating growth and job creation. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union. but that doesn't mean we're going to abolish all the rules. the recognition of qualifications may, in some cases, differ from one state to another. there are still regulated professions: lawyers and doctors, for example, remain the domain of the member states, because of their highly sensitive nature. it is quite normal that in certain cases we may demand more, for the safety of consumers and patients. our long-term aim remains to move towards harmonisation in the more distant future, but things are not so simple: at the moment, this is not yet possible. finally, in order to move towards a more unified and better regulated european professional world, it is useful to consider the possible introduction of a voluntary european professional card. the latter would greatly facilitate the mobility of professionals, by granting them a genuine status.
in writing. the recognition of professional qualifications in europe is still subject to cumbersome and costly administrative procedures which discourage the mobility of professionals. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which proposes ways of changing this situation, in particular by simplifying procedures based on information and by ensuring the transparency of decisions and reducing delays. it is also necessary to update the sometimes very dusty classification of economic activities and the minimum training requirements. as regards health professionals, i have been particularly attentive to supporting the establishment of a proactive alert system to alert other states to cases where a professional is sanctioned. in addition, on the question of the professional card, which the european socialists have been calling for for many years, we want to make it easier for professionals to do so, to improve the exchange of information between the authorities and to ensure the safety of customers and patients. i hope that these elements will be taken into account in the commission's future proposal for the revision of the 2005 directive.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of the mcclarkin report which responds to the need to simplify and update the existing 15 directives on the recognition of professional qualifications. the modernisation of this legislation is one of the 50 proposals of the european commission in the single market act and one of the 12 growth levers identified by commissioner barnier. the report also introduces a proactive alert mechanism to ensure the provision of services by healthcare professionals and makes proposals to promote the integration of healthcare professionals.
in writing. i support mrs mcclarkin's report on the implementation of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications (directive 2005/36/ec) adopted today in plenary, as it is an important contribution by the european parliament to the debate launched by the european commission following the publication of the green paper last june. recognition of professional qualifications is necessary to facilitate the mobility of workers within the internal market. the existing directive, adopted in 2005, needs to be modernised and improved, in particular in terms of simplification for citizens, ensuring the protection of public health and safety (health professions) and building trust in the system.
in writing. i wanted to support the report by our colleague mr mcclarkin on the implementation of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications, for which i was rapporteur for the epp group. the question of professional mobility is closely linked to the question of growth and competitiveness in our internal market. in this report we call for greater professional mobility and therefore for more simplification and efficiency in the procedures for the recognition of professional qualifications. we call in particular on the european commission, which will present its proposal for the revision of the 2005 directive in mid-december, to make progress on the introduction of a european professional card on the basis of the voluntary participation of the professional sectors concerned. this could be a further step towards a people's europe. we also want to introduce more trust and security into the recognition system by introducing practical tools for european citizens such as the proactive alert system which we wish to see introduced when a health professional is subject to a regulatory measure for his registration or his right to provide a service.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of the directive on the recognition of professional qualifications. the european union is based on a single market. this integrated single market can only function effectively if european workers are able to practise their profession freely in the member state of their choice. the knowledge and expertise acquired in one member state must be recognised in another european state. the issue of the recognition of professional qualifications is fundamental to the integration of our economies. this report will make it easier and shorter for doctors, midwives, dentists, pharmacists, architects and other professionals to work throughout the european union, without jeopardising the safety of citizens. intra-european mobility must be promoted in the interests of a dynamic and competitive european economy. too few europeans are still using this opportunity. the aim is to reduce the barriers to trade and to encourage these beneficial exchanges.
in writing. the completion of the internal market and the free movement of workers cannot be achieved without easy recognition of professional qualifications between member states - this is a priority of the single market act to promote economic growth within the union. but in order to be fair, effective and to protect european citizens, procedures must be simplified while maintaining a high level of quality. the report by emma mcclarkin meets these expectations and i welcome it. the commission's proposals are in line with the necessary objective of modernising the 2005 directive. efforts should therefore focus on intensifying exchanges between competent authorities, making useful information accessible via an online portal and one-stop shops, providing an electronic professional card for european workers and, last but not least, protecting patients through increased supervision of healthcare professionals. i now invite the european commission to take these measures into account in the proposal it will publish in december on the modernisation of the 2005 directive.
in writing. the union was built on economic cooperation, which must remain the driving force behind our integration. to overcome the crisis, we need all the skilled labour available throughout europe. i therefore support the application of the logic of the single market to skilled workers, to promote and encourage their mobility within the union. of course, each member state organises and offers its own training, but workers applying for mobility are faced with bureaucratic and time-consuming procedures, which are therefore dissuasive. simplified, common and transparent procedures for the recognition of professional qualifications are essential for the optimal functioning of our economies. these advances need to be confirmed, particularly with the internal market information system (imi) and the professional card. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the information provided by the member states is not misused. to maintain its economic leadership in the face of the emerging powers of the brics, the union must above all avoid brain drain and optimise the skills of its workers. i therefore naturally voted in favour of this report in order to promote the employment of highly qualified workers in europe and to establish the union as a global hub of innovation.
in writing. sensitive to the issue of consumer protection, i voted in favour of the triantaphyllides report. consumer protection requires an overall strategy that allows, on the one hand, to defend their interests and inform them of their rights, and, on the other hand, to empower them to encourage more sustainable consumption. from 2012, an agenda will identify all consumer initiatives and feed into the union's consumer policy. the european parliament calls on the european commission to pursue a more proactive policy with a view to establishing a more coherent legal framework.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this report which will set new standards for the protection of european consumers by ensuring better implementation of existing legislation. by adopting this report, we are thus strengthening the fight against inequalities, in particular by encouraging sustainable consumption, combating misleading advertising and increasing the safety of our citizens in the face of the trade in dangerous products.
in writing. consumer protection is a major challenge area: not only to ensure food safety, health and product safety, but also to tackle the problem of reducing inequalities between consumers in europe or the establishment of a low-carbon economy. that is why i voted in favour of the alternative resolution tabled by the rapporteur to return to a number of points which could not be adopted in the committee on the internal market because of the opposition of the ppe. in particular, the consumer protection programme should include measures to protect minors against misleading advertising. as a vulnerable group, children are a perfect target for advertisers, especially through television. finally, the legal vacuum in the field of collective redress should be filled by a commission proposal to enable consumers to have their rights better protected.
in writing. consumer protection is a major concern for the european parliament. it reflects his desire to put the citizen at the heart of his actions. in the run-up to the publication of the european commission's communication on the consumer agenda in early 2012, parliament set out its priorities for effective consumer protection, respect for consumer rights, product safety and better accessibility for the most vulnerable consumers. the report, which has been widely adopted by the european parliament, sets ambitious guidelines for the next consumer policy strategy. i therefore wanted to vote in favour of this report, which confirms my concern to improve the daily life and well-being of my fellow citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr triantaphyllides' report on a new strategy for consumer policy as it aims to identify the european parliament's priorities for the european commission's preparation of the next 'consumer agenda' including the commission's future initiatives on consumer protection, which is due to be published next year. it seems to me particularly important to emphasise the logic of 'consumer empowerment', i.e. providing consumers with the means to make optimal decisions for themselves through an understanding of their preferences and knowledge of the instruments at their disposal.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by kyriakos triantaphyllides on a new strategy for consumer policy, for which i was rapporteur for the epp group. this report sets out clear milestones for the consumer agenda which the european commission will propose early next year. empowering consumers, informing them better, ensuring the safety of the products they have access to, implementing existing legislation swiftly and ensuring that all actors know their rights and obligations - these must be the priorities of european and national legislators and decision-makers, but also of businesses and consumer associations for the years to come. above all, i think it is appropriate to call for a real reflection to find the right balance between the degree of information that consumers really need, the use they make of it when they make purchases and the administrative and financial burdens that this creates for businesses. we must, through the policies we adopt, give consumers the keys to understanding the rules in place and to having their free will through clear and useful information, which is really assimilable.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr triantaphyllides on the new strategy for consumer policy. this report, which i helped to draw up, sets out the specific points we want to see addressed by the commission when it proposes its 'consumer protection agenda' in early 2012. we want this agenda to be ambitious, coherent and concrete, placing consumers at the heart of a functioning single market. our parliament has stressed consumer safety, the importance of education and information - transparent, comparable - to be provided to consumers, and the means of redress to be made available to them. we also address several emerging challenges: the need to move towards sustainable consumption patterns, the need to meet the specific needs of older people in our ageing europe, the issue of social inclusion and vulnerable consumers, and the need to take account of new labelling requirements (fair trade, carbon footprint, etc.). finally, we call - once again - for greater consistency in european consumer protection policies and for a renewed reflection on the distribution of this portfolio within the commission.
in writing. consumer spending generates more than half of the gross domestic product of the european union (eu). in the current context of crisis, which undeniably has an impact on consumer behaviour, the development and adoption of this new strategy was a necessary step. that is why i voted in favour of this report in the plenary. among its main objectives, i particularly support the idea of basing all future actions on a comprehensive approach that puts consumers at the heart of the single market. because consumer confidence is a powerful economic driver, we must work to improve consumer information and to unify the legal framework for consumer protection at european level, while taking into account the needs and particularities of each consumer group, especially the most vulnerable (young people, the disabled).
in writing. the crisis we are currently experiencing is a crisis of confidence affecting our banks and our businesses, and seriously threatening the economic recovery. in this climate of mistrust, it is essential to support consumption by maintaining the relationship of trust between the buyer and the seller. in this way we will contribute to informed and regular consumption, which is essential for the eu's economic growth. the european union is clearly moving in this direction with this report, which i supported and which seeks to provide even more comprehensive information to consumers who are at the heart of the single market. citizens should be able to benefit from clear and accurate information on all products they buy, whether health, safety or sustainability. i believe that there is immense progress to be made in certain sectors, where tariff plans are deliberately made incomprehensible to the consumer, where switching suppliers is laborious and costly and where automatic renewal of expired contracts is commonplace. it is high time that the commission tackled these obstacles to competition and consumer choice.
in writing. the online gambling industry is attracting more and more internet users in europe and generating significant profits in the billions of euros. this enthusiasm for the sector, however, conceals irregularities which affect the european consumer in the first place. online gambling is not subject to the same rules in all member states. the sector is also threatened by illicit operators who undermine the internal market. that is why, in the interests of legal certainty and the protection of european consumers, particularly minors, i voted in favour of the creutzmann report, for which i was rapporteur for opinion in the committee on economic and monetary affairs. in my report to the econ committee, which was subsequently incorporated into the final report, i emphasized in particular the protection of minors, the fight against illegal offers and the protection of the integrity of sport.
in writing. protecting the integrity of sport in europe is an increasingly complex task, particularly with the rise of the internet and new means of fraud. following up on the european commission's green paper on online gambling, we have adopted a report which is moving in the right direction. while recognizing the competence of the states in this area, we recall the added value that could be brought by coordination at european level. i welcome the fact that the report calls for a stronger fight against the black market and abuse, that it focuses on the protection of minors and vulnerable consumers, who are more exposed to gambling addiction, but also that it calls for the establishment of a blacklist of providers of illegal gambling and gambling. finally, the right to bet, which france was the first to introduce in its legislation, is recognised in this text: the idea is that the property rights of the organisers of sports competitions in their competitions should be recognised, so that a fair financial return can be obtained to continue protecting the integrity of sport and to strengthen the fight against fraud and match-fixing.
in writing. i did not vote for the creutzmann report on gambling. in its original version, it was not as clear as it is, and sometimes contradictory, on the respect of the exclusive competence of the member states to regulate gambling and chance, to maintain national monopolies, to decide on the allocation of tax revenues from betting, to enact the prohibitions they wish, to set the level of consumer protection. moreover, it was almost silent on horse betting, which is nevertheless used, particularly in france, to support the equine sector, while several paragraphs were devoted to sports betting and the rights of the organisers of sporting events on the events they manage. the equine sector, which is also threatened by brussels, which is attacking the legitimacy of the vat rate it benefits from, is of great economic and social importance in many rural areas. a little more attention to this activity and its specific challenges would have been welcome. the report as amended violates the principle of subsidiarity and does not even mention this sector.
in writing. online gambling is booming in europe and it does not stop at borders. there is also a vast unregulated black market on the internet. it would therefore be better to introduce a legal offer of gambling and gambling on the internet. a licensing model seems to be the best solution, provided that it is based on the principle of non-discriminatory competition. with this system, which has already been successfully introduced in some member states such as france and italy, the national regulatory authorities set the conditions for the issuing of licences. given the cross-border nature of such games, a coordinated approach at european level could prove very effective in combating illegal gambling and protecting children and vulnerable consumers. we need to move towards more regulation to combat the risks of addiction and to combat money laundering.
in writing. i welcome the adoption by a large majority of the creutzmann report which defends the principle of a controlled opening of the online gambling market. the report follows the publication of the european commission's green paper last march, which was a response to the increase in fraud in a growing market. the report succeeds in reconciling a coordinated approach at european level while emphasising the decision-making role of the member states by ensuring respect for the principle of subsidiarity. above all, it promotes the right to bet as a property right, the proceeds of which could be reallocated to finance betting on horse racing, equestrian sports and the horse economy. this support is essential for the safeguarding and sustainability of the equine sector, which also contributes to the vitality of rural areas.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr creutzmann's report on online gambling and gambling in the internal market because it stresses the importance of strengthening cooperation between member states in an essentially crossborder area, in particular in consumer protection and the fight against fraud and money laundering, while recognising that the decision to liberalise the market is a matter for the member states. the model put forward is that of a "controlled" opening according to a national licensing system.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my colleague jürgen creutzmann on online gambling. in view of the growth of this sector and its cross-border nature, we call in this report for more cooperation between national regulatory authorities, under the coordination of the european commission, in order to develop common standards and take joint action against providers of online gambling and gambling services that engage in illegal practices. the report also calls for the introduction of a european system for the exchange of information on gambling. this controlled opening up must be done in particular by means of a model of licences allocated at national level. the report also stresses the need to ensure the integrity of sport to avoid fraud and rigged sports competitions that flourish due to the rise of online betting. finally, the report looks at the fair financial return to the sports sectors, recommending the introduction of a betting right, a kind of property right, which would allow the organisers of sporting events to assert their rights against online betting operators.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on online gambling. online gambling is growing in popularity and is worth €10 billion a year in europe. it is a matter of regulating this new economic sector to prevent fraud and illegal practices that can reach our citizens. it is also necessary to take into account vulnerable persons who can easily enter into harmful dependence on gambling and betting, especially as the internet facilitates their access. these areas remain national competence, with the member states being responsible for public order and health. however, given the transnational nature of the internet, it is also appropriate to strengthen cooperation between member states. the aim is to improve payment security, to combat illegal transactions and to think together about the problems of addiction.
in writing. today, 10% of all gambling in europe takes place online - on the internet, but also via mobile phones, or interactive tv platforms. in this context, national regulations are no longer sufficient to adequately protect consumers or to effectively prevent operators of illegal or fraudulent gambling. it is therefore necessary to increase cooperation between national regulatory authorities in this sector and to consider the establishment of common minimum european standards - while respecting the principle of subsidiarity. i have of course supported the main points of this report. as regards the 'right to bet', i am pleased that parliament has supported the idea of recognising the property rights of organisers of sporting events at european level, and of establishing legally binding agreements between organisers of sporting events and operators. i was opposed to the idea of calling for a regulation of 'slip bets'. this type of betting is particularly dangerous for consumers, and i want the possibility of banning it altogether to be preserved.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on online gambling in the internal market. since the internet is by its nature a cross-border medium, european legislation in this area is more than necessary. i therefore call for concerted action at the level of the 27 to combat illegal gambling, money laundering, addiction and fraud, particularly in sport. the report stresses that such regulation should, in particular, channel the natural propensity of the population to gamble by limiting advertising to what is strictly necessary to direct potential gamblers towards the legal offer. it should also require that any advertising for online gambling be accompanied by a message warning against excessive or pathological gambling. it will be up to each member state, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, to take the most appropriate measures in this fast-growing sector. this is also a concrete action at european level to better protect citizens.
in writing. with the exponential growth of the online gambling market in recent years, there are many dangers: addiction, especially among young people, cheating, crime, the power of money in the sports world and the protection of data. the internet is a game of borders and the principle of subsidiarity required rapid action by the union, in close coordination with the states. these are concerns that i share with my political family, to ensure legal certainty for consumers, the integrity of sport and the enjoyment of gambling. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which proposes clear solutions such as the fight against illegal operators, the limitation of advertising and the fair redistribution of funds to the sports sectors. however, i regret that our request to mention the equine sectors separately in order to make their current funding sustainable was not accepted. it is a strategic area for my region, closely linked to its heritage and to our terroir. i will remain vigilant to ensure that the interests of equestrian activities are preserved. it is also about protecting our traditions and all the activities derived from the equestrian centres.
in writing. at this parliamentary session, an urgent appeal was made to stop the increasing bee mortality. bees are essential to the stability of our ecosystem. therefore, i voted in favour of the tabajdi report, which calls on the european union to act to protect them by increasing investment in research into new veterinary products for bees, by informing farmers about the use of pesticides, and by monitoring imports from third countries.
in writing. the increase in bee mortality is a serious matter. bees play a fundamental role in the balance of the environment and food production in europe. in fact, about three quarters of european food production depends on bee pollination. the beekeeping sector also provides income for 600 000 european citizens. the european union must therefore do more to protect this species, which is almost at risk. that is why we want to set up national surveillance systems and develop harmonised european standards to better collect data on bee health. member states should also share the results of their research in this field. but above all, farmers must be made aware of the use of pesticides that are good for the health of bees.
in writing. i have chosen to support this text because i believe it is essential to highlight the role bees play in our agriculture and our environment, and to support beekeepers who are currently facing difficult challenges. indeed, beekeeping plays a crucial role in our rural areas and provides an important service to the ecosystem through pollination which helps to maintain biodiversity. it is currently estimated that 84% of plant species and 76% of food production in europe depend on bee pollination, with an estimated economic value of €15 billion per year in the eu. in recent years, there has been a marked decline in their numbers. new diseases, parasitic mites, lack of pollen, and possible phytosanitary interactions threaten them, with serious consequences for the food chain. let's help our beekeepers protect their hives! to understand these phenomena better, we need better information with pan-european monitoring. we must also make it easier to develop new veterinary medicines specifically for them. i tabled amendments to emphasize these points and i am glad to see that we have been heard.
in writing. although the health of bees may seem to be an original concern, it actually has a significant impact on our environment, the preservation of the food chain and the economy. that is why i wanted to support this initiative, which makes it possible to raise awareness among european actors and citizens of a problem that is specific but has many consequences. it is estimated that 84% of plant species and 76% of food production in europe depend on bee pollination. the economic value of honey is estimated at 15 billion euros a year. the increase in bee mortality therefore poses a serious threat to the stability of the chain and to an entire economy that lives on the production of honey products. this is why the tabajdi report recommends a comprehensive analysis of the bee population, the beekeeping sector and colony losses in the eu. it also called for better consideration of this issue in agricultural and research policies and in veterinary legislation.
in writing. this is a very important report. we underestimate the role bees play in our agriculture and our environment. beekeeping, through pollination, helps to maintain biodiversity. i have supported this report in this light.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on bee health and the challenges facing the beekeeping sector, to combat the increasing bee mortality and to coordinate action to protect a species that will be rapidly threatened. the beekeeping sector is an integral part of european agriculture and, through pollination, provides important benefits for the environment, the economy and society, thus ensuring food security and the maintenance of biodiversity. it is estimated that 84% of plant species and 76% of food production in europe depend on bee pollination. however, there has been a decline in the number of bee colonies both in the european union and in other parts of the world. we therefore ask the european commission to take a series of measures in different areas such as research, veterinary products or the cap after 2013 to combat this phenomenon. this also requires addressing the lack of reliable and comparable data on the number of hives, beekeepers and colony losses in the eu.
in writing. bees provide a crucial and necessary step in the reproduction of plant species: pollination. by transferring pollen from one plant to another, they ensure the sustainability and biodiversity of our crops, and thus our food security. the overuse of pesticides, climate change, monoculture and parasitism have caused the colony collapse of bees. their disappearance is endangering our agriculture. it is the survival of the vast majority of plant species and our food production, but also the incomes of 600 000 people in europe, amateurs and professionals, that are at stake. moreover, because of the specific nature of this form of beekeeping, there is no training for beekeepers, no awareness-raising for farmers, and no specialized veterinary industry. today, the state of emergency is finally declared. it is important to protect this sector as soon as possible by encouraging the establishment of young beekeepers, supporting research by the pharmaceutical industry, establishing a permanent dialogue between the various actors and creating a harmonised european network of census. the preservation of biodiversity, the quality of our food and the survival of the bee industry will depend on our willingness to act.
in writing. public services are essential for european citizens because they meet basic needs. the european rules governing their financing are expiring, and it is time to reform them. the european parliament has therefore adopted recommendations for reform in an own-initiative report to the european commission. it is up to the european commission, acting as the competition authority, to reform these rules. as rapporteur on this matter for my political group, the epp, i welcome its adoption. we wanted to send a strong message to the european commission that public services should benefit from a clear and robust legal framework. it is important that public service providers, whether local authorities or private providers, are able to provide accessible and quality services while respecting the rules. we have therefore voted in favour of simpler and more transparent rules. we ask that the eligibility criteria for state aid be better adapted to local realities. we also confirmed our wish to take account of the specific nature of social services as recognised by the lisbon treaty.
in writing. it should be stressed that the european commission has taken a step in the right direction by recognising the specificity of the sgeis. i regret, however, the choice of legal basis: by choosing to base its proposal solely on article 106 (state aid) the commission chooses to ignore the novelties of the lisbon treaty and the possibility of fully involving the european parliament by using article 14. it's a shame, though. the simon report makes this clear and provides food for thought: yes, we need more clarification, yes, it seems quite appropriate and necessary to introduce some flexibility in the application of the state aid rules. in particular, compensation granted which does not affect trade between member states should be exempted from notification, and account should be taken of the exclusively local nature of certain public services. finally, we must not forget the objective of promoting high quality services that are accessible to all. i hope that the commission will take parliament's view into account when preparing the revision of the monti-kroes package.
in writing. i voted against the simon report. it is true that it is in the right direction, that of relaxing the rules restricting public support to services of general interest. but he's not starting from the right premises. the commission's idiotic distinction between services of general interest, social services of general interest and services of general economic interest is nothing but a ruse to deny the very principle of public service and the absolute right of the states, as recognised by the treaties, to define public services, to organise them and to decide on the way they are financed. it is also used in network activities to squeeze markets out of the private sector, to break up national monopolies and replace them with private oligopolies, to socialise losses and to leave the construction and maintenance of networks to the public authorities, and thus to the taxpayer. one of two things: either the service is a public service, whether economic or otherwise, or it is only a part of the normal commercial activity. in the first case, it does not have to be subject to the vague and fluctuating adjustments of the ultra-liberal policies of the european union, but it must be excluded from the scope of the competition rules and those governing public subsidies.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague peter simon because we certainly need more simplification, clarity and proportionality on state aid for public services of general interest. we must emphasise that the sgeis have a major role to play in the eu in helping to achieve the objectives of economic, social and territorial cohesion. in particular, i supported a reference that, without the presence of the state, these services would not be provided or not sufficiently provided. therefore, we emphasise the reference to article 14 and protocol 26 tfeu and the discretionary role of the member states in the financing, organisation and provision of sgeis. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the principle of equal treatment to all workers in the same sector. finally, we must call for universal access for sgeis and reiterate our call to the european commission for a proposal for a horizontal legal framework for sgeis by the end of 2011.
in writing. services of general economic interest (sgeis) contribute to social, economic and territorial cohesion, as well as making a significant contribution to the economic performance and competitiveness of the member states. preserving their specificity while ensuring a minimum of competition to ensure that they function optimally is an important issue for europe. this report follows the proposals made by the commission last september on the revision of the rules for financing sgeis. i voted for it. it emphasises in particular the specific nature of regional and local sgeis which, since they do not affect competition in the internal market, should be subject to a simplified procedure. the commission is also asked to adapt the rules - by simplifying them - for social services of general interest (ssigs), which do not have to be feared to affect trade between member states. it also supports the maintenance of the existing exemption from notification, without thresholds, for hospitals and social housing, and the commission's proposal to extend this exemption to other areas of the gss.
in writing. i supported this report in plenary because it sets clear guidelines for the future reform of state aid for services of general economic interest (sgeis), namely: transparency and simplification. transparency is needed: public funds must be allocated and managed according to rules that are known to all, so that all beneficiaries are treated equally. simplification is equally important: local authorities and local service providers need to be able to understand and implement them easily, which is not always the case today and can pose legal uncertainty issues. but i will be careful about one thing: this simplification cannot be at the expense of transparency. finally, i welcome the rapporteur's reminder to the commission that public services must be of high quality and accessible to all sections of the population.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution expressing the european parliament's orientations in the context of the revision of state aid applicable to sgeis that the commission proposed last october. this report largely echoes the proposals of the intergroup on social affairs, of which i am vice-chairman, and peter simon, the epp rapporteur on this text. although some of the wording in the report cannot be minor, the report is generally in the right direction as it supports the need to take better account of the specificities of public, economic or social services (pes). in addition to the demand for an increase in the thresholds for state aid and for an extension of the exempted sectors, i welcome in particular the reaffirmation of the principle of subsidiarity and the demand that the sigis not be regarded as benefits reserved for the disadvantaged or that account be taken of the specific nature of the intervention of local authorities and their grouping. i also welcome the ep's position that this reform of state aid is only part of the necessary clarification of the legal regime applicable to sgeis. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution so that the european parliament can exert pressure on the commission to force it to change its doctrinal positions.
in writing. in a crisis, the gap between rich and poor tends to widen. one in five europeans is now at risk of falling into poverty. europe has set itself the target of reducing the number of people at risk of poverty by 20 million as part of the europe 2020 strategy. to achieve this, a comprehensive approach involving all the actors concerned (ngos, social service providers, etc.) must be put in place. similarly, better use of eu funds will help achieve the europe 2020 strategy's goals for inclusive, smart and sustainable growth. i am committed to the principles of solidarity and social cohesion and have voted in favour of the daerden report.
in writing. as the crisis drags on, with the result that poverty and social insecurity are increasing, and as the necessary but insufficient austerity plans are being taken to their full extent by already vulnerable populations, there is an urgent need for the 116 million people at risk of poverty and social exclusion in the eu. this report is not a legislative one, but it does have the merit of drawing up a fairly complete picture of the situation and of suggesting some ways of improving the situation by advocating a model of society based on 'social' values. developing relevant european action will require the development of national platforms for combating poverty, but also the full use of the possibilities available in the lisbon treaty, first and foremost the famous horizontal social clause. only by taking the social impacts of each european policy into account will we be able to achieve the famous social dimension of the eu, which seems so far away today! since the preservation of social rights in the union is fundamental, the specificity of social services of general interest must be recognised and the consideration of sectoral legislative initiatives to promote the quality and accessibility of these services must continue.
in writing. the scale of poverty in europe, which is estimated to affect some 116 million people, calls for strong action. i voted in favour of this report because it helps to promote the european values of justice and solidarity. the diversity of the poor population calls for a coordinated strategy to ensure the best possible protection for each of them (women, young people, working poor, etc.). to this end, the eu could play a pivotal role in raising awareness, coordinating and financing. i was particularly pleased to see in this report a paragraph supporting the maintenance of the budget of the european programme of aid to the most deprived (pead) at at least an equivalent level for the coming years.
in writing. it is a great victory for us to have adopted this report which calls on the commission to work towards the introduction of binding legislation on an adequate minimum income, at the level of the poverty line, as a necessary tool to achieve the realistic objective of lifting 20 million people out of poverty by 2020. to combat poverty, it is not enough to talk about growth: with 8.4% of working poor in the eu, employment is no longer a protection against poverty. i welcome the fact that the environmentalists' proposal to tax high incomes has been approved. it is high time that heads of state and government understood that they are not here to serve the interests of the richest 1% but to defend the 99%! i welcome the central role of people living in poverty in the implementation of this platform. today we must make politics 'with' and not just 'for' the poorest. i regret that our request for a framework directive on the quality and accessibility of social services of general interest has been rejected. universal access to public services is fundamental to protecting the poorest.
in writing. as usual, this parliament focuses on minorities, preferably those extra-european minorities already ultra-assisted. the presence of these groups imposes a huge social cost on the community, since the vast majority of their members are not working. they are given priority, in view of their family and social situations, in social housing at the expense of the modest european citizens. the continuous and massive arrival of newcomers - 200,000 a year in france alone - is automatically putting pressure on the rents of a shortage of housing stock. i would have preferred the report to have focused on the 42 million europeans who are considered poor, but also on the 116 million who are at risk of becoming so! these figures are staggering, and they are not just due to the crisis. the downward pressure on european incomes is old: competition from immigrant workers, competition from low-wage countries, ecb policies against hypothetical wage inflation, pension reforms... the general impoverishment of the retired, the low- and unskilled, the working class and, increasingly, the middle classes, is the direct consequence of your policies. but of course, that is not mentioned in this report. i therefore voted against.
in writing. the report on the european platform against poverty by frédéric daerden points to a sad paradox: while 116 million europeans are at risk of poverty and 42 million of them live in extreme material deprivation, the eu 2020 strategy sets the target of reducing the number of people at risk of poverty to only 20 million! any sign of weakness? the european union is not a political union. unfortunately, this is what one might think, given the "solution" found for the programme of assistance to the most deprived: it will be saved for 2012 and 2013... but subject to unacceptable counterparts, namely the definitive abolition of this programme and the abandonment of any social policy at european level from 2014. this proposal is a provocation at a time when citizens are being hit hard by the crisis and austerity plans. it may reinforce the feeling of economic, social and moral decline. that is why, in keeping with the idea of a progressive and united europe, the mobilization around this programme must not stop: i will, for my part, pay particular attention to it in the context of the negotiations on the financial perspectives after 2013.
in writing. i supported the report by my colleague frédéric daerden because it is absolutely necessary for the european union to mobilise and act to fight poverty and social exclusion. the figures speak for themselves and are unmistakable: about 115 million europeans are living in poverty. this report proposes concrete and multidimensional solutions to combat poverty, such as access to education and vocational training for all. but we must also ensure that budgetary austerity policies do not undermine social protection and employment. that is why i attach great importance to the necessary role of national and european budgets, including the esf and the eafrd. i also support the report's call for an evaluation mechanism involving the european parliament and based on specific indicators to ensure that member states monitor their fight against poverty, which is a prerequisite for our effective fight against social exclusion and poverty.
in writing. 116 million people in the european union are at risk of poverty and 42 million live in extreme material deprivation. the economic and financial crisis and the sharp rise in food prices have left 43 million people in food poverty. in the face of this situation, it is essential to strengthen the involvement of civil society in the development of a european strategy at all levels of governance. that is why i supported this report.
in writing. 42 million europeans live in extreme material deprivation without the means to support themselves to lead a decent life. in view of these figures - and the economic outlook for the coming months - the european platform against poverty and social exclusion is of paramount importance. the report by my colleague frédéric daerden contains several key ideas. the text calls for the commission/eurostat to have a comprehensive scoreboard on poverty and social exclusion and for the improvement and comparability of national poverty statistics. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (emah) was adopted unanimously. it also called for respect for the fundamental principles of the ilo and the concept of decent work and quality jobs to be implemented in the area of job creation. it also recommends that appropriate taxation of very high wages be implemented to help finance social protection systems and minimum income. these are the right ideas, and i wanted to support them with this vote.
president of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, the past few weeks have again shown how much is at stake for the european union today. we must react quickly and decisively to events that affect every citizen and every household in europe. against this background, it is more essential than ever that our institutions strengthen our cooperation and show common resolve to deliver rapid and effective responses to the crisis. the basis for a successful response is to have a clear consensus about where europe is heading. i believe that the commission and this parliament share this consensus – this ambition for a european union that is stable and strong, that is open and really united. the commission work programme is a key building block to achieving this vision. it is therefore particularly important that it rests on a series of intensive exchanges between our two institutions. this intensive dialogue has been decisive in determining the focus of the programme for 2012. through the conference of committee chairs, the committee of presidents, and the structured dialogue between commissioners and committees – and i would also add, mr president, the political dialogue which we had with you when you were invited several times to the college of commissioners – through all these occasions we have been able to explore key measures across the full range of our work. the state of the union debate was at the core of this work. it set the tone. we were right to be ambitious for europe. our common messages were heard. many of them are indeed reflected in the recent european council conclusions, and they provide the backbone of the programme. the events of the last weeks only confirm that we are at a key moment in the history of our union. to secure the reforms that europe needs to transform itself, we have to win the confidence of our citizens and also of investors. we need a european renewal, and regaining confidence requires swift and decisive action. we are constantly being called upon to take swift decisions. last week we reshaped the commission’s rules to give a special role to the new task of vice-president for economic and monetary affairs. this was done as a matter of urgency to allow vice-president rehn to appear before this parliament’s committee on economic and monetary affairs on 23 november also as vice-president for the euro. for next week, we have accelerated the annual growth survey. we will also present new proposals on further deepening european union and euro area economic governance to provide further stability, discipline and convergence, and to complement the reforms agreed through the so-called ‘six-pack’. since we are going to have the opportunity tomorrow to discuss these matters in more detail, i will not go into this part now, but i know that we have the support of this parliament for such decisive action. the political consensus that we are shaping together to tackle the crisis is the springboard for this action. i can now say the same should be true for next year’s programme. by the end of 2012, we should see the ambitious measures we are putting forward today being passed into national law. we should see implementation starting to bite and have a real impact, and we will have further measures proposed by the commission. we know well what our common priorities are: we must achieve sustainable and job-creating growth; we must bring public finances back on track; we must restore confidence in our european union’s ability to get out of the economic crisis. over the next year, we can show that the european union has what we need to overcome the crisis and restore growth. it has the vision we need in the shape of our political consensus for action on this renewal. it should have the tools we need, with the transparent and democratic approach enshrined in the community method, and it has the collective determination we need to carry through ideas into action. our joint determination has also managed to move opposition in council to the programme of aid to the most deprived persons. following our insistence, council finally approved this scheme for the most deprived persons yesterday. the commission has already tabled a new proposal for after 2013. it is now up to this parliament and the council to decide on it. one thing should be clear: the commission does not give up on having this kind of programme after 2013. the commission has focused its work programme for 2012 on reinforcing stability and responsibility, while at the same time stimulating growth, doing everything we can to counter the very negative outlook we have today for the economic situation in europe. with the europe 2020 strategy we have the blueprint for achieving sustainable and job-creating growth. we now have to keep up the momentum and agree and implement changes that bring real benefit. we have to be coherent and consistent in implementation. we cannot just approve measures and then afterwards forget about their implementation. it is extremely important to follow on. europe 2020 can be the spark to a virtuous circle of growth, and i can count on your support to help give this process the political momentum it needs. the work of the european semester will be critical over the next year, to drill down action into member states and ensure that all parts of europe help each other to recover. part and parcel of this work is of course to ensure sound public finances. we cannot do this by turning our backs on ways to improve revenues. that is why we need to keep up the pressure for a financial transaction tax, and why we will be looking at new measures to tackle tax havens and counter vat fraud. we will also make a focused proposal on protecting the financial interests of the european union, including by criminal law. we will also press on with financial sector reform. key proposals will be on the table by the end of this year, including ones on bank resolution. next year we will press on with measures on investor protection, critical to deepening confidence in the sector. institutions for occupational retirement provision are also a sector to work on next year. the backbone of our strength, as we have said so often, is the single market. it has made us what we are today, the world’s largest economy. we need to further develop it and bring it into the 21st century so that it can continue to generate growth. twenty years on from its inception, we can show that the single market remains a key motor for sustainable growth in europe. this is why we have proposed fast-tracking the priority proposals set out in the single market act. we have accelerated our work on these proposals and we are asking the legislators to work to see these in law by the end of next year. there is a wide range of proposals now on the table. if we want to have a real impact on growth, and quickly, we need to adopt them and see them implemented. the european patent, roaming charges, the energy savings directive – these are all examples where early adoption would also show a european union determined to do everything possible to boost growth. the modern european economy also rests heavily on the digital single market. we will address the risks of electronic services being hampered by incompatible national copyright regimes, with a proposal on rules for the cross-border licensing of online music. a pan-european framework for electronic identification and signatures will give the confidence needed to boost electronic transactions across the european union. growth is also generated by consumers. their confidence is key to boosting demand. a comprehensive consumer agenda will provide a secure foundation for consumer transactions in the single market, while revised rules on general product safety will offer a clear framework both for consumers and manufacturers. the growth we need to achieve in the european union has to go hand in hand with the creation of sustainable jobs. we need to give a new momentum to flexicurity to drive a jobs-rich recovery, closely involving the social partners. more than ever, social dialogue is necessary both at european and at national level. we will help young people to move around europe with a youth on the move card. we also want to look again at the handling of supplementary pension rights of people who change jobs: this must not be allowed to remain an obstacle. i am also determined that we do not lose sight of our longer-term need to build an economic recovery that is sustainable. next year will be a key moment of transition to the revised emissions trading system. the rio+ summit will remind us of our global obligations for sustainability and green growth, looking in particular at a new water strategy. new proposals on emissions for passenger cars and vans will spur innovation and give manufacturers the necessary regulatory certainty. we will also draw the conclusions for legislation from the stress tests following the fukushima accident. i believe that next year we will see important initiatives in the field of green growth. i know that now, in the face of the difficult situation in economic and budgetary terms of many of our member states, speaking about this agenda is not so popular, but i believe that we need these kinds of initiatives more than ever and we are working precisely on linking some of our initiatives in terms of climate action and protection of the environment with the e-economy, the digital economy, so that we can indeed have important breakthroughs in terms of our action for green growth. providing security and justice in a borderless europe continues to be a big challenge. for an open europe to work, we need to make sure that its border regime is up-to-date. modernisation and the use of new technology will ensure that the system encourages cross-border activity while providing the necessary safeguards. i also believe this is a time of real opportunity for the european union on the global stage. this is key to recovery. we will be taking forward a wide range of bilateral trade negotiations, as well as continuing to make the case for a european approach in fora such the wto, the g20 and the g8. at the same time, we must continue to respond to the dramatic changes in the southern mediterranean. i believe we have a responsibility to do everything we can to help the post-transition societies there to develop successfully, and the commission is determined to support that process. i believe that longer-term stability and prosperity in our close neighbours is also – apart from our commitment to important values – in our very urgent interest. i know that we already have a wide agenda on the table. the measures on economic governance, on the single market, on financial services, not to mention the multi-annual financial framework, will make huge demands on us all over the coming year, and we know that we are also going to deal with these very important initiatives against a backdrop of economic financial instability, where the news coming from europe and also from other parts of the world is not always the best. that makes us need more than ever this spirit of responsibility and solidarity among the member states and among the european institutions. i believe that confidence comes through showing that the european union has the determination to act. i believe that in the past we have seen that, sometimes, it is under conditions of huge pressure and precisely when we are resisting or reacting to crises that the european union is able to show how important it is for the prosperity of our citizens. i hope the commission can count on your support in joining us in delivering concrete, ambitious action.

president of the european court of auditors. − mr president, i would like first of all to thank you for all the kind words that you have been so gently addressing to the european court of auditors. on behalf of all those who work there, my deepest thanks. we are indeed committed to continue further cooperation with this house, with the relevant committee, the budgetary control committee, and with all the committees – covering agriculture, regional development, or any other area – which find that our work is of relevance for the discharge of their responsibilities. this annual report provides this chamber with more detailed information. we have provided you with quantifiable indicators that might prove confusing to a non-expert reader. but we explain clearly that this offers you a kind of thermometer whereby you can compare a series of areas which are most likely to affect, and have a financial impact on, the payments underlying the budget. we can see the evolution since 2006 and we will be able to see how the situation develops after 2010;
