in writing. in favour of greater transparency in the activities of meps, i voted in favour of the report by my colleague carlo casini. the code of conduct aims to make members more accountable by declaring professional activities carried out in parallel with and before their term of office. the code of conduct also contains provisions on their parliamentary remuneration and any external remuneration and sanction mechanisms in the event of breaches of the code.
in writing. we all remember the scandal of meps who 'sold' their amendments to fake lobbyists who were in fact journalists. although the case concerned only a small minority of members, it was part of a general atmosphere of suspicion towards the political class and cast doubt on the integrity of members. by establishing strict rules on declaration of financial interests and the prevention of conflicts of interest, the code of conduct aims to improve transparency and thus - i hope - the image of meps in the public eye. a member will have to declare his parallel professional activities and those he had before his mandate, and the rapporteur may be removed from his role as rapporteur if a conflict of interest is discovered. the issue with the code of conduct is the restoration of accountability. it is a question of ensuring that such cases, which are harmful to all, do not happen again in the future!
in writing. i voted in favour of the introduction of this new code of conduct for meps. this code prohibits members from engaging in lobbying activities in parallel with their mandate, it prohibits us from receiving gifts of more than 150 euros, it obliges us to notify all our activities and remuneration during and before our mandate, and it obliges us to declare any membership of an association, any type of interest in a company or structure called "influence" and any other type of financial interest. in particular, i supported amendment no 10, which proposed to remove the threshold of eur 5000 for members to declare all paid outside activities. by setting these strict rules, parliament is thus seeking to bring about greater transparency and clarity in its day-to-day activities. it is also a question of restoring the external image of the meps and of combating the anti-parliamentarism that surrounds them. the challenge of this code is also to restore the responsibility of everyone; however, i regret that such measures are adopted only in response to scandals (remember the scandal of the 3 mps caught in flagrant corruption by lobbyists in march 2011).
in writing. i supported the creation of a strengthened code of conduct for meps to send a clear signal about my demands for transparency and respect by elected members of a number of ethical rules. i therefore consider it essential to prevent members from exercising a secondary professional activity involving lobbying activities which could unduly influence the exercise of their mandate. and to make sure that the possibility of abuse is clearly excluded, sanctions must be provided for, as is proposed in this code of conduct. finally, i rejected the initiatives to weaken this system, which some considered "too transparent" and which would not have achieved the objective of restoring the confidence of the citizens in their elected representatives.

in writing. in the face of the economic and financial crisis, the european parliament showed its resolve and ambition by adopting last september the economic governance package, which contains six legislative proposals all aimed at strengthening the eu's economic governance. these include the implementation of a european semester, which provides a forum for the evaluation and coordination of member states' economic and budgetary policies before they are adopted. while i am convinced that such coordination is essential to bring europe out of the crisis, i note that the berès report does not draw enough lessons from the first european semester, which was launched last july.

in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution by my colleague pervenche berès because it is essential that the emergence of european economic governance goes hand in hand with increased democratic control. in the face of the major changes that will have to take place if the union is to emerge from the crisis, it is essential that the decisions taken by europe have strong democratic legitimacy. this legitimacy can only be guaranteed by the european parliament's membership and participation in the annual elaboration of the broad guidelines of the eu's economic policy. it is particularly important that parliament should participate in the european semester procedure, during which each of the 27 draft national budgets is evaluated by the european commission. at the end of this procedure, parliament should have the opportunity to amend the macroeconomic policy guidelines proposed to the member states. this democratic development also requires a strengthened dialogue with national parliaments and the social partners, in order to support the coherence of european economic policy and to ensure that the eu2020 objectives are taken into account. finally, it is imperative that the revision of the treaties be possible only with the agreement and, where appropriate, the participation of parliament.

in writing. in may 2010, the commission proposed the introduction of a six-month period of stricter budgetary surveillance. this process has been in place since january 2011. the aim of the european semester is to strengthen coordination between member states and the european institutions while the budget lines for the following year are still at the draft stage. the aim is to ensure that national budgets are compatible with the stability or convergence programmes presented a few months ago and with the economic guidelines adopted at european level. during these six months (january to july), the budgetary and structural policies of the member states will be reviewed, on the basis of the information they provide, in order to detect any inconsistencies or signs of imbalance. i supported this resolution on the first european semester because it calls in particular for a strengthening of parliamentary control over the governance of the euro area both at national and european level. to strengthen the legitimacy of community action and to analyse the proposed measures, it is only natural that the representatives of the peoples should be involved.

in writing. in 2009, 161 000 people were infected with hiv in the european union and neighbouring countries, bringing the total number of people living with hiv to more than 2.2 million according to unaids and who estimates. the phenomenon is particularly worrying in eastern european countries, which are much more affected. i supported this resolution in plenary, as it recalls the commitments made at the high level meeting on hiv/aids at the united nations general assembly in 2011, including to ensure access to treatment for 15 million people living with hiv worldwide by 2015 and to reduce hiv infections by 50% by 2015. this can be achieved by combining all prevention and health policies in the member states, drawing on all the stakeholders: not only associations and ngos, medical staff, pharmaceutical laboratories, but also trade unions and the various national ministries. the eradication of this worldwide epidemic can only be achieved by this coordination of all actors.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which shows a strong political will on the part of the european parliament, and indeed the european union and its member states, to get involved in the fight against hiv/aids. the fight against this epidemic and all other stds or co-infectious diseases requires strong action by the public authorities. the european parliament is sending a strong signal, including by having the intelligence to remind us that the victory over this scourge is first and foremost a matter of prevention and 'sexual education' and 'close links between sexual and reproductive health services'. equally important is the european parliament's commitment to combating the stigma faced by people living with hiv/aids. such discrimination can even lead to the denial of medical care, which is unacceptable. it is a good thing that more than three quarters of the members of parliament are committed to this, which is not the case. i am sorry to see that some elected officials, no doubt influenced by reactionary movements, have such a backward attitude on such a subject. fundamentalists are not always muslims and not always from across the mediterranean.
in writing. convinced that the european neighbourhood policy contributes to the strengthening of democratic principles and good governance and stability in our immediate neighbourhood, i voted in favour of the legutko report. under the european neighbourhood policy, the eu is linked to a number of countries, including ukraine, by action plans. the association agreements are the first step in bringing them closer together. parliament recommended that the negotiations be based on the progressive establishment of a free trade area, respect for the rule of law, which had been undermined by the tymoshenko affair, and the maintenance of its political independence.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the negotiations on the eu-ukraine association agreement, firstly because it insists strongly on the conditionality of this agreement with the protection and promotion of human rights, and secondly because it recalls the strategic interest of ukraine for the european union, not only in terms of energy potential but also in terms of managing migration flows and fighting organised crime. the european union must remain firm in its values and principles, which is why the association agreement must be a real window of economic and commercial opportunity for ukraine, but it must demand in return that ukraine respects the european environmental commitment in its energy activities, that it respects democratic values, the independence of the judiciary, human rights and fundamental freedoms and, above all, that it respects all the commitments it has made under this association agreement. it is important to bear in mind that ukraine is now at the doorstep of the union, and that our closer ties with that country are linked to the effectiveness of our free trade area and our area of freedom, security and justice.
in writing. the european union has a strong interest in developing relations with third countries where they can benefit both parties in terms of political stability or economic opportunities. the association agreement currently being negotiated between the eu and ukraine responds to this logic - particularly in view of ukraine's geopolitical importance, its history and its resources - but goes further. it is a new type of agreement, more ambitious and even more promising, since it presupposes a significant implementation of the community acquis in the third country concerned. i therefore welcome the vote on the report by ryszard antoni legutko, who supports these negotiations, while expressly calling for respect for the rule of law and human rights - citing in particular the recent, worrying, conviction of former prime minister yulia tymoshenko. i also particularly welcome the european parliament's willingness to resume a necessary and effective dialogue with president yanukovych, the demand for reform of the judicial and electoral systems and the plan to strengthen energy cooperation to secure europe's energy supply.
in writing. as vice-chair of the foreign affairs committee and as a member of the international trade committee, i was able to follow all the work on these recommendations. when the international trade committee temporarily suspended its vote on the day of the sentencing of yulia tymoshenko, i approved this decision, which was a signal to ukraine that the european union is not only promoting its values, it is also defending them in practice. the recommendations presented to the plenary take full account of this consideration and that is why i voted in favour of them. i will, however, remain vigilant during the negotiations, because beyond my concerns about human rights, i also have doubts about the content of the trade part of this agreement. on the latter point, it will be important for ukraine to agree to make real concessions, in particular on the elimination of tariff and non-tariff barriers to exports and the acceptance of geographical indications.
in writing. in order to strengthen the competitiveness of european businesses and the safety of consumers, the european parliament calls for the modernisation of electronic systems in customs services. this modernisation requires a harmonised application of european customs legislation and simplification of customs procedures. i believe that this modernisation is essential for the proper functioning of the internal market, the fight against counterfeiting and the protection of intellectual property rights, and i therefore voted in favour of the salvini report.
in writing. i voted for the salvini report on the modernisation of customs services. the report recalls that customs must have sufficient resources to cope with their increased responsibilities. this is accompanied by a requirement for simplification, standardisation and modernisation of customs legislation and customs procedures.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the modernisation of the european customs strategy. with the dismantling of the internal borders of the european union, customs must have sufficient resources to face new challenges, particularly in terms of security and the prevention of illegal trafficking.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr salvini's report which stresses the crucial role played by customs services in protecting the internal market and consumers. modernisation must include simplification of procedures, taking into account the needs and expectations of smes and strengthening consumer protection and intellectual property rights. on the other hand, i believe that the list rules should be extended without restriction to complement the general principle of non-preferential origin of products based on the criterion of last substantial transformation, as they clarify the legal framework and thus reduce costs for economic operators (i therefore did not support paragraph 45 of the report).
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report from the committee on the internal market and consumer protection on the modernisation of customs services. parliament called on the commission and the member states to explore the possibility of further strengthening customs cooperation and regulatory harmonization in order to improve the functioning of the customs union. it is essential to simplify and modernise customs procedures and to increase the use of modern computer tools. thus, strengthening the fight against infringements, the illegal entry of counterfeit goods and products contributes to the overall competitiveness of the union, allowing businesses to take account of reliable information concerning the economic market.
in writing. this report is an opportunity to recall the crucial and protective role of customs authorities. they are responsible for the safety of goods and people on a daily basis, they must ensure that intellectual property, health regulations, immigration and product safety are respected - and all this without jeopardising freedom of movement within the european union! however, it is important to point out a common problem facing the customs authorities of the member states: the lack of resources. and let us be realistic, we cannot ask them to be the "fortress guards" and to deal with every situation, while cutting off their financial and human resources. i therefore hope that, in support of their efforts to dematerialize and rationalize controls, their cooperation and funding will be strengthened. this is the price at which we can continue to ensure effective and adequate protection for our citizens and businesses.

agreement with morocco. let me start first with the interim protocol. you are now going to decide whether or not this protocol can be concluded. the lead committee has adopted a positive recommendation, but i know that many of you are not convinced, so let me explain our position. as you know, this one-year protocol – an interim protocol – was agreed with morocco in february this year, just before the previous one expired. i am convinced that this decision was right. i believe even now that we have done the right thing. why? because the interim protocol provided us with the time to address those legal and political issues which are related to fishing in the waters of the western sahara. we have pressed morocco to provide us with reliable information that the local population benefits from the exploitation of these waters, as is required by international law. these efforts have given some potentially positive results. for the first time, the current protocol includes a formal requirement for morocco to report on benefits and their geographic distribution, and in so doing it sets an important precedent for any future protocol. with regard to economic and environmental issues, the mandate to extend the previous protocol did not leave us much room for manoeuvre during the last round of negotiations. in other words, we really did not have the possibility to go for a better agreement referring to economic and environmental issues. however, it is clear that any future negotiations will have to result in a better deal. after all, this interim protocol made it possible for fishing activities to continue without interruption. i know that a lot of you are not convinced about this, but i would just like to remind you that this is really important for some hundreds of european vessels fishing there, most of which are small-scale vessels. on the basis of a decision taken by the council in july, the protocol is now being applied provisionally. also be judged. the winds of change that have affected the southern mediterranean and some countries beyond have touched morocco too. so what is the commission’s assessment of this? the commission assessment is that, in morocco, the authorities have launched a significant process of reform with the elaboration of a new constitution, increasing democratic accountability and respect for human rights as well as the successful holding of parliamentary elections which have brought new forces to power. the european union, at all levels, has welcomed these changes. this house has also called for the eu to support the process of democratic reform in morocco. that is the framework we have to bear in mind when making our decisions. as i said in the committee on fisheries last month, the deal with morocco that we should be aiming at? first, on economic profitability. we are definitely seeking value for money. it is imperative that any new protocol should ensure a better utilisation of available fishing possibilities as well as an overall financial envelope that clearly reflects market value, as other committees of this house are asking for. second, on environmental sustainability. this means that we will be defining fishing possibilities based on best available scientific advice and also that we will be targeting only the surplus. third, on international legality. with regard option of including the waters off western sahara, then we would need to demonstrate, through a strict and rigorous reporting mechanism, that there are economic benefits for the regions and local populations concerned. this would become a condition in the new protocol. on all these issues, we will draw on the conclusions from the implementation of the present protocol as well as from the debates in this house. the committee on fisheries last month recommended that parliament consent to the conclusion of the protocol. if that approach is followed by this house, then we will very soon be ready to move ahead towards a better protocol to this agreement.

i'm the reporter. - madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, europe is currently facing major changes: economic, monetary, social, demographic and migration. the changes which are sweeping and shaking europe are considerable and call for a rethinking of european policies. europe is at a turning point and it is our responsibility to meet these challenges. one of the major challenges we will face in the coming years is the shortage of labour. our weak demographic dynamic is the european achilles' heel. by 2050, one in three europeans will be over 65 and 20 million skilled jobs will be unfilled. it would take 3.2 million immigrants a year by 2050 to maintain the age pyramid as it is today. this demographic deficit justifies and makes it necessary to resort to immigration. it is time to accept this state of affairs, to take stock of these changes and finally to act accordingly. the european commission, aware of this problem, has proposed a set of measures: the blue card directive in 2009, the single permit directive, the directive on seasonal workers and intra-group transfers seek to address these issues. the time has come to seize this opportunity. the single permit directive is partly a response to this labour force crisis which is looming on the european horizon. it also makes it possible to control the workforce. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. the single european act allows workers from third countries to come to work in europe on a harmonised and regulated basis. it protects workers in third countries from smugglers and other mafia networks who exploit and abuse their vulnerability. the procedures for applying for permits are greatly simplified. a single residence and work permit can be obtained in a maximum of four months. applications may be submitted by the employer in europe or by the worker in the third country in which he is present. in addition, there is a right of appeal in the member state procedure in which the person makes the request. the information on the single permit is also standardised and clarified for the whole of the european union. these are the same as those on the work permit. additional information may be requested. they remain optional and their content is very limited. the single permit, in addition to considerably simplifying the procedures for residence and work permits, makes it possible to assign a common set of rights to workers from third countries and to workers from the european union. until now, there has been a real disparity between member states, and we could not be satisfied with that. it was abnormal not to recognize the rights of foreign workers who contribute so much to our economies. this is a just and necessary step. equal treatment of workers is at the heart of this directive, which places workers from third countries on an equal footing with european workers. workers from third countries enjoy the same rights as european workers as regards their wages and dismissal conditions. the same rules also apply to the recognition of diplomas, freedom of association and membership of a professional organisation, social security, tax benefits and access to public goods and services. in addition, people who have a job will benefit from equal treatment in access to education and employment. employment services will also be available to the unemployed and, therefore, to those who need them most. the export of pensions will no longer be subject to the existence of bilateral agreements between member states and third countries. equal treatment will be the rule here too. this is a step forward in recognising the value of the work of citizens from third countries and taking this into account when assuring them of their pension rights. as a member of the group of the european people's party, i am very proud to have taken part in these long negotiations. i would like to thank the european commission, and especially cecilia malmström and her services, who have made it possible for the directive to come into being. i also thank the successive presidencies - spanish, belgian, hungarian and polish - for their commitment. i thank my colleagues in this house for their relevant proposals and their support in the negotiations. we can now rejoice in the result of our efforts. this is a welcome development and reflects the image of a europe of dignity and justice, which respects every worker who contributes to european growth.

mr president, the umpteenth european summit of the last chance will very likely have the same results as the previous ones. in its forced march towards technocratic federalism in the most total disregard of the elementary rules of democracy, this summit has set in stone the policy of austerity and the submission of national budgets to the dictates of the commission and the court of justice with, at the core, automatic financial sanctions for the states. markets dreamed of it, governments did it. the consequences will be a collapse in consumption and an explosion in our public deficits. the problem of sovereign debt is not behind us, it is ahead of us. one thing remains, however, and it is the real beneficiaries of this umpteenth summit for nothing. once again, the banking and financial sector is privileged, to the detriment of the states and taxpayers. europeans are watching, powerless, as private debt is being transferred onto their shoulders, with the complicity of a political class at the service of the banks and the financial markets. this, the people will not forgive you!
mr president, i think that this agreement raises a number of questions. the first of these is the following. this agreement was presented as a historic, decisive and solution to the crisis. i'm not at all sure. i think it is just one more step, not necessarily the best, and obviously it will not be able to solve the crisis. i am afraid that the answer is no. in fact, in the economic, social and financial uncertainties we are living through, it is not very relevant to add periods of legal uncertainty. that's my first point. as regards the content, we were told that budgetary discipline would be made constitutional. i think this deal is lame. the europe we need is a europe which has budgetary discipline on the one hand and budgetary solidarity on the other. as you said, mr barroso, we cannot have one without the other, or the other without the other! it is enough to consider that europe can guarantee, through the ecb, attractive loans to indebted countries, provided that they carry out the structural reforms that are needed at home, not because europe asks them to, but for themselves. so the two must go together. the last point is that we are told that we are going to build an intergovernmental europe. i think this is a mistake. it is a mistake to deny community inspiration. it is a mistake to turn away from community institutions, democracy and democratic control of our institutions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first a few thoughts on the currency. the nineteenth century was dominated by the pound sterling, the twentieth century by the dollar; in the 21st century, we don't know how currencies will organize themselves. that's one of the issues that the g20 chairman brought to the table. we have a duty to organise the management of our currency. traditionally, we had a currency for a state. we are experimenting with a currency for one region, a supranational currency. it is good news, mr president, that we have achieved this economic zone of 26 states. hungary, which changed its mind, denmark, which was not obliged to, joined the eurozone. that's good news! the united kingdom is a large european country. we know why it did not join the euro area: it is because of financial services, as you said, mr president. and because in reality he does not want a financial transaction tax, for which a political consensus is emerging. the second good news is financial stability. all our great democracies except greece which is a special case - the findings say so - have changed their governments, have taken serious measures on financial management. we are in the process of organizing the financial stability of our continent. that's good news! i do not believe in contagion and we must uphold the golden rules and reform our stability pact. there are two issues that are not resolved. first, the growth. mr president, i think it is time for a specific european council to examine the conditions for growth and a major european investment plan. secondly, the enormous disappointment of the democrats, who have not heard a word - contrary to the letter from mrs merkel and president sarkozy - about a parliamentary dimension. it is not normal that the heads of state or government have not given a parliamentary dimension to economic governance! i suggest you do something about it. in writing. the new treaty that the german right wants to be adopted would deprive the member states of fiscal policy, imposing on them austerity policies that are about to plunge europe into recession without reducing deficits. economic policy choices would be enshrined in the constitutions and subject to the authority of a court of justice. automatic sanctions would be applied to countries with government deficits exceeding 3% of gdp. but this treaty does not provide for any response to the economic and social emergency: neither eurobonds nor intervention by the ecb on the primary market to buy government bonds. why, then, should we be surprised by the rise of euroscepticism? it is becoming urgent to show that a progressive economic strategy is possible. we call for the creation of a european treasury, of which the efsf could be the embryo, and an independent rating agency, backed by the european court of auditors. the power to rate sovereign debts would be taken away from private agencies, which have clear conflicts of interest. we also propose an investment pact to boost the economy by excluding investment expenditure from the calculation of government deficits. with an increased community budget through eurobonds and the ftt, we would finance the upward convergence of competitiveness levels and social and fiscal standards.

in writing. i welcome the adoption of this draft directive, which complements the legal arsenal we are developing at european level in the field of procedural guarantees. in december 2009, the council adopted the stockholm programme, which sets out the priorities for the establishment of a genuine european area of freedom, security and justice. it is an ambitious programme, particularly in terms of procedural guarantees, through the establishment of a minimum set of procedural rights to be granted to persons involved in criminal proceedings. the rights of these people must be strengthened and a balance must be struck between the considerable progress made in cooperation on the part of the prosecution and the long delay in the rights of the defence. the text adopted today is the second measure adopted in this area, with another directive on the right of access to a lawyer currently being discussed within the european institutions, and a directive on legal aid planned for 2012. the adoption of this directive represents real progress, but there is still a long way to go before we have real guarantees for the rights of the defence within the european union.

in writing. the completion of the internal market requires the creation of a single area of justice, operating under common rules and ensuring that citizens' rights are guaranteed in a uniform manner. thus, any european citizen suspected of a crime within the union must have his or her fundamental rights respected in any member state. i welcome the adoption of the birgit sippel report in this respect. this text, by establishing common minimum standards, ensures a right to information within the union, valid as soon as the person is informed that he is the subject of suspicion. this immediacy of information is, in my view, paramount. i also welcome the extension of the range of rights associated with this right to information, which makes it quite satisfactory as it covers both translation, interpretation, assistance by a lawyer, information on the charge, access to evidence or the right to remain silent, and the provision of a statement of rights containing information on the legal conditions of arrest and detention. although this text is only a step in the roadmap on procedural rights, the provisions it contains are indispensable. i hope that they will be addressed in the future comprehensive legislative package that the commission will present shortly.

in writing. i supported the adoption of this directive because it will change the daily lives of many people particularly women and make them safer from their abusers. the european protection order is fundamental to help victims benefit from decisions issued by a national authority, valid in all eu countries, including a prohibition on the aggressor approaching the victim within a certain distance if there is a court decision to that effect, contacting the victim (by telephone, fax, mail, internet, etc.), going to certain defined places, such as the victim's home or places she frequents. finally, i welcome the adoption of a provision whereby, in the event of a violation of this decision, the member state of reception of the victim could impose penalties on the aggressor, whether criminal or not: this is an essential guarantee to restore calm to the victims of unacceptable violence.
in writing. i voted today in favour of the report introducing the directive on a european protection order. this new instrument will enable a person protected by criminal law in one eu country to benefit from similar protection when travelling to another member state, if he or she so requests. this new instrument will greatly help victims of violence to lead a normal life in another member state of the european union. originally designed to protect victims of gender-based violence across the european union, the scope of this tool has been extended to protect any victim of any form of violence (harassment, abduction, stalking or attempted murder), both men and women, who can benefit from this new protection. this is a further step towards the establishment of a european area of justice.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the european protection decision, which will allow us to take an important step towards establishing genuine crossborder protection for victims of violence. the text will concern victims who are protected in a member state, in accordance with their national criminal law, because of an act or behaviour which has been established to be likely to endanger their life or physical, psychological or sexual integrity. in many cases, the member state of the victims then prohibits the aggressor from going near the residence of the person subject to the protection measure or to places frequented by the person, or provides for a prohibition on contact or approach to the victim. from now on, these victims will be able to apply for a 'european protection decision' to extend this protection to other member states where they wish to go (or already reside). thanks to parliament's action, this decision can also be extended to the family of the protected persons. i am very concerned about the protection of victims and i regard this text as a step forward which will soon be complemented by our work on the civil aspect.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which aims to harmonise the protection of victims of different types of crime in the different member states: sexual violence, harassment, abduction, persecution or attempted murder. the aim is, in theory, to prevent such crimes and offences as well as to mitigate the consequences for the victims. the aim is to protect more specifically those affected in their physical and/or sexual integrity. these people are mostly women. it is also necessary to approximate the laws and judicial systems of the member states. however, these advances have not been achieved without difficulty. it took almost a year for the council to take a decision on the first proposal voted by the european parliament. it is obviously much more difficult to harmonize criminal legislation in the interests of vulnerable populations than to amend the treaties to impose budgetary austerity. understand who can.
in writing. the single permit was a commendable initiative at the outset. today's vote is a step forward, but the directive is far from the idea of a framework directive. the single permit should have been the framework directive for an immigration package, creating the same conditions for all on the basis of the principle of equal treatment, without excluding categories of workers. the risk of a fragmented labour market exists here: equal treatment is accompanied by many exceptions and certain categories of workers are excluded from the scope. the report is therefore mixed, but the current negotiations on the sectoral directives resulting from the single permit are continuing and they give us the opportunity to do better. we are currently advocating in the european parliament a progressive vision of the rights of movement and social rights for a particularly vulnerable category, namely seasonal workers. this immigration package will only be progress if it brings with it an improvement in the living and working conditions of workers from third countries.
in writing. with the adoption of the single permit, we have taken a further step towards equal treatment of workers, but also towards the development of a coherent immigration policy, by reducing the inequality of rights between citizens of the union and third-country nationals legally working in a member state. the single permit directive thus complements other measures on legal immigration, such as the blue card, and should also facilitate immigration insofar as it meets the needs of the european labour market. the 'single permit' will make it possible to obtain a work and residence permit by means of a single procedure, thus greatly reducing administrative formalities. holders of a single permit will be able to enjoy a set of basic rights comparable to those of eu workers, such as basic decent working conditions, recognition of qualifications, the right to join trade unions and access to pensions, social security. the aim is to create equivalent minimum conditions throughout the union, to recognise that such third country nationals contribute, through their work and the taxes they pay, to the union's economy.
in writing. after numerous trilogues and a failed first reading, parliament voted in favour of the draft directive on the creation of a single residence and work permit for third-country nationals. last year, when we voted on the first reading, i voted against this draft directive because it allowed the member states to issue additional documents in addition to the single permit, totally ruining the very idea of the 'single permit'. the revised text deletes this reference and calls on the member states to draw up 'correspondence tables' which enable the commission to check the transposition of the directive. that is why i voted for this new text, which provides for a single application procedure which is simpler, faster for people wishing to come to work in the territory of a state, and guarantees a common base of rights to be granted to these workers. it is true that the text is not perfect. i would have liked this text to be much more comprehensive and not to exclude certain categories of workers such as posted workers or seasonal workers, or to guarantee more rights. but i think that a lot of progress has been made in the negotiations, particularly with regard to working conditions, access to vocational training and pension rights, etc.
in writing. i abstained on the adoption of this single licence, which has only one name. the council has also adopted a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. however, even if the result is not what the socialists wanted, there are several positive elements: firstly, workers from third countries covered by this directive will now be able to enjoy the transfer of their pension rights under the same conditions as nationals of the member state where they worked, and secondly, the principle of equal treatment prevails for vocational training, access to advice provided by employment services, access to housing and the right to associate and join a trade union organisation. with a council and a european parliament dominated by the right, it seemed difficult to go any further, even if the overall result remains unsatisfactory.
in writing. i am against this legislation merging the applications for residence and work permits of migrants into a single procedure: it puts a new corner in the equality between all employees and the rights of certain workers. there will be no more workers, but european and non-european wage-earners, not to mention illegal immigrant workers. worse still, this text establishes a link between residence permits and work permits and makes the former dependent on the duration of the latter. the european union, which prides itself on defending human and social rights, decides to consider migrants only as a simple adjustment variable of the workforce that does not deserve the same rights as other employees. what is presented as progress is in reality nothing more than the institutionalisation of the growing inequality between all those living in the union. the european parliament rejected this text at first reading a year ago, so it is difficult to understand why some members have changed their position, when the text before us today is virtually identical to that at first reading.
in writing. in the face of the economic and financial crisis, european solidarity is more relevant than ever. this european solidarity is at the heart of the union's rural development policy, which provides support to regions with economic backwardness through the european agricultural fund for rural development (eafrd). at present, some member states are no longer able to co-finance certain development projects because of a lack of liquidity. in favour of a strong rural development policy, i voted in favour of a european parliament resolution to temporarily increase the co-financing rate for certain projects (which can be increased to 95% in very specific cases). these projects will be targeted and will have to contribute to the economic recovery of greece and portugal in particular.
in writing. with the adoption of the paolo de castro report, the eu finally seems to be able to be both helpful and supportive. in order to respond to the crisis, europe decided to take transitional measures until the end of 2013, granting member states in financial difficulty such as greece, romania and portugal very favourable co-financing rates of up to 95% to finance rural development projects to encourage economic recovery. i supported the increase in eafrd co-financing rates to ensure that eu countries with weak growth prospects and weak public finances do not see their projects halted on the ground. however, this positive approach to supporting countries in financial difficulty with regard to rural development must also be accompanied by a similar approach in these countries for regional development projects. it is by ensuring synergy between the projects financed by the various european funds that we can make an effective and lasting contribution to the economic development and growth of these states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which makes it possible to temporarily support the european states most in difficulty by relieving them of part of the funding for national social policy and rural development. this is a good example of how european funds can be better allocated to meet the needs of our territories in difficult times without increasing the contribution of our states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report because the european union needs to increase its support for its regions, especially rural ones, in order to promote economic recovery. the commission proposal to temporarily increase the maximum union co-financing rate for eafrd (european agricultural fund for rural development) programmes in states in difficulty which are beneficiaries of the european financial stabilisation mechanism (euro area) or the balance of payments financial support mechanism (non-euro area) should therefore be supported. the commission proposal is paradoxical, however, since it also supports the franco-german proposal to suspend the disbursement of regional funds to states in difficulty in order to force them to control their public accounts. sanctioning these states by suspending cohesion policy funds, while offering them increased support for eafrd programmes, amounts to arbitrary discrimination against non-agricultural areas. to overcome the economic crisis, the european union must provide support to all regions in difficulty.
in writing. the euro area and europe as a whole is plunged into the most serious crisis since 1945, in an unprecedented financial turmoil. this crisis has struck a number of states with particular violence and threatens the stability of europe as a whole. the agreement reached by the heads of state and government on friday must therefore be accompanied by concrete measures to enable the states most affected by the crisis to continue their investment plans and programmes for the future. because europe is also solidarity. and when funds exist, programmes and projects have been committed, but cannot be implemented because of insufficient resources in states in financial difficulties, it is up to the eu to act quickly by setting up, exceptionally and with the guarantee that it will have no long-term budgetary impact, appropriate financial assistance. the decision to support six countries by temporarily raising the eafrd participation rates and therefore reducing the national contribution is a logical solution and consistent with the decision taken at the end of november to raise the cofinancing rates of the structural funds.
in writing. to help our companies gain market share abroad, we must demand the removal of trade barriers that impede trade between the eu and its trading partners, but also reciprocity in market access. to this end, it is necessary to keep an inventory of such barriers and to set up an early warning mechanism. in view of the growth of world trade outside the european union, it is becoming urgent for the commission to present a legislative proposal on a reciprocity instrument for access to public contracts in third countries. the impact of foreign direct investments on the internal market also needs to be assessed in order to prevent any detrimental consequences they may have on european innovation and know-how in certain strategic sectors. the know-how of our european companies in the fields of infrastructure, transport, construction and high technology is recognised worldwide, so it is up to us to do everything we can to enable them to gain access to new markets.
in writing. free movement is a founding principle of the european economic community and in a world where the interdependence of economies has also revealed its weaknesses, it is essential to consolidate the basis of trade on fairer foundations, where the principle of reciprocity is respected. the fact is that the european union still faces unjustified tariff and regulatory barriers from some of its partners, which limits our companies' access to these high-potential markets and investment. by 2015, 90% of global growth will be generated outside the european union. it's a parameter we can't ignore. it's not a parameter we can ignore. the future of our companies will also be played out beyond our borders. i therefore support the measures proposed in this report to remove these unjustified restrictions: an inventory by the commission of the main obstacles, the establishment of an early warning mechanism, the strengthening of public procurement disciplines which could lead, by next year, to the presentation of a reciprocity instrument for access to public contracts in third countries.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by robert sturdy on barriers to trade and investment. as rapporteur for the imco opinion on this subject, i welcome the fact that the european parliament is setting clear guidelines for the european commission to enable european companies to compete on equal terms with their foreign competitors, especially since by 2015, 90% of global growth will be generated outside the european union. it is therefore important to clearly identify the trade barriers that impede trade between the european union and its trading partners and to remove them in order to help our companies gain market share abroad. the european union's trade policy must be based on the principles of reciprocity, fairness and fair competition. i am also pleased to see that the european parliament supports the idea of launching a reflection at european level on the desirability of assessing the impact of foreign direct investments on the internal market in order to prevent any possible harmful consequences they might have on european innovation and know-how in certain strategic sectors. that was the aim of one of the amendments i tabled.
in writing. for the first time this year, the european commission has taken stock of the barriers to trade and investment that our companies face in third country markets. this initiative, which i welcome, will make it possible to combat these obstacles more effectively and thus help to open up new markets. the european parliament's report on this report proposes complementary solutions, two of which seem particularly interesting to me. first, to keep an up-to-date inventory of these barriers, which companies could consult to better equip themselves before entering a market. the second is to set up an early warning mechanism based on the expertise and knowledge of the field of the union's delegations and embassies and consulates abroad. both of these solutions can be implemented quickly without incurring any additional costs. that is why i supported them in the vote.
in writing. i voted against this report which praises the ultra-liberal dogma: "let us remove all the barriers to world trade (here the non-tariff barriers are in question) and trade will bring prosperity to all those who make it their religion". it goes without saying that in the midst of the economic crisis, when every day brings new unemployed and excluded, this text is a provocation that ignores the worsening of social inequalities and environmental issues. i refuse this free-trade, no-rules, no-morals, forward flight. trade is not just about trade and profit. they must allow the movement of people, ideas and goods, taking into account each country and each population, and serve the building of new solidarities.

in writing. i voted in favour of the new european rules on the composition and labelling of fruit juices set out in the perello rodriguez report. these rules will improve consumer information on the contents of juices. the label without added sugars will no longer be misused. the new rules will also help to protect the consumer, particularly those with diabetes, by clearly distinguishing between fruit juices and nectars with different sugar content.
in writing. new labelling rules for fruit juices and nectars have been approved by the european parliament, providing greater transparency for consumers. the aim is to inform consumers so that they have clear indications as to what is a genuine juice and what is not. these rules are intended to prevent potentially misleading names being given to fruit juice mixtures and to specify the claim 'without added sugars' in order to ensure that the presence of sugars or sweeteners is quickly and clearly known. from now on, a mixture of two juices will also have to be given a name which fully reflects its content. consumers must be informed as much as possible so that they can make informed purchases of food products such as fruit juices.
in writing. the vote to improve the labelling of fruit juices and nectars will prevent europeans from being misled about the composition of these products, especially when they are mixtures of several juices. this will enable consumers to know, in the case of a juice mixture, the exact proportion of each fruit used in the mixture. the name of the juice mixture should also better reflect the actual composition of the beverage, indicating the different fruits used. moreover, clearer information on the sugar and sweetener content of these products will also be added to the labels. in concrete terms, fruit juices will by definition not contain any added sugar or sweetener, unlike nectars, for which europeans with diabetes or following a particular diet will now be able to choose better products that suit them.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report specifying the contents of fruit juice drinks in order to give our citizens guarantees about the contents of the products they buy and thus enable them to make better informed consumer choices. it is essential to have a transparent exchange within the single market.
in writing. it was essential to provide consumers with the best possible information on the different types of fruit juices on the market (fruit juice, fruit juice based on concentrate or nectar) and on their composition. i am particularly pleased that the possibility of adding mandarin/clementine juice to orange juices without mentioning it in the sales description has not been adopted. to put tangerine juice in orange juice without declaring it was a fraudulent practice and a real deception! this would also have the effect of exposing the orange juice market to distortions of competition. the addition of sugar is now prohibited for all fruit juices and the directive provides for a special mention on the labelling to inform the consumer of this change.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which is a compromise with the council to clarify the labelling of fruit nectars containing sweeteners, the labelling of fruit juices containing several fruits, and the use of water in fruit juices.
in writing. the european union must ensure that its citizens have access to products that meet high standards of quality, sustainability and fairness. this is particularly true in the food sector, where consumers are usually very careful about their nutrition and health. i therefore voted in favour of the report by mr perello rodriguez on the directive on fruit juices and certain similar products intended for human consumption. new rules are needed. i particularly welcome the measures to clarify the different types of juice, to remove sugar from the list of authorized ingredients, to clearly and transparently label the proportions of fruit contained in the juice and to control the flavourings used. moreover, the application of such rules to products manufactured in europe as well as to those to be imported is fundamental. this report is aimed at improving consumer information and protection, and at finding the best possible quality for the products we consume every day, and i welcome this.
in writing. since the use of phosphates is bad for the environment, we must gradually learn to do without them. this has already been the case in france since 2007. i voted in favour of this report because it allows the ban on phosphates to be extended to the whole of the european union to products for washing laundry and dishes. thanks to the european union, our environment and our health are better protected.
in writing. detergents are the third largest source of phosphate discharges to surface water, after agriculture and waste water. phosphates are used in detergents to reduce water hardness and improve washing. they are extremely harmful to the ecological balance of the waters of lakes and rivers, and especially to aquatic life. indeed, it is these phosphates that promote the growth of algae that kill other aquatic species by depriving them of oxygen. the adoption of a directive aimed at limiting the use of phosphates is therefore a step forward in our fight to improve water quality and sustainable development. this is only a step forward, because the text deals for the moment only with the quantity of phosphates per wash and will not apply to dishwashers until 2015.
in writing. the european marine environment and inland waterways are heavily polluted by phosphates contained in laundry and dishwashing products. when phosphates are released into streams or the sea, they promote the growth of algae that are harmful to aquatic life. the proportion of phosphorus allowed in washing powders must therefore be reduced as much as possible, and thus european aquatic environments must be preserved. european consumers will benefit from more environmentally friendly cleaning products from 2017.
in writing. i supported the adoption of this report which will significantly reduce the use of phosphates in detergents. this measure is in line with the french environmental charter and the european policy of preserving fauna and flora, by encouraging the use of products that are more respectful of our environment.
in writing. phosphates are mainly used to increase the efficiency of washing and are largely responsible, together with nitrates, for the development of algae and green or red tides. i am pleased that the revision of the regulation significantly limiting the use of phosphates and phosphorus compounds in detergents was adopted by a large majority. although this has already been the case in france since 2007, i am very pleased that the ban on phosphates in eu household laundry will be extended to all member states from january 2013. this is a double victory, since, under pressure from the european parliament, the member states have extended the ban on the use of these phosphates also to dishwasher detergents. i would remind you that in france 20 million washing machines are made every day and that 88 kg of household products are used by french households every year.
in writing. the environment is a precious commodity and we must do everything in our power to preserve it. france has already banned phosphates in laundry detergents since 2007, but this measure was not applied in all of europe. phosphates in wastewater contribute to the growth of algae, which cause green and red tides and damage aquatic fauna and flora. this measure, which will be extended to dishwashing products, will be applicable from january 2013, and i am glad of it, because if we take the case of france alone, twenty million washing machines are made daily and 88 kg of household products are used per household each year.
in writing. i have supported this report which makes it possible to strengthen consumer protection and environmental protection by reducing to minimum levels the presence of phosphates in detergents in the european union. the reduction of the presence of phosphorus compounds in waste water will help to combat the eutrophication process in lakes and rivers (algae growth).
in writing. i voted today in favour of the newton dunn report on the use of phosphates and other phosphorus compounds in household textile detergents. in future, washing machine powders and dishwashing detergents will have to be almost free of phosphorus. parliament and the council also wanted to include dishwasher detergents in this legislation, while giving enough time - until 2017 - for manufacturers to adapt their products. the deadline is 2013 for washing machine powders. although such provisions have already been in force in france since 2007, i welcome the fact that the ban on phosphates is being extended to all member states, as their release into inland waterways leads, together with nitrates, to the proliferation of green algae that suffocate fish and destroy other forms of aquatic life.
in writing. the harmfulness of phosphate discharges into our seas has been demonstrated. the latter are indeed implicated in the unfortunately well-known phenomenon of 'green tides'. they are loaded with nutrients and cause a massive growth of algae, releasing toxins that endanger marine fauna and flora but also alter the quality of the water. a considerable proportion of these phosphates come from the waste from detergents used in washing machines and dishwashers. the fact that alternatives to the use of phosphates in cleaning products existed made action essential. i therefore supported the report by mr bill newton dunn. i appreciate his commitment to a ceiling on the level of phosphates in products and i particularly welcome his efforts to extend the application of this regulation not only to textile detergents - as the commission had originally proposed - but also to dishwasher detergents. i also support his request for a future evaluation of the extension of application to industrial and institutional detergents. finally, the choice of a regulation was entirely appropriate in order to ensure uniform implementation within the single market.

in writing. now more than ever, morocco needed the support of the european union, not only in the current context of the arab spring, but also and above all because morocco is one of our closest partners. this agreement was necessary because it allowed 10 member states to fish in moroccan waters in exchange for financial compensation for the development of moroccan fisheries policy throughout moroccan territory. the european parliament cannot and must not abandon a historic partner of the eu. we must now do everything we can to consolidate the partnership agreements with morocco and propose new ones on new bases in order to support the democratic process under way.
in writing. because morocco is committed to sustainable fishing, and because hundreds of european fishermen and thousands of moroccan workers depend on it, i voted in favour of extending the protocol to the fisheries agreement between the european union and morocco. today's vote against extending the agreement is very regrettable. the risk today is that it will undermine the negotiations on the next agreement that the european union needs, not to mention the negative signal sent to one of our most reliable partners.
in writing. i supported the eu-morocco fisheries partnership agreement. i regret that a large majority of members voted against the extension of this fisheries protocol. we are sending a very negative signal to morocco at a time when we must support this great country in the process of political and economic reform and democratization which it has initiated. the negative vote by parliament is all the more distressing as the agreement is already in force and was due to expire in february 2012. it allowed 10 member states to fish in moroccan waters in exchange for financial compensation for the development of moroccan fisheries policy throughout moroccan territory. in practical terms, this means that 120 european fishing vessels will have to stop their activities in moroccan waters immediately! in the end, it is perhaps a total abandonment of the partnership agreements with morocco that is to be feared, which would be highly detrimental to the development of morocco and the relations we have so far built with that country.

in writing. the european parliament called on the eu member states to increase cooperation in the defence sector. the crisis has revealed the weaknesses of the european defence and security policy, which requires a thorough reform. each year, member states spend a total of €200 billion on defence, which is only one third of the us budget. states are undergoing a cure of austerity and defence budgets are being affected. the budgetary constraint weighs on the defence capabilities of our states and upsets our relations with our partners, particularly the united states, which must bear the costs of this disengagement, as the libyan case shows. there are significant risk pockets in the sahel and the horn of africa that can pose threats to europe. we must therefore have an ambitious security and defence policy, both in terms of operations and capabilities, a policy of means which encourages the pooling and sharing of certain capabilities in the search for optimum use.

persistence of mass unemployment and the explosion of precarious work. according to the european agency for safety and health at work, 168 000 people die in europe each year from work-related accidents and diseases, more than half of them from cancer and a quarter from cardiovascular disease. how can we not be shocked by this growing number? as rapporteur on the evaluation of this european strategy for health and safety at work, which will end in 2012, my conclusions are clear. it would be a moral mistake to turn a blind eye to suffering at work. it would also be an economic mistake, since all the studies show that accidents and occupational diseases are costly, both to our health and social security systems and to our companies. this strategy must be more ambitious, more coherent and above all much more courageous from 2013 onwards. the legislative framework must be strengthened and the legislation adapted to new risks, such as psychosocial risks, musculoskeletal disorders and nanomaterials. stress at work should not be treated by mere training, which is completely inadequate when one in two european workers is exposed to risks affecting his mental health. the truth must be said loud and clear: workers suffer most from the sudden reorganisation of work, its intensification and the failure of management methods. in addition, many employees warn of risks to people and the environment. these people need to be protected. i am proud that we are here in parliament asking the european commission for a directive to protect these famous whistleblowers. the european commission right to the protection of their health. in addition, we are seeing an increase in the outsourcing of jobs and the emergence of cascading subcontracting. new workers are emerging from the prevention sphere: precarious workers, fake selfemployed, subcontracted workers, particularly in the nuclear sector. given the exposure to high levels of radiation and the danger associated with the handling of
