in writing. despite some reservations, i voted in favour of this report, which sets ambitious and positive targets, including reducing co2 emissions in the transport sector by 2020. however, i regret that mega trucks (these giant trucks up to 60 tonnes and 25 metres long) are mentioned in this report. these road monsters are a real danger to road safety, because they are not suited to infrastructure at all and they can seriously damage it. the report also calls for the development of a european transport policy that is more environmentally friendly and more environmentally friendly.
in writing. i supported the report on the roadmap for a single european transport area, as it includes a number of road safety and co2 reduction objectives and stresses the importance of internalising external costs (noise for example).
in writing. although this is an own-initiative report, this text reminds the commission and the member states of our concerns about the delay in implementing a genuine european transport area. we are first and foremost elected representatives of the people, and we know the realities facing our citizens, to live them on a daily basis. that is the meaning of my vote in favour of this text. a lot has been achieved in the last 20 years. but there is still a long way to go. i would like to recall one of the essential roles of transport networks: to plan our territories correctly and sustainably. europe is sometimes too absent from these issues, whereas territorial cohesion is now one of its prerogatives. i hope that this report will be seen as a new beginning for the european union's action in our territories. supporting the transeuropean transport networks is not enough. it is now necessary for europe to promote territorial projects around the establishment of these major infrastructures. i am thinking in particular of the arrival of high-speed rail lines, which are making such a good contribution to the opening up of the territories and are also an important lever for local development.
in writing. the single market cannot function without the creation of a european transport area, which is essential to ensure that trade can take place between the different member states of the union without technical barriers, without additional costs and in a sustainable manner. i welcome the adoption of the report by mr grosch, entitled 'roadmap for a single european transport area', which supports the objectives of interoperability of transport systems in europe and the reduction of their environmental footprint. building on the proposals set out in the commission's white paper published last march, it takes up ideas that are highly relevant and indispensable to improving transport systems in europe, such as the principle of ease of use, the best use of rail, inland waterway and maritime transport, and the promotion of clean urban transport. this must of course be done with respect for workers, quality of services, safety standards, the environment, at prices that are affordable for all and in a technologically neutral way. these elements are included in the report, and i welcome this.
in writing. i voted against the report on the single european transport area. this text proposes a european area which aims to improve transport conditions solely through the ultra-liberal dogma that, as always, it is up to the market to take the lead. the objectives, however praiseworthy they may seem, are swept away by these deadly logics. on the contrary, public aid is welcome both for the financing of infrastructure and technological programmes such as galileo. and of course, this financial support is not subject to any strategic assessment of the need and effectiveness of the establishment of such corridors. here again, public money could be put to better use.
in writing. the green paper on the application of eu criminal justice legislation in the field of detention reveals an alarming picture of prison overcrowding and the increasing number of prisoners in pre-trial detention suffering from physical or mental disorders, as well as a high number of deaths and suicides. conditions of detention must be compatible with human dignity. the rights of suspects or accused persons must be guaranteed, including the right not to be subjected to inhuman or degrading treatment. furthermore, pre-trial detention must remain an exceptional measure and be applied for a limited period only. the european union must remain a model for the protection of fundamental rights. we therefore ask the commission to come forward with a proposal for a law on the rights of persons deprived of their liberty containing minimum standards for the conditions of imprisonment and detention, as well as uniform standards for compensation for persons wrongfully detained or sentenced.
in writing. decent prison conditions are needed in a union of states of law such as the european union. prisoners must be able to enjoy the same fundamental rights as non-captive citizens. unfortunately, the conditions in prisons in many member states are deplorable. overcrowding and suicides are all too often associated with the reality of european prisons. in order to improve prison living conditions, the commission will have to propose new legislation guaranteeing the protection of the fundamental rights of european prisoners and limiting the use of pretrial detention. member states are also invited to increase their funding for prisons. the conditions of life for prisoners must be improved because the rehabilitation of offenders begins in prison.
in writing. i was a co-signer of this joint resolution of our european parliament, and i welcome its adoption: in it we urge the eu states to take urgent measures to ensure respect for the fundamental rights of prisoners, especially vulnerable persons, and we ask the european commission to propose a law on persons deprived of their liberty and minimum standards for conditions of detention. the conditions of detention in the european union are regularly condemned by the european court of human rights (echr) in strasbourg. the latest conviction, a judgment of 20 january 2011, where the echr once again points to the french prison conditions for violation of article 3 (prohibition of inhuman and degrading treatment). the european prisons are suffering from many problems, there are human rights abuses, a denial of the dignity of the detained persons, etc. but respect for human rights must not stop at the prison gates, and we must quickly remedy this shameful situation.
in writing. detention conditions in europe are characterised by a very wide disparity, whether in terms of pretrial detention, prison overcrowding, or the detention of minors and third-country nationals. but we have a duty to ensure that the rights of european citizens deprived of their liberty are respected, wherever they are in europe. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the european commission to come forward with a legislative proposal to define and implement minimum standards on conditions of detention and uniform standards for compensation for those wrongfully detained or sentenced. member states should devote appropriate resources to the rehabilitation of certain prisons where living conditions are alarming, and ensure that preventive detention is used only as a last resort. it is also essential to ensure the best interests of detained minors and to ensure that states have effective and independent national mechanisms for monitoring prisons and detention centres in order to prevent torture or other inhuman and degrading treatment.
in writing. in europe, more than 630 000 people are currently incarcerated. the european parliament had to react to the alarming picture presented by the european commission in its green paper on prisons in europe - prison overcrowding, massive use of pretrial detention, a high number of prisoners suffering from physical or mental disorders, a high number of deaths and suicides. we therefore urge the member states to take urgent measures to ensure that the fundamental rights of prisoners, especially the vulnerable, are respected and protected. the commission must also submit a legislative proposal on the rights of persons deprived of their liberty. europe must define and implement both minimum standards for conditions of incarceration and detention and uniform standards for compensation for those wrongfully detained or sentenced. i have supported this resolution and i now hope that action will be taken quickly, both at national and european level.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution, which is the result of the joint work of all the political groups. there are almost 700 000 people in prison in europe at the moment, and these citizens have rights that must be respected. the purpose of this resolution is to highlight the current shortcomings and to propose ways of improving this disastrous situation. the text points to the failure to comply with european regulations in terms of detention in many eu member states, which leads to prison overcrowding, high suicide rates and a lot of physical and mental suffering. the resolution also calls on the commission and the council to recognise certain categories of prisoners as particularly vulnerable, including minors and illegal immigrants, and to translate this recognition into rights. the european union, the champion of respect for human rights, would have everything to gain from enforcing its own fundamental rights even in our prisons. let us hope that this will not be another pious wish, and that this "good" will displayed will not be once again dismissed as a piece of paper.
in writing. relations between the european union and uzbekistan are governed by a partnership agreement concluded in 1996. partnership and cooperation agreements (pcas) between the eu and non-eu countries are designed to promote and consolidate democracy and contribute to the economic development of the countries concerned. in this case, the aim is to extend the agreement to the textile sector. however, several cases of forced child labour in the cotton production sector have been identified. before approving such a protocol, rapporteur george sabin cutas proposed that the international labour organisation (ilo) investigate the matter. i am in favour of such a procedure and have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which will ensure legal certainty in trade between the union and the republic of uzbekistan. the implementation of these measures is of course conditional on all the contracting parties complying with the rules laid down by the international labour organisation.
in writing. i supported this report on the signing of an agreement between uzbekistan and the european union on textiles, as it underlines the european parliament's commitment to the protection of children and the fight against forced labour. in the context of this report, the european parliament asks the council to obtain satisfaction on a number of points relating to child labour before concluding the agreement. i have supported recital l, which denounces the penalties imposed on children, teachers and their parents for not complying with work obligations (cotton harvesting).
in writing. i support the pressure on uzbekistan proposed in this report to end forced child labour. this should be a precondition for any partnership agreement, which is clearly not something the negotiators are concerned about. but i am against the desire to privatise and liberalise the agricultural sector which this report advocates. i'll abstain from it.
in writing. this interim report confirms our concerns about the general situation of human rights, democratisation and the rule of law in uzbekistan. i am particularly concerned about the repeated allegations of forced labour, especially of children. several sources tell us that during the cotton harvest, schools are closed and children and teachers have to go to work in the fields, for little or no pay. we have called on the commerce commissioner, karel de gucht, several times, but have never received a satisfactory explanation or commitment. i voted in favour of this report because it makes the approval of a future trade agreement with uzbekistan conditional on confirmation by ilo observers that concrete reforms have been implemented and have produced tangible results, resulting in the effective phasing out of the practice of forced labour and forced child labour at national, provincial and local levels.
in writing. i voted against several paragraphs of the resolution on the mobility of workers within the european union, and against the resolution as a whole, because i consider that this resolution, added at the last minute to the agenda of the plenary session, has not been the subject of sufficient debate in the parliamentary committees concerned. moreover, although we are deeply european and strongly defend the free movement of workers within the eu every day, i believe that the current economic context requires us to concentrate our efforts at national level, in order to combat youth unemployment in particular.
in writing. i voted against the resolution on the free movement of workers in the european union. the aim of this text was to open the labour markets of the eu member states fully to romanian and bulgarian workers. the resolution was added to the agenda of the plenary in extremis and was not examined in advance by the committee responsible. the member states have until 31 december this year to use the possibility offered by the treaties to postpone the full opening of their labour markets by two years. the european parliament, through this resolution, expresses its wish to see the barriers to the full free movement of romanian and bulgarian workers removed by the end of this year. that is why i voted against this resolution. of course, i am in favour of the free movement of workers within the european area, but the unprecedented crisis we are going through, the extent of unemployment - especially among young people - forces us to concentrate all our efforts at national level so that our fellow citizens can find their way back to employment.
in writing. the resolution calls on the member states to lift the transitional restrictions they impose on bulgarian and romanian citizens. it recalls that the right to live and work in another member state of the union is a fundamental element of citizenship of the union. in this sense, it sends a positive political signal. but it supports the commission's proposal to allow states to justify the maintenance of their restrictions where the resolution i proposed with my group calls for the lifting of these restrictions before the end of 2011, in line with the accession timetable. the right of workers to freedom of movement and establishment cannot be allowed to take precedence over the free movement of capital in this europe. the decline in civil rights in europe is a disgrace.
in writing. this report highlights many of the points i share in respecting human rights and the environment. unfortunately, this is just a mask for imperialist views. the text sees central asia primarily as a "potential source of energy security for the union". it also called on the countries of central asia to join the wto and to implement 'market-oriented structural reforms'. i vote against it.
in writing. accidents and work-related illnesses now affect between 168 000 and 7 million european citizens. although there is european legislation on health and safety at work, these figures are still too high! i therefore voted in favour of the delli report which calls for an evaluation of the effects of new technologies and for the inclusion of nanomaterials, the use of which poses certain risks, in the legislation in force.
in writing. every year, 168 000 european citizens die from work-related accidents or diseases, and 7 million are victims of accidents at work. the increasing number of sick leave for physical and psychological reasons is a sign of the great unease in the world of work in europe today. ensuring health and safety at work is therefore one of the major challenges in the daily lives of employees. good working conditions are necessary to ensure trust in the relationship between workers and employers. i fully support the values advocated by mrs delli's own-initiative report, which was adopted by a very large majority on thursday 15 december. the recognition and assessment of the potential risks associated with the use and presence of new technologies - such as nanomaterials - in the workplace is an important step forward. above all, awareness of the challenge of work-related stress is crucial. stress is a major barrier to productivity in europe and is characterised by a real feeling of malaise among many workers. to counteract this, there is still a need to increase awareness and understanding among employers, workers and their representatives.
in writing. technological developments and changing economic and social conditions are constantly changing workplaces and practices. the european parliament called for the adoption of a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work and for the adoption of a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to asbestos at work. in this context, persons responsible for warning of potential risks at their workplace must be able to enjoy a certain degree of protection in order to avoid that these persons are subject to pressure (threat of dismissal, etc.). we, the members of the european parliament, ask the commission to propose a directive on this matter in the near future. moreover, stress at work is not yet sufficiently taken into account by employers, workers and their representatives, which is why we also want the commission to take the necessary measures to ensure that the framework agreement on stress at work in the eu is properly implemented in each member state.
in writing. the delli report aims to propose a mid-term evaluation of the european strategy for health and safety at work 2007-2012. i was very much involved in this issue, and i was the epp's fictitious rapporteur for the kadenbach opinion in the envi committee. i supported this report in plenary because it is a good report, which seeks to take account of the new psychosocial, environmental and physical issues (in particular musculoskeletal disorders).
in writing. this text is a good start. it's too bad it's only declarative. it develops a comprehensive conception of the risks of occupational accidents and diseases. it stresses in particular the precarious nature of work and its consequences for workers' health. the committee is concerned about the progressive taxation of workers in atypical forms of work, such as part-time work, teleworking, reduced hours, sunday work and night work. it also called for the introduction of sanctions for companies which do not respect workers' rights and for the strengthening of labour inspection. these are all positive points which make me vote for this text despite the wish it expresses to 'extend the working life of older workers' which may raise the retirement age of our fellow citizens, which i condemn. i shall vote in favour of it, however.
in writing. we have legislated a lot on health and safety at work: the osh framework directive, several specific directives, the reach regulation... yet more than 160 000 european citizens die each year from work-related illnesses or accidents. it is therefore important to ensure that the spirit of the texts is respected when they are implemented in the member states and to ensure that the crucial role of labour inspectorates on the spot is strengthened. this report, which i supported, proposes in parallel to adapt and develop this european legislative acquis, to take account of several current challenges, including: the prevention of psychosocial risks at the workplace; the preservation of physical and mental integrity in a context of extended working life; or the consideration of potential risks linked to new technologies, dangerous substances, nanomaterials. finally, the prevention and protection policies must be adapted to cover new categories of workers at risk (chemical risks, radioactive substances, toxic substances) or workers with atypical forms of employment (temporary, posted, seasonal, part-time or teleworking workers, etc.).
for the gue/ngl group mr president, i will not comment on the assassination of mr rafiq tagi, nor on the human rights situation in azerbaijan. i have had the opportunity to do so before in this house. i would like to express my regret, once again, at the choice of our emergencies and the way we deal with them. i would like to speak about the situation of the refugees in the ashraf camp: 3,500 people are currently in that camp, including 1,000 women and many children. the united states has just announced the withdrawal of its troops by december 31, 2011; i do not regret it, but i am thinking that from this date, no protection will be provided to the refugees in camp ashraf. what will happen to them, as the iraqi government continues to consider them terrorists? the un, the council of europe, mrs ashton are all calling for protection for these people. unhcr says he needs time. why has the council of ministers refused to take account of mrs ashton's request to take in these refugees who have links with their member states? i believe - and i will stop here, mr president - that once again, unfortunately, the french government has been in the forefront. i'm really sorry about that.
for the gue/ngl group mr president, we are once again going to be outraged by the situation in afghanistan and pakistan, and in particular by the situation of women's rights, including the right to vote. it has already been said, these countries are the unfortunate champions of violations of women's rights: life expectancy, rape, murder, honor killings. the list is long and many of my colleagues have already given examples. i don't think the presence of military forces in afghanistan has brought anything to afghan women, nor will the withdrawal of these forces make anything worse. however, we must put pressure on these countries to change things, and not just from a legal point of view. we have partnership agreements with these countries, so let's use them to good effect, in the interest of the civilian population, in the interest of human rights, in the interest of democracy. let us learn from the mistakes of the past, especially in the maghreb! let us live the clauses of democracy and human rights, and we shall all be better off.
author. - mr president, i am a little surprised that we are here today to consider an emergency resolution on human rights in tunisia. i would have preferred the majority of this parliament to have paid more attention to this before december 2010. we know, as do the tunisian democrats, how silent the european union was until 14 february 2011 on the human rights violations under the ben ali regime. i must admit that the first line of our resolution is not without flavour in this respect. read it and you'll see! but the past is the past, and it can't be rewritten. we can just try to learn from it. tunisia is moving towards a democratic transition. the elections on 23 october were a success. the results are in. we must respect the choice of the tunisian people. it is to be welcomed that the new tunisian authorities have already signed a large number of international conventions. we must help them to implement them without interfering. the former rcdists are still flooding the administration, especially the judiciary and the police. the burps mentioned here bear witness to this. let us help the new tunisia, but let us avoid giving it lessons. and above all, commissioner, let us avoid being more demanding of this new tunisia than we have been in the past in terms of democracy and human rights. let's be careful how we deliver messages to them. i think it's very important.
in writing. it's been a year since ben ali left power. a year later, however, the same practices as under the old regime are still in place. the regular use by the police of violent practices and acts against the population, contrary to tunisia's international human rights commitments, is also noted. the events at tunis-carthage airport on 13 november are one example. zacharia bouguira, a student, witnessed acts of violence by the police against a group of young moroccans. he filmed the scene with his cell phone so that it could be broadcast. his initiative was immediately stopped by a security guard, and he was severely beaten. a complaint has been filed. i therefore call on the authorities to engage in a process of reform of the security sector (including police and justice), to ensure the independence of the judiciary and to guarantee the freedom and independence of the press and media. i believe that for these reforms to be accepted by the population, the broadest possible involvement of civil society organisations active in this field is necessary.
